cases.title: de Bruijn `Expr.bvar` / `Expr.fvar` lowered to a NAMED `Term::Var`
cases.lean: Expr.bvar, Expr.fvar, binder names as hints, hygienic/inaccessible names
cases.target: Term::Var(String) — kernel/src/term.rs:447. Every `bvar i` becomes the *name* of the binder `i` levels out, after a freshening pass that makes every binder name in the emitted term globally distinct from every other binder it could shadow.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term` has exactly one variable form, `Var(String)`; there is NO `bvar`/`fvar` distinction and no de Bruijn index); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:57-61 (`Var` is resolved by NAME against `Context`, which context.rs:228-236 implements as a `HashMap<String, Arc<Term>>` — so two binders with the same name are literally the same key and the inner one *erases* the outer); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1088-1110 (`substitute_avoiding` alpha-renames a binder only when the REPLACEMENT's free variables would be captured — it does not repair a term that was already emitted with a wrong name); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:137-140 (`is_meta`: any `Var` whose name starts with `?` is treated as an elaborator metavariable, not as a bound variable); kernel/src/recheck.rs (the second kernel converts back to de Bruijn — a naming bug shows up as a disagreement between the two kernels, not as a clean error)
guards: Catches the "binder names are only hints, so reuse them verbatim" translator. Lean binder names are non-unique *by design*: `fun x => fun x => x` is a legal `Expr` whose two `x` binders are distinguished only by de Bruijn index. Emitting both as `Var("x")` does not fail — `Context` is a name-keyed map, so the inner binding simply shadows the outer, and the term still typechecks with the WRONG variable resolved at every occurrence that meant the outer one. This is the canonical silent mistranslation: `infer_type` succeeds, the inferred type is plausible, and the meaning is different.

Catches emitting Lean's *inaccessible* / macro-scoped names (`x✝`, `n✝¹`, `_uniq.1234`) verbatim. `Universe`/`Term` names are flat `String`s with no interning discipline, so `x✝` and `x✝¹` are distinct keys and happen to work — but a sanitiser that strips the dagger collapses them onto one key, reintroducing the capture above. Any sanitiser must be injective over the binders live at each point.

Catches a sanitiser that emits a `?`-prefixed name. `elaborate.rs:137-140` classifies `Var("?x")` as a metavariable and `instantiate` will silently replace it with whatever the metavariable context has solved for `?x` — i.e. a bound variable is rewritten into an unrelated term. `?` must never appear in a translated binder name.

Catches confusing `fvar` with `Term::Global`. A Lean free variable is a *local* hypothesis and must become `Term::Var`; lowering it to `Term::Global` sends it through `get_global` (context.rs:449: inductives → constructors → definitions → declarations), where it either fails with `UnboundVariable` or — far worse — resolves to a same-named global from the prelude.
oracle: For every binder in the emitted term, the set of binder names in scope at that point has no duplicates; no emitted `Var` name starts with `?`; `infer_type` succeeds; and re-checking the same term through `recheck.rs`'s de Bruijn kernel yields the same type. A term that passes `infer_type` but not the de Bruijn re-check is a naming bug.

cases.title: `Expr.sort` at concrete levels — the `Sort n` / `Type n` index shift
cases.lean: Expr.sort, Prop, Sort 0, Sort 1, Type, Type 0, Type 1, Type 2
cases.target: Term::Sort(Universe) — kernel/src/term.rs:445. `Prop` ≡ `Sort 0`  ⟼ `Sort(Universe::Prop)` `Type 0` ≡ `Sort 1` ⟼ `Sort(Universe::Type(0))` `Type n` ≡ `Sort (n+1)` ⟼ `Sort(Universe::Type(n))`
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:167-191 (`Universe::{SProp, Prop, Type(u32), Var, Succ, Max, IMax}` — `Prop` is a SEPARATE constructor from `Type(0)`, and `Type` carries a concrete `u32`, not a level expression); kernel/src/term.rs:266-276 (`to_lnat`: LOGOS's internal decision encoding is `Prop = 0`, `Type n = n+1` — the SAME shift Lean uses between `Sort` and `Type`, which is exactly why copying it into the surface representation produces an off-by-one); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:54 (`Sort(u) : Sort(u.succ())`)
guards: Catches the off-by-one that comes from reading LOGOS's internal `to_lnat` encoding (term.rs:266-276, where `Type n ↦ n+1`) and using it as the surface mapping. Lean's `Expr.sort (.succ .zero)` is `Type 0`, so `Sort (n+1)` must become `Type(n)`, NOT `Type(n+1)`. Every level in the file is then one too high. Because LOGOS is cumulative (type_checker.rs:1330-1336), a uniformly-too-high level still accepts every term that the correct one did — the error only surfaces when a *declared* type says `Type 0` and the computed one says `Type 1`, typically many declarations later.

Catches `Prop ↦ Universe::Type(0)`. They are distinct enum constructors and the kernel dispatches on them SYNTACTICALLY in three soundness-critical places: the large-elimination gate (type_checker.rs:277-288 matches `Term::Sort(Universe::Prop)`), definitional proof irrelevance (type_checker.rs:1553-1560, same match), and `imax` (term.rs:222-228, where `imax(a, Prop) = Prop` but `imax(a, Type 0) = max(a, Type 0)`). Mapping `Prop` to `Type(0)` therefore (a) silently disables proof irrelevance, (b) silently disables the large-elimination restriction, and (c) makes every `∀` into a proposition predicative. None of the three produces an error. See T01-001 and T01-010 for the full treatment.

Catches `Sort u` for a *variable* `u` being forced into `Type(u32)`. `Universe::Type` takes a concrete `u32`; there is no `Type(<expr>)` form. A `Sort u` must become `Sort(Universe::Var("u"))`, which is only bindable on a definition — see T01-003.
oracle: For each `Expr.sort` in the source, the emitted `Universe` matches the table in `@target` exactly (structural equality on the `Universe` enum, not `Universe::equiv`, which would hide a `Prop`/`Type 0` confusion under cumulativity); and `infer_type(Sort(u))` returns `Sort(u.succ())` with the level the Lean kernel reports for the same `Expr`, modulo the documented `Prop` discrepancy of T01-010.

cases.title: `Expr.const` with an empty level list lowers to `Term::Global`, never `Term::Const`
cases.lean: Expr.const (levels := []), references to monomorphic declarations
cases.target: Term::Global(String) — kernel/src/term.rs:448. `Term::Const { name, levels }` (term.rs:458) is reserved for universe-POLYMORPHIC references only (see T01-006).
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Global(String)` and `Const { name, levels }` are two different variants); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:63-67 (`Global` is resolved by `ctx.get_global`); kernel/src/context.rs:449 (`get_global` searches, in order, inductives → constructors → definitions → declarations — FIRST match wins); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:69-85 (`Const` is resolved ONLY by `ctx.get_universe_poly`, a disjoint map; a `Const` naming a plain definition is `UnboundVariable` no matter how many levels it carries); kernel/src/reduction.rs:82-91 (delta for `Const` looks in `universe_polys` and, on a miss OR an arity mismatch, silently returns the term UNREDUCED — no error)
guards: Catches `Expr.const n []` ⟼ `Term::Const { name: n, levels: vec![] }`, which is the obvious structural match and is wrong. `infer_type` sends `Const` to `get_universe_poly` (type_checker.rs:70-72), which does not contain plain definitions, so the reference fails as an unbound variable. That failure is at least loud — the dangerous half is `reduce_step` (reduction.rs:82-91), which on the same miss returns the term unchanged with no diagnostic. So a `Const` that *is* registered but with the wrong level arity becomes silently OPAQUE: every `rfl`-style proof that needed it to unfold now fails, and the translator sees "the theorem did not prove", not "the reference was malformed".

Catches ignoring `get_global`'s lookup PRECEDENCE (context.rs:449). LOGOS keys are flat `String`s with one namespace shared by inductives, constructors, definitions and axioms. If the translator emits a definition named `Nat` (say, from Lean's `MyLib.Nat` flattened to `Nat`), every later `Global("Nat")` resolves to the prelude INDUCTIVE instead, because inductives are searched first. The definition is simply never reachable, and nothing reports it. (Name flattening in general is T02-011 / T02-020; this case guards only the resolution-order half of it.)

Catches emitting a constructor reference as `Global` of the *inductive*'s name or vice versa. `Nat.succ` and `Nat` are separate keys in separate maps; a translator that mangles both to the same flat string makes `get_global` return the inductive's sort where a constructor's type was meant.
oracle: Every emitted `Term::Global(n)` satisfies `ctx.get_global(n).is_some()`, and `ctx.get_universe_poly(n).is_none()`; every emitted `Term::Const { name, levels }` satisfies `ctx.get_universe_poly(name)` with `params.len() == levels.len()`. Additionally, no emitted name resolves through `get_global` to a declaration of a different kind than the Lean source referenced.

cases.title: Dependent function type whose binder is used in the codomain
cases.lean: Expr.forallE (dependent), ∀ / Π binder
cases.target: Term::Pi { param: "n", param_type: Global("Nat"), body_type: <uses Var "n"> }
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:463 (Term::Pi has a named `param`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:108 (Pi formation computes the result sort with `imax`, matching Lean)
guards: Catches binder-name erasure. LOGOS's Display renders a Pi whose `param == "_"` as a non-dependent arrow `A -> B` (term.rs:585-590). A translator that lowers every `forallE` with `param := "_"` — tempting, since Lean's binder names are only hints — produces a term that *prints* as an arrow while its body contains `Var("_")`, which then either captures a later `_` binder or fails lookup. Lean's de Bruijn body must be inspected: emit a fresh name iff `bvar 0` occurs, `"_"` iff it does not.

Also catches name capture: two nested binders both named `n` are legal in Lean (de Bruijn) but in LOGOS's *named* representation the inner shadows the outer, and `substitute` alpha-renames only when the replacement's free variables collide (type_checker.rs:1088). Nested same-name binders must be freshened at emit time.
oracle: LOGOS `infer_type` on the emitted term returns a `Sort`; and `is_subtype` against the translation of Lean's inferred type succeeds. Additionally the emitted `param` must not be `"_"` for this case.

cases.title: `Expr.lam` — nesting, the mandatory domain type, and the dropped `BinderInfo`
cases.lean: Expr.lam, BinderInfo.{default, implicit, strictImplicit, instImplicit}, nested `fun`
cases.target: Term::Lambda { param: String, param_type: Box<Term>, body: Box<Term> } — kernel/src/term.rs:464. Nested `fun`s become nested `Lambda`s, outermost first. Binder kind is recorded OUT OF BAND, on the enclosing declaration, via `Context::set_binder_kinds(name, kinds)` with `ParamKind::{Explicit, Implicit, Instance}`.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:464-468 (`Term::Lambda` has exactly three fields — there is no `binder_info`); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1016-1027 (`ParamKind` has THREE variants — `Explicit`, `Implicit`, `Instance`; Lean's `strictImplicit` has no counterpart, see T05-002); kernel/src/context.rs:201 (`set_binder_kinds` is keyed on a declaration NAME, so an anonymous lambda has nowhere to carry its binder kinds); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:112-131 (`Lambda` inference requires `param_type` to be a well-formed sort — the domain is not optional and cannot be inferred from context); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:474-500 (`check_type`'s Lambda-against-Pi special case, which is what tempts a translator to leave the domain as a placeholder)
guards: Catches leaving `param_type` as `Term::Hole` when Lean's binder type came from the expected type rather than from the source. `check_type` (type_checker.rs:468-471) accepts ANY term against a `Hole` expected type and `types_equal` (type_checker.rs:1594-1597) treats a `Hole` as matching anything, so the lambda typechecks — and the `Hole` then propagates into the inferred `Pi`'s `param_type`, where it makes every later application of that function typecheck regardless of the argument's type. See T00-016; this is the single most common way a `Hole` escapes.

Catches recording binder kinds on the LAMBDA. There is no field for them. They must be lifted to the enclosing declaration with `set_binder_kinds`, and a lambda that is not the body of a named declaration (an argument, a match case, a motive) simply cannot carry them — so `fun {α : Type} (a : α) => a` passed as an argument loses its implicitness, and every use site the translator generates must then supply `α` explicitly. A translator that emits the same call shape for both kinds produces either an arity mismatch or, worse, an argument silently bound to the wrong parameter.

Catches flattening nesting. `Term::Lambda` is unary; `fun a b c => e` is three nested `Lambda`s and the ORDER is load-bearing — `infer_type` builds the `Pi` outside-in (type_checker.rs:125-130), so a reversed telescope produces a well-typed function of the wrong type, which then still applies to arguments of the swapped types.

Catches collapsing `strictImplicit` (`⦃x⦄`) onto `Implicit`. `ParamKind` has no strict variant (elaborate.rs:1018-1027), and `Implicit` makes the elaborator insert a metavariable EAGERLY (elaborate.rs:1029-1035) where Lean would have waited for a later explicit argument — changing which unification problems are solvable.
oracle: No emitted `Lambda` has `Hole` as its `param_type`; the emitted telescope order matches the Lean `Expr` binder order; `infer_type` returns a `Pi` whose spine is the translation of Lean's inferred type; and for every named declaration the recorded `binder_kinds` vector has the same length as the declaration's leading `Pi` telescope.

cases.title: `Expr.app` — left-nested binary spines, partial application, argument order
cases.lean: Expr.app, `f a b c`, partial application, `Expr.getAppFn` / `getAppArgs`
cases.target: Term::App(Box<Term>, Box<Term>) — kernel/src/term.rs:470. `f a b c` is `App(App(App(f, a), b), c)`: binary, LEFT-nested, head innermost.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:470 (`App` is binary — there is no n-ary application node and no separate head/args representation); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:144-181 (`App` inference: infer the function's type, NORMALIZE it if it is not already a `Pi`, check the argument against `param_type`, then `substitute` the argument into `body_type`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:176 (the result type is `substitute(body_type, param, arg)` — so argument order determines which binder each argument lands in); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1267-1299 (`spine` decomposes a left-nested `App` chain — the canonical shape the rest of the elaborator assumes)
guards: Catches right-nesting. `App(f, App(a, App(b, c)))` is a *well-formed* `Term` and will be reported as `NotAFunction` only if `a`'s type is not a `Pi` — but when the arguments are themselves functions (higher-order code, a motive, a fold), `a b c` is perfectly well-typed and the whole thing typechecks as `f (a b c)`. That is a completely different term with a plausible type, and no error is produced.

Catches reversing the argument order. `type_checker.rs:176` substitutes positionally; with two arguments of the same type (`f : Nat → Nat → Nat`) a swap is undetectable by the kernel and changes the value. The file below therefore includes a non-commutative function at two same-typed arguments.

Catches placing universe levels in the spine. For a universe-polymorphic head, the levels belong on the `Term::Const { name, levels }` NODE (term.rs:458), not as leading `App` arguments; a translator that models Lean's `Expr.const n [u]` as `App(Global(n), <level>)` produces a term whose head has the wrong arity and whose first "argument" is a sort. See T01-006.

Catches *eagerly beta-reducing* a partial application into a lambda in order to "normalise" it. `type_checker.rs:148-152` already normalizes the function's type when it is not a `Pi` head, so no such help is needed, and reducing changes the term the certificate records.

Catches dropping implicit arguments that Lean elaborated in. Lean's `Expr` spine is fully explicit; the `@`-form and the non-`@`-form produce the SAME `Expr`. A translator that re-derives the spine from surface syntax will emit too few arguments, and `infer_type` will then return a `Pi` where a saturated type was expected — a type that is still well-formed, so it propagates.
oracle: `Expr.getAppFn` / `Expr.getAppNumArgs` on the Lean side and `elaborate::spine` on the LOGOS side agree on head and arity for every application in the file; `infer_type` of the emitted term equals the translation of Lean's inferred type; and a partially applied spine infers a `Pi` with exactly the remaining binders.

cases.title: `Expr.letE` lowers to `Term::Let`, which is zeta-TRANSPARENT during type checking
cases.lean: Expr.letE, `let x : A := v; b`
cases.target: Term::Let { name: String, ty: Box<Term>, value: Box<Term>, body: Box<Term> } — kernel/src/term.rs:475.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:475 (`Term::Let` carries the ANNOTATED type `ty` as well as the value — both must be emitted; the type is not optional); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:133-142 (`Let` inference: check `ty` is a sort, check `value : ty`, then `substitute(body, name, value)` and infer the type of the RESULT — i.e. the let-bound name is zeta-expanded away before the body is typed, so the body sees `x ≡ v` definitionally, not an opaque hypothesis of type `A`); kernel/src/reduction.rs:298 (`reduce_step` on `Let` performs the same zeta substitution); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1088-1110 (`substitute_avoiding` — the substitution used, capture-avoiding but O(size) per crossed binder)
guards: Catches lowering `letE` to a beta-redex `App(Lambda { param, param_type: A, body }, v)`. This is the standard "lets are just applications" move and it is WRONG here: the `App` rule (type_checker.rs:144-177) types the lambda's body with `x : A` OPAQUE and only substitutes into the resulting *type* afterwards. So any body whose type or whose later definitional equalities depend on `x`'s VALUE stops typechecking. `Term::Let` is not sugar for that redex in LOGOS — it is strictly stronger. (T00-017 is the dedicated dependent-body case; this guard is its converse, and it matters even for non-dependent bodies because it silently changes which `rfl`s go through.)

Catches the opposite error: lowering Lean's `have` (`letFun`) to `Term::Let`. Lean's `have` is deliberately OPAQUE — the elaborator does not let the goal see the value — so translating it to a zeta-transparent `Let` makes LOGOS accept proofs that Lean rejects. That is the over-permissive direction, which the kernel will not catch. See T00-019.

Catches dropping the `ty` field or filling it with `Term::Hole`. `type_checker.rs:139` calls `infer_sort(ctx, ty)`, but `check_type` accepts anything against a `Hole` expected type (type_checker.rs:468-471), so a `Hole` here disables the check that the value actually has the annotated type — and the annotation is the only place the Lean-side type is recorded. See T00-016.

Catches assuming `Let` restores SHARING. It does not: `type_checker.rs:141` substitutes the value at EVERY occurrence before typing the body, so a value used `n` times is checked `n` times, and nested lets multiply. A translator that introduces `Let` nodes to compress a large term makes checking exponentially slower, not faster, and can push `normalize` past its 10000-step fuel (reduction.rs:52-69). See T00-022.
oracle: The emitted term is a `Term::Let` (not an `App`/`Lambda` pair); `infer_type` succeeds and yields the translation of Lean's inferred type; and `def_eq(Let{x,A,v,b}, b[x:=v])` holds — the test that distinguishes `Let` from the beta-redex encoding.

cases.title: `Expr.lit` — `Nat` literals and `String` literals land in different LOGOS worlds
cases.lean: Expr.lit (.natVal n), Expr.lit (.strVal s), OfNat.ofNat elaboration
cases.target: `Expr.lit (.natVal n)`  ⟼ `Term::Lit(Literal::Nat(BigInt))`, typed `Global("Nat")` `Expr.lit (.strVal s)`  ⟼ `Term::Lit(Literal::Text(String))`, typed `Global("Text")`
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:13-44 (`Literal::{Int(i64), Float, Text(String), Duration, Date, Moment, BigInt, Nat(BigInt)}` — `Nat` and `Int` are SEPARATE literal constructors, and there is no `String`/`Char` literal, only `Text`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:294-312 (`Lit` typing: `Nat(_) ↦ Global("Nat")`, `Int(_)`/`BigInt(_) ↦ Global("Int")`, `Text(_) ↦ Global("Text")`; a negative `Literal::Nat` is a `CertificationError`); kernel/src/prelude.rs (`Nat` is an INDUCTIVE with constructors `Zero`/`Succ`; `Int` is an OPAQUE zero-constructor inductive whose ring and order laws are AXIOMS at prelude.rs:92-340; `Text` is likewise opaque with no operations at all); kernel/src/reduction.rs:330-345 and kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1480-1493 (the Peano bridge: `Literal::Nat(n)` is DEFINITIONALLY `Succ^n Zero`, peeled one `Succ` at a time)
guards: Catches `Nat` literal ⟼ `Literal::Int`. It typechecks — `Literal::Int` is a perfectly good literal — but its inferred type is `Global("Int")` (type_checker.rs:296), and in LOGOS `Int` is a completely different kind of object from `Nat`: opaque, zero constructors, no `Zero`/`Succ`, arithmetic only via the axioms at prelude.rs:92-340. The consequence is not a type error at the literal; it is that every later `Match` on that value has no constructors to match, every `Fix` over it fails the structural guard, and the Peano bridge (type_checker.rs:1480-1493) never fires — so `2 + 2 = 4` becomes unprovable by computation and provable only from the ring axioms, if at all.

Catches translating Lean's `String` to a LOGOS `String`. There is none. The only text carrier is `Literal::Text`, typed `Global("Text")`, an opaque prelude inductive with ZERO operations — no `++`, no `length`, no decidable equality (LOGOS_FACTS: `String` operations absent). A translator that emits `Text` and carries on will produce statements it can never prove and cannot even state (`s.length` has no target). The literal itself is `translate`; anything that *operates* on it is `reject` — T10-016.

Catches failing to see through `OfNat`. A numeral in Lean source is elaborated to `@OfNat.ofNat Nat 3 instOfNatNat`, i.e. an APPLICATION, not an `Expr.lit`, unless the elaborator has already reduced it. A translator that matches only on `Expr.lit` emits a four-argument spine referring to `OfNat`, `instOfNatNat` and `Nat.lit` — none of which exist in the LOGOS prelude — instead of a literal. It must run `Nat.fromExpr?` / `whnf` first. The dual error is *over*-eager: seeing through `OfNat` for a non-`Nat` type and emitting a `Literal::Nat` where the Lean type was `Int` or a user type with its own `OfNat` instance.

Catches BigInt canonicalisation. `Literal::Nat` carries a `BigInt`, so a literal beyond `i64` is representable — but `Literal::Int` is `i64` (term.rs:14) and `Literal::BigInt` is a *third* variant that also types as `Int`. Round-tripping a large `Nat` through `Literal::Int` truncates silently. See T10-002.
oracle: Every translated Lean `Nat` literal emits `Literal::Nat` with the exact `BigInt` value and infers `Global("Nat")`; every Lean `String` literal emits `Literal::Text` and infers `Global("Text")`; and `def_eq(Lit(Nat(3)), Succ (Succ (Succ Zero)))` holds, confirming the Peano bridge is reachable from the emitted form.

cases.title: `Expr.mdata` is erased — LOGOS `Term` has no metadata carrier
cases.lean: Expr.mdata, Lean.mkAnnotation, pp annotations, source positions, doc comments
cases.target: The mdata WRAPPER is dropped and its payload expression is translated in its place: `mdata k e` ⟼ `translate e`. A loss record naming SOURCE_METADATA is emitted per distinct mdata key encountered.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (the complete `Term` enum: `Sort`, `Var`, `Global`, `Const`, `Pi`, `Lambda`, `App`, `Match`, `Fix`, `MutualFix`, `Let`, `Lit`, `Hole` — there is NO `mdata`, no annotation node, and no side table keyed on terms); kernel/src/context.rs (the `Context` maps carry name → type/body only; there is no attribute map, no position map, no docstring map — LOGOS_FACTS "no namespaces, no `Name` type, no visibility, no attributes, no reducibility hints"); kernel/src/certificate.rs:28 (`PRELUDE_VERSION` is the only provenance a certificate carries — there is nowhere to record a source span)
guards: Catches translating `Expr.mdata` as an APPLICATION of some identity function, which is the tempting way to "keep" the annotation. There is no `id` in the LOGOS prelude (LOGOS_FACTS: the registered inductives and axioms are enumerated and `id` is not among them), so `Global("id")` fails `get_global` (context.rs:449) with `UnboundVariable`; and if the translator instead DEFINES an `id` to wrap with, every annotated subterm gains a delta-redex that changes term size, changes `normalize`'s step count against the 10000-step fuel (reduction.rs:52-69), and blocks the syntactic `Term::Lambda`/`Term::Global` matches that `try_structure_eta` (type_checker.rs:1391-1417) and the termination guard (termination.rs) rely on.

Catches recursing into `mdata` as if it were an opaque leaf. `Expr.mdata` WRAPS a real subterm; a translator that pattern-matches `Expr` without an `mdata` arm will either fall into a catch-all that emits `Term::Hole` (see T00-016, where a `Hole` makes `types_equal` match anything) or throw on a term shape that is completely routine. mdata can appear at ANY position, including as the head of an application and as a binder's domain, so `Expr.consumeMData` must be applied before every structural test, not once at the top.

Catches erasing mdata *uniformly*. The `letFun` annotation is semantically load- bearing (it is how `have` is distinguished from `let` in the elaborated `Expr`), and dropping it turns an opaque `have` into a zeta-transparent `Let`, which makes LOGOS accept proofs Lean rejects. The mdata arm must therefore INSPECT the key and branch, not blanket-strip. See T00-019.

Catches claiming the loss is nil because "the term is unchanged". The term is unchanged; the DIAGNOSTIC SURFACE is not. After erasure there is no way to map a LOGOS `KernelError` back to a Lean source span, so every downstream failure in this corpus is reported against a term the user never wrote.
oracle: `Expr.consumeMData` applied to the Lean side and the emitted `Term` agree structurally; a loss record with category SOURCE_METADATA exists and enumerates the distinct mdata keys erased; and no emitted term contains a wrapper introduced solely to carry an annotation.
loss: SOURCE_METADATA. Everything Lean threads through `Expr.mdata` disappears: source positions (so no LOGOS diagnostic can ever point back at Lean source), pretty-printer hints (`pp_using_anonymous_constructor`, `pp_nodot`), the `letFun` marker that distinguishes `have` from `let` (T00-019 — that one is NOT acceptable to drop silently), and inlining/compiler pragmas. Acceptable for the pretty-printer and position keys because they have no semantic content in Lean either; the erasure must still be RECORDED, because a translator that cannot say which annotations it dropped cannot later prove it dropped only the inert ones.

cases.title: `Expr.mvar` reaching the translator — an uninstantiated metavariable must be refused
cases.lean: Expr.mvar, `?a`, `_` placeholders, delayed-assignment metavariables from tactic blocks
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (the `Term` enum has NO metavariable variant — LOGOS_FACTS states this explicitly: "There is no `Proj`, no metavariable variant, no `mdata`, no `fvar`/`bvar` distinction"); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:137-140 (`is_meta`: LOGOS models elaborator metavariables as `Term::Var` names beginning with `?` — a NAMING CONVENTION inside the elaborator, not a kernel form) and elaborate.rs:142-150 (`instantiate` must have replaced every one of them before the kernel sees the term); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:313 (`Term::Hole => Err(KernelError::CannotInferHole)`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:455-471 (but `check_type` ACCEPTS a `Hole` term against any `Sort`, and accepts any term against a `Hole` expected type) and kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1594-1597 (`types_equal` returns `true` whenever EITHER side is a `Hole`), which is why the kernel is not a backstop here
guards: Catches `Expr.mvar ⟼ Term::Hole`, the natural-looking mapping. It is the worst available option. `CannotInferHole` fires only if the `Hole` lands in a position that `infer_type` actually visits (type_checker.rs:313); a `Hole` sitting in an argument's TYPE, in a `Pi`'s `param_type`, or in a `Let`'s annotation is never inferred — it is only ever *compared*, and `types_equal` (type_checker.rs:1594-1597) says a `Hole` equals anything. The leniency also leaks into `is_subtype`'s fast path (type_checker.rs:1314), so a single surviving `Hole` in a theorem's statement makes that statement satisfiable by a proof of something else entirely. See T00-016.

Catches `Expr.mvar ⟼ Term::Var("?m_1")`, i.e. reusing LOGOS's own metavariable convention. `elaborate.rs:137-140` will classify that `Var` as a metavariable and `instantiate` (elaborate.rs:142-150) will substitute whatever the ambient `MetaCtx` happens to have solved for the name `?m_1` — a name the translator invented, whose collision with a genuine elaborator metavariable is entirely accidental. The result is a term silently rewritten to something unrelated, with no error at any stage.

Catches "the metavariable is obviously `Nat`, so instantiate it". Guessing is a soundness decision disguised as a convenience: LOGOS is cumulative (type_checker.rs:1330-1360), so a guessed type that is merely a SUPERTYPE of the right one still typechecks everywhere, and the error surfaces only where the two differ.

Catches reading the `Expr` before `instantiateMVars`. Every term in this file elaborates to an mvar-free `Expr` — but only AFTER instantiation. A translator hooked in at `Term.elabTerm` rather than at the finished `Declaration` sees live `mvar`s for each `_` below, and `⟨_, rfl⟩`'s witness is assigned only when `rfl` is unified. Delayed-assignment metavariables (produced by every `by` block) are not resolved even by `instantiateMVars` until the tactic block closes.
oracle: The translator runs `instantiateMVars` and then asserts the `Expr` contains no `.mvar`; if any remains it exits non-zero with E_UNINSTANTIATED_METAVARIABLE and writes NO declaration. Independently: the emitted `Term` for every declaration in the corpus contains no `Term::Hole` and no `Term::Var` whose name starts with `?`.
diag: E_UNINSTANTIATED_METAVARIABLE — must name the metavariable, the declaration it was found in, and the position in the term. Must NOT emit a `Term::Hole`, a `Term::Var("?…")`, or a guessed instantiation.

cases.title: `Expr.proj` on library structures — `Prod`, `Sigma`, `Subtype` are not in LOGOS at all
cases.lean: Expr.proj, Prod.fst/.snd, Sigma.fst/.snd, Subtype.val, `.1` / `.2`
cases.target: For each Lean structure the source projects out of, the translator must FIRST emit a `Context::add_structure(name, params, fields)` declaration, and then lower each `Expr.proj S i e` to the generated field DEFINITION applied to the structure's parameters and then the receiver: `p.1` with `p : Prod α β` ⟼ `App(App(App(Global("Prod_fst"), α), β), p)`.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term` has no `Proj` variant — `Expr.proj` has no direct counterpart); kernel/src/context.rs:271-369 (`add_structure` desugars a record into an indexed inductive, a `{name}_mk` constructor, and one ordinary DEFINITION per field whose body is a `Term::Match`); kernel/src/context.rs:295-301 (the generated inductive is `pis(params, Term::Sort(Universe::Type(0)))` — the sort is HARD-CODED to `Type 0`); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1262-1299 (`elaborate_dot` builds `{hname}_{field}` applied to the receiver's type arguments FIRST and the receiver LAST); kernel/src/prelude.rs and LOGOS_FACTS ("Absent entirely: `Subtype`, `Sigma`, `PSigma`, `Option`, `List`, `Prod`, `Sum`, `Fin`, `Char`, `Array`, `String` operations, `UInt*`, `HEq`, `Setoid`, `Quotient`"); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1391-1417 (`try_structure_eta`, reachable only from `def_eq_normalized` at :1473-1478, and only for names in the `structures` registry)
guards: Catches assuming `Prod`/`Sigma`/`Subtype` EXIST in the LOGOS prelude and emitting `Global("Prod_fst")` without declaring anything. `get_global` (context.rs:449) then fails with `UnboundVariable` — the loud case — but a translator that pre-seeds a partial prelude gets the far worse case: `Prod` declared with `add_inductive` (UNCHECKED, context.rs:253) and no constructors, so every `Match` on it has `cases.len() == 0 == ctor count` and vacuously passes the positional check at type_checker.rs:254-260. A projection out of it then returns whatever the motive says.

Catches emitting the projection with the receiver FIRST. `elaborate_dot` (elaborate.rs:1290-1296) applies the structure's parameters before the receiver, so `Prod_fst p` is an arity error at best and, when `α` and the receiver happen to have compatible types (`Prod Type Type`), a silently wrong term.

Catches translating `Expr.proj` as an opaque AXIOM `Prod_fst : Prod α β → α` via `add_declaration` (context.rs:434). It typechecks and it is consistent — and it makes `(a, b).1 = a` UNPROVABLE, so every downstream `rfl` about a pair fails for a reason the translator cannot attribute.

Catches translating `Sigma` as `Prod`. `Sigma`'s second field's TYPE mentions the first field's VALUE; `add_structure` supports that (context.rs:307-320 rewrites earlier field references), but a translator that erases the dependency emits a non-dependent pair whose projections have the wrong types and whose `Match` motive is constant — which still typechecks for the non-dependent instances in a test suite.
oracle: Each projected Lean structure has a corresponding `add_structure` in the emitted context; each `Expr.proj S i e` becomes `Global("S_field_i")` applied to the receiver's type arguments then the receiver; `def_eq(⟨a,b⟩.1, a)` holds; a loss record carries PROJECTION_PRIMITIVITY and LIBRARY_STRUCTURE_SYNTHESIS; and any projection at a universe level above `Type 0` is REJECTED rather than emitted.
loss: PROJECTION_PRIMITIVITY. Lean's `.proj` is a kernel primitive reducing in ONE iota step; the LOGOS encoding is a delta-unfold to a `Match`, so reduction costs two steps and counts against `normalize`'s 10000-step fuel (reduction.rs:52-69), and eta holds only inside `def_eq`, never under `normalize`.

LIBRARY_STRUCTURE_SYNTHESIS. `Prod`, `Sigma` and `Subtype` are not declared anywhere in LOGOS, so the translator must MANUFACTURE them. Their Lean definitions are universe-polymorphic (`Prod : Type u → Type v → Type (max u v)`), and `add_structure` pins the result to `Type 0` (context.rs:300) — so the synthesised `Prod` is only the `Type 0` instance. Every use at a higher level is outside the fragment (T01-007) and must be rejected, not silently reused.

PROOF_IRRELEVANT_FIELD. `Subtype`'s second field is a PROOF. `add_structure` builds the inductive at `Type 0`, so `{n : Nat // n > 0}` becomes a `Type 0` record with a `Prop`-typed field — legal, but its `Subtype_property` projection is a large elimination out of a `Prop`-sorted field, and the derived `Match` motive target is pinned to `Type 0` by recursor.rs:64-71. Subtype equality by proof irrelevance (`Subtype.ext`) has no counterpart and must be re-derived.

cases.title: Deep normalisation — `normalize`'s 10000-step fuel expires SILENTLY
cases.lean: definitional equality by `rfl` requiring many reduction steps, Nat GMP acceleration
cases.target: The term translates structurally (there is nothing special about its shape); the degradation is in the CHECKING BUDGET. The translator must emit a loss record naming NORMALIZATION_FUEL for every declaration whose Lean-side conversion check is known or estimated to exceed LOGOS's step budget.
evidence: kernel/src/reduction.rs:40-41 and :52-69 (`normalize` runs `reduce_step` under a hard `let mut fuel = 10000;` and, on exhaustion, `return current` — the PARTIALLY reduced term, with no error, no flag and no diagnostic); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1366-1375 (`def_eq` normalizes BOTH sides and then compares — two independently truncated normal forms); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1309-1323 (`is_subtype` does the same, after a `types_equal` fast path); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1480-1493 (the Peano bridge peels ONE `Succ` per recursive call, so a `Nat` literal of size `n` costs `n` steps to compare against a Peano term); kernel/src/reduction.rs:330-345 (`extract_constructor`'s literal→`Succ` bridge, the other half of the same cost)
guards: Catches treating a conversion FAILURE as evidence that the translation is wrong. When fuel runs out, `def_eq` returns `false` — indistinguishable from a genuine type mismatch. A translator that reacts by "fixing" the term (inserting a coercion, weakening a type, or falling back to `add_declaration` to axiomatise the equation) converts a budget problem into a soundness problem. `add_declaration` (context.rs:434) will accept `theorem big_arith : … = …` as an AXIOM without a murmur, and the resulting library is then unsound with respect to nothing — it is simply no longer a translation of the Lean source.

Catches the far more dangerous converse: fuel exhaustion making a check SUCCEED. `is_subtype` (type_checker.rs:1309-1316) tries `types_equal` FIRST, and `types_equal` treats `Term::Hole` as matching anything (type_checker.rs:1594-1597). If a truncated normal form still contains a `Hole` the translator left behind (T00-016), the truncation is what stops the `Hole` from ever being reached and reported — so adding fuel would have caught the bug and the default budget hides it.

Catches NON-DETERMINISM. Fuel is counted per `normalize` CALL, not per declaration. The same subterm can be compared once inside a small type (succeeds) and once inside a large one (truncates), so the same equation is accepted in one declaration and rejected in the next. A translator that caches "this equation is definitional" from a successful check will emit terms that do not re-check.

Catches assuming Lean's `Nat` acceleration carries over. Lean's kernel special-cases `Nat` literals with GMP; LOGOS accelerates only *equality* of two `Literal::Nat`s (type_checker.rs:1485) and otherwise falls back to unary peeling. `2 ^ 20 = 1048576` is one Lean kernel step and roughly a million LOGOS steps.
oracle: For each declaration the harness records LOGOS's `reduce_step` count during checking; any declaration whose count reaches 10000 must have a matching NORMALIZATION_FUEL loss record. Re-running with an unbounded fuel must not change any accept/reject verdict — a verdict that flips is a fuel-hidden bug.
loss: NORMALIZATION_FUEL. A Lean `rfl` whose kernel conversion check Lean discharges with GMP-accelerated `Nat` arithmetic in O(1) becomes, in LOGOS, a unary Peano computation costing O(n) reduction steps. Above 10000 steps the check does not fail loudly — it silently compares two half-reduced terms. The loss is that a definitional equality true in Lean is NOT decidable in LOGOS at the declared budget, so the proof must be restated propositionally (via the `Int` ring axioms at prelude.rs:92-191, or via `reduceBool`/`ofReduceBool` at prelude.rs:1195-1219) rather than left to conversion.

cases.title: `@[reducible]` / `@[irreducible]` — LOGOS has no transparency control
cases.lean: @[reducible], @[irreducible], abbrev, TransparencyMode, `with_unfolding_all`
cases.target: Every Lean definition, whatever its reducibility, becomes `Context::add_definition(name, ty, body)` — which is unconditionally delta-TRANSPARENT. An `@[irreducible]` definition has only one faithful alternative, `Context::add_declaration(name, ty)` (an opaque axiom), which loses the body entirely. The translator must pick `add_definition` and record the loss.
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:442 (`add_definition(name, ty, body)` — the ONLY definition form; it takes no reducibility argument and there is no later API to set one); kernel/src/context.rs:434 (`add_declaration(name, ty)` — type only, no body, the only way to make something opaque, and it makes it opaque FOREVER); kernel/src/reduction.rs:36-91 (`reduce_step` unfolds a global whenever `ctx.get_global`/`get_universe_poly` yields a body — there is no transparency gate, no `TransparencyMode`, and no per-call setting); kernel/src/context.rs (the `Context` maps carry name → type/body only: no attribute map, no reducibility hint map — LOGOS_FACTS: "no visibility, no attributes, no reducibility hints")
guards: Catches translating `@[irreducible]` as `add_declaration` (an axiom). It preserves opacity, which looks faithful, and it is a catastrophe: the body is gone, so every equation the definition was supposed to satisfy becomes unprovable, and — worse — an `add_declaration` with a `Prop` type is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a genuine axiom in the emitted context. A proof library that acquires axioms this way has no way to report its own trusted base. This is the same failure mode as T11-014 (`sorry` smuggled in as an axiom), reached by a different route.

Catches translating `abbrev` (which is `@[reducible] def`) as anything other than a definition — in particular as a notation to be inlined at every use site, which changes term size and blocks the syntactic matches `try_structure_eta` (type_checker.rs:1391-1417) and the termination guard (termination.rs) perform.

Catches silently accepting the over-permissive direction. A translator that verifies its output by "does LOGOS accept it" will see the `@[irreducible]` case pass and conclude the translation is faithful. It is not: LOGOS accepted MORE than Lean would. The verification obligation runs the other way — every `rfl` the LOGOS side discharges must correspond to a `rfl` Lean's elaborator discharges at DEFAULT transparency, and that is exactly the fact this attribute destroys.

Catches dropping `@[reducible]` on a TYPE synonym used as a class instance head. In Lean, instance search unfolds reducible definitions only; in LOGOS, `add_instance` (context.rs:184) is a flat `Vec<(Term, Term)>` matched first-wins, with no unfolding policy at all — so which instance is found can differ. That divergence is T07-008's subject; here the guard is simply that the reducibility that DROVE Lean's choice is gone by the time LOGOS resolves.
oracle: Every Lean definition, regardless of attribute, appears in the emitted context via `add_definition` with its body intact; no `add_declaration` is emitted for anything that had a body in Lean; and a loss record with category TRANSPARENCY_HINT lists each declaration whose Lean reducibility was not `default`.
loss: TRANSPARENCY_HINT. Lean's four transparency levels (`reducible`, `instances`, `default`, `all`) collapse to one. Two consequences, in opposite directions: (a) `@[irreducible]` becomes transparent, so LOGOS proves by `refl` statements that Lean's default elaboration refuses — the OVER-PERMISSIVE direction; (b) `@[reducible]` becomes merely transparent rather than preferentially unfolded, so LOGOS's `normalize` unfolds it at the same priority as everything else and spends fuel it did not need to (reduction.rs:52-69, T00-012). Acceptable only because Lean's reducibility is an ELABORATION hint with no effect on the Lean kernel: the kernel unfolds everything. So the translated term is still a faithful translation of the Lean *kernel* term — what is lost is the ability to reproduce Lean's elaboration behaviour, i.e. whether a given `rfl` would have been accepted at the source level.

cases.title: Function eta — present in LOGOS, but ONLY inside `def_eq`, never in `normalize`
cases.lean: definitional eta for functions, `(fun x => f x) = f` by `rfl`
cases.target: No special term is emitted: eta is a property of the CONVERSION relation, not of the syntax. The obligation is on the translator's own equality oracle — it must decide LOGOS definitional equality with `type_checker::def_eq`, never with `normalize` + structural comparison.
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1451-1466 (η-conversion in `def_eq_normalized`: when exactly ONE side is a `Lambda`, the binder is pushed into the context and the other side is APPLIED to `Var(param)` and normalized, then compared under the binder); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1366-1375 (`def_eq` normalizes both sides first, then calls `def_eq_normalized` — so eta fires only after normalisation, on the normal forms); kernel/src/reduction.rs:36-120 (`reduce_step` has beta, delta, zeta, iota, quotient, primitive and `reduceBool` arms — there is NO eta-expansion arm, so `normalize` never eta-expands and two eta-equal terms have DIFFERENT normal forms); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1594-1597 (`types_equal`, the alpha-equivalence fast path, has no eta arm either — it is called FIRST from both `def_eq` at :1367 and `is_subtype` at :1314)
guards: Catches the translator using `normalize(a) == normalize(b)` as its definitional- equality oracle. This is the obvious, cheap implementation and it is WRONG for exactly this case: `normalize` (reduction.rs) has no eta rule, so `λx. f x` and `f` normalize to distinct terms and the oracle reports them unequal — while the LOGOS KERNEL, via `def_eq_normalized` at type_checker.rs:1451-1466, reports them equal. The translator then "repairs" a term that needed no repair: it eta-expands or eta-contracts to force syntactic agreement, changing the emitted term, or it decides the Lean `rfl` does not translate and emits a propositional proof obligation that has no proof.

Catches the one-sided shape of the rule. `def_eq_normalized`'s eta arms fire only when EXACTLY one side is a `Lambda` (`if !matches!(b, Term::Lambda { .. })`, type_checker.rs:1453). When both sides are lambdas the congruence arm at :1507-1515 handles them, and when NEITHER is (both are stuck applications), eta is never attempted. So `f` versus `g` where both are eta-expandable but neither is syntactically a lambda is NOT decided by eta — a translator that assumes "LOGOS has eta, so any two extensionally equal functions are convertible" is assuming extensionality. It does not have it: `funext` is ABSENT from the LOGOS trusted base (prelude.rs; LOGOS_FACTS: "There is no `Classical.choice`, no `propext`, no `funext`"). See T06-011.

Catches eta interacting with the fuel budget. The eta arm calls `normalize(ctx, App(b, Var(param)))` (type_checker.rs:1456) — a FRESH `normalize` with a fresh 10000-step budget (reduction.rs:40), inside a comparison that has already normalized both sides once. A translator that eta-expands large functions to "help" multiplies the normalisation work and can push an equation that was decidable past the budget (T00-012).

Catches assuming eta holds for the DEPENDENT case for free. The eta arm extends the context with `param : param_type` taken from the LAMBDA side only (type_checker.rs:1454) and never checks that the non-lambda side's type is a `Pi` with that domain. If the two domains differ (which cumulativity permits — `Type 0 ≤ Type 1` at type_checker.rs:1333), `App(b, Var(param))` is still formed and normalized, and comparison proceeds under a binder typed by the wrong side.
oracle: For each pair below, LOGOS `def_eq` returns true; and the harness additionally asserts that `normalize(lhs) != normalize(rhs)` structurally for at least the first pair — the test that a `normalize`-based oracle would have failed. No emitted term is eta-modified relative to the Lean `Expr`.

cases.title: Deep binder shadowing — alpha-equivalence when binders are NAMES, not indices
cases.lean: nested binders reusing one name, alpha-equivalent `Expr`s, hygienic shadowing
cases.target: Nested `Term::Pi` / `Term::Lambda` / `Term::Fix` / `Term::Let` whose `param` / `name` fields are GLOBALLY FRESH within the emitted declaration — one freshening pass over the whole term, not a per-binder decision.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:463-476 (`Pi.param`, `Lambda.param`, `Fix.name`, `Let.name` are all plain `String`s); kernel/src/context.rs:228-241 (`Context::add`/`extend` insert into a `HashMap<String, Arc<Term>>` — a second binder with the same name REPLACES the first, so the outer binding becomes unreachable rather than being shadowed in a stack); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1600-1607 (`types_equal` compares `Var` names LITERALLY: `(Var(n1), Var(n2)) => n1 == n2` — there is no index, so alpha-equivalence is implemented by RENAMING, at :1611-1620 for `Pi` and :1507-1515 for `Lambda`, where the second term's binder is `substitute`d to the first's name); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1088-1110 (`substitute_avoiding` freshens a binder when it would capture a free variable of the REPLACEMENT — so the rename used by the congruence rules is itself capture-safe); kernel/src/term.rs:577-590 (`Display` prints `Π({param}:{ty}). {body}` — two nested binders of the same name print IDENTICALLY, with nothing to distinguish them); kernel/src/recheck.rs (the second kernel converts to de Bruijn deliberately, so a naming error shows up as a DISAGREEMENT between kernels rather than as an error)
guards: Catches reusing Lean's binder names verbatim. It is very nearly safe — the kernel's own congruence and substitution are capture-correct — and that is exactly what makes it dangerous, because the failure is not in the kernel. It is in every OTHER consumer: `Display` (term.rs:577-590) renders `Π(n:Nat). Π(n:Fin n). Nat` with two indistinguishable `n`s, so any round-trip through printed form (a certificate dump, a literate-surface re-parse, a diff between two translator versions) reads back a DIFFERENT term — the inner `n` in `Fin n` now refers to the inner binder. The term that was checked and the term that is stored are then not the same term.

Catches freshening PER BINDER instead of per term. A pass that renames a binder only when it collides with an enclosing binder still produces collisions with names introduced later by the kernel itself: `derive_recursor` (recursor.rs:79-81) generates binders literally named `A0`, `A1`, `Idx0`, `Idx1`, and `add_structure` (context.rs:295-320) generates projection bodies with its own binders. A Lean binder innocently named `A0` collides with a generated one inside a derived term, where the translator's freshening pass never ran.

Catches assuming `Context::extend` behaves like a stack. It does not — it is a map insert (context.rs:228-241). So after `ctx.extend("n", Nat).extend("n", Fin n)` the OUTER `n` is gone from the context entirely. Any code the translator writes that looks up a binder by name after extending (for instance, to compute a motive) reads the wrong type, and the resulting `Match` motive is well-typed against the wrong discriminant type.

Catches asymmetric freshening between a TERM and its TYPE. A declaration is emitted as a (type, body) pair (context.rs:442). If the freshening pass runs independently on each, the same Lean binder gets two different fresh names, and the body no longer matches the type's telescope. `check_type`'s `Lambda`-against-`Pi` rule (type_checker.rs:474-500) prefers the Pi's parameter type and will happily accept the mismatch, binding the body's variable to the wrong name and leaving the other dangling.
oracle: Walking the emitted term, no binder name is ever introduced while a binder of the same name is already in scope; `infer_type` succeeds; the de Bruijn re-checker in `recheck.rs` agrees with `type_checker.rs` on the inferred type; and `parse(Display(term))` — where a surface parser exists — yields a term `def_eq` to the original.

cases.title: `Term::Hole` surviving into emitted output — `types_equal` matches it against ANYTHING
cases.lean: implicit arguments the translator cannot reconstruct, `_` in types, match motives, erased instance arguments
cases.target: (none — a `Term::Hole` must never appear in translator output, in ANY position)
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1594-1597 (`types_equal`: `if matches!(a, Term::Hole) || matches!(b, Term::Hole) { return true; }` — a `Hole` is equal to EVERY term); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1309-1316 (`is_subtype` calls `types_equal` as its FAST PATH before normalising, so the leniency is reached on the cheapest, most-travelled route) and kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1366-1368 (`def_eq` does the same); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:455-471 (`check_type` accepts a `Hole` TERM against any `Sort`, and accepts ANY well-typed term against a `Hole` EXPECTED type); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:313 (`infer_type(Hole)` is `CannotInferHole` — the ONLY place a `Hole` is refused, and it is reached only when the `Hole` is in a position that is inferred rather than merely compared); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1104 (`substitute_avoiding` propagates a `Hole` unchanged, so it survives every reduction and every instantiation); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:142-150 (`instantiate` likewise leaves `Hole` alone — the elaborator's metavariable machinery does not solve it)
guards: This is the corpus's canonical "it typechecked, therefore it is fine" refutation. A single `Hole` in a TYPE makes every comparison against that type succeed. If the translator emits `theorem thm : <statement with a Hole> := <proof>`, then `check_type(proof, statement)` short-circuits through `types_equal` (type_checker.rs:1596) and returns `Ok(())` for a proof of something else entirely. The theorem is recorded, `verified == true` is reported (verify.rs:31-43), and the library now contains a certified statement that nothing proves. Nothing anywhere emits a warning.

Catches the belief that `CannotInferHole` (type_checker.rs:313) is a backstop. It fires only for a `Hole` that `infer_type` visits. `infer_type` visits a `Pi`'s `param_type` (via `infer_sort` at :96) but NOT the argument position of an application whose function type is already a `Pi` — there the argument is only `check_type`d (:171), and `check_type` against a non-`Hole` expected type calls `types_equal` first. So a `Hole` as a *type argument* of a polymorphic function (`@Eq _ a b`, `@List.cons _ x xs`) is never inferred and never reported.

Catches using `Hole` as a placeholder "to be filled in later" in a multi-pass translator. There is no later: `substitute_avoiding` (type_checker.rs:1104) and `instantiate` (elaborate.rs:142-150) both preserve `Hole` verbatim, so a `Hole` written in pass 1 is still there in the certificate. If a pass-structured translator needs a placeholder it must use its own sentinel OUTSIDE the `Term` type and assert the sentinel is gone before handing anything to the kernel.

Catches emitting `Hole` for an ERASED instance argument. Instance arguments are reconstructible — `Context::add_instance` (context.rs:184) holds a flat `Vec<(Term, Term)>` matched first-wins — so the translator must resolve them, accept that the resolution may differ from Lean's (T07-008), and RECORD that divergence. Substituting a `Hole` converts a recorded divergence into an unrecorded unsoundness.

Catches emitting `Hole` for a `Match` motive. `infer_match` computes the result type as `beta_reduce(App(motive, discriminant))` (type_checker.rs:271); with a `Hole` motive that is `App(Hole, disc)`, which is not a `Sort`, so the large-elimination gate at :277-288 — `matches!(normalize(infer_type(return_type)), Sort(Prop))` — takes the wrong branch and the `Prop`-elimination restriction is silently skipped.
oracle: A structural walk of every emitted `Term` (declaration types, bodies, structure field types, constructor types, recursor types) finds zero `Term::Hole` nodes. This check must be run on the output, NOT inferred from the kernel accepting the output — the kernel accepting it is precisely the symptom.
diag: E_HOLE_IN_OUTPUT — must name the declaration, the path to the `Hole` inside the term, and the Lean subterm that could not be reconstructed. The translator must write NO declaration for that Lean declaration.

cases.title: `let` whose BODY'S TYPE depends on the bound value — zeta in the type, not just the term
cases.lean: Expr.letE with a dependent body, `let n := 3; (v : Fin n)`
cases.target: Term::Let { name, ty, value, body } — kernel/src/term.rs:475. The dependency is carried by LOGOS's `Let` typing rule, which zeta-substitutes BEFORE inferring the body's type; no extra machinery is needed and none may be substituted for it.
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:133-142 — the whole rule: `let _ = infer_sort(ctx, ty)?;  check_type(ctx, value, ty)?; let unfolded = substitute(body, name, value);  infer_type(ctx, &unfolded)`. The body is never typed with `name` in the context at all; it is typed AFTER the value has been substituted in, so the inferred type mentions the VALUE. Contrast kernel/src/type_checker.rs:144-177 (`App`): the function's body type is computed with the parameter OPAQUE (`ctx.extend(param, param_type)` at :121 for the `Lambda` that produced it) and the argument is substituted into the RESULT type only, at :176 — which is strictly weaker. kernel/src/reduction.rs:298 (`reduce_step` on `Let` performs the same zeta step, so the term and its type agree); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1088-1110 (`substitute_avoiding` — capture-avoiding, and O(size) per crossed binder, which is what makes this rule expensive)
guards: Catches the "a `let` is just a beta-redex" lowering, `App(Lambda { param, param_type: A, body }, v)`. For a NON-dependent body the two are interchangeable, so a test suite of ordinary `let`s will not distinguish them. For a dependent body the redex fails: the `Lambda` rule (type_checker.rs:112-131) types `body` with `param : A` opaque, so `Fin n` cannot reduce to `Fin 3`, the `Fin` literal does not check, and the declaration is rejected. A translator that hits this and "fixes" it by weakening the body's type, inserting a cast, or axiomatising the index bound has converted a lowering bug into a permanent loss.

Catches the SILENT half of the same bug. When the body's type mentions `n` but the declaration's DECLARED type also mentions `n`-free spellings only (because Lean already zeta-reduced it away in the stated type), the beta-redex encoding produces a term whose inferred type is `Π(n : Nat). …` applied — which normalizes to the same thing, so it passes. It fails only where the value's identity is needed inside the body's own elaboration, which is a strictly smaller set of positions than a test suite covers. Both encodings must therefore be compared on the DEPENDENT instances below, not on the easy ones.

Catches zeta-substituting in the term but not in the declared TYPE. A declaration is `add_definition(name, ty, body)` (context.rs:442) and the kernel checks `body` against `ty`. If the translator pre-zeta-reduces the body (turning `let n := 3; Fin n` into `Fin 3`) but copies Lean's stated type verbatim (`let n := 3; Fin n`), the two are still `def_eq` — but the emitted type now contains a `Let` that the certificate records and that every downstream consumer must re-zeta. Pick one and be consistent.

Catches the COST. `type_checker.rs:141` substitutes the value at every occurrence, and `substitute_avoiding` walks the body computing `all_var_names` at each binder it might capture (type_checker.rs:1060-1071). Nested dependent lets — each of whose values mentions the previous — expand multiplicatively, and `normalize`'s 10000-step fuel (reduction.rs:40) is shared across the whole check. A translator that introduces `Let` nodes to make a term *smaller* makes the CHECK bigger. See T00-022.
oracle: The emitted term is a `Term::Let`; `infer_type` succeeds; the inferred type is `def_eq` to the translation of Lean's inferred type; and the harness additionally checks that replacing the `Let` with `App(Lambda …)` makes `infer_type` FAIL — the test that the dependency is real and that the correct form was chosen for a reason.

cases.title: `fun | pat => ..` — pattern lambdas must be re-expressed as a POSITIONAL `Match`
cases.lean: fun | pat => .., match-expressions, the equation compiler, auxiliary `match_1` defs
cases.target: Term::Match { discriminant, motive, cases } — kernel/src/term.rs:469. `cases` is a `Vec<Term>` with EXACTLY one entry per constructor, in the inductive's REGISTRATION order, each entry a `Term::Lambda` telescope over that constructor's non-parameter arguments.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:469 (`Match { discriminant, motive, cases: Vec<Term> }` — there is no pattern field, no wildcard, no guard, no fall-through); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:254-260 (`cases.len()` must equal the constructor count; a mismatch is an error, and the association of case to constructor is by POSITION only — there is no tag on a case); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:733-760 and :827-844 (each case's expected type is the constructor's argument telescope, beta-reduced against the motive — so a case must be a `Lambda` chain over exactly those arguments); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:271 (the match's result type is `beta_reduce(App(motive, discriminant))`); LOGOS_FACTS: "`Match` is the PRIMITIVE; recursors are derived terms. This is the inverse of Lean 4. There are no patterns, no wildcards, no nested patterns, no `casesOn`/`brecOn`/`noConfusion`/`injection`."
guards: Catches preserving SOURCE ORDER of the alternatives. `cases` is positional (type_checker.rs:254-260): case `i` is the case for constructor `i` as registered by `add_constructor` (context.rs:419). Lean lets the author write the alternatives in any order, and `Col.blue` first is perfectly idiomatic. Emitting the source order produces a `Match` with the right ARITY and the wrong SEMANTICS — every branch runs for the wrong constructor. When the branches have the same type (all `Nat` below) nothing type-checks differently; the function simply computes something else. This is the highest-frequency silent mistranslation in the whole `Match` area.

Catches translating the AUXILIARY definition instead of the match. Lean's equation compiler emits `T00_018.pc.match_1` (and `brecOn`/`below` for recursive functions) and the function body is an APPLICATION of that auxiliary. A translator working on the final `Expr` sees `Expr.const ``pc.match_1` and, finding no LOGOS counterpart, is tempted to emit it via `add_declaration` — an AXIOM with the matcher's type, which is inhabited and therefore consistent, and which makes every equation of the function unprovable. The matcher must be UNFOLDED (`Meta.withTransparency .all` / `Split.simpMatch` / `matchMatcherApp?`) back to `casesOn`, and the `casesOn` mapped to a `Term::Match`.

Catches emitting a case as a BARE BODY rather than a `Lambda` telescope. For a nullary constructor the two coincide, so an enum-only test suite passes. For `Nat.succ k` the case must be `λ(k:Nat). …`; a bare body leaves `k` free and `infer_type` reports `UnboundVariable` — or, if a same-named binder happens to be in scope, resolves it to the WRONG variable (T00-001).

Catches including PARAMETERS in the case telescope. `type_checker.rs:756` and :832-844 bind only the constructor arguments beyond the inductive's parameters; a translator that lowers Lean's `casesOn` minor premise verbatim includes the parameters and the arity check fails — or worse, for a parameterless inductive it silently does not.

Catches `n + 1` as a pattern. Lean's `n+1` is sugar for `Nat.succ n` via `OfNat` and the equation compiler; it is NOT a numeric guard. A translator that reads the surface pattern rather than the elaborated matcher will try to emit an arithmetic test, for which LOGOS has no form at all.
oracle: For each `Match` emitted, `cases.len()` equals `ctx.get_constructors(ind).len()`, and case `i` is `def_eq` to the Lean alternative for constructor `i` *as registered*, not as written; `infer_type` succeeds; and for each constructor `C` the harness checks `def_eq(f (C args…), <the Lean alternative for C> args…)` — the test that catches a permuted `cases` vector, which no type check will.

cases.title: `have` in term mode (`letFun`) — Lean's opaque binding versus LOGOS's transparent `Let`
cases.lean: `have h : T := v; b` in term mode, Lean.Expr `letFun` annotation, mdata key `letFun`
cases.target: Term::Let { name, ty, value, body } — kernel/src/term.rs:475 — together with a loss record naming OPACITY. There is no opaque local binding in LOGOS: `Term::Let` is zeta-transparent by construction, and the only other candidates are `App(Lambda …)` (which is opaque but breaks dependent bodies, T00-017) and a top-level `add_declaration` (which is a global axiom, not a local binding).
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (the `Term` enum has exactly one local-binding form with a value, `Let`; there is no opaque variant); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:133-142 (`Let` inference zeta-substitutes the value into the body BEFORE inferring — `substitute(body, name, value)` — so the body always sees `name ≡ value`); kernel/src/reduction.rs:298 (`reduce_step` on `Let` performs the same zeta step, so the transparency is not merely a checking artefact: it is in the reduction relation); kernel/src/context.rs:434 vs :442 (`add_declaration` = opaque, `add_definition` = transparent — both GLOBAL, neither local); Lean side: `have` elaborates to `letFun v (fun h => b)` under an mdata annotation, so the translator's `Expr.mdata` arm (T00-009) is where the two are distinguished
guards: Catches the blanket mdata strip. `have` and `let` differ in the elaborated `Expr` ONLY by the `letFun` marker and the `letFun` constant; a translator whose `Expr.mdata` arm is `| .mdata _ e => translate e` (T00-009's correct default for pretty-printer keys) erases exactly the information that distinguishes them. The mdata arm must INSPECT the key.

Catches translating `have` as `App(Lambda …)` "because it is opaque". That preserves opacity faithfully and breaks every `have` whose body's TYPE mentions the bound name — and `have` is routinely used that way in dependent code. Worse, the two encodings are not interchangeable per-declaration: a translator that picks between them by trying one and falling back silently produces a development where some `have`s are transparent and some are not, with no record of which.

Catches the over-permissive direction being mistaken for success. LOGOS accepting a `have`-derived term is NOT evidence of faithfulness — it accepts strictly more here by construction. The conformance obligation is the reverse inclusion: anything the translated development proves must be provable in Lean from the same source. A harness that only checks "LOGOS accepted it" cannot see this class of error at all.

Catches treating `letFun` as an ordinary constant to be looked up. `letFun` is not in the LOGOS prelude; emitting `Global("letFun")` fails `get_global` (context.rs:449), and defining one via `add_definition` produces an extra delta-redex at every `have`, inflating every proof term and blocking the syntactic shape tests in `try_structure_eta` (type_checker.rs:1391-1417) and `termination.rs`.
oracle: Every Lean `have` in term mode emits a `Term::Let` and a loss record with category OPACITY; `infer_type` succeeds. Additionally, for each such declaration the harness re-elaborates the Lean source with `have` replaced by `let` and asserts the Lean side still compiles — a `have` that would NOT survive that replacement is a case where the opacity was load-bearing and the degradation must be escalated.
loss: OPACITY. Lean's `have` deliberately hides the value from the goal: during elaboration the hypothesis `h : T` is available but `h`'s DEFINITION is not, so a proof that needs `h ≡ v` fails at the source level. Translating to `Term::Let` makes that definition visible, so LOGOS proves strictly MORE than Lean did. Acceptable only in the narrow sense that the resulting term is still a well-typed inhabitant of the translated type — the Lean proof, re-elaborated, is still a proof. It is not acceptable to SUPPRESS the record, because the translated development is no longer a conservative image of the Lean one: a later Lean-side change that breaks the source still typechecks in LOGOS.

PROOF_TERM_SIZE. `have` exists largely to SHARE a proof: `have big : P := <large>; <uses big five times>` is one copy in Lean. `Term::Let`'s zeta rule (type_checker.rs:141) substitutes the value at every occurrence before checking, so the checked term is five copies. Nested `have`s multiply. This interacts directly with `normalize`'s 10000-step fuel (reduction.rs:40) — see T00-012 and T00-022.

cases.title: `show T from e` and `(e : T)` — ascription is erased by Lean before translation
cases.lean: (e : T), show T from e, show T by tac, Lean.Meta.mkExpectedTypeHint
cases.target: The ascription leaves NO trace: `(e : T)` ⟼ `translate e`. No wrapper, no coercion function, no `Term::Let` with `ty := T`.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (there is no ascription, cast, or type-annotation variant in `Term`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:50-52 (`infer_type` is purely synthesising — there is no bidirectional entry point a translator could hand an expected type to except `check_type`, which returns `()` and produces no term); kernel/src/prelude.rs (the registered globals are enumerated in LOGOS_FACTS and there is NO `id` — so there is no identity function to wrap with, either); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:452-471 and :1309-1323 (`check_type` uses `is_subtype`, i.e. CUMULATIVE subsumption — a strictly more permissive test than Lean's definitional equality, which is why the ascription cannot be re-derived downstream)
guards: Catches emitting an ascription as an application of an identity function. `Global("id")` does not resolve (context.rs:449) and a locally defined `id` adds a delta-redex at every ascription: term size grows, `normalize`'s 10000-step fuel (reduction.rs:40) is consumed, and the syntactic head tests in `try_structure_eta` (type_checker.rs:1391-1417), the termination guard (termination.rs:378-400) and `elaborate::spine` (elaborate.rs:1276) all see `id` where they expected a constructor or a recursive call.

Catches emitting the ascription as `Term::Let { name: "_", ty: T, value: e, body: Var("_") }` in order to "keep" the type. It typechecks — `Let` checks `value` against `ty` (type_checker.rs:140) — and it introduces a binder literally named `_`, which `Display` renders indistinguishably from a non-dependent `Pi`'s binder (term.rs:583-588) and which collides with every other `_` binder the translator emits (T00-004, T00-015).

Catches the reverse error: erasing the ascription at the SYNTAX level. `(3 : Int)` and `(3 : Nat)` are the same surface tokens and different `Expr`s — the ascription is what selected the `OfNat` instance, and `Literal::Nat` versus `Literal::Int` are different LOGOS worlds with different types (`Global("Nat")` vs `Global("Int")`, type_checker.rs:294-302) and completely different theories (`Nat` inductive with `Zero`/`Succ`; `Int` opaque with axiomatised ring laws at prelude.rs:92-191). The erasure is sound ONLY post-elaboration. A `Syntax`-level translator must not do it.

Catches treating the erased ascription as still ENFORCED. In Lean, `(e : T)` requires `typeof(e)` and `T` to be definitionally equal. Once erased, the only remaining check is whatever the enclosing position performs — and enclosing positions in LOGOS use `check_type`/`is_subtype`, which admits `Prop ≤ Type 0 ≤ Type 1` and `Pi` variance (type_checker.rs:1330-1360). So a translator that relies on "the ascription will be re-checked anyway" is relying on a WEAKER check than the one it deleted. If the ascription was the only thing pinning a universe level, the level is now free to float up. See T01-009.

Catches `show T by tac`, where the ascription is attached to a TACTIC block. The tactic ran in Lean and produced a term; the ascription is erased along with the tactic, and what must be translated is the resulting `Expr`. A translator that tries to map the tactic to a LOGOS script surface (Tier 8/12) instead of translating the produced term has changed the trust story entirely — see T12-013.
oracle: The emitted term for `(e : T)` is structurally identical to the emitted term for `e` written without the ascription; no `id`-like wrapper and no zero-use `Let` appears; and for each ascribed/unascribed pair below the two emitted terms are literally equal, not merely `def_eq`.

cases.title: Very deep application spines and telescopes — named substitution is QUADRATIC
cases.lean: long application spines, long binder telescopes, terms whose normal form is deep
cases.target: The structural translation is unremarkable — a left-nested `Term::App` chain (term.rs:470) and a nested `Term::Pi`/`Term::Lambda` telescope. The degradation is in the CHECKING COST, and the translator must emit a loss record naming SUBSTITUTION_COMPLEXITY for any declaration whose spine or telescope depth exceeds the threshold it can check inside LOGOS's fixed budgets.
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1060-1071 (`freshen` calls `all_var_names(body, &mut avoid)` — a FULL WALK of the body — for every binder that might capture a free variable of the replacement); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1082-1110 (`substitute_avoiding` recurses through every binder, invoking `freshen` where needed; LOGOS_FACTS records this as "O(size) per binder comparison — quadratic on deep telescopes"); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:176 (every single `App` step in `infer_type` performs one `substitute(body_type, param, arg)` — so an n-argument spine performs n substitutions, each over a body that is itself O(n)); kernel/src/reduction.rs:40 and :52-69 (`normalize`'s 10000-step fuel is counted in `reduce_step` calls and, on exhaustion, silently returns the partially reduced term); kernel/src/term.rs:470 (`App` is BINARY, so an n-argument spine is n heap-allocated `Box` layers — depth, not width)
guards: Catches sizing the translation by Lean's `Expr` node count. Lean's `Expr` is hash-consed, so a spine that shares its head and its arguments counts once; the translated `Term` is a tree (T00-022) and counts every occurrence. A translator that budgets from the Lean side under-reports, sometimes exponentially, and then hits the fuel limit on a declaration it had classified as small.

Catches "introduce `Term::Let` to share the repeated subterm and shrink the spine". `Let`'s typing rule zeta-substitutes the value into the body BEFORE inferring (type_checker.rs:141), so the checked term is exactly the expanded one — the `Let` reduces source size and does nothing at all for checking cost. It makes matters worse when the value is large and used many times.

Catches treating a fuel-exhausted comparison as a translation error. On exhaustion `normalize` returns `current` (reduction.rs:56) with no signal; `def_eq` then compares two truncated terms and answers `false`. The translator must not respond by weakening the emitted type, inserting a cast, or falling back to `add_declaration` (context.rs:434) — the last of which converts a performance limit into a silent new axiom.

Catches assuming the cost is in the SOURCE. The declarations below are all short. The expensive ones are short *because* their cost is in the normal form: `tower`'s spine and `wide`'s telescope are both generated by reduction, not written.
oracle: The harness records LOGOS's `reduce_step` count and peak `Term` depth per declaration; any declaration whose count reaches 10000 or whose depth exceeds the re-checker's recursion limit carries a SUBSTITUTION_COMPLEXITY loss record. Re-running with unbounded fuel must not change any accept/reject verdict.
loss: SUBSTITUTION_COMPLEXITY. A Lean `Expr` application spine is flat (`getAppArgs` is O(n)) and Lean's kernel instantiates a telescope with a single de Bruijn `instantiateRev` pass. LOGOS's named representation pays O(n) per argument in `substitute_avoiding` and O(n) again in `freshen`'s `all_var_names` walk, for O(n²) total on the spine and O(n²) on the binder telescope. Acceptable in the sense that the RESULT is identical; not acceptable to leave unrecorded, because at scale the cost turns into a `normalize` fuel exhaustion (reduction.rs:52-69) that is SILENT and therefore indistinguishable from a genuine conversion failure. See T00-012.

SPINE_DEPTH. The binary `App` makes the emitted term a deep left spine. Every consumer that recurses structurally — `substitute_avoiding` (type_checker.rs:1082), `types_equal` (:1595), `normalize` (reduction.rs:36), the de Bruijn re-checker (recheck.rs), `Display` (term.rs:596) — recurses to that depth. The depth is a function of the NORMAL FORM, not of the source: `tower 5000` below is a nine-token Lean term whose normal form is a 5000-deep spine.

cases.title: `Expr` is a hash-consed DAG; LOGOS `Term` is a TREE — sharing cannot be restored
cases.lean: Expr pointer sharing, maxSharing, whnf caching, repeated subterms after beta/delta
cases.target: A plain structural translation to `Term` (term.rs:443-545), which is a `Box`-recursive tree with no interning and no back-references, PLUS a loss record naming TERM_SHARING that reports the expansion factor (translated node count divided by Lean `Expr` node count under `maxSharing`).
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term` is an owned `Box`-recursive enum — there is no `Rc`/`Arc` inside a `Term`, no hash-consing table, no node identity, and therefore no way to express "this subterm is that subterm"; `Arc` appears only in `Context`'s top-level maps, kernel/src/context.rs:228-241, i.e. between DECLARATIONS, never within a term); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:133-142 (`Let` — the one construct that LOOKS like it restores sharing — is zeta-substituted into the body before the body is inferred, so the checked term is the fully expanded one); kernel/src/reduction.rs:298 (`reduce_step` on `Let` does the same, so the expansion is in the reduction relation too, not just in checking); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1082-1110 (`substitute_avoiding` COPIES the replacement at every occurrence — beta reduction therefore duplicates rather than shares); kernel/src/reduction.rs:40 and :52-69 (`normalize`'s fixed 10000-step fuel, silently exhausted); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1060-1071 (`freshen`'s full-body `all_var_names` walk, the other half of the quadratic cost — see T00-021)
guards: Catches "reintroduce sharing with `Term::Let`". This is the single most natural repair and it does nothing. `type_checker.rs:141` zeta-substitutes the let's value into the body BEFORE inferring the body's type, so a `let` binding a large value used n times is checked as n copies — the same n copies the translator was trying to avoid, plus a `Let` node. There is NO construct in LOGOS that makes the kernel see a subterm once. The only real sharing boundary is a top-level `add_definition` (context.rs:442), because a `Global` reference is not unfolded until `reduce_step` chooses to (reduction.rs:36-91) — so the genuine mitigation is to LIFT the shared subterm to a named global, which changes the declaration structure and must itself be recorded.

Catches budgeting from the Lean side. A translator that measures a declaration by `Expr` node count under `maxSharing` and concludes "small, will check fine" is measuring the DAG. The doubling chain below is a dozen `Expr` nodes and a thousand-node `Term`. The prediction must be made on the translated tree.

Catches assuming beta reduction preserves size. `substitute_avoiding` (type_checker.rs:1082-1110) copies the argument into every occurrence of the parameter, so one beta step on `(fun x => f x x) big` doubles `big`. Lean's kernel does the same in principle but its result is hash-consed back down; LOGOS's is not. A chain of k such steps is 2^k.
