Catches concluding that the loss is nil because the two terms are `def_eq`. They are — that is exactly why this is `degrade` and not `reject`. The loss is in COST and in the translator's ability to predict cost, and the failure mode it produces is a SILENT fuel exhaustion (reduction.rs:56) reported as a conversion failure. A harness that only checks final acceptance will see this case as clean until the day a declaration crosses the threshold.

Catches trying to recover sharing by pointer-comparing translated subterms. `Term` derives structural `PartialEq` (term.rs:441) and has no node identity; two equal subterms are indistinguishable from one shared subterm, so a post-hoc "re-share" pass cannot tell which occurrences Lean actually shared — and it does not matter, because no `Term` can record the answer.
oracle: A loss record with category TERM_SHARING reports, per declaration, the Lean `Expr` node count under `maxSharing` and the emitted `Term` node count; the emitted term is `def_eq` to the Lean term's translation; and no `Term::Let` is introduced by the translator for the purpose of sharing (lets that were in the Lean source are fine).
loss: TERM_SHARING. Lean's `Expr` is a hash-consed DAG: `f x x` holds ONE `x` node with two references, and `whnf` results are cached so a repeated redex reduces once. The translated `Term` holds two independent copies, and each is reduced independently. For the doubling chains below the factor is 2^k. Acceptable in the sense that the DENOTATION is identical — a tree and its DAG share a unique unfolding — and LOGOS has no representation in which the sharing could be preserved. Not acceptable to leave unrecorded: the expansion factor is precisely what predicts whether a declaration will exhaust `normalize`'s fuel, and a translator that cannot report it cannot predict its own failures.

cases.title: `Prop` ≡ `Sort 0` — a DISTINCT `Universe` constructor, never `Type(0)`
cases.lean: Prop, Sort 0, impredicative ∀ into Prop, proof irrelevance, Prop-valued inductives
cases.target: Term::Sort(Universe::Prop) — kernel/src/term.rs:445 + term.rs:175. NOT `Term::Sort(Universe::Type(0))`, which is a different enum constructor.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:167-191 (`Universe::{SProp, Prop, Type(u32), Var, Succ, Max, IMax}` — `Prop` and `Type(0)` are separate variants); kernel/src/term.rs:222-228 (`imax`: `imax(a, Prop) = Prop` — the IMPREDICATIVITY rule — versus `imax(a, Type n) = max(a, Type n)`, the predicative one); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:104-110 (Pi formation uses `a_sort.imax(&b_sort)`, so the choice of constructor decides whether a `∀` is a proposition); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:277-288 (the large-elimination gate matches `Term::Sort(Universe::Prop)` SYNTACTICALLY, after `normalize`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1547-1567 (`proof_irrelevant` matches `Term::Sort(Universe::Prop) | Term::Sort(Universe::SProp)` — same syntactic test); kernel/src/recursor.rs:64-71 (`derive_recursor` branches on `Term::Sort(Universe::Prop)` to decide the motive target); kernel/src/term.rs:266-276 (`to_lnat`: `Prop ↦ Const(0)`, `Type n ↦ Const(n+1)` — the level-DECISION encoding, where `Prop` really is level 0, which is what makes the confusion plausible)
guards: Catches `Prop ⟼ Universe::Type(0)` on the reasoning that "`Prop` is `Sort 0` and `Sort 0` is level 0". LOGOS's own `to_lnat` (term.rs:268-271) agrees that `Prop` is level 0 — and that is a DECISION-PROCEDURE encoding, not the surface representation. Four things break, none of them loudly: (1) IMPREDICATIVITY. `imax(a, Prop) = Prop` (term.rs:224) versus `imax(a, Type 0) = max(a, Type 0)` (term.rs:227). `∀ (α : Type), α → α` is a `Prop` in Lean and becomes `Type 1` under the mistranslation — a strictly larger sort, which LOGOS's cumulativity (type_checker.rs:1333) then accepts everywhere the smaller one was accepted. (2) PROOF IRRELEVANCE silently switches OFF. `proof_irrelevant` (type_checker.rs:1553-1560) fires only when both sides' types infer to `Sort(Universe::Prop)`. Under the mistranslation every proof becomes a `Type 0` inhabitant, so two proofs of the same statement are no longer definitionally equal, and every `rfl` that relied on irrelevance fails — reported as a conversion failure, never as a universe bug. (3) The LARGE-ELIMINATION GATE silently switches OFF. `type_checker.rs:277-288` guards elimination of a `Prop` inductive into a larger sort. With the discriminant typed `Sort(Type 0)` the guard never runs, so `Or`, `Exists` and any other multi-constructor proposition may be eliminated into `Type` — extracting computational content from a proof. This is an UNSOUNDNESS, not a precision loss. (4) `derive_recursor` (recursor.rs:64-71) picks the wrong motive target, so the generated eliminator has the wrong type.

Catches the converse, `Type 0 ⟼ Universe::Prop`, which is what a translator does if it decides to "normalise" `Sort n` uniformly. The declaration is unusable in a way that only shows up as a conversion failure at the use site, attributed to the use site.

Catches `Sort u` ⟼ `Universe::Type(0)` ("u is unknown, default it"). `Sort u` in Lean RANGES over `Prop` as well, and LOGOS's own decision core encodes that (term.rs:270-272): `Type 0 ≤ u` is FALSE precisely because `u` may be `Prop`. A hand-built `Max(Type(0), Type(0))` therefore reaches the rest of the kernel in a shape nothing else produces. The visible symptom is that a `rfl` which should hold by delta-unfolding does not — attributed to the theorem, not to the reference. A translator that drops a level it believes is "determined by the context" produces exactly this.

That compiles, typechecks, and is wrong the moment the source instantiates the inductive at two different levels — the two instantiations collapse to one LOGOS global, so `List (List α)` and `List α` share a declaration whose recursor can only eliminate into `Type 0`. Every downstream proof is then checked against a type that is not the one the Lean source meant. Because LOGOS is *cumulative* (type_checker.rs:1330-1360) while Lean is not, the resulting terms very often still typecheck — so the kernel will not catch this for you.

Second tempting wrong move: emitting the inductive as a universe-polymorphic *definition* via `add_universe_poly` (context.rs:218) so that `Term::Const` resolves. That makes the type delta-transparent, so it is no longer an inductive: it has no constructors, cannot be matched on, and `add_constructor` will refuse to attach to it.

Third: monomorphising *per instantiation* (`List@0`, `List@1`) is sound-ish for the types but breaks as soon as a universe-polymorphic *proof* quantifies over `u`, because there is no level variable to bind. If the translator does this it must still reject any declaration whose universe parameters are not fully determined at every use site, and must emit a loss record — see T01-008.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NO_UNIVERSE_POLYMORPHIC_INDUCTIVE and writes no declaration into the LOGOS context.
diag: E_NO_UNIVERSE_POLYMORPHIC_INDUCTIVE — must name the inductive, list its universe parameters, and state that LOGOS inductives carry a fixed sort. Must NOT suggest a silent monomorphisation.

cases.title: Per-instantiation monomorphisation — the only partial escape from T01-007, with its own losses
cases.lean: universe-polymorphic inductive instantiated at finitely many levels; universe-polymorphic lemmas ABOUT it
cases.target: One COMPLETE set of LOGOS declarations per distinct universe instantiation appearing in the source: `add_indexed_inductive("Box@0", …)` / `add_indexed_inductive("Box@1", …)` (kernel/src/context.rs:374), their own `add_constructor_checked` calls (context.rs:545), and their own `derive_recursor` + `add_definition` (kernel/src/recursor.rs:36). Plus a loss record naming UNIVERSE_MONOMORPHISATION that enumerates the instantiations emitted.
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:253, :374, :419, :545 (`add_inductive`, `add_indexed_inductive`, `add_constructor`, `add_constructor_checked` — none takes a universe-parameter list, which is why T01-007 is a rejection and this is the only fallback); kernel/src/context.rs:218 (`add_universe_poly` binds parameters for DEFINITIONS only); kernel/src/recursor.rs:36 and :64-71 (`derive_recursor` synthesises `(type, term)` with the motive target HARD-CODED: `Sort(Prop)` for a non-subsingleton `Prop` inductive, `Sort(Type 0)` for everything else — so even `Box@1`'s recursor eliminates only into `Type 0`); kernel/src/context.rs:449 (`get_global` is keyed on a flat `String`, so `Box@0` and `Box@1` are unrelated globals with no relation recorded anywhere); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1330-1360 (`is_subtype_normalized`: cumulativity applies to two `Sort`s and covariantly under a `Pi` codomain; every OTHER position, including a type constructor's argument, is INVARIANT and delegates to `def_eq_normalized`)
guards: Catches monomorphising at `Type 0` ONLY and reusing that declaration everywhere. This is T01-007's headline trap and it is worth restating here because monomorphisation is the very path that invites it: having decided to monomorphise, it is tempting to emit one instance and let cumulativity absorb the rest. It will — `Type 0 ≤ Type 1` holds (type_checker.rs:1333) — right up to the point where the collapsed instances are compared in an INVARIANT position (a type constructor's argument, type_checker.rs:1356-1358), where `def_eq_normalized` compares the two `Box@0`s and finds them equal, because they are. Two Lean types that were distinct have become one.

Catches discovering the instantiation set from the declaration rather than from the WHOLE PROGRAM. A translator that emits `Box@0` when it first sees `Box Nat` and then meets `Box Type` must go back and emit `Box@1` — and every already-emitted term that mentioned `Box` must be re-checked against which instance it meant. A single-pass translator cannot do this and will silently attach the second use to the first instance.

Catches monomorphising the TYPE and forgetting the CONSTRUCTORS, the RECURSOR, or the `Match` cases. `add_constructor` (context.rs:419) is UNCHECKED — it will happily attach `Box@1_mk : Π(α : Type 1). α → Box@0 α` to the wrong inductive, and `Match`'s positional check (type_checker.rs:254-260) only counts cases, so a `Match` on a `Box@1` value with `Box@0`'s cases passes the count test.

Catches a polymorphic LEMMA. `polyBoxId` below quantifies over `u`; there is no level variable to bind on a non-definition and the lemma is about an inductive, so it can only be emitted once per instantiation — which is fine ONLY because this file instantiates it finitely. A source that proves a lemma for all `u` and then applies it at a level determined by a later module has no finite instantiation set, and the translator must REJECT rather than guess a set.

Catches the naming scheme colliding. LOGOS keys are flat `String`s with one namespace (context.rs:449); `Box@0` is a name the translator invented, and a Lean declaration literally named `Box@0` — or a different mangling that produces the same string — key to the same slot. The mangling must be injective and must be checked against `get_global` before registration (T02-020).
oracle: For each universe-polymorphic inductive, the emitted context contains one complete declaration group per distinct instantiation reachable in the source (type, constructors via `add_constructor_checked`, derived recursor); no two Lean instantiations share a LOGOS global; a loss record with category UNIVERSE_MONOMORPHISATION enumerates them; and the translator EXITS NON-ZERO if any use site's level is not statically determined, rather than emitting a default.
loss: UNIVERSE_MONOMORPHISATION. The single Lean declaration becomes N unrelated LOGOS declarations. Anything the Lean source states ONCE about all levels must be restated N times, and anything it states for a level variable cannot be restated at all. Acceptable only when (a) the set of instantiations is finite and fully determined statically, and (b) no polymorphic lemma quantifies over the level. Both conditions must be CHECKED, not assumed; when either fails the verdict escalates to T01-007's rejection.

RECURSOR_LEVEL_CEILING. `derive_recursor` pins the motive target to `Sort(Type 0)` (recursor.rs:64-71). Monomorphising `Box` at `Type 1` gives you a `Box@1` whose ELEMENTS live at `Type 1` and whose recursor still eliminates only into `Type 0`. So monomorphisation does not actually recover large elimination at the higher level — it recovers the type and loses the eliminator. Any Lean proof that recurses over a `Type 1`-valued container into a `Type 1` motive has no image.

CROSS_LEVEL_IDENTITY. In Lean, `Box.mk` at level 0 and at level 1 are the SAME constant at two instantiations, so a lemma proved about `Box.mk` applies to both. After monomorphisation `Box@0_mk` and `Box@1_mk` are different globals; nothing in the LOGOS context records that they were one declaration, and no lemma transfers.

cases.title: Cumulativity mismatch — LOGOS admits `Prop ≤ Type 0 ≤ Type 1`; Lean 4 admits NOTHING
cases.lean: ULift, PLift, explicit universe lifting, `Type 0` vs `Type 1` argument positions, Lean's non-cumulative `Sort` hierarchy
cases.target: (none — no sound translation of a term whose Lean typing DEPENDS on the absence of cumulativity, and no licence to use LOGOS's cumulativity to resolve any level mismatch the translator could not otherwise resolve)
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1330-1336 (`is_subtype_normalized`: `(Term::Sort(u1), Term::Sort(u2)) => u1.is_subtype_of(u2)` — the cumulativity arm); kernel/src/term.rs:242-246 (`Universe::is_subtype_of` = `level_leq`, with the doc "Cumulative subtyping `self ≤ other`, decided over the level normal form. Sound for variables: `u ≤ u`, `Type 0 ≤ u`, `u ≤ succ u` hold"); kernel/src/term.rs:266-276 (`to_lnat`: `Prop ↦ 0`, `Type n ↦ n+1` — so `level_leq(Prop, Type 0)` is `0 ≤ 1`, TRUE: a proposition is admitted wherever a `Type 0` is expected); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1338-1355 (the Π arm: CONTRAVARIANT in the domain, COVARIANT in the codomain — so `Type 1 → Nat ≤ Type 0 → Nat`, a rule Lean has in no form whatsoever); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1356-1358 (every OTHER position is INVARIANT and delegates to `def_eq_normalized` — cumulativity is SHALLOW); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1309-1316 (`is_subtype` is what `check_type` calls at :452, so cumulativity is on the main path of every application, every declaration body check, and every `Match` case check); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1473-1478 (structure eta and, at :1567, `proof_irrelevant` sit inside `def_eq_normalized`, i.e. below the cumulative layer); Lean 4 side: `Type 0` is not a subtype of `Type 1` in any judgement — `ULift` / `PLift` (`Init.Core`) exist precisely because the coercion does not
guards: THIS IS THE CORPUS'S CENTRAL SOUNDNESS ASYMMETRY, stated as a rule: a translator may never use LOGOS's acceptance of a term as evidence that the term is a faithful translation. LOGOS's typing relation is STRICTLY LARGER than Lean's on exactly this axis. Every universe bug in Tier 1 — the `Type n` off-by-one (T01-002), the `Prop` sort off-by-one (T01-010), monomorphisation at the wrong level (T01-007, T01-008), defaulting an unresolved level (T01-012) — produces a term whose level is TOO HIGH, and `is_subtype_normalized`'s universe arm forgives every one of them upward. The kernel is therefore blind to the entire class. Conformance must be checked against Lean's judgement, re-derived, not against LOGOS's acceptance.

Catches ERASING `ULift` / `PLift`. `ULift.up` and `ULift.down` look like noise — they are the identity on the underlying value — and a translator that drops them produces `big Nat` where Lean wrote `big (ULift Nat)`. In Lean that is a hard error ("`Nat` has type `Type` but is expected to have type `Type 1`"). In LOGOS it typechecks, because `is_subtype_normalized` at :1333 answers `Type(0).is_subtype_of(Type(1))` = true. The emitted development then no longer needs the lift, which means it no longer needs `ULift` at all, which means every lemma about `ULift.up`/`ULift.down` in the source has no counterpart — and the two Lean types `ULift.{1} Nat` and `Nat`, which are genuinely distinct, have been identified.

Catches the Π-VARIANCE arm, which is the half a translator is least likely to expect. `is_subtype_normalized` at :1338-1352 makes `Type 1 → Nat ≤ Type 0 → Nat` (contravariance) and `Nat → Type 0 ≤ Nat → Type 1` (covariance). Lean has NEITHER. So a translator that hits a function-type mismatch — because it monomorphised a level, or because it got an off-by-one — will find that LOGOS silently accepts the function at a domain Lean never permitted, and the wrongly-typed function then propagates through every application.

Catches `Prop ≤ Type 0`. `level_leq(Prop, Type 0)` is `0 ≤ 1`, true (term.rs:268-271). So a PROOF is admitted wherever a `Type 0` value is expected. Lean refuses this outright — `PLift` exists for it. The consequence is worse than a level slip: once a `Prop` inhabitant sits in a `Type 0` position, `proof_irrelevant` (type_checker.rs:1547-1567) may still fire on it (it tests the inferred type's sort, not the position), so two DIFFERENT values in that position are definitionally equal. Computation over them is then not well-defined.

Catches the belief that "LOGOS is cumulative, so levels do not matter". Cumulativity is SHALLOW (type_checker.rs:1356-1358): it fires between two `Sort`s and covariantly under a `Pi` codomain, and NOWHERE else. Inside a type constructor's argument the comparison is INVARIANT and goes to `def_eq_normalized`, where two `Sort`s are compared by `equiv` (type_checker.rs:1496) — mutual `level_leq`, i.e. genuine equality. So `Box (Type 0)` and `Box (Type 1)` are NOT interchangeable even though `Type 0` and `Type 1` are. A translator that relies on cumulativity therefore produces a development that works at the top level and fails one constructor deep — the worst possible failure distribution, because the simple tests pass.

Catches "reject only when the levels differ". The mismatch is not always visible as a level: `is_subtype`'s FAST PATH is `types_equal` (type_checker.rs:1314), which returns true when either side is a `Term::Hole` (:1595-1597). A `Hole` left in a type (T00-016) therefore hides a cumulativity reliance behind a comparison that never examined the levels at all.
oracle: The translator re-derives Lean's judgement for every subterm it emits and asserts that each emitted `check_type`/`is_subtype` obligation would ALSO be discharged by definitional equality alone — i.e. by `def_eq_normalized` with the cumulative arms of `is_subtype_normalized` disabled. Any obligation that needs `u1.is_subtype_of(u2)` with `u1 != u2`, or that needs the `Pi` variance arm, is reported as E_CUMULATIVITY_RELIANCE and the declaration is not written. Re-checking the whole emitted corpus with a non-cumulative `is_subtype` must produce zero new failures.
diag: E_CUMULATIVITY_RELIANCE — must name the declaration, the two levels, and the exact position at which the translator's emitted term would be accepted only by `is_subtype_normalized`'s universe arm. Must state that Lean rejects the corresponding coercion. The translator must write NO declaration.

cases.title: `Prop : Type 0` (Lean) versus `Prop : Type 1` (LOGOS) — an off-by-one INSIDE LOGOS
cases.lean: Prop as a TYPE rather than as a sort: `(Prop : Type)`, `Prop → Nat`, a `Prop`-typed structure field, a container of propositions
cases.target: (none — any term in which `Prop` occupies a TERM position, i.e. one whose own sort is computed, has no faithful LOGOS translation)
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:194-201 — `Universe::succ`: `Universe::SProp | Universe::Prop => Universe::Type(1),` `Universe::Type(n) => Universe::Type(n + 1),` kernel/src/type_checker.rs:54 — `Term::Sort(u) => Ok(Term::Sort(u.succ()))`. Together: `infer_type(Sort(Prop)) = Sort(Type(1))`, i.e. LOGOS says `Prop : Type 1`. Lean says `Prop = Sort 0` and `Sort 0 : Sort 1 = Type 0`, i.e. `Prop : Type 0`. The discrepancy is not merely a disagreement with Lean — it is INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT in LOGOS. kernel/src/term.rs:266-276 (`to_lnat`), the ℕ-model that `level_leq` and therefore `equiv` and `is_subtype_of` are decided over, maps `Prop ↦ Const(0)` and `Type n ↦ Const(n+1)`. In that model the successor of `Prop` (0) is 1, which is `Type 0`. But `succ` returns `Type(1)`, which `to_lnat` reads as 2. So LOGOS's successor operation and LOGOS's level-ordering decision procedure disagree about `Prop` by exactly one, and only about `Prop`. kernel/src/term.rs:205-216 and :219-237 (`max` / `imax` — both take their operands' levels as given, so the shift propagates through every Π formation at type_checker.rs:104-110); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:452 and :1309-1336 (`check_type` → `is_subtype` → `level_leq`, which uses the CORRECT `to_lnat` model — so a term whose sort was computed one too high is compared against a bound computed correctly, and fails); kernel/src/context.rs:295-301 (`add_structure` pins the record's sort to `Term::Sort(Universe::Type(0))`) and context.rs:545 (`add_constructor_checked` performs a universe check — which a `Prop`-typed field will now fail, while context.rs:419's UNCHECKED `add_constructor` will not)
guards: Catches the belief that this is harmless because `Prop` is usually a CODOMAIN. It usually is, and there `imax(a, Prop) = Prop` (term.rs:224) absorbs the operand entirely, so the shift never appears: every theorem statement, every `∀` into a proposition, every `And`/`Or`/`Ex`, is unaffected. A conformance suite made of THEOREMS will pass at 100% while the defect is live. The shift appears only where `Prop`'s OWN sort enters a `max` as the strict maximum — that is, where `Prop` sits in a DOMAIN position, a structure field, or a container argument. Those are data-level constructs, which a proof-oriented test suite barely exercises.

The crisp discriminator, worked out: `Prop → Nat`. Lean  — domain `Prop : Sort 1` (level 1); codomain `Nat : Sort 1` (level 1); `imax(1,1) = 1`; result `Sort 1` = `Type 0`. LOGOS — domain sort `succ(Prop) = Type(1)`; codomain sort `Type(0)`; `imax(Type 1, Type 0) = max(...) = Type 1`; result `Type 1`. One level apart. And `Prop → Type` is NOT a discriminator: there the codomain's own level (`Type 0 : Type 1`) already equals the shifted `Prop` level, so `max` returns the same answer in both systems. A translator that tests only the second case concludes there is no bug.

Catches "just bump every level that mentions `Prop` down by one". The compensation is not expressible: `Universe::Type` takes a concrete `u32` (term.rs:177) and there is no level-subtraction form, so the correction must be applied by the translator to every computed sort — and it cannot be applied to a level VARIABLE, because `Var(u)` ranges over the ℕ-model including 0 = `Prop` (term.rs:270-272). A translator that shifts concrete levels and leaves variables alone makes `level_leq`'s case-split on the `Prop`-ness of a pivot variable (term.rs:322-360) answer against a model that no longer matches the terms.

Catches "map `Prop` to `Universe::Type(0)`, then `Prop : Type 1` comes out right". It does come out right — `succ(Type(0)) = Type(1)`, matching Lean's `Type 0 : Type 1` for the thing that used to be `Prop`. And it destroys impredicativity (`imax(a, Type 0) = max(a, Type 0)`, term.rs:227), definitional proof irrelevance (`proof_irrelevant` matches `Sort(Universe::Prop)` syntactically, type_checker.rs:1553-1560), and the large-elimination gate (same syntactic match, type_checker.rs:277-288). Trading a level shift for the loss of the `Prop`-elimination restriction trades a precision bug for an UNSOUNDNESS. See T01-001.

Catches the interaction with `add_structure`. A Lean `structure` with a `Prop`-typed field is `Type 0` in Lean. `add_structure` hard-codes the record's sort to `Type 0` (context.rs:300) — so the record's declared sort is right — but the constructor's field is `Sort(Prop)`, whose own sort LOGOS computes as `Type 1`. The UNCHECKED `add_constructor` (context.rs:419) accepts it; `add_constructor_checked` (context.rs:545), which performs the universe check, does not. The same declaration is therefore accepted or refused depending on which registration path the translator took — and the unchecked path is the one that "works". This is T11-013's trap reached through the universe layer.

Catches the direction of failure being mistaken for safety. Here LOGOS computes a level too HIGH, and `is_subtype` only forgives going UP (term.rs:242-246), so the declaration below that states `Type` is REJECTED — a loud failure. A translator that responds by relaxing the stated level to `Type 1` has made the failure quiet and has changed the type of the declaration. Every consumer that stated `Type 0` then fails in turn, and the shift propagates through the whole development, one declaration per round of "fixes".
oracle: For every declaration, the translator recomputes the sort Lean assigned and the sort `type_checker::infer_type` assigns to the emitted term, and asserts `Universe::equiv` between them. Any declaration where they differ — and they differ exactly when `Sort(Prop)`'s own sort is the strict maximum of a level computation — exits non-zero with E_PROP_SORT_OFFBY1 and writes nothing. The harness additionally asserts, directly against the kernel, that `infer_type(Sort(Prop)) == Sort(Type(1))` and that `is_subtype(Sort(Type(1)), Sort(Type(0)))` is FALSE — pinning both halves of the defect so that a future LOGOS release which fixes `succ` flips this case, rather than silently changing its meaning.
diag: E_PROP_SORT_OFFBY1 — must name the declaration, the sort Lean assigns (`Type n`) and the sort LOGOS computes (`Type (n+1)`), and state that the discrepancy originates in `Universe::succ`'s `Prop` arm. Must NOT emit the declaration at a bumped level and must NOT emit `Prop` as `Type 0` to sidestep it.

cases.title: Auto-bound universe parameters — generated names, and a POSITIONAL level list
cases.lean: autoImplicit/relaxedAutoImplicit universe auto-binding, `def f (α : Type u)` with no `.{u}`, `Type _`, Mathlib's `Type*` (which expands to auto-bound `Type _`)
cases.target: `Context::add_universe_poly(name, params, ty, body)` (kernel/src/context.rs:218) with `params` equal to Lean's `ConstantInfo.levelParams` IN ORDER, plus a loss record naming AUTOBOUND_LEVEL_PROVENANCE. References are `Term::Const { name, levels }` (term.rs:458) with `levels` in the same positional order.
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:218-225 (`add_universe_poly` stores `params: Vec<String>`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:83-85 (`let subst = params.iter().cloned() .zip(levels.iter().cloned()).collect();` — the parameter/level association is POSITIONAL, by zip, with no name matching on the caller's side); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:75-82 (arity mismatch is a `CertificationError`) versus kernel/src/reduction.rs:83-90 (the SAME mismatch in a reduction position returns the term unreduced, silently); kernel/src/term.rs:179 and :271 (`Universe::Var(String)`, compared by NAME through `to_lnat` — so level-variable names are a flat global namespace); kernel/src/context.rs:253, :374, :419, :434 (no universe-parameter list on inductives, constructors or declarations — so an auto-bound level on any of those has no binder; T01-003, T01-007); kernel/src/term.rs:256-265 (`Universe::substitute`, which `instantiate_universes` drives, replaces `Var(v)` by `subst[v]` and leaves an unmatched `Var` UNCHANGED — `.unwrap_or_else(|| self.clone())` at term.rs:262 — so a missing parameter is not an error, it is a silently uninstantiated level)
guards: Catches deriving the parameter ORDER from the TYPE rather than from `ConstantInfo.levelParams`. `type_checker.rs:83-85` zips positionally, so the order is the contract. Lean orders auto-bound parameters by first occurrence in the elaborated signature, which is NOT the order they appear in the surface syntax once implicit binders and instance arguments have been inserted and reordered. A swapped pair is undetectable whenever the level expression is symmetric (`max u v`, T01-004) and silently wrong where it is not.

Catches the FLAT NAMESPACE of generated names. Every auto-bound declaration in a Lean file gets its own `u_1`; `Universe::Var` compares by name (term.rs:271), so a translator that copies the names verbatim makes the first universe parameter of EVERY auto-bound declaration in the corpus the same level variable. Inside one declaration this is harmless (the substitution is per-`Const`); across declarations it makes `Universe::equiv` report two unrelated levels equal, weakening every constraint the source imposed. Names must be freshened per declaration.

Catches a MISSING parameter being silent. `Universe::substitute` (term.rs:260-263) leaves an unmatched `Var` unchanged rather than erroring, so if `params` omits a variable that occurs in `ty`, `instantiate_universes` returns a type still containing the free `Var` — and `infer_sort` will accept it, and `level_leq` will answer questions about it. The declaration is registered with a level that no instantiation can ever fix. The arity check at type_checker.rs:75-82 does NOT catch this: it compares `params.len()` to `levels.len()`, not `params` to the variables actually occurring.

Catches auto-binding on a NON-definition. Lean will auto-bind a universe on an `inductive`, a `structure`, an `axiom` or an `instance` just as readily as on a `def`, and LOGOS has a binder for none of them (context.rs:253, :374, :419, :434). An auto-bound `inductive` is T01-007's rejection reached by accident — the source never wrote a universe parameter, so a translator that keys its polymorphic-inductive check on "did the source write `.{u}`" will miss it entirely. The check must be on `levelParams.isEmpty`, not on the surface syntax.

Catches `Type _` being treated as `Type 0`. Lean elaborates the `_` to a level metavariable and then either solves it from the context or AUTO-BINDS it. Which of those happened is only visible in the finished `ConstantInfo`; a translator that reads the pre-elaboration `Syntax`, or that defaults an unsolved level, monomorphises a declaration Lean made polymorphic. An unsolved level that is NOT auto-bound is T01-012's rejection.

Catches assuming `set_option autoImplicit false` removes the issue. It removes auto-binding of TERM-level implicits; universe auto-binding is governed separately and `def f (α : Type u)` still binds `u` under the default settings. The translator must read the elaborated declaration, never infer the setting.
oracle: For every declaration, the emitted `params` equals Lean's `ConstantInfo.levelParams` as an ORDERED list, modulo a per-declaration freshening that is injective across the corpus; every `Universe::Var` occurring in the emitted type or body is a member of that declaration's `params`; every reference is a `Term::Const` whose `levels.len()` matches; and a loss record with category AUTOBOUND_LEVEL_PROVENANCE lists each declaration whose universe parameters were auto-bound rather than written.
loss: AUTOBOUND_LEVEL_PROVENANCE. Lean's auto-bound parameters are named by the elaborator (`u_1`, `u_2`, …), ordered by first occurrence, and their EXISTENCE is a consequence of elaboration settings (`autoImplicit`, `relaxedAutoImplicit`) rather than of the source text. The generated names carry no meaning and are not stable across Lean versions or across edits to the signature. Emitting them verbatim into `add_universe_poly`'s `params` is correct but records nothing about where they came from, so a later re-translation that produces a different generated name yields a different LOGOS declaration for an unchanged source. Acceptable because the names are internal to `add_universe_poly`'s substitution; the loss must be recorded so that declaration-level diffs can be attributed.

cases.title: Level metavariables — `Universe` has no metavariable form; levels must be EXPLICIT
cases.lean: Lean.Level.mvar, `Type _`, `Sort _`, universe unification, instantiateLevelMVars
cases.target: (none — an unresolved universe level has no LOGOS representation)
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:167-191 (the complete `Universe` enum: `SProp`, `Prop`, `Type(u32)`, `Var(String)`, `Succ`, `Max`, `IMax` — there is NO metavariable variant, and no `Hole`-like wildcard at the level layer); kernel/src/term.rs:458 (`Term::Const { name, levels: Vec<Universe> }` — the level list is a concrete `Vec`, so every entry must be a fully-formed `Universe`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:75-85 (`Const` inference requires `params.len() == levels.len()` and then substitutes — there is no unification step and no constraint store anywhere in the kernel); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:137-140 (LOGOS's own metavariables are `Term::Var` names beginning with `?` — a TERM-level convention that has no level-level analogue, so there is not even a hack available); kernel/src/term.rs:266-276 (`to_lnat`, with the doc at :270-272: "every universe VARIABLE ranges over all of ℕ (so a variable may be `Prop`, which is what closes the `Sort u := Nat` unsoundness — `Type 0 ≤ u` is false, since `u` could be `Prop`)"); kernel/src/term.rs:256-265 (`Universe::substitute`: an unmatched `Var` is returned UNCHANGED at :262, so a level variable that no binder covers is silently retained)
guards: Catches `Level.mvar ⟼ Universe::Var(name)`. These are not the same thing and the difference is a quantifier. A metavariable is an EXISTENTIAL — "there is some level making this well-typed, not yet determined". A `Universe::Var` bound by `add_universe_poly` (context.rs:218) is a UNIVERSAL — "for every level". Turning the first into the second strengthens the declaration: it claims the definition works at EVERY level, including `Prop` (term.rs:270-272 is explicit that a variable ranges over `Prop`). LOGOS will not catch the strengthening, because a universally quantified declaration is checked only at its parameters, and `level_leq` is sound for variables by case-splitting — so the declaration typechecks and asserts more than Lean ever proved.

Catches `Level.mvar` left as a FREE `Universe::Var` with no binder. `Universe::substitute` (term.rs:260-263) returns an unmatched `Var` unchanged rather than erroring, and `infer_sort` (type_checker.rs:520-525) will return it happily. So the declaration is registered carrying a level that no `Term::Const` can ever instantiate, and every `level_leq` question about it is answered by case analysis over a variable that means nothing. Nothing errors at any point.

Catches DEFAULTING to `Universe::Type(0)`. This is not a conservative approximation in either direction. Too strong: it fixes `u := Type 0`, so any use at a higher level is rejected — and, because LOGOS is cumulative (type_checker.rs:1330-1336), a great many of those uses are NOT rejected, they are silently absorbed upward, collapsing distinct instantiations onto one declaration (T01-007, T01-008). Too weak: it excludes the `Prop` instantiation that `Sort _` may have been solved to, so a proof-level use has no image.

Catches reading the level BEFORE `instantiateLevelMVars`. Every `Type _`/`Sort _` below carries a live `Level.mvar` during elaboration; Lean solves them by unification against a later argument or a declared type, or auto-binds them (T01-011). A translator hooked in before that point sees metavariables in declarations whose finished `ConstantInfo` has none. This is the level-layer twin of T00-010: read the FINISHED declaration, run `instantiateLevelMVars`, and assert the result is mvar-free — `Expr.hasLevelMVar` is the check, and it must be applied to the type AND the value.

Catches "the level is obviously determined, so infer it myself". LOGOS has no constraint store and no level unifier — `type_checker.rs:83-85` performs a SUBSTITUTION, not a unification — so any level the translator infers is the translator's own claim, checked by nothing downstream. Lean's level solver has already run and either succeeded (in which case the answer is in the `ConstantInfo`) or failed (in which case the Lean declaration does not exist). There is no third case in which the translator should be solving levels.

Catches a metavariable surviving in a `Term::Const`'s `levels`. The arity check at type_checker.rs:75-82 counts entries; it does not inspect them. A `levels` vector of the right LENGTH containing a defaulted or invented level passes, and `instantiate_universes` (term.rs:256-265) substitutes it into the type without complaint. The emitted reference then has a concrete, wrong type.
oracle: After `instantiateLevelMVars`, every translated declaration's type and value satisfy `!hasLevelMVar`; any that does not exits non-zero with E_UNRESOLVED_LEVEL and writes nothing. Every emitted `Universe::Var(n)` is a member of its declaration's `add_universe_poly` `params` (no free level variables anywhere in the emitted context); and no emitted level was chosen by the translator rather than read from Lean's elaborated declaration.
diag: E_UNRESOLVED_LEVEL — must name the declaration, the position, and the Lean `Level.mvar` identifier. Must NOT default the level, must NOT turn it into a `Universe::Var`, and must write NO declaration.

cases.title: `SProp` — vestigial in LOGOS; emitting it is INVENTING a universe Lean does not have
cases.lean: (no Lean 4 counterpart) — the Lean constructs a translator is tempted to map onto it: definitionally proof-irrelevant `Prop`s, `Subsingleton`, squash types, `PUnit`-like propositions, `Eq` proofs
cases.target: (none — `Universe::SProp` must never appear in translator output)
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:170-174 (`Universe::SProp` exists, documented as "the DEFINITIONALLY-proof-irrelevant sort (S) … the bottom of the hierarchy (`SProp ≤ Prop ≤ Type n`) … impredicative"); and then, in the whole workspace, `SProp` is READ in exactly four places and CONSTRUCTED in none of them: kernel/src/term.rs:208, :222 (absorbed by `max`; `imax(a, SProp) = SProp`), kernel/src/term.rs:196-198 (`succ(SProp) = Type(1)` — the same off-by-one as `Prop`, T01-010), kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1553-1560 (`proof_irrelevant` accepts `Sort(Universe::Prop) | Sort(Universe::SProp)`), kernel/src/recheck.rs:757 (the de Bruijn re-checker's copy of the same test), kernel/src/reduction.rs:4539 (`Universe::SProp => Term::Global("USProp")` — a reflection token); kernel/src/context.rs:253, :271, :374, :419, :545 — NO registration path takes an `SProp` sort in any distinguished way, and nothing in kernel/src/prelude.rs declares an `SProp` inductive, so the sort is uninhabitable by any declared type; kernel/src/recursor.rs:64-71 — `derive_recursor`'s motive target is `Sort(Prop)` for a non-subsingleton `Prop` inductive and `Sort(Type 0)` for EVERYTHING ELSE; there is no `SProp` arm, so an `SProp`-sorted inductive would get a `Type 0` eliminator; kernel/src/type_checker.rs:277-288 — the large-elimination gate tests `Term::Sort(Universe::Prop)` ONLY; an `SProp`-sorted discriminant does not match and the restriction is NOT APPLIED; kernel/tests/sprop.rs:44-56 — the only exercise of the sort is a unit test asserting the level algebra (`SProp : Type 1`, `SProp ≤ Prop ≤ Type 0`, and not the converses)
guards: THE SOUNDNESS HOLE, stated plainly. The large-elimination gate at type_checker.rs:277-288 fires only when the discriminant's type infers to `Term::Sort(Universe::Prop)`. An inductive registered at `Sort(Universe::SProp)` — which `add_inductive` (context.rs:253) will accept, being UNCHECKED — does not match that pattern, so a multi-constructor proposition placed in `SProp` may be eliminated into `Type` with no restriction at all. Meanwhile `proof_irrelevant` (type_checker.rs:1553-1560) DOES match `SProp`, so any two of its inhabitants are definitionally equal. Together: two definitionally equal proofs can be eliminated into two distinct `Type`-level values. That is an inconsistency, reachable by a translator that thought it was being precise.

Catches the premise itself. Lean 4 has no `SProp`. There is therefore no Lean construct that SHOULD map to `Universe::SProp`, and any emission of it is the translator inventing a universe. The temptation is real because several Lean idioms LOOK like `SProp`: `Prop` already has definitional proof irrelevance in Lean, so a translator reading LOGOS's `SProp` documentation ("definitionally proof-irrelevant") may reasonably conclude that Lean's `Prop` maps there. It does not: Lean's `Prop` maps to `Universe::Prop` (T01-001), which LOGOS also gives definitional proof irrelevance (type_checker.rs:1547-1567) — the feature is already available at the correct sort.

Catches mapping `Subsingleton`, a squash type, or a single-constructor `Prop` to `SProp` on the grounds that they are "more irrelevant" than an ordinary proposition. They are ordinary `Prop`s in Lean and must stay `Universe::Prop`. LOGOS's notion of a subsingleton is a PROPERTY computed from the constructor list (`is_subsingleton_prop`, type_checker.rs:1688-1716), not a sort — see T01-014.

Catches emitting `SProp` "because it is the bottom of the hierarchy and therefore safe". It is the bottom for SUBTYPING (`level_leq`; kernel/tests/sprop.rs:51-56), and that is exactly what makes it unsafe here: `SProp ≤ Prop ≤ Type 0` means an `SProp`-sorted thing is admitted in every position, so the mistranslation is absorbed silently everywhere by cumulativity (T01-009) instead of failing at the declaration.

Catches `imax(a, SProp) = SProp` (term.rs:222-224). Once ONE thing is at `SProp`, every Π into it collapses to `SProp` too, so the sort propagates through the development along exactly the paths that `Prop` would have — but into the branch of the kernel that has no elimination gate and no recursor arm.

Catches relying on `succ(SProp)`. term.rs:196-198 gives `Type(1)`, inheriting T01-010's off-by-one wholesale — so even the "harmless" act of mentioning `Sort SProp` as a type lands at the wrong level.
oracle: A structural walk of every emitted `Term` (declaration types, bodies, constructor types, structure field types, recursor types) finds zero `Universe::SProp` nodes, and no `Context::add_inductive`/`add_indexed_inductive`/`add_structure` call in the emitted context carries an `SProp` sort. Any Lean declaration the translator classified as `SProp`-eligible exits non-zero with E_NO_SPROP.
diag: E_NO_SPROP — must name the Lean declaration and the LOGOS universe the translator was about to emit, and state that Lean 4 has no `SProp` so no Lean construct maps to it. No declaration may be written at `Sort(SProp)`.

cases.title: Large elimination from `Prop` — LOGOS's subsingleton gate differs from Lean's, in BOTH directions
cases.lean: False.elim, Eq.rec / ▸, And.rec into Type, Acc.rec, Or (refused), motive restrictions
cases.target: A `Term::Match` (kernel/src/term.rs:469) whose motive targets the translated Lean motive, subject to LOGOS's gate at kernel/src/type_checker.rs:277-288 — plus, where the Lean elimination is universe-polymorphic, a loss record naming LARGE_ELIM_LEVEL_CEILING. Where LOGOS's gate is STRICTER than Lean's the loss record is LARGE_ELIM_REFUSED; where it is LOOSER the translator must REJECT (see `@note`).
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:277-288 (the gate: if the discriminant's type is a `Prop` and the return type is not, the inductive must satisfy `is_subsingleton_prop`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1688-1716 (`is_subsingleton_prop`: 0 constructors ⇒ true; exactly 1 constructor ⇒ every constructor argument BEYOND THE INDUCTIVE'S ARITY must have sort `Prop`; ≥ 2 constructors ⇒ false) and :1719-1724 (`pi_param_count`, the "arity" it skips — a COUNT of leading `Π`s in the inductive's own type, applied positionally to the CONSTRUCTOR's telescope); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:655-678 (`infer_indexed_match` repeats the same gate for indexed families); kernel/src/recursor.rs:64-71 (`derive_recursor`'s motive target is HARD-CODED: `Sort(Prop)` for a non-subsingleton `Prop` inductive, `Sort(Type 0)` for everything else — never `Type 1`, never a level variable); Lean's rule, for contrast: an inductive proposition eliminates into a larger sort iff it has at most one constructor and every constructor argument is either a proof or APPEARS IN THE RESULT TYPE'S INDICES — the second disjunct is the one LOGOS does not implement
guards: Catches translating a `Prop` elimination into `Type` without checking WHICH gate applies. The two systems agree on the easy cases — `False` (0 constructors), `Eq` and `And` (1 constructor, propositional arguments), `Or` (2 constructors, refused by both) — so a suite built from those tells you nothing.

Catches the LOOSER direction, which is a soundness hole. `is_subsingleton_prop` (type_checker.rs:1700-1711) computes `arity = pi_param_count(<the inductive's type>)` and then SKIPS the first `arity` arguments of the CONSTRUCTOR's telescope, checking only the rest. Those are two different telescopes. For `Sneaky : Nat → Prop` with `mk : (junk : Nat) → Sneaky 0`, the arity is 1 and the constructor has exactly one argument — `junk`, which is DATA, not a proof, and which does NOT appear in the result type's index (`Sneaky 0`). LOGOS skips it as though it were the index and returns `true`. Lean refuses this elimination (its `Sneaky.rec` motive is restricted to `Prop`). So LOGOS will large-eliminate a proposition that carries a genuine `Nat`, while `proof_irrelevant` (type_checker.rs:1547-1567) simultaneously makes `Sneaky.mk 0` and `Sneaky.mk 1` definitionally equal — two definitionally equal proofs yielding two distinct `Nat`s. A translator must detect this shape and refuse it, because LOGOS will not.

Catches keying the gate on the SOURCE's motive rather than on the emitted one. `type_checker.rs:278-279` classifies the RETURN TYPE by `normalize(infer_type(return_type))`, where `return_type` is `beta_reduce(App(motive, discriminant))` (:271). A motive the translator emitted as `Term::Hole` (T00-016) makes `infer_type` fail or return a non-`Sort`, and the `large` test at :279 then takes the wrong branch — the restriction is skipped entirely.

Catches relying on `derive_recursor` to reproduce Lean's `.rec`. It does not: the motive target is hard-coded (recursor.rs:64-71), so the derived `Eq_rec` eliminates into `Type 0` and nothing higher, and the derived recursor for a multi-constructor `Prop` targets `Sort(Prop)` regardless of what the source asked for. `Match` is the primitive in LOGOS and `.rec` is derived — the inverse of Lean (T03-021) — so a Lean proof written through `.rec` must be re-expressed as a `Match`, and its level re-checked against the ceiling.

Catches assuming the gate runs at all. `add_inductive` and `add_constructor` (context.rs:253, :419) are UNCHECKED; `is_subsingleton_prop` reads `ctx.get_constructors` (type_checker.rs:1689), so an inductive registered with the wrong constructor list — or with none — answers the gate's question from data the translator supplied. Zero constructors returns `true` unconditionally (type_checker.rs:1691), so a `Prop` inductive whose constructors the translator failed to register large-eliminates freely.
oracle: For each `Prop` elimination: if Lean's motive targets a sort above `Type 0`, a LARGE_ELIM_LEVEL_CEILING loss record exists; if Lean permits the elimination and `is_subsingleton_prop` returns false, a LARGE_ELIM_REFUSED loss record exists; and if `is_subsingleton_prop` returns TRUE while Lean's rule refuses — the arity-skip hole — the translator exits non-zero and writes nothing. The harness independently asserts, against the kernel, that `is_subsingleton_prop(ctx, "Sneaky")` is `true` while `Sneaky.rec`'s Lean motive is `Prop`-restricted, pinning the divergence so a future LOGOS fix flips this case rather than silently changing its meaning.
loss: LARGE_ELIM_LEVEL_CEILING. Lean's `False.elim`, `Eq.rec`, `And.rec` and `Acc.rec` are universe-POLYMORPHIC: they eliminate into `Sort u` for any `u`. LOGOS's derived recursors are pinned to `Sort(Type 0)` (recursor.rs:64-71) and are not universe-polymorphic (T01-007), so an elimination into `Type 1` or into a level variable has no image. `False.elim h : Type 1` below is exactly this. Acceptable only in the sense that the `Type 0` instance survives; every higher instance must be monomorphised (T01-008) or rejected.

LARGE_ELIM_REFUSED. LOGOS's gate is stricter than Lean's for any single-constructor proposition whose non-proof constructor arguments are justified by APPEARING IN THE INDICES rather than by being propositional. `Acc` survives because its data argument sits inside the arity prefix that `is_subsingleton_prop` skips; a differently-ordered constructor of the same shape does not. When LOGOS refuses an elimination Lean allowed, the proof must be restructured, and that restructuring must be recorded.
note: DISAGREEMENT WITH INDEX.md. INDEX.md classifies T01-014 as `degrade`, and that is right for the case as a whole: the dominant direction is Lean-accepted eliminations that LOGOS refuses or can only perform at `Type 0`, which is a loss. But the `Sneaky` shape above is not a loss — it is a `reject`. LOGOS's gate ADMITS a large elimination that Lean denies, and combined with definitional proof irrelevance that admission is inconsistent. This case is therefore written as `degrade` to match the index, with the `Sneaky` sub-class carrying a mandatory rejection obligation in the guards and the oracle. I believe the index should split this into T01-014 (`degrade`, ceiling/refusal) and a new `reject` case for the arity-skip hole, and that T11-020's blanket `degrade` for "large-elimination gate differs from Lean's" under-classifies the same defect.

cases.title: `def` — a delta-transparent global definition
cases.lean: def, Lean.DefinitionVal, ReducibilityStatus.regular
cases.target: Context::add_definition(name: String, ty: Term, body: Term)
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:442-444 (`add_definition` stores `name -> (ty, body)` in the `definitions` map); kernel/src/context.rs:54-57 (definitions are documented as transparent — "they unfold during normalization (delta reduction)"); kernel/src/context.rs:474-476 (`get_definition_body` returns `None` for axioms, constructors and inductives — only definitions carry a body); kernel/src/context.rs:449-464 (`get_global` precedence: inductives → constructors → definitions → declarations)
guards: Catches emitting a `def` as `add_declaration` (an axiom). That compiles, and every *statement* about the function still typechecks, but the body is gone: `double 2 = 4` becomes unprovable by `rfl`/`decide` because there is nothing to delta-unfold. The failure surfaces only in downstream proofs, arbitrarily far from the mistranslation.

Catches emitting the *body* where the *type* goes. `add_definition` takes `(name, ty, body)` positionally with both `Term`s adjacent and no validation at the call site — `add_definition` performs **no typecheck at all**, unlike Lean's `addDecl`. A swapped pair is accepted silently and only explodes later inside `infer_type` of some unrelated term.

Catches dropping the declaration's own typecheck. Lean's kernel checks `body : ty` at `addDecl` time. LOGOS's `add_definition` is a bare `HashMap::insert`. A conforming translator must call `infer_type`/`is_subtype` on the pair itself and refuse to register when it fails, or an ill-typed definition sits in the context poisoning everything that unfolds it.
Catches name shadowing: `add_definition` is `HashMap::insert`, so registering a name that already exists **silently overwrites** it with no error. See T02-020.
oracle: After translation the LOGOS context has a *definition* (not a declaration) under the flattened name; `get_definition_body` returns `Some`; `infer_type(body)` is a subtype of the emitted type; and `normalize(App(Global(name), args))` reduces past the global.

cases.title: `theorem` — there is no theorem form in LOGOS; it is a `Prop`-typed definition
cases.lean: theorem, Lean.TheoremVal, proof irrelevance at the declaration level
cases.target: Context::add_definition(name, ty, proof_term)  — the same API as `def`
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:442-444 (`add_definition` is the only body-carrying registration; there is no `add_theorem`, and no `Declaration` enum with a `theorem` arm — the context is parallel maps only, context.rs:20-100); kernel/src/context.rs:434-436 (`add_declaration` = axiom, type only); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1547-1567 (`proof_irrelevant` is a *conversion* rule, not a declaration-level erasure)
guards: Catches the translator treating `theorem` as `add_declaration` "because proofs are irrelevant anyway". That is exactly how a proof library becomes a pile of axioms: every theorem silently turns into an assumption, `sorry`-equivalent, and the certificate still verifies because the axiom is in the context. The distinction `is_definition(name)` (context.rs:467) is the only way to tell afterwards, and by then the provenance is lost.

Catches the inverse asymmetry with Lean: Lean's `theorem` bodies are *irreducible* for delta (the kernel will not unfold a theorem during defeq except in special cases), while LOGOS's `add_definition` is unconditionally transparent (context.rs:54-57). So a LOGOS proof term *can* be unfolded where Lean's cannot. That direction is harmless for soundness but changes reduction behaviour and the `normalize` fuel budget (reduction.rs:52-69); a translator that also relies on theorem-opacity for performance will not get it.
Catches emitting the *statement* rather than the *proof term* as the body. Since `add_definition` never typechecks, `add_definition("foo", P, P)` is accepted.

Catches losing the proof entirely for a theorem proved `by tac`. The translator must read the elaborated `TheoremVal.value` (the finished proof term), not the tactic block — LOGOS has no way to replay a Lean tactic.
oracle: The emitted name is a *definition* whose stored type normalizes to a `Sort(Prop)`, whose body `infer_type`s to that type, and `is_definition(name) == true`.

cases.title: `axiom` — an opaque, body-less global
cases.lean: axiom, Lean.AxiomVal, Environment.addDecl on an axiom
cases.target: Context::add_declaration(name: &str, ty: Term)
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:434-436 (`add_declaration` stores `name -> ty` in `declarations`, the axiom/hypothesis map); kernel/src/context.rs:50-52 (documented as "axioms/hypotheses … no body"); kernel/src/context.rs:474-476 (`get_definition_body` is `None` for a declaration, so nothing delta-unfolds); kernel/src/prelude.rs:78 (`dne` is registered this way — the entire classical content of LOGOS is one `add_declaration`)
guards: Catches emitting an axiom as a *definition* with some placeholder body. A `Term::Hole` body is the worst version: `types_equal` treats `Hole` as matching **anything** (type_checker.rs:1594-1597), so the fake definition typechecks against every use and the axiom becomes an unsound universal.

Catches losing the axiom from the trust report. LOGOS has no `#print axioms`: the `declarations` map is the *entire* record of what is assumed, and `iter_declarations` (context.rs:520) is the only audit surface. A translator must emit a machine-readable list of every `add_declaration` it performs, because a downstream certificate that verifies against an enlarged axiom set is not evidence of anything. The certificate's `PRELUDE_VERSION` (certificate.rs:28, "logos-coc-1") pins only the *prelude's* axioms, not translator-added ones.

Catches translating a Lean axiom whose statement is refutable in LOGOS's prelude. LOGOS already assumes `dne` plus 16 `Int` ring/order axioms (prelude.rs:92-340); an incoming Lean axiom is added to *that* set, not to an empty one, so the consistency obligation is joint. A translator must at minimum record the union.

Catches the `get_global` precedence trap (context.rs:449-464): declarations are looked up **last**. If a name is registered both as a definition and as a declaration, the declaration is invisible — the type reported is the definition's.
oracle: The emitted name resolves via `get_global` but `is_definition(name) == false` and `get_definition_body(name) == None`; and the translator's loss/trust report lists the axiom by name and type.

cases.title: `abbrev` — the `@[reducible]` hint has no carrier in LOGOS
cases.lean: abbrev, @[reducible], ReducibilityStatus, TransparencyMode
cases.target: Context::add_definition(name, ty, body)  + a loss record
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:442-444 (`add_definition` is the only definition form; the stored triple is `name -> (ty, body)` with **no** reducibility field); kernel/src/context.rs:20-100 (the whole `Context` — there is no transparency map, no `ReducibilityStatus` analogue, and no `TransparencyMode` parameter anywhere); kernel/src/reduction.rs:52-69 (`normalize` unfolds whatever `get_definition_body` returns, with a single global fuel of 10000 and no per-constant policy)
guards: Catches a translator that "preserves" `abbrev` by inlining its body at every use site. That is semantically right and operationally catastrophic: `normalize` has a hard fuel of 10000 steps and **silently returns the partially-reduced term** when it runs out (reduction.rs:52-69), so inlining a chain of abbreviations turns a successful conversion check into a silent failure that reports as a *type mismatch* on an unrelated term. Substitution is also O(size)-per-binder (type_checker.rs:1088), so inlining is quadratic.
Catches a translator that maps `abbrev` to `add_declaration` to "keep it abstract". Backwards: `abbrev` is the *most* transparent form in Lean.
Catches silently succeeding. Degrade means the loss record is mandatory: a conformance run that emits the right term and no `REDUCIBILITY_HINT` record fails.
oracle: The emitted declaration is a definition with the abbreviation's elaborated body, and the loss report contains REDUCIBILITY_HINT naming this declaration.
loss: REDUCIBILITY_HINT. Lean distinguishes `@[reducible]` (unfolded by `whnf` at `.instances` transparency, so typeclass search sees through it), `regular`, and `@[irreducible]` (never unfolded without `unfold`). LOGOS has exactly one behaviour: always transparent. The hint is dropped.

ELABORATION_BEHAVIOUR. Because `abbrev` is reducible, Lean's instance search and unifier see through it; a `def` with the same body would block them. After translation both collapse to the same thing, so a *Lean* development that relied on a `def` being opaque to instance search has no LOGOS counterpart — see T00-013.

cases.title: `example` — an anonymous declaration needs a generated, collision-free LOGOS name
cases.lean: example, Lean.Elab.Command.elabExample, `_example` internal naming
cases.target: Context::add_definition(<generated name>, ty, body)
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:442-444 (`add_definition` takes a `String` name — there is no anonymous registration path); kernel/src/context.rs:20-100 (every global map in `Context` is keyed by `String`; there is no `Name` type, no anonymous/hygienic component, and no `Nat`-indexed macro scope); kernel/src/context.rs:449-464 (`get_global` is a plain map lookup, so two `example`s that generate the same name are indistinguishable)
guards: Catches the translator *dropping* `example`s. They are the cheapest conformance evidence a Lean file carries: each one is a closed, fully elaborated term that the LOGOS kernel can be asked to check. Silently skipping them means the translator's own regression surface disappears, and an `example` that Lean accepted but LOGOS rejects goes unnoticed.

Catches naive name generation. Lean's internal name for an example is `_example`, and *every* example in a module gets it — they do not collide in Lean because the declaration is never added to the environment under that name. In LOGOS `add_definition` is `HashMap::insert`, so emitting `_example` for each one means example N silently overwrites example N-1 and only the last is ever checked. The generated name must be unique per source position.

Catches a generated name that collides with a *user* name. LOGOS names are flat `String`s with no reserved namespace, so a scheme like `example_1` can be produced by a user declaration `example_1` or by flattening `example.1`. The scheme must use a character that cannot appear in a flattened Lean name, or must be checked against the context before insertion. See T02-020.
Catches emitting an `example` as an *axiom*: it has a body, and its whole value is that the body typechecks.
oracle: Every `example` in the source produces exactly one LOGOS registration; the emitted names are pairwise distinct and distinct from every user name in the module; and each body `infer_type`s to its stated type.

cases.title: `opaque` — an axiom plus a discharged inhabitation obligation
cases.lean: opaque, Lean.OpaqueVal, the `Inhabited`/`Nonempty` side condition
cases.target: Context::add_declaration(name, ty)   (the witness is *not* emitted)
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:434-436 (`add_declaration` — type only, opaque, no body); kernel/src/context.rs:474-476 (`get_definition_body` is `None`, so `opaque` never delta-unfolds, matching Lean); kernel/src/context.rs:20-100 (no `OpaqueVal` analogue and no place to store the unused witness value)
guards: Catches translating `opaque` as `add_definition` with the *inhabitation witness* as the body. Lean's `opaque x : T := v` deliberately hides `v`: the value exists only to prove `T` non-empty, and unfolding to it is unsound with respect to the author's intent (this is precisely how Lean models `IO`, `unsafeCast` targets, and FFI constants). Emitting `add_definition(name, T, v)` makes `x` *definitionally equal* to the placeholder — so `x = v` becomes provable by `rfl` in LOGOS while it is unprovable in Lean. That is a term Lean rejects being accepted by LOGOS: a soundness-shaped divergence, not a cosmetic one.

Catches dropping the inhabitation obligation. `opaque` is safe in Lean *only* because Lean checked the witness. `add_declaration` checks nothing (context.rs:434-436 is a bare `HashMap::insert`), so an `opaque` whose type turns out to be empty becomes a plain inconsistent axiom. The translator must verify the witness in Lean before emitting, and must record the resulting assumption exactly as it records a real `axiom` (see T02-003).

Catches conflating `opaque` with `@[irreducible] def`. `@[irreducible]` still has a body Lean can be told to unfold; `opaque` has none. Both degrade to *different* LOGOS forms (definition vs declaration), so mapping them to the same thing loses a real distinction in one direction and is unsound in the other.
oracle: The emitted name is a *declaration* (not a definition); `get_definition_body` is `None`; no witness term appears anywhere in the emitted context; and the trust report lists the name among assumed constants.

cases.title: `partial def` — no termination proof, and LOGOS has no opaque-recursion escape
cases.lean: partial def, the compiler-only implementation + `Inhabited`-backed opaque constant
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:321-343 (`Term::Fix` typing calls `crate::termination::check_termination` unconditionally — "THE GUARDIAN"); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:349-377 (same for `MutualFix` via `check_termination_mutual`); kernel/src/termination.rs:1-14,21-44 (the guard is a purely syntactic Giménez/Coq structural check over a match-bound smaller variable — there is no measure, no well-founded relation, no `Acc`-driven escape); kernel/src/context.rs:434-436 (`add_declaration` gives a type with no body, so the defining equations are gone)
guards: Catches the tempting fallback: emit `partial def loop : Nat → Nat` as `add_declaration("loop", Nat → Nat)`. It compiles, every call site typechecks, and the function is now an **uninterpreted constant** — `loop 0` is stuck, no equation holds, and any Lean theorem about `loop` that was proved by `unfold`/`simp` on its equations becomes either unprovable or, if the translator also emitted the equations as axioms, an assumed-consistent recursive equation. `partial`'s whole point in Lean is that its logical content is *exactly* "there is some inhabitant of this type"; re-asserting the equations is unsound in general.

Catches the other fallback: emit the recursive body as a `Term::Fix`. The guard refuses it — which is the correct outcome — but a translator that then *retries* through an unchecked path has done real damage. Note that `add_definition` performs no typecheck at all (context.rs:442-444), so a `Fix` body can be parked in the context without ever passing `check_termination`; it only fails later, when someone happens to `infer_type` it. A translator must reject at emit time, not rely on the kernel to notice.

Catches translating `partial` as `Acc`-based well-founded recursion. LOGOS's prelude registers `Acc`/`Acc_intro` (prelude.rs:1379), but the termination guard is purely structural: recursion *through* an accessibility proof is not a structural descent and is refused. See T04-015.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_PARTIAL_DEF_UNREPRESENTABLE and writes **no** declaration — neither a definition nor a declaration — for the partial function.
diag: E_PARTIAL_DEF_UNREPRESENTABLE — must name the declaration, state that its recursion is unjustified, and state that LOGOS's only recursion forms (`Term::Fix`, `Term::MutualFix`) are gated by the syntactic structural guard. Must NOT fall back to `add_declaration` (that turns the function into an axiom with no defining equations, silently) and must NOT fall back to `add_definition` with the recursive body (that is rejected by the guard, or worse, accepted by an unchecked path).

cases.title: `unsafe def` — outside the logic; there is nothing to translate it *into*
cases.lean: unsafe def, unsafeCast, `implemented_by`, the unsafe/safe declaration split
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:20-100 (the entire `Context`: `inductives`, `constructors`, `declarations`, `definitions`, … — there is no unsafe/compiler-only compartment and no `implemented_by` table, so an unsafe declaration has nowhere to live except the *trusted* maps); kernel/src/context.rs:434-436 and :442-444 (`add_declaration` and `add_definition` both feed `get_global`, context.rs:449-464, which the type checker consults with no notion of trust level); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:321-343 (every `Fix` is termination-checked — there is no unchecked recursion form to park an unsafe function in)
guards: Catches the "it's just an axiom" fallback. Emitting `add_declaration` for an `unsafe def` promotes a declaration Lean *refused to admit to its own logic* into a LOGOS axiom the kernel will happily use. For `unsafeCast : α → β` that axiom is immediately inconsistent: it inhabits `Nat → False`.

Catches following `@[implemented_by]`. A safe declaration with an unsafe implementation has *two* bodies in Lean; only the safe one has logical content. A translator that reads the implementation (because it is the one that actually runs) emits the unchecked term. The rule is: translate the safe body, ignore the implementation, and record nothing about it.

Catches leaking an unsafe declaration through a *safe* one that mentions it. Lean enforces the safe/unsafe barrier at `addDecl`; LOGOS has no barrier, so if the translator emits the unsafe constant at all, any later safe declaration referencing it links up silently.
Catches degrading rather than rejecting. There is no loss record that makes this acceptable: the information lost is the *entire* soundness argument.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_UNSAFE_DECLARATION and the LOGOS context contains no entry (definition, declaration, inductive or constructor) for any `unsafe` name.
diag: E_UNSAFE_DECLARATION — must name the declaration and state that `unsafe` code is excluded from Lean's own logical environment (it is not checked for termination, not checked for type soundness across `unsafeCast`, and may not be referenced by safe declarations), so there is no property for LOGOS to preserve. Must produce no LOGOS output at all, including no axiom.

cases.title: `noncomputable` — an extraction marker with no LOGOS carrier
cases.lean: noncomputable def, noncomputable section, `Classical.choice`-dependent definitions
cases.target: Context::add_definition(name, ty, body)  + a loss record
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:442-444 (`add_definition` stores `(ty, body)` only — no computability flag, no compiler IR, no `@[extern]` table); kernel/src/context.rs:20-100 (the `Context` has no code-generation compartment at all); kernel/src/reduction.rs:52-69 (`normalize` unfolds any definition body it finds — it has no notion of a body that "must not be run"); kernel/src/prelude.rs:1195-1219 (`reduceBool`/`ofReduceBool` — the one place LOGOS wires an *evaluator* into kernel reduction, and the only place computability is load-bearing)
guards: Catches the translator *rejecting* `noncomputable` declarations. They are ordinary definitions logically; refusing them would drop most of a classical development for no soundness reason.

Catches the translator translating `noncomputable` to `add_declaration` (an axiom) "because it cannot be evaluated". That throws away a body Lean fully checked, and turns a theorem provable by unfolding into an assumption.

Catches the *real* hazard hiding behind this case: a `noncomputable` Lean definition is usually noncomputable because it uses `Classical.choice`, and **`Classical.choice` is absent from the LOGOS trusted base** (prelude.rs:78 declares `dne` as the only classical axiom; there is no `choice`, no `propext`, no `funext`). So the *body* of such a definition frequently does not translate at all — that is a `reject` under T06-009, not a degrade. A translator that sees `noncomputable`, emits the loss record, and moves on without inspecting the body for `Classical.choice` will emit a term mentioning an unregistered global, which `get_global` (context.rs:449-464) resolves to `None` and the checker reports as an unbound name far from the cause.
oracle: The emitted declaration is a definition with the same body; the loss report contains COMPUTABILITY_MARKER; and if the body mentions `Classical.choice` the translator instead reports the T06-009 rejection rather than the loss.
loss: COMPUTABILITY_MARKER. In Lean `noncomputable` records that the definition has no executable compiler implementation (typically because it goes through `Classical.choice`). It has **no** effect on the logic: the definitional content is identical. LOGOS keeps the definitional content and drops the marker.

EXTRACTION_VIABILITY. A LOGOS context assembled from a Lean development can no longer report which globals are runnable. That matters for exactly one LOGOS feature: `reduceBool` (prelude.rs:1195-1219) reduces by invoking the CBV evaluator (reduction.rs:109-115). A `reduceBool` applied to a term whose head unfolds into a noncomputable definition will not reduce, and the failure looks like a `decide` failure rather than a computability error.

cases.title: `instance` — a definition plus an entry in a flat, first-match-wins instance list
cases.lean: instance, Lean.Meta.InstanceExtension, instance priorities, discrimination trees
cases.target: Context::add_definition(name, ty, body)  followed by Context::add_instance(ty: Term, value: Term)
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:184-186 (`add_instance` pushes onto a flat `Arc<Vec<(Term, Term)>>` — no discrimination tree, no priority, no keying); kernel/src/context.rs:67-71 (documented: "each `(type, value)` is an instance the elaborator may resolve … Searched by unifying `type` against the required class type"); kernel/src/context.rs:210-213 (`instances()` hands the raw slice back, in insertion order); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1017-1027 (`ParamKind::Instance` — an instance-implicit argument is resolved only *after* the explicit arguments, so the class's type variables are pinned first)
guards: Catches emitting only the `add_definition` and forgetting `add_instance`. The instance then exists as an ordinary global that nothing will ever find: LOGOS has no attribute system to scan (see T02-013), so the *only* way an instance becomes resolvable is an explicit `add_instance` call. Every `[Foo α]` argument downstream then fails to synthesise, and the error names the *use site*, not the missing registration.

Catches the argument order. `add_instance(ty, value)` takes the **class type first** and the witness second (context.rs:184). Both are `Term`s, both are accepted without a check, and a swapped pair produces an instance database in which nothing ever unifies — search silently returns no match rather than erroring.

Catches ignoring insertion order. LOGOS instance resolution is **first match wins** over a `Vec` in registration order; Lean's is priority-ordered with a most-recently-declared tiebreak and backtracking. A translator that emits instances in source order reproduces Lean's *default* behaviour only when no priorities are used and no backtracking is needed. Any `instance (priority := …)` must be re-ordered into the `Vec` by hand, and any development relying on backtracking must be reported — see T07-008.

Catches emitting the instance as an *axiom*. A class method is a structure projection applied to the instance value (context.rs:310-362); with no body the method never reduces and `Add.add 1 2` is stuck.
oracle: The class type appears in `instances()` paired with a value whose `infer_type` is a subtype of it; an instance-implicit argument of that class resolves; and the emitted order of `instances()` matches Lean's resolution order for this module.

cases.title: Namespaces and hierarchical `Name` — LOGOS keys are flat `String`s
cases.lean: namespace, `Lean.Name` (`.str`/`.num`/`.anonymous`), `export`, `_root_`
cases.target: Context::add_definition / add_declaration / add_inductive under a *flattened* `String` key produced by a documented, injective mangling of `Lean.Name`
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:20-100 (every global map is `HashMap<String, …>`: `inductives`, `constructors`, `inductive_params`, `constructor_order`, `declarations`, `definitions`, `universe_polys`, `binder_kinds`, `implicit_args`, `structures`, `mutual_blocks` — there is no `Name` type anywhere in the kernel); kernel/src/context.rs:449-464 (`get_global` is a flat map lookup with a fixed precedence, not a namespace resolution); kernel/src/term.rs:452-458 (`Term::Global(String)` and `Term::Const { name: String, .. }` — the term language itself carries only flat strings); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1285 (dot notation is resolved by string concatenation, `format!("{hname}_{field}")`)
guards: Catches the obvious mangling `Foo.bar ⟼ "Foo_bar"`, which is **not injective**: a Lean declaration literally named `Foo_bar` maps to the same key, and `add_definition` is a bare `HashMap::insert` (context.rs:442-444) that overwrites without error. That collision is the `reject` case T02-020; this case exists to make the translator *choose* a mangling and declare it, so that the collision is detectable rather than accidental.

Catches a mangling that collides with LOGOS's own generated names. `add_structure` synthesises `{name}_mk` and `{name}_{field}` (context.rs:304,311), and the nested compiler synthesises `{elem}${container}`, `{repr}_to_{c}`, `{repr}_from_{c}` (inductive_compile.rs:214-216). A Lean `Point.mk`, `Point.x`, or `RTree_to_TList` lands on top of them.

Catches assuming the LOGOS prelude's namespace is free. The prelude already occupies `Nat`, `Zero`, `Succ`, `Bool`, `true`, `false`, `Eq`, `refl`, `And`, `Or`, `Ex`, `True`, `I`, `False`, `Acc`, `Decidable`, `Int`, `Text`, `EList`, `TList`, `Quot`, … (prelude.rs:533-1460). A Lean `Nat` from a different development silently *overwrites* the prelude's `Nat` — including the `Literal::Nat` ↔ `Succ`/`Zero` bridge that `extract_constructor` (reduction.rs:330-345) hard-codes by name.
Catches dropping the mapping table. The loss record must include the full `Lean.Name → String` map, or nothing downstream can interpret a LOGOS error message.
oracle: The emitted `Lean.Name → String` mangling is injective over the module's declarations, disjoint from the prelude's names and from every LOGOS-generated name shape; and the loss report contains NAME_STRUCTURE with that table.
loss: NAME_STRUCTURE. The hierarchical shape of `Lean.Name` is destroyed. After flattening there is no way to ask "which declarations are in namespace `Foo`", no `open`, no `export`, no `_root_` escape, and no per-namespace resolution — every name is global and absolute.

NUMERIC_AND_HYGIENIC_COMPONENTS. `Name.num` components (macro scopes, hygiene markers, `_@._hyg.123`) have no textual counterpart that is guaranteed round-trippable. The mangling must be documented and injective, or two hygienically distinct Lean names collapse.

cases.title: `private` / `protected` / `scoped` / `local` — LOGOS has no visibility at all
cases.lean: private def, protected def, scoped instance, local instance, local notation
cases.target: Context::add_definition / add_declaration / add_instance with no visibility qualifier  + a loss record
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:20-100 (the `Context` carries no visibility, no module boundary, no scope stack — the global maps are flat and permanently open); kernel/src/context.rs:449-464 (`get_global` has one resolution path for everyone); kernel/src/context.rs:184-186 (`add_instance` pushes to a single global `Vec`; there is no scoped-instance compartment to pop); kernel/src/context.rs:442-444 (`add_definition` is a bare `HashMap::insert`, so a "private" name occupies the same key space as a public one)
guards: Catches the highest-consequence version of this: a `local instance` deliberately installed for one section — a common Lean idiom for temporarily overriding a default — becomes a **permanent, high-priority** LOGOS instance. Because resolution is first match wins over insertion order (context.rs:67-71, :210-213), that override now silently wins for the rest of the development, changing which method body every later `[Class α]` argument resolves to. Nothing errors; the proofs just talk about a different structure.

Catches `private` name mangling. Lean's private names carry a module-hash component (`_private.Module.0.Foo.bar`). A mangling that *drops* the private prefix makes two private declarations of the same short name in two modules collide (T02-020); a mangling that keeps it produces a LOGOS key containing `.` and digits that no human can match to a source declaration. Either way the choice must be documented in the loss record.

Catches assuming `protected` is inert. It is inert *logically*, but it changes which short name resolves at a use site in Lean; translation must read the resolved `Name` from the elaborated term, never re-resolve a short name.
oracle: Every visibility-qualified declaration is emitted; the loss report lists each with VISIBILITY, and every `local`/`scoped` instance additionally with SCOPE_LIFETIME and its position in the emitted instance `Vec`.
loss: VISIBILITY. `private`, `protected`, `scoped` and `local` all erase to "unconditionally visible, forever". Nothing downstream can reconstruct the intended interface of a translated module.

SCOPE_LIFETIME. `local instance` and `scoped instance` are *supposed* to leave the instance database when their section/namespace closes. `add_instance` has no removal API (context.rs:184-186 is push-only), so a local instance registered during translation is permanently in the flat `Vec` that resolution walks first-match-wins.

cases.title: `@[simp]`, `@[ext]` and attributes generally — LOGOS has no attribute system
cases.lean: @[simp], @[ext], @[instance], @[inline], attribute … , Lean environment extensions
