cases.target: Context::add_definition(name, ty, body)  + a loss record; for the *effects* that matter, an explicit re-encoding — `Context::add_instance` for `@[instance]`, `Context::add_hint` for a lemma intended to drive `auto`
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:20-100 (the `Context` has no attribute map; the only attribute-shaped surfaces are the purpose-built `instances`, `coercions`, `binder_kinds`, `implicit_args` and `hints` fields, each written by its own dedicated API); kernel/src/context.rs:658-674 (`add_hint`/`get_hints`/`is_hint` — the *entire* extensible-lemma-database surface LOGOS has, a `Vec<String>` for the `auto` tactic); kernel/src/simp.rs (the simplifier is a fixed set of built-in rules, not an attribute-populated rewrite set — there is no `simp` lemma registry to add to); kernel/src/context.rs:184-186 (`add_instance` — the only way an `@[instance]` attribute's effect can be reproduced)
guards: Catches translating `@[simp] theorem foo` by emitting the theorem and assuming downstream `simp` will find it. It will not: there is no registry. A translator that also rewrites Lean `by simp` proofs into LOGOS `simp` produces scripts that fail with an unhelpful "no progress" rather than a missing-lemma error.

Catches silently dropping `@[instance]`. `instance` the *command* and `@[instance]` the *attribute applied later* have the same effect in Lean. A translator that only handles the command form emits the second as a plain definition, and every downstream instance-implicit argument fails to synthesise (see T02-010).

Catches translating `@[ext]` as if it produced logical content. `@[ext]` generates a *lemma* (`Foo.ext`) — that generated declaration is what must be translated, if anything; the attribute itself is inert. The same rule as `deriving` (T02-017): translate the handler's *output*, never the clause.

Catches using `add_hint` as a general attribute dumping ground. `add_hint` feeds exactly one consumer — the `auto` tactic's fallback (context.rs:654-657) — and entries are tried in insertion order. Registering a large Lean simp set as hints changes `auto`'s search space and its termination behaviour.
oracle: Every attributed declaration is emitted; the loss report lists each attribute by name with ATTRIBUTE_SYSTEM; `@[instance]` additionally produces an `add_instance` call; and no emitted LOGOS tactic script relies on a lemma that was only reachable through a Lean attribute.
loss: ATTRIBUTE_SYSTEM. Every attribute is erased. Nothing in the emitted LOGOS context records that a lemma was `@[simp]`, that a structure had `@[ext]`, or that a definition was `@[inline]`.

SIMP_SET. The single most consequential erasure. In Lean a large fraction of proofs are `by simp`, and they close *because* of the ambient simp set. LOGOS's script-level `simp` takes **no lemma-list argument at all** (it is arity-0) and rewrites with a fixed built-in rule set, so there is no target to translate the simp set into. Any Lean proof whose term was produced by `simp` must be translated as its *elaborated proof term*, never as the tactic.

cases.title: `mutual def` block — one `Term::MutualFix`, projected once per member
cases.lean: mutual … end over `def`s, Lean's `WellFounded`/structural mutual compilation
cases.target: Term::MutualFix { defs: Vec<(String, Term)>, index: usize }, registered with one Context::add_definition per member, each at its own `index`
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`MutualFix { defs, index }` is a *term*, not a declaration form — the whole block is one term and each member is a projection of it); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:349-377 (typing a `MutualFix` infers every member's type structurally, runs `termination::check_termination_mutual`, then re-checks each body with *all* siblings in scope, and returns `types[index]`); kernel/src/termination.rs:21-44 (`GuardContext.fix_positions` maps every member of the block to its structural argument position — "a call to ANY member must decrease")
guards: Catches emitting each member as its own single `Term::Fix`. The sibling call is then a free `Var`/`Global` that either does not resolve or resolves to a *separately* declared fixpoint; in the latter case `check_termination` (which is single-block, type_checker.rs:321-343) sees the sibling call as a call to an unrelated function and imposes no descent requirement on it. Two mutually recursive functions each "structurally recursive" on nothing at all then pass the guard, and the pair diverges — the classic way to admit a non-terminating definition into a kernel.

Catches getting `index` wrong. `MutualFix { defs, index }` returns `types[index]` (type_checker.rs:376). All members are typed and all bodies are checked regardless, so an off-by-one in `index` produces a term that **typechecks fine** and simply denotes the wrong function. Registering `isEven` with the body of `isOdd` is a silent, total semantic inversion that no kernel check will catch.

Catches re-building the block per member. Emitting N separate `MutualFix` terms that differ only in `index` is correct but quadratic: `infer_type` on a `MutualFix` types *and* re-checks every body (type_checker.rs:356-374), so an N-member block costs O(N²) body checks, on top of `substitute`'s O(size)-per-binder cost (type_checker.rs:1088). The block should be built once and shared.

Catches assuming Lean's mutual block shape survives. Lean may compile a `mutual` block by structural recursion, by well-founded recursion, or by packing the arguments into a sum type. Only the *structural* compilation has a LOGOS counterpart; the others are T04-004/T04-015 rejections. The translator must read how Lean actually compiled the block, not the surface `mutual` keyword.
oracle: One `MutualFix` term with `defs.len()` equal to the block size; each member is registered with a distinct, correct `index`; `infer_type` succeeds (so `check_termination_mutual` passed); and each member's inferred type matches the translation of Lean's type for that member.

cases.title: `where` clauses — auxiliary declarations that must be lifted, not inlined
cases.lean: def … where, Lean's `mkAuxDefinition` lifting of `where` bodies
cases.target: one Context::add_definition per lifted auxiliary (its own flat name, closed over the parent's binders as explicit leading parameters), plus the parent definition referring to it by `Term::Global`
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:442-444 (`add_definition` is flat and unnamespaced: a lifted auxiliary needs its own top-level `String` key); kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term::Let { name, ty, value, body }` exists, so a *non-recursive* `where` body may alternatively stay local — but `Let` has no `Fix`, so a recursive one cannot); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:321-343 (a recursive auxiliary must become `Term::Fix`, which is termination-checked); kernel/src/context.rs:449-464 (`get_global` is a flat lookup — a lifted `Foo.go` and a user's `Foo_go` are the same key, see T02-020)
guards: Catches inlining the `where` body at each call site instead of lifting it. For a *recursive* `where` that is not merely wasteful, it is impossible: the body refers to itself, so inlining does not terminate. For a non-recursive one used k times it multiplies term size by k, and LOGOS's `normalize` has a hard fuel of 10000 steps that **silently returns a partially-reduced term** when exhausted (reduction.rs:52-69) — so the inlined version can fail a conversion check the lifted version passes, reported as an unrelated type mismatch.

Catches forgetting that Lean's `where` auxiliaries capture the parent's binders. Lean lifts `go` in `def f (n : Nat) … where go := … n …` to a top-level `f.go : Nat → …` with `n` as a *leading parameter*. A translator that emits `go` without that parameter leaves a dangling `Term::Var("n")` in the body. Because `add_definition` performs no typecheck (context.rs:442-444) the broken definition is accepted, and the dangling `Var` only fails when something eventually normalizes through it — at which point the error names `n`, not the `where`.

Catches the name of the lifted auxiliary. Lean names it `f.go`; flattened that is `f_go`, which collides with any user declaration `f_go`. The lifting scheme must go through the same injective mangling as every other name (T02-011).
Catches choosing `Term::Let` for a *recursive* `where`. `Let` is zeta-transparent and has no fixpoint; recursion must be `Fix`, and `Fix` must pass the structural guard.
oracle: Each `where` auxiliary appears as its own LOGOS definition whose type is the parent's captured telescope followed by the auxiliary's own; the parent's body mentions it as a `Global` and contains no residual free `Var` from the parent's binders; and no auxiliary body is duplicated.

cases.title: `let rec` — a local fixpoint; `Term::Let` cannot carry the recursion
cases.lean: let rec (term and tactic position), Lean's `letRec` lifting to an auxiliary
cases.target: Term::Fix { name, body }, bound by Term::Let or lifted to its own Context::add_definition
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Let { name, ty, value, body }` has **no** recursive scope — `value` is checked in the ambient context, so `name` is not in scope inside it; the only recursive forms are `Fix` and `MutualFix`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:321-343 (`Fix` typing runs `termination::check_termination` — "THE GUARDIAN" — then re-checks the body with the fixpoint name bound to its structurally-inferred type); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:349-377 (`MutualFix` — the *only* other recursive form, and the one a fused or split translation would wrongly reach for); kernel/src/termination.rs:48-62 (`check_termination` extracts the structural parameter from the body and requires every recursive call to descend)
guards: Catches emitting `let rec f := body in e` as `Term::Let { name: "f", value: body, … }`. LOGOS's `Let` is **not** recursive: the occurrence of `f` inside `body` is a free `Var("f")` that does not resolve to the binding. Worse, if the surrounding term has *another* binder named `f`, the named representation lets the free occurrence be captured by it (`substitute_avoiding`, type_checker.rs:1088, only alpha-renames when the *replacement's* free variables collide). The result typechecks and computes something else entirely.

Catches assuming `let rec` is always liftable to a top-level definition. It is, but only after closing over the enclosing binders — exactly the capture obligation of T02-015. A lifted body that still mentions the parent's `Var`s is accepted by `add_definition` without any check (context.rs:442-444).

Catches flattening *nested* `let rec`s into one block. Two independent local fixpoints are two `Fix` terms, one inside the other's body; fusing them into a `MutualFix` changes what the termination guard requires, because `check_termination_mutual` demands that a call to **any** member descend (termination.rs:21-44) — a fusion can therefore be rejected where the honest nesting is accepted, and, in the other direction, a translator that splits a genuinely mutual pair into two `Fix`es escapes the descent requirement entirely (see T02-014).

Catches the zeta-transparency difference. `Term::Let` is transparent (it zeta-reduces during `normalize`), so a `let rec` lifted into a `Let`-bound `Fix` will be unfolded at every use; Lean's `let rec` is lifted to an auxiliary *definition* and stays folded. Both are sound; only one keeps term size linear under the 10000-step fuel (reduction.rs:52-69).
oracle: The emitted term contains one `Fix` per `let rec`, each of whose `infer_type` succeeds — meaning the structural guard passed — and whose body has no free variable escaping into the enclosing term; the result type matches the translation of Lean's inferred type.
note: Lean 4's `let rec` has no mutual (`and`) form — two sibling `let rec`s cannot see each other — so the `MutualFix` obligation for *local* recursion is exercised through `where` in T02-015 and through `mutual def` in T02-014. This file therefore tests the single-`Fix` path plus nesting.

cases.title: `deriving Repr, BEq, …` — translate the handler's *output*, never the clause
cases.lean: deriving, deriving instance, `Lean.Elab.Deriving` handlers (Repr, BEq, Hashable, Inhabited, DecidableEq, Ord, ToString)
cases.target: for each generated declaration: Context::add_definition for the instance body plus Context::add_instance for the class registration; and a loss record for every class whose generated body is not translatable
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:20-100 (no `deriving` mechanism, no derive-handler registry, and no environment extension to hook one into); kernel/src/context.rs:184-186 (`add_instance` — the only registration path for the generated instances); kernel/src/prelude.rs:34-35,923-1186 (the *only* decidable-equality artefacts in LOGOS are two hand-written definitions, `decEqBool` and `decEqNat`; there is no generic `DecidableEq` derivation — see T03-023); kernel/src/term.rs:13-44 (`Literal` has `Text(String)`, but LOGOS has **no string operations at all**, so a derived `Repr`/`ToString` body has no target — see T10-016)
guards: Catches translating the `deriving` *clause* — e.g. emitting some LOGOS marker that says "this type has BEq". There is no such marker. The only thing that exists after translation is whatever declarations Lean's handler actually produced, and those are ordinary definitions. The translator must read the post-elaboration environment.

Catches emitting the derived instance as a *definition* only, without the matching `add_instance`. The instance then exists but is unreachable by resolution, so every `[BEq α]` argument downstream fails to synthesise (T02-010).

Catches silently approximating `DecidableEq`. A derived `DecidableEq Foo` for a user inductive has a real, structural body that Lean generated; LOGOS has only `decEqBool` and `decEqNat` and no way to synthesise the rest. Mapping a derived `DecidableEq Foo` onto `decEqNat` because the fields happen to be `Nat` produces an instance that decides the wrong equality — it compares one field and ignores the constructor tag. See T03-023.
Catches translating the derived instance's *equations* as axioms when the body does not translate. That converts an unimplementable instance into an assumed one.
oracle: Every declaration Lean's derive handlers added to the environment is either translated (definition + `add_instance`) or reported in the loss record by name and class; the `deriving` clause produces no LOGOS artefact of its own; and no derived instance is mapped onto a prelude definition for a different type.
loss: DERIVE_CLAUSE. The `deriving` clause itself vanishes. Nothing in the LOGOS context records that an instance was generated rather than written, so a later re-derivation cannot be distinguished from a user instance.

UNTRANSLATABLE_HANDLERS. `Repr`, `ToString` and `Hashable` generate bodies over `Std.Format`/`String`/`UInt64`, none of which exist in LOGOS (`String` operations, `UInt*` and `Char` are all absent). Those derived instances must be dropped with a loss record, not approximated.

cases.title: `section` + `variable` — binders are inserted by Lean before the translator sees anything
cases.lean: section … end, variable, variable [inst], autoBound section variables
cases.target: Context::add_definition with the *closed* type and body Lean produced, plus Context::set_binder_kinds recording where the inserted binders are implicit or instance-implicit
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:20-100 (the `Context` has no section stack and no ambient binder list — every registered type is closed); kernel/src/context.rs:199-208 (`set_binder_kinds` / `binder_kinds` — the only carrier for implicit/explicit/instance positions); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1017-1027 (`ParamKind::{Explicit, Implicit, Instance}`; instance positions are resolved *after* the explicit arguments, so their position matters); kernel/src/context.rs:82-86 (`implicit_args` — the legacy "N leading implicits" model that `binder_kinds` supersedes; using it for an interleaved telescope is wrong)
guards: Catches translating the *surface* declaration instead of the elaborated one. `def f : Nat := n` inside `variable (n : Nat)` elaborates to `f : Nat → Nat`. A translator reading syntax emits a body with a free `Var("n")`; `add_definition` accepts it without any check (context.rs:442-444), so the dangling variable is discovered only when something normalizes through `f`, and the error names `n`.

Catches getting the *order* of inserted binders wrong. Lean inserts section variables in declaration order, but only those actually used (and their dependencies). A translator that inserts all section variables, or inserts them in source order regardless of dependency, produces a type with the right binders in the wrong positions. Since LOGOS is cumulative and `is_subtype` is structural on `Pi` telescopes (type_checker.rs:1330-1360), a permuted telescope of same-sorted binders can still typecheck at every call site while meaning something different.

Catches dropping `set_binder_kinds`. A `variable {α : Type}` becomes an *implicit* leading binder; if the translator records nothing, LOGOS falls back to the `implicit_args` count model (context.rs:82-86) which assumes implicits are all *leading*. An interleaved telescope (`{α} (n) [Inst α]`) is then mis-modelled and every application inserts the wrong number of metavariables.

Catches `variable [Inst α]`. The inserted binder is `ParamKind::Instance`, and LOGOS resolves instance positions only after the explicit arguments (elaborate.rs:1017-1027). Recording it as `Implicit` makes resolution fire before `α` is pinned, and the flat first-match instance search (context.rs:184-186) then picks whatever entry unifies with an unsolved metavariable — i.e. the first one.
oracle: Each declaration's emitted type is closed (no free `Var`), equals the translation of Lean's `ConstantInfo.type`, and `binder_kinds(name)` matches Lean's `BinderInfo` sequence position for position.

cases.title: `open … in` — name resolution completes before translation begins
cases.lean: open, open … in, open scoped, `Lean.Elab.OpenDecl`, ambiguous-name resolution
cases.target: the resolved `Term::Global(<flattened canonical name>)` — `open` itself emits nothing
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:452-458 (`Term::Global(String)` and `Term::Const { name, .. }` carry a single flat, absolute name — there is no relative or scope-dependent reference form); kernel/src/context.rs:449-464 (`get_global` is a plain map lookup: the name in the term must already be the key); kernel/src/context.rs:20-100 (no open-namespace stack, no alias table, no `export` map); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1285 (even *dot notation* is resolved by string concatenation against the receiver's type head, not by scope)
guards: Catches emitting the *short* name that appeared in the source. `open Foo in def g := bar` must emit `Global("Foo_bar")`, not `Global("bar")`. Because `add_definition` does not typecheck (context.rs:442-444), a term carrying the unresolved short name is registered happily, and `get_global("bar")` returns `None` only when something later normalizes through it.

Catches the far worse version of the same bug: the short name *does* resolve, to something else. LOGOS's global namespace is flat and already populated by the prelude (`Nat`, `Bool`, `true`, `false`, `Eq`, `refl`, `And`, `Or`, `Ex`, `True`, `False`, `Acc`, `Decidable`, `Int`, `TList`, `Quot`, …, prelude.rs:533-1460). A source that writes `succ` under `open Nat` and is translated as `Global("succ")` silently binds to the **prelude's** `Succ`-adjacent names rather than to the Lean declaration it meant. Nothing errors; the proof is simply about a different constant.

Catches re-resolving names at translation time. Lean's resolution is order- and scope-sensitive and can be *ambiguous* (two opens providing the same short name, disambiguated by elaboration or by an explicit prefix). A translator must read the already-resolved `Expr.const` from the elaborated term and must never re-run resolution against its own model of the namespaces.

Catches treating `open` as a declaration. It produces no environment entry, so it must produce no LOGOS registration — in particular no alias definition `add_definition("bar", ty, Global("Foo_bar"))`, which would create a *second* delta-transparent name for the same thing and double the surface for T02-020 collisions.

Catches `open scoped`. It brings scoped notation and scoped instances into view; the notation is expanded before translation (T09-001), but a scoped *instance* becoming visible changes which instance an obligation resolves to — and LOGOS's instance list is global and permanent (T02-012).
oracle: No LOGOS registration corresponds to any `open` command; every emitted `Global`/ `Const` name is the flattened *canonical* Lean name of the constant the elaborated term refers to; and the emitted term is unchanged if the source's `open`s are rewritten to fully qualified names.

cases.title: Flat-name collision — `Foo.bar` and `Foo_bar` become the same LOGOS key
cases.lean: hierarchical `Lean.Name`, namespaces, auto-generated names (`.mk`, `.rec`, field projections, `where` auxiliaries, derive handlers)
cases.target: (none — no sound translation for the colliding pair)
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:20-100 (every global map is `HashMap<String, …>`; there is no `Name` type, no namespace component, no visibility, nothing to distinguish two Lean names that flatten alike); kernel/src/context.rs:442-444 (`add_definition` is `Arc::make_mut(&mut self.definitions).insert(name, (ty, body))` — a plain `HashMap::insert`, so a second registration under the same key **silently returns the old value and discards it**; no error, no warning); the same is true of `add_inductive` (:253-255), `add_constructor` (:419-428), `add_declaration` (:434-436) and `set_inductive_params` (:380-382); kernel/src/context.rs:449-464 (`get_global` precedence — inductives → constructors → definitions → declarations); kernel/src/reduction.rs:304-313 (delta reduction reads `get_definition_body`, i.e. the `definitions` map **directly**, bypassing that precedence); kernel/src/context.rs:304,311 (`add_structure` synthesises `{name}_mk` and `{name}_{field}`); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1285 (dot notation is resolved by `format!("{hname}_{field}")`); kernel/src/inductive_compile.rs:211-216 (the nested compiler synthesises `{elem}${container}`, `{repr}_to_{c}`, `{repr}_from_{c}`)
guards: The same-map case: two Lean definitions, `Foo.bar` and `Foo_bar`, both key to `"Foo_bar"`. The second `add_definition` **overwrites** the first. Every term the translator already emitted that refers to the first now refers to the second, silently, with a type that may well still check — LOGOS is cumulative (type_checker.rs:1330-1360), so a `Nat`-valued global replaced by another `Nat`-valued global is completely invisible to the kernel. This is the canonical way a translated proof library ends up proving a *different theorem* than the source.

The cross-map case, which is strictly worse. A Lean **inductive** `Foo_bar` and a Lean **definition** `Foo.bar` do not overwrite each other — they land in *different* maps. `get_global("Foo_bar")` then returns the **inductive's** sort (inductives are checked first, context.rs:449-453), while `normalize(Global("Foo_bar"))` unfolds to the **definition's** body (reduction.rs:304-313 reads `definitions` directly). The kernel's typing and its reduction now disagree about what one name means. Nothing reports an error; conversion checks simply start succeeding or failing for reasons that have no relation to the source.

The generated-name case. LOGOS generates `Point_mk` and `Point_x` for a structure (context.rs:304,311), and `elaborate_dot` *resolves* `p.x` by building that exact string (elaborate.rs:1285). A Lean declaration literally named `Point_x` therefore does not merely collide — it becomes what every `p.x` in the translated development resolves to. Likewise `Point.mk` (Lean's own constructor) and a user's `Point_mk`.

The prelude case. The LOGOS prelude already owns `Nat`, `Zero`, `Succ`, `Bool`, `true`, `false`, `Eq`, `refl`, `And`, `Or`, `Ex`, `True`, `I`, `False`, `Acc`, `Decidable`, `Int`, `Text`, `EList`, `TList`, `Quot`, `dne`, `add`, `le`, … (prelude.rs:78-1460). A Lean declaration flattening onto any of them overwrites a *trusted base* entry. Overwriting `Nat` in particular breaks the hard-coded `Literal::Nat` ↔ `Succ`/`Zero` bridge (reduction.rs:330-345, type_checker.rs:1480-1493), which is keyed by those literal strings.

Catches "detect collisions by checking `get_global` before inserting". That check is necessary but not sufficient: it misses a collision against a name the translator has not emitted *yet*, and it misses the cross-map case for `set_inductive_params`, `set_binder_kinds`, `register_struct_info` and `constructor_order`, each of which is its own map with its own silent `insert`. Collision detection must be a whole-module pre-pass over the mangled key space, including every LOGOS-generated name shape and the prelude's names.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_FLAT_NAME_COLLISION naming both Lean declarations and the shared key, and the LOGOS context receives **no** registration from this module. In particular, running the translator twice must not produce a context in which some name's `get_global` type and `get_definition_body` body come from different Lean declarations.
diag: E_FLAT_NAME_COLLISION — must name **both** Lean declarations, the single `String` key they map to, and which LOGOS map(s) each would land in. Must emit no registration for either. A rename is *not* an acceptable automatic repair: the chosen key is part of the translator's public contract (every downstream LOGOS term, error message and certificate refers to it), so the collision has to be surfaced to a human.

cases.title: Simple enum inductive — registration order *is* the match order
cases.lean: inductive with nullary constructors, `Lean.InductiveVal`, `casesOn`
cases.target: Context::add_inductive(name, Sort(Type 0)) followed by one Context::add_constructor_checked(ctor, name, Global(name)) per constructor, in Lean's declaration order
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:253-255 (`add_inductive` records `name -> sort`; it is **unchecked** — a bare `HashMap::insert`); kernel/src/context.rs:419-428 (`add_constructor` appends to `constructor_order`, "HashMap doesn't preserve insertion order, so we track it explicitly"); kernel/src/context.rs:498-515 (`get_constructors` returns them *in registration order*); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:253-266 (a `Match` must supply exactly `constructors.len()` cases, and case *i* is checked against constructor *i* of that order — matching is **positional**, there are no patterns and no tags); kernel/src/context.rs:545-560 (`add_constructor_checked` = positivity + `check_constructor_universes`, the only checked registration path)
guards: Catches registering constructors in any order other than Lean's. LOGOS `Match` has **no patterns**: `cases[i]` is the branch for `get_constructors(ind)[i]`. Permuting two nullary constructors of the same inductive produces a `Match` that typechecks perfectly — all the branches have the same type — and computes the wrong answer for every input. This is the cheapest possible catastrophic mistranslation, and the kernel cannot detect it in principle.

Catches using `add_inductive` + `add_constructor` (both **unchecked**, context.rs:253,419) instead of `add_constructor_checked` (context.rs:545). For a simple enum the checks happen to pass, so the difference is invisible *here* — which is exactly why the habit must be established here rather than at T03-015, where the unchecked path admits a paradox.

Catches emitting the wrong sort. Lean's `inductive Colour where | red | green` lives in `Type 0`; a translator that writes `Sort(Prop)` because the type has no fields makes it a proposition, and LOGOS's large-elimination gate (type_checker.rs:277-290) then refuses to let any `Match` on it return a `Type` value — an error at the *use* site, far from the declaration.

Catches inventing `Colour.rec`. LOGOS does **not** create a recursor at declaration time; `recursor::derive_recursor` (recursor.rs:36) synthesises one and the caller must `add_definition` it. If the Lean source mentions `Colour.rec` (or `casesOn`), that global does not exist until the translator asks for it. See T03-021.
oracle: `get_constructors(name)` returns exactly Lean's constructor names in Lean's order; the inductive's sort is `Type 0`; a `Match` whose `cases` are built in that order reduces on each constructor to the intended branch.

cases.title: Recursive inductive (`Nat`-like) — and the prelude's hard-coded literal bridge
cases.lean: inductive with a recursive constructor argument, `Nat.zero`/`Nat.succ`, numeric literals via `OfNat`
cases.target: Context::add_inductive(name, Sort(Type 0)) plus Context::add_constructor_checked for each constructor, the recursive one typed `Pi { param_type: Global(name), body_type: Global(name) }`
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:545-560 (`add_constructor_checked` runs `positivity::check_positivity`, which permits an occurrence of the inductive to the right of every arrow — positivity.rs:60-80); kernel/src/prelude.rs:533-541 (the prelude registers `Nat` with constructors `Zero` and `Succ`, **by those exact strings**); kernel/src/reduction.rs:330-345 (`extract_constructor` bridges `Literal::Nat(n)` to `Succ`/`Zero` by name, so a numeral is *definitionally* `Succ^n Zero`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1480-1493 (the same bridge inside `def_eq_normalized`); kernel/src/termination.rs:1-14 (the structural guard's notion of "smaller" is a match-bound argument of the scrutinee — the reason recursion on this shape is accepted)
guards: Catches translating a Lean `Nat` — or any user inductive that flattens to the key `"Nat"`, `"Zero"` or `"Succ"` — as a fresh registration. Those three strings are load-bearing in the LOGOS kernel: the numeral/Peano bridge is keyed on them literally (reduction.rs:330-345). Re-registering `Nat` with different constructors, or in a different order, silently changes what every `Literal::Nat` in the context means, including inside the prelude's own `decEqNat` (prelude.rs:1027-1186). The translator must map Lean's `Nat` onto the *existing* prelude inductive and must refuse to overwrite it (see T02-020).

Catches the opposite error: mapping a user's own Peano-shaped inductive onto the prelude's `Nat` because it "looks the same". The user type has no literal bridge, no `decEqNat`, and is a genuinely different type in the Lean source; identifying them makes `MyNat`-typed and `Nat`-typed terms interchangeable, which they are not.

Catches getting the recursive constructor's type shape wrong. `Succ`'s LOGOS type must be `Pi { param: "_", param_type: Global("Nat"), body_type: Global("Nat") }`. Writing the domain as anything else — say a `Var` left over from a parameter telescope — is accepted by `add_constructor` (context.rs:419-428, unchecked) and by `add_constructor_checked` only if positivity happens to pass, and then breaks the termination guard, which identifies smaller variables by the *inductive type name* of the structural parameter (termination.rs:33-37).

Catches constructor order once more, but with consequences: `Match` is positional (type_checker.rs:253-266), and here the two branches have *different* shapes (one takes a predecessor argument, one does not), so a swapped order produces a case type mismatch — a loud failure rather than a silent one. That asymmetry is worth pinning: enums fail silently (T03-001), recursive types usually fail loudly.
oracle: `get_constructors` matches Lean's order; the recursive constructor's registered type has the inductive itself as its domain; structural recursion over the type typechecks (so `check_termination` accepted it); and no prelude name was overwritten.

cases.title: Parameterised inductive — the one shape where `add_inductive`'s default is right
cases.lean: inductive with uniform type parameters, `InductiveVal.numParams`, `numIndices = 0`
cases.target: Context::add_inductive(name, Pi{"α", Sort(Type 0), Sort(Type 0)}) — or, equivalently and preferably, Context::add_indexed_inductive(name, arity, num_params = arity) — plus Context::add_constructor_checked per constructor, each constructor's type carrying the parameter telescope explicitly
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:246-255 (`add_inductive`: "All of the arity is treated as uniform parameters (0 indices) unless `set_inductive_params` records a smaller parameter count"); kernel/src/context.rs:399-411 (`inductive_num_params` defaults to the full arity; `inductive_num_indices` is `arity − params`, hence 0); kernel/src/context.rs:384-389 (`inductive_arity` counts the leading `Π`s of the stored sort); kernel/src/recursor.rs:52-72 (`derive_recursor` splits the arity telescope at `num_params` and abstracts the recursor over the parameters); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:685-700 (`compute_indexed_case_type` instantiates a constructor's leading `num_params` from the *discriminant's* parameter arguments — the reason the split must be right)
guards: Catches omitting the parameter from the *constructor* types. LOGOS constructors carry their full type including the parameter telescope: `cons` is `Π(α:Type 0). α → MyList α → MyList α`, not `α → MyList α → MyList α`. A constructor registered without the leading `Π(α)` is accepted unchecked by `add_constructor` (context.rs:419-428), and then `compute_case_type` builds a case type whose binders do not line up with the discriminant's parameters — producing a `Match` that fails to typecheck with a message about the *branch*, not about the declaration.

Catches the universe. A `MyList (α : Type 0)` must be declared with sort `Π(α : Type 0). Type 0`. Lean's `List : Type u → Type u` is universe-polymorphic and has **no** LOGOS counterpart at all (T01-007); this case is deliberately restricted to the monomorphic `Type 0` instance, and a translator must not silently turn the polymorphic Lean declaration into this one.

Catches a *non-uniform* "parameter". Lean rejects a parameter that varies across constructors, demoting it to an index. LOGOS's `add_inductive` will happily register it as a parameter (it is unchecked), and `compute_indexed_case_type` will then instantiate it from the discriminant — meaning the constructor's own choice of that argument is discarded. That is the T03-005 rejection; this case pins the boundary from the safe side.

Catches forgetting `add_constructor_checked`'s universe test. A `Type 0` inductive may not store a `Type 0`-typed field (`check_constructor_universes`, type_checker.rs:545-580). `MyList` storing an `α : Type 0` *value* is fine; a constructor storing the *type* `α` itself is not — see T03-022.
oracle: `inductive_arity(name)` equals Lean's `numParams`, `inductive_num_indices(name)` is 0, every constructor's registered type begins with the parameter telescope, and a `Match` on a value of the type typechecks with the parameters supplied by the discriminant.

cases.title: Indexed family (`Vect`) — `num_params` must be declared, and what is still lost
cases.lean: inductive family with indices, `InductiveVal.numIndices`, dependent elimination
cases.target: Context::add_indexed_inductive(name, full_arity_sort, num_params)  — **not** `add_inductive` — plus Context::add_constructor_checked per constructor, each constructor's declared return type carrying its own index expressions
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:371-382 (`add_indexed_inductive(name, sort, num_params)`: "the first `num_params` leading arguments are uniform parameters and the rest are indices that vary per constructor"); kernel/src/context.rs:38-44 (the `inductive_params` map, "Absence means *all of the arity is parameters*"); kernel/src/context.rs:399-411 (`inductive_num_params` defaults to the full arity); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:602-678 (`infer_indexed_match`: the motive is `Π(indices…). Π(z : I params indices). Sort`, the result is the motive applied to the *discriminant's* index arguments, and coverage requires one case per constructor); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:631-638 (coverage is a bare count check — **no index unifier, no impossible-case elimination**); kernel/src/recursor.rs:59-71 (`derive_recursor`'s motive target is hard-coded to `Sort(Prop)` for a subsingleton `Prop` inductive and `Sort(Type 0)` otherwise); kernel/src/prelude.rs:1439 (`Eq` itself is registered this way, with `num_params = 2`)
guards: Catches calling `add_inductive` instead of `add_indexed_inductive`. That is the `reject` case T03-005 and it is *silent*: `inductive_num_params` then defaults to the full arity (context.rs:399-406), the length index is treated as a uniform parameter, and `compute_indexed_case_type` instantiates it from the discriminant — so `Vect.nil`'s declared index `0` and `Vect.cons`'s declared index `n+1` are both discarded and replaced by the scrutinee's. The family collapses into a *parameterised* type in which `nil : Vect α n` for every `n`.

Catches an off-by-one in `num_params`. For `Vect (α : Type) : Nat → Type` the answer is 1, not 0 and not 2. Passing 0 makes `α` an index, so every constructor's `α` is taken from the discriminant rather than being uniform, and `derive_recursor` (recursor.rs:72-73) builds a recursor with an empty parameter telescope.

Catches registering constructor types without their index expressions. `Vect.nil`'s registered type must literally end in `Vect α Zero` and `Vect.cons`'s in `Vect α (Succ n)`; `compute_indexed_case_type` reads those result indices off the declared type (type_checker.rs:685-700). A constructor declared to return `Vect α n` for a fresh `n` typechecks at registration (`add_constructor` is unchecked) and destroys the family.
oracle: `inductive_num_params(name)` equals Lean's `numParams` and `inductive_num_indices(name)` equals Lean's `numIndices`; each constructor's registered result type carries its own index expression; an indexed `Match` typechecks; and the loss report contains INDEX_UNIFICATION.
loss: INDEX_UNIFICATION. LOGOS's indexed `Match` does not unify the scrutinee's indices with each constructor's result indices. Every constructor needs a branch even when its indices provably cannot match — `Vect.cons` must be given a case in a match on a `Vect α 0`. Lean discharges those branches automatically; a LOGOS translation has to synthesise an inhabitant of an unreachable branch's type. See T03-019 and T04-014.

RECURSOR_MOTIVE_UNIVERSE. The derived recursor's motive targets `Type 0` (or `Prop` for subsingletons) and nothing else (recursor.rs:59-71). A Lean proof that eliminates an indexed family into `Type 1` — e.g. building a *type* by recursion on the index — has no derived recursor to use. Cumulativity (`Prop ≤ Type 0`, type_checker.rs:1330-1360) rescues the downward direction only.

INDEX_ARITHMETIC. Lean's `Vect α (n+1)` index is a `Nat` expression that the elaborator normalises during unification. LOGOS's indexed case type (`compute_indexed_case_type`, type_checker.rs:685-700) instantiates parameters from the discriminant and otherwise compares index terms up to `normalize`, whose fuel is 10000 and which silently returns partial results (reduction.rs:52-69). Index expressions that Lean reduces cheaply can therefore fail to line up.

cases.title: Params/indices misdeclaration — `add_inductive`'s default silently flattens a family
cases.lean: InductiveVal.numParams / numIndices, indexed inductive families
cases.target: (none — no sound translation via `add_inductive`; the *only* correct call is `add_indexed_inductive(name, sort, num_params)` with `num_params` equal to Lean's `numParams`, and a translator that cannot determine it must refuse)
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:246-255 (`add_inductive`'s doc: "All of the arity is treated as uniform parameters (0 indices) unless `set_inductive_params` records a smaller parameter count" — and the body is a bare `HashMap::insert`, **unchecked**); kernel/src/context.rs:38-44 (the `inductive_params` map; "Absence means *all of the arity is parameters* (0 indices) — so every non-indexed inductive behaves exactly as before this map existed"); kernel/src/context.rs:399-411 (`inductive_num_params` falls back to `inductive_arity`; `inductive_num_indices` is then 0); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:200-300 vs :602-678 (the **non-indexed** `Match` path is taken whenever `num_indices == 0`; the indexed path, with its motive-over-indices discipline, is never entered); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:685-714 (`compute_indexed_case_type`: a constructor's leading `num_params` arguments are instantiated from the **discriminant's** parameter arguments — so anything counted as a parameter has its constructor-declared value *discarded*); kernel/src/recursor.rs:52-73 (`derive_recursor` splits the arity at `num_params`; a wrong split yields a recursor with the wrong motive arity); kernel/src/reduction.rs (ι-reduction skips exactly `inductive_declared_params` arguments of a constructor, context.rs:391-397 — a wrong count skips the wrong arguments)
guards: **This is the central trap of the tier.** The natural translation of `inductive Vect (α : Type) : Nat → Type` is "register the arity `Π(α:Type 0). Nat → Type 0`", i.e. `add_inductive`. That call succeeds. It is also silently wrong: `inductive_num_params` now reports **2**, so the length index is treated as a uniform parameter. Every subsequent `Match` takes the non-indexed path (type_checker.rs:200-300), the motive never abstracts over the index, and the constructors' declared indices (`Vect α 0`, `Vect α (n+1)`) are replaced by whatever the discriminant carries. The family collapses: after translation, `Vect.nil : Vect α n` for *every* `n`, and `vhead : Vect α (n+1) → α` becomes a partial function that the kernel believes is total. Nothing errors — the declaration registers, the matches typecheck, and the proofs "go through".

Catches the same bug through `add_structure`. `add_structure` calls `add_indexed_inductive(name, ind_type, params.len())` (context.rs:301) — it always declares *all* of its telescope as parameters. So a Lean structure with an index cannot be routed through `add_structure` at all; doing so re-introduces this collapse under a different API.

Catches the off-by-one in the other direction: declaring *too few* parameters. With `num_params = 0` for `Vect`, `α` becomes an index, so `compute_indexed_case_type` instantiates no parameters and each constructor must supply its own `α` from the discriminant's index list — which changes the case types and, where the sorts line up, still typechecks. `derive_recursor` then builds a recursor with an empty parameter telescope (recursor.rs:72-73) whose motive has the wrong arity.

Catches deriving the split heuristically from the arity's shape. It cannot be read off the sort: `Π(α:Type 0). Nat → Type 0` is the arity of both a 2-parameter type and a 1-parameter/1-index family. The split is a *separate fact* that lives in `InductiveVal.numParams` and must be transported explicitly.

Catches "it round-tripped, so it is fine". Because LOGOS is cumulative (type_checker.rs:1330-1360) and `add_inductive`/`add_constructor` are unchecked, a collapsed family typechecks end to end. `infer_type` succeeding is not evidence.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_PARAM_INDEX_SPLIT_UNKNOWN for any inductive it cannot split correctly, and for every inductive it *does* register, `inductive_num_params(name) == numParams` and `inductive_num_indices(name) == numIndices`. Additionally: a match on `Vect α 0` must **not** accept a `Vect.cons` value, and `Vect.nil` must **not** typecheck at index `1`.
diag: E_PARAM_INDEX_SPLIT_UNKNOWN — must name the inductive, report Lean's `numParams` and `numIndices`, and state that the declaration was **not** registered. Must not fall back to `add_inductive`.

cases.title: `mutual inductive` — one transactional block registration, never N separate ones
cases.lean: mutual … inductive … inductive … end, cross-referencing constructors
cases.target: Context::add_mutual_inductives(&[MutualInductive { name, sort, num_params, constructors }, …]) — a single call carrying every member
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:562-614 (`add_mutual_inductives`: positivity of every constructor is checked **against the whole block before any mutation**, then universe consistency in a temp environment, then all headers, then all constructors, then block membership — "the registration is TRANSACTIONAL: if any constructor violates positivity, nothing is added"); kernel/src/positivity.rs:36-47 (`check_positivity_mutual` treats the block as one inductive: a sibling to the right of every arrow is a recursive occurrence, a sibling in a domain is a cross-block paradox); kernel/src/context.rs:605-612 (membership is recorded only for a block of ≥ 2 members — a single-member "block" records nothing); kernel/src/context.rs:616-621 (`mutual_block_of`); kernel/src/recursor.rs:179-212 (the mutual recursor takes one motive per member and routes a sibling recursive occurrence to the sibling's fixpoint)
guards: Catches registering the members one at a time with `add_inductive` / `add_constructor`. Both are **unchecked** (context.rs:253, :419), so the registration succeeds — but three things are lost. (1) Positivity is never checked *across* the block, so `Tree`'s constructor storing a `Forest` and `Forest`'s storing a `Tree → False` is admitted: a cross-block paradox that `check_positivity_mutual` exists to catch. (2) `mutual_blocks` is never populated, so `mutual_block_of` returns `None` and `derive_recursor` builds a *standalone* recursor that recurses only on itself — a sibling occurrence becomes an opaque field and structural recursion through the pair is no longer derivable. (3) The registration is not transactional, so a failure halfway leaves a half-declared block in the context.

Catches ordering the members wrong. The block's `num_params` is taken from `block[0]` (recursor.rs:193-199) and every other member is checked against it; and each member's constructors are registered in block order, which fixes the positional order every `Match` on that member depends on (type_checker.rs:253-266). Lean's declaration order must be preserved exactly.

Catches declaring the members with different parameter counts. `derive_recursor` refuses a block whose members disagree (recursor.rs:200-207) — that is T03-007. Here the counts agree, which is the precondition for this case being `translate` at all.

Catches forgetting that a sibling occurrence is a *recursive* occurrence for termination too. `check_termination_mutual` requires a call to **any** member to descend (termination.rs:21-44); a translator that emits two independent `Fix`es over a mutual pair escapes that requirement entirely (see T02-014).
oracle: One `add_mutual_inductives` call per Lean `mutual` block; `mutual_block_of(m)` returns the full ordered member list for every member; each member's `inductive_num_params` is equal; `derive_recursor` succeeds for each member; and structural recursion across the pair typechecks.

cases.title: Mutual block with disagreeing parameter counts — the recursor cannot be derived
cases.lean: mutual inductive with per-member parameters; Lean's own "number of parameters mismatch in mutually inductive datatypes" check
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/recursor.rs:192-207 (`derive_mutual_recursor` takes `num_params` from `block[0]` and then, for every member, errors with "auto-recursor: mutual block members disagree on parameter count" if `inductive_num_params(name).min(arity(name)) != num_params`); kernel/src/recursor.rs:208-212 (the shared `param_tele`, `tp_names` and `param_types` are all read off `block[0]` — every member is *assumed* to take that exact telescope); kernel/src/context.rs:562-614 (`add_mutual_inductives` checks positivity and constructor universes but **never** compares `num_params` across members — the block registers happily and the failure surfaces only at recursor derivation); kernel/src/context.rs:246-255 and :399-411 (the default is "all of the arity is parameters", which is what *produces* the disagreement in practice)
guards: The Lean-illegal direct form is commented out below, because Lean refuses it with "number of parameters mismatch in mutually inductive datatypes". The translator must never *synthesise* that shape either. The realistic way it gets synthesised is the T03-005 bug: registering each member with `add_inductive`, whose default parameter count is the member's **full arity**. In a Lean-legal block whose members have different numbers of *indices* — which Lean permits — that default assigns different parameter counts to different members, and `derive_recursor` then refuses the whole block.

Catches the deferred-failure trap. `add_mutual_inductives` returns `Ok` for a block with mismatched counts: positivity and universe checks pass, headers and constructors are inserted, and `mutual_blocks` is populated (context.rs:595-612). The context now contains a block for which no recursor can ever be derived, and the error appears later at an unrelated call site as `CertificationError("auto-recursor: …")`. The translator must verify the agreement *itself*, before emitting.

Catches "patching" the mismatch by padding the shorter member's parameter list. The recursor's shared telescope comes from `block[0]` (recursor.rs:208-212), so padding means the padded member's constructors are checked against parameters it does not actually take; `compute_indexed_case_type` (type_checker.rs:685-714) then instantiates those positions from the discriminant and silently discards whatever the constructor declared there.

Catches splitting the block to dodge the check. Registering the members separately removes cross-block positivity (`check_positivity_mutual`, positivity.rs:36-47) and leaves `mutual_block_of` empty, so `derive_recursor` builds standalone recursors that treat a sibling occurrence as an opaque field — no recursion through the pair. That is a different, quieter corruption, not a fix.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_MUTUAL_PARAM_MISMATCH and the LOGOS context contains no member, no constructor and no `mutual_blocks` entry for the block. Separately, for every mutual block the translator *does* emit, `derive_recursor` must succeed for every member.
diag: E_MUTUAL_PARAM_MISMATCH — must name the block, list each member with the parameter count the translator assigned it, and state that a LOGOS mutual block shares **one** parameter telescope taken from its first member. Must register **nothing**: `add_mutual_inductives` does not itself check the agreement, so a translator that "tries it and sees" leaves a permanently unusable block in the context.
note: Lean itself rejects the declaration this case is named for, so it cannot appear as compiling source. It is reproduced verbatim in the comment block below, together with Lean's exact diagnostic. The compiling declarations in this file are the **nearest legal boundary**: mutual blocks that Lean accepts because their members share parameters but differ in *index* count. Those are the blocks on which the "arity is parameters" default produces the illegal shape inside LOGOS, and they are therefore the actual input a translator will meet.

cases.title: Nested inductive through a list-like container — the specialisable fragment
cases.lean: inductive with a recursive occurrence nested inside a container (`RTree := node : List RTree → RTree`), Lean's nested→mutual compilation
cases.target: Context::add_nested_inductive(&NestedDecl { name, sort: Sort(Type 0), constructors }) — which compiles to a mutual block plus kernel-checked conversion isos
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:623-652 (`add_nested_inductive` runs the **untrusted** `inductive_compile::compile_nested`, registers the resulting block through the trusted mutual machinery, then `infer_type`s every iso and requires it to match its declared conversion type both ways); kernel/src/inductive_compile.rs:1-22 (the whole strategy: replace `TList RTree` by a fresh sibling `RTree$TList` defined mutually with `RTree`, plus isos `RTree$TList ↔ TList RTree`); kernel/src/inductive_compile.rs:256-270 (**refused unless `decl.sort` is exactly `Type 0`**: "specialized siblings are `Type 0`; higher-universe nesting is not supported"); kernel/src/inductive_compile.rs:218-232 (**only pure unary containers**: every constructor argument must be the bare element `A` or a recursive `Container A`; anything else is `ArgKind::Other` and the compile is refused); kernel/src/inductive_compile.rs:118-136 (`analyze_container_ctor` takes `params[0]` as *the* element parameter — the container must have exactly one); kernel/src/inductive_compile.rs:302-327 (the emitted siblings are `Type 0` with `num_params: 0`); kernel/src/inductive_compile.rs:288-295 (a declaration with no nested occurrence is refused — "register it directly")
guards: Catches declaring the nested type directly with `add_inductive` + `add_constructor_checked`. `check_positivity` treats `TList RTree` as a parameter type in which `RTree` occurs, and `is_recursive_arg` accepts a *block member applied to its parameters* — so `TList RTree` may well pass positivity while being nothing of the kind. Even where it passes, the resulting inductive has no recursor that can recurse *through* the list, because `constructor_analysis` (recursor.rs:126) has no way to see the nested recursive occurrences. The recursion the Lean source performs is then underivable.

Catches attempting the nesting at a sort other than `Type 0`. `compile_nested` refuses outright (inductive_compile.rs:259-270), so this fails loudly — but a translator that "helpfully" downgrades the declared sort to `Type 0` to get past the check has changed the type.

Catches dropping the isos. `add_nested_inductive` returns the iso names (`NestedInfo`, inductive_compile.rs:58-64); those are the only bridge between the specialised sibling and the generic container, and a translator that discards them leaves every `List RTree`-typed subterm of the source untranslatable.

Catches assuming the compile is trusted. It is explicitly untrusted (inductive_compile.rs:19-22); soundness comes from the mutual positivity check and from `add_nested_inductive`'s own `infer_type` of each iso (context.rs:639-647). A translator that bypasses `add_nested_inductive` and registers the compiled block by hand skips the iso check.
oracle: The nested type is registered via `add_nested_inductive`; `mutual_block_of(name)` lists the specialised siblings; each returned iso name resolves to a definition whose inferred type is its declared conversion type; and the loss report contains NESTING_IS_NOT_PRIMITIVE.
loss: NESTING_IS_NOT_PRIMITIVE. The nested type does not exist in LOGOS as such. What exists is a mutual block plus a pair of isomorphisms. Every term the Lean source wrote at type `List RTree` must be transported across `RTree$TList_to_TList` / `_from_TList`, and those transports are *not* definitional: they are ordinary definitions that must be unfolded, under the 10000-step `normalize` fuel (reduction.rs:52-69).

GENERIC_CONTAINER_LEMMAS. The sibling `RTree$TList` is a **different inductive** from `TList`. Nothing proved about `TList` in general applies to it; every lemma must be re-proved for the specialisation or routed through the isos. Lean's nested inductives share the container's API.

SIBLING_PARAMETERS. Emitted siblings carry `num_params: 0` (inductive_compile.rs:322-327). A nested inductive that was *parameterised* in Lean (`RTree α := node : List (RTree α) → RTree α`) therefore loses the parameter on the sibling, and the block's shared telescope (recursor.rs:208-212) is taken from `block[0]` — which the compiler also emits with `num_params: 0` (inductive_compile.rs:300-305). The parameter must be monomorphised before the nested declaration is attempted.

CONTAINER_MUST_PRE-EXIST. `specialize` requires the container to be a *registered inductive* already (`ctx.is_inductive(c)`, inductive_compile.rs:210). Lean's `List` is not in the LOGOS prelude at all (T10-012), so the translator must first declare a monomorphic list-like container and then nest through *that*.

cases.title: Nested inductive through `Prod`/`Array`/a binary container — outside the specialisable fragment
cases.lean: inductive nested inside a non-unary or non-pure container (`T := mk : Array T → T`, `T := mk : List (Nat × T) → T`)
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/inductive_compile.rs:218-232 (the fail-closed gate: for each of the container's constructors, if any argument kind is `ArgKind::Other(_)` the compile errors — "only pure containers like `List`/`TList`"); kernel/src/inductive_compile.rs:92-101 (`ArgKind` has exactly three cases: `Elem` (the bare element parameter), `Recursive` (`Container A`), and `Other`); kernel/src/inductive_compile.rs:118-136 (`analyze_container_ctor` takes `params[0]` as **the** element parameter and classifies every later argument against it — a *second* type parameter is therefore `Other`, so no binary container is ever specialisable); kernel/src/inductive_compile.rs:246-252 (anything that is not a nesting inside a *registered* container at all is refused outright); kernel/src/inductive_compile.rs:256-270 (and the whole declaration is refused unless its sort is exactly `Type 0`); kernel/src/context.rs:20-100 (LOGOS has no `Array`, no `Prod`, no `Sigma` — see T10-011, T10-013 — so the container would have to be declared first, and declaring `Prod` does not make it unary)
guards: Catches specialising a **binary** container. `Prod A B`'s constructor is `Π(A).Π(B). A → B → Prod A B`; `analyze_container_ctor` binds `A` as the element and then meets `B`, whose type is `Type 0` — `ArgKind::Other`. The compile is refused. A translator that "helps" by picking one of the two parameters as *the* element and treating the other as a fixed field produces a sibling that mirrors only half the container, and the isos it emits will not typecheck against the generic form — but only *after* `add_mutual_inductives` has already registered the block (context.rs:634-647), leaving a partial declaration behind.

Catches specialising a container whose constructor stores a non-element field. `Array` in Lean is a structure over `List`; any faithful LOGOS stand-in stores at least one field that is neither the element nor a recursive occurrence, so it is `Other` and refused. The same is true of a length-indexed vector, a rose tree with a label, or any container with a size field.

Catches nesting under a **function type**. `T := mk : (Nat → T) → T` is strictly positive and Lean accepts it — but the head of that argument type is a `Pi`, not a `Global` container (`is_nested_container_type`, inductive_compile.rs:152-160, tests the head), so `compile_nested` does not treat it as a nesting at all. It is an ordinary positive recursive occurrence and must be registered *directly* (T03-002), never through `add_nested_inductive` — which would refuse it with "no nested container occurrence" (inductive_compile.rs:288-295). Getting this backwards in either direction is a real failure mode.

Catches nesting at a sort other than `Type 0`, including `Prop`. The gate (inductive_compile.rs:259-270) is on the *declared* sort of the nested inductive, not on the container's, and there is no fallback.

Catches "degrade instead of reject". There is no loss record for this: the mutual block that would have to be emitted does not exist, so there is no term to emit alongside a note. Emitting the un-nested approximation — declaring the field as an opaque type, or dropping the container — produces an inductive that Lean's source never mentioned and whose recursor recurses over nothing.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NESTING_NOT_SPECIALISABLE naming the container and the offending argument; no member of the would-be block, no sibling, and no iso is registered.
diag: E_NESTING_NOT_SPECIALISABLE — must name the inductive, the offending container, and the specific constructor argument whose kind is neither the element nor a recursive occurrence. Must register nothing: the mutual block and the isos are emitted together, and half of them is worse than none.

cases.title: `structure` — one call that registers an inductive, a constructor, N definitions and the eta metadata
cases.lean: structure … where, `Lean.StructureInfo`, the anonymous constructor `⟨…⟩`
cases.target: Context::add_structure(name, params, fields) — a *single* call; anything assembled by hand is missing something
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:257-369 (`add_structure` registers, in this order: the inductive via `add_indexed_inductive(name, ind_type, params.len())` (:301), the constructor `{name}_mk` (:304-306), one **definition** `{name}_{field}` per field whose body is a `Term::Match` (:308-363), and the `StructInfo` that gates eta (:365-368)); kernel/src/context.rs:117-127 (`StructInfo { mk, num_params, projections }`); kernel/src/context.rs:88-92 (the `structures` registry: "Only these one-constructor inductives get DEFINITIONAL ETA … never inferred for arbitrary one-constructor inductives"); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1391-1417 (`try_structure_eta`, gated on `struct_info`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1446-1478 (eta fires only inside `def_eq_normalized`, never in `normalize`); kernel/src/context.rs:314-328 (a later field's type may reference an earlier field, and `add_structure` rewrites those references to projections applied to the discriminant — dependent fields are supported); kernel/src/context.rs:299-301 (**the sort is hard-coded to `Type 0`** — see T03-012)
guards: Catches hand-assembling the structure from `add_inductive` + `add_constructor` + projections. That produces something that typechecks and computes but is **not** in the `structures` registry, so `try_structure_eta` never fires for it (type_checker.rs:1391-1400 returns `None` when `struct_of_constructor` is `None`). Lean proves `⟨p.x, p.y⟩ = p` by `rfl` using definitional eta; after a hand-assembled translation that goal is simply false definitionally, and the failure appears as an unrelated conversion error in whatever proof depended on it.

Catches the projection's argument order. `add_structure` builds each projection as `Π(params). Π(s : Name params). Tᵢ` (context.rs:330-339), so `p.x` is `Point_x <params…> p`, parameters **first**. `elaborate_dot` reproduces exactly that order (elaborate.rs:1285-1299). Emitting `Point_x p` for a parameterised structure is an arity error at best and a silently-wrong application at worst.

Catches the generated names. The constructor is `{name}_mk` and the projections are `{name}_{field}` — literal string concatenation (context.rs:304, :311). Those keys are claimed the moment `add_structure` runs, and a Lean declaration that flattens onto one of them overwrites it (T02-020). The translator must reserve them.

Catches emitting the *fields* in the wrong order. `StructInfo.projections` is in field order (context.rs:367), the constructor's telescope is in field order (:305), and the `Match` case is `λ(fields). fieldᵢ` (:348) — a permutation makes `p.x` return `p.y` with no type error whenever the fields share a type.

Catches dropping the *dependent* field rewriting. If field `b`'s type mentions field `a`, the projection type must be `Tᵦ[a := Name_a params s]` (context.rs:314-331). A translator that emits `Tᵦ` with a free `Var("a")` gets a projection whose type has a dangling variable, accepted unchecked by `add_definition`.
oracle: `struct_info(name)` is `Some`, with `mk == "{name}_mk"`, `num_params` equal to the structure's parameter count, and `projections` in Lean's field order; `def_eq` proves `{name}_mk (Name_f₁ p) … (Name_fₙ p) ≡ p`; and each projection applied to a literal constructor reduces to the corresponding argument.

cases.title: Structure projection — Lean's primitive `Expr.proj` has no LOGOS counterpart
cases.lean: structure, Expr.proj, dot-notation field access, structure eta
cases.target: A `Match`-bodied global definition per field, produced by Context::add_structure, applied to the receiver: `p.fst`  ⟼  `App(App(App(Global("Point_x"), <params>), p))`
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:271-369 (add_structure desugars a record into an inductive, one `{name}_mk` constructor, and one ordinary *definition* per field whose body is a `Term::Match`); kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term` has NO `Proj` variant); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1391-1417 (`try_structure_eta` exists but only inside `def_eq`, only for structures in the `structures` registry, never in `normalize`)
guards: Catches the translator emitting a projection as an *opaque axiom* (which would make `⟨a, b⟩.1 = a` unprovable) or as a `Match` inlined at each use site (which blows up term size and breaks the `structures` registry lookup that gates eta, so eta silently stops firing).
Catches the translator forgetting that `add_structure` field definitions take the structure's parameters *before* the receiver, so `p.x` is `Point_x α β p`, not `Point_x p`.
oracle: Emitted term typechecks; and `def_eq(⟨a,b⟩.1, a)` must hold in LOGOS; and the loss record must contain PROJECTION_PRIMITIVITY.
loss: PROJECTION_PRIMITIVITY. Lean's `.proj` is a kernel primitive that reduces in one iota step and participates in eta. The LOGOS encoding is a delta-unfold to a `Match`, so (a) reduction is two steps not one, (b) the projection is only definitionally transparent while the structure stays registered, and (c) structure eta holds only in `def_eq`, not under `normalize` — so a proof that relies on `normalize` seeing `⟨p.1, p.2⟩ ≡ p` will fail even though `def_eq` would accept it.

SORT_PINNING. `add_structure` hard-codes the structure's sort to `Type 0` (context.rs:300). A Lean structure in `Type u` for `u ≥ 1`, or in `Prop`, cannot be declared this way at all — that case is `reject`, see T03-012.

cases.title: Structure in `Prop` or `Type u` (u ≥ 1) — `add_structure` hard-codes `Type 0`
cases.lean: structure in Prop, structure in Type 1, structure with a `Type`-valued field
cases.target: (none — no sound translation through `add_structure`)
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:299-301 (`let ind_type = pis(params, Term::Sort(Universe::Type(0)));` followed by `add_indexed_inductive(name, ind_type, params.len())` — the sort is a **literal** `Type(0)`, not a parameter of `add_structure`); kernel/src/context.rs:268-270 (the doc says so: "The structure lives in `Type 0` (fields over `Type 0` carriers) — the common case for the algebraic hierarchy"); kernel/src/context.rs:271-276 (the signature — `params` and `fields`, no sort argument, so there is nowhere to pass one); kernel/src/context.rs:88-92 and :365-368 (only `add_structure` writes the `structures` registry via `register_struct_info`, and only entries in that registry get definitional eta); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1391-1417 (`try_structure_eta` is gated on `struct_of_constructor`, i.e. on that registry); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:545-580 (`check_constructor_universes`: a `Type k` inductive may not store a field whose sort exceeds `Type k` — so a `Type 0` structure cannot hold a `Type 0`-typed field, which lives in `Type 1`); kernel/src/term.rs:169-191 (`Universe::Type(u32)` — `Prop` is a *separate* constructor, not `Type 0`, so "Prop is close enough to Type 0" is false in LOGOS too)
guards: Catches silently re-sorting a `Prop` structure to `Type 0`. In Lean a `structure … : Prop` is a proposition: it is subject to proof irrelevance and to the large-elimination restriction, and its inhabitants are not data. Registering it at `Type 0` makes it data. Because LOGOS is **cumulative** (`Prop ≤ Type 0 ≤ Type 1`, type_checker.rs:1330-1360) while Lean is not, almost every term that mentioned the structure still typechecks — so the kernel will not catch this. What changes is that `is_subsingleton_prop` (type_checker.rs:1688) no longer applies, the large-elimination gate (type_checker.rs:277-290) no longer fires, and a `Match` on the structure may now extract a `Type`-level value from what the source called a proof.

Catches silently re-sorting a `Type 1` structure **down** to `Type 0`. This is the direction cumulativity does *not* rescue: a structure with a `Type`-valued field genuinely lives in `Type 1`, and registering it at `Type 0` makes `check_constructor_universes` reject the constructor — if the translator went through `add_constructor_checked`. If it went through the unchecked `add_constructor` (context.rs:419-428), which is what `add_structure` itself calls (context.rs:306), **the universe violation is never checked at all** and a Girard/Hurkens-shaped declaration enters the context.

Catches the "just use a plain inductive at the right sort" repair. `add_inductive` does take a sort, so a `Prop` or `Type 1` record *can* be registered as a one-constructor inductive with hand-written projections — but nothing calls `register_struct_info`, so the type is absent from the `structures` registry and **definitional eta is gone**. Every Lean proof that closed by `rfl` on `⟨p.1, p.2⟩ = p` fails. That is a degrade, not a translation, and it must be reported as one rather than passed off as success.

Catches assuming `Prop` structures are rare. `And`, `Iff`, `Exists` and every bundled `Prop`-valued class are of this shape; LOGOS's own `And`/`Ex` are registered as plain inductives at `Prop` (prelude.rs:1815, :1925) precisely *because* `add_structure` could not do it.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_STRUCTURE_SORT_UNREPRESENTABLE for any structure whose Lean sort is not `Type 0`, and registers nothing for it. For every structure it does emit, `get_global(name)` normalizes to a sort ending in `Type 0` and `struct_info(name)` is `Some`.
diag: E_STRUCTURE_SORT_UNREPRESENTABLE — must name the structure and its Lean sort, and state that `Context::add_structure` registers every record at `Sort(Type 0)`. Must not silently re-sort the structure, and must not fall back to a hand-assembled inductive (that loses definitional eta, T03-010).

cases.title: `structure … extends` — flattening vs. parent-as-field, and the lost subtyping
cases.lean: structure … extends, `Lean.StructureInfo.parentInfo`, `toParent` coercions, inherited field access, diamond inheritance
cases.target: Context::add_structure(child, params, parent_fields ++ own_fields) — a **flattened** record — plus an explicitly emitted `Child_toParent` definition and, if the source relies on it, Context::add_coercion; and a loss record
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:257-276 (`add_structure` takes a flat `fields: &[(&str, Term)]` slice; there is no parent list, no `StructureParentInfo` analogue, and no inheritance concept anywhere in `Context`); kernel/src/context.rs:117-127 (`StructInfo { mk, num_params, projections }` — three fields, none of which records a parent); kernel/src/context.rs:308-363 (projections are generated for exactly the fields passed in, named `{child}_{field}`, so an inherited field's projection is `Child_x`, a **different global** from `Parent_x`); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1267-1299 (`elaborate_dot` builds `format!("{hname}_{field}")` from the *receiver's own type head* — so `c.x` on a child resolves to `Child_x` and never to `Parent_x`); kernel/src/context.rs:188-197 (`add_coercion` — a flat `Vec<(Term, Term, Term)>`, the only place a `Child → Parent` conversion can live); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1330-1360 (`is_subtype_normalized` gives cumulativity for *sorts* and variance for `Pi` only — there is **no** structural or nominal subtyping between two inductives)
guards: Catches the "parent-as-field" encoding: registering `Child` with a field `toParent : Parent` plus the child's own fields. It is closer to Lean's `parentInfo`, and it breaks inherited field access: `c.x` elaborates via `elaborate_dot` to `Child_x`, which in that encoding does not exist — so every inherited projection in the translated source fails to resolve. The translator must either flatten *and* synthesise `Child_x` definitions, or keep the parent field *and* synthesise `Child_x := Parent_x (Child_toParent c)` for every inherited field. Doing neither is the common bug.

Catches the field **order** after flattening. Lean places the parent's fields first, in parent order, then the child's own. `add_structure` builds the constructor's telescope and the `projections` list in the order it is given (context.rs:305, :308-312), and `Match` is positional, so a reordered flattening silently permutes the anonymous-constructor arguments `⟨…⟩` at every use site.
Catches forgetting that a `Prop`-valued or `Type 1`-valued parent drags the child out of `add_structure`'s reach entirely, because the sort is hard-coded (context.rs:299-301, T03-012).
Catches emitting `Child_toParent` as an axiom. It must be a definition — `Parent_mk` applied to the child's inherited projections — or the round-trip law `(Child_toParent c).x = c.x` is unprovable.
oracle: `Child` is a registered structure whose `projections` list begins with the parent's field names in parent order; `Child_toParent` is a *definition* satisfying `Parent_x (Child_toParent c) ≡ Child_x c` for every inherited field; and the loss report contains INHERITANCE_STRUCTURE.
loss: INHERITANCE_STRUCTURE. After flattening there is no parent. `Parent` and `Child` are unrelated LOGOS inductives; nothing records that one extends the other, and no later declaration can be checked against the relationship.

PARENT_COERCION_IS_NOT_SUBTYPING. Lean lets a `Child` be used where a `Parent` is expected by inserting `Child.toParent`. LOGOS has no subtyping between inductives, so every such use site must have the conversion **inserted explicitly** at translation time; `add_coercion` only helps the LOGOS *elaborator*, not the kernel, and it is searched first-match-wins over a flat list.

SHARED_FIELD_IDENTITY. A flattened `Child` has its own `Child_x` projection. A Lean lemma stated about `Parent.x` does not apply to `c.x` for `c : Child` after translation — the two are different globals over different types. Every inherited lemma must be re-stated or transported through `toParent`.

DIAMOND_COLLAPSE. When two parents share a field, Lean identifies the field once and records both parent projections. Flattening produces a single field and *two* distinct `toParent` conversions that must be proved to agree; nothing in LOGOS checks that they do (see T07-005, T07-013).

cases.title: `class` as a structure — LOGOS has no class concept, only a record plus a list
cases.lean: class … where, `Lean.ClassExtension`, method projections, instance-implicit binders
cases.target: Context::add_structure(class_name, params, fields) for the carrier, plus one Context::add_instance(class_type, instance_value) per instance, plus Context::set_binder_kinds(f, [.., ParamKind::Instance, ..]) for every declaration with an instance-implicit binder; and a loss record
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:20-100 (there is no `classes` map — a class is *only* a structure in the `structures` registry plus entries in the `instances` `Vec`); kernel/src/context.rs:257-276 and :299-301 (`add_structure`, sort hard-coded to `Type 0`); kernel/src/context.rs:181-186 (`add_instance` — flat `Vec<(Term, Term)>`, "Searched by unifying `type` against the required class type"); kernel/src/context.rs:210-213 (`instances()` returns the raw slice: resolution is first-match-wins in insertion order); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1017-1027 (`ParamKind::Instance`: resolution is DEFERRED until all explicit arguments have been unified, so the class's type variables are pinned first); kernel/src/context.rs:199-208 (`set_binder_kinds` — the only carrier for *which* binder is instance-implicit); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1267-1299 (a method call is a projection: `Class_method <params> inst`)
guards: Catches registering the class carrier with `add_inductive` + hand-written projections instead of `add_structure`. The carrier is then absent from the `structures` registry, so definitional eta never fires for it (type_checker.rs:1391-1400) — and eta is exactly what makes `⟨Class.method inst⟩ = inst` hold, which every "instance is determined by its methods" argument relies on.

Catches omitting `set_binder_kinds`. A declaration `f (α : Type) [C α] (n : Nat)` has kinds `[Explicit, Instance, Explicit]`. Without them LOGOS falls back to the `implicit_args` count model (context.rs:82-86), which can only express *leading* implicits — so an interleaved instance binder is mis-modelled and elaboration inserts arguments at the wrong positions.

Catches recording an instance binder as `Implicit`. `ParamKind::Instance` is deliberately resolved **after** the explicit arguments (elaborate.rs:1017-1027); an `Implicit` binder is solved by unification immediately. Marking `[C α]` implicit therefore triggers instance search while `α` is still a metavariable, and the flat first-match scan (context.rs:181-186) returns whichever entry unifies with an unsolved variable — in practice the first instance in the list, regardless of type.

Catches a class whose carrier is not `Type 0`. A `class` in `Prop` (a bundled proposition) or one storing a `Type`-valued field is outside `add_structure`'s reach entirely — that is the T03-012 rejection, and a class does not get an exemption.

Catches translating a class *without* its instances. The carrier alone is inert: every `[C α]` obligation downstream fails to synthesise, and the error names the use site rather than the missing `add_instance`.
oracle: The class carrier is in the `structures` registry with its methods as `projections`; each Lean instance produces one `add_instance` whose class type unifies with the carrier applied to that instance's arguments, in Lean's resolution order; every declaration with an instance-implicit binder has matching `binder_kinds`; and the loss report contains CLASS_IDENTITY and INSTANCE_SEARCH_SEMANTICS.
loss: CLASS_IDENTITY. Nothing distinguishes a class from an ordinary structure after translation. `Context` has a `structures` registry and an `instances` list; a structure with no instances and a class with no instances are the same object.

INSTANCE_SEARCH_SEMANTICS. Lean's resolution is a tabled, backtracking search over a discrimination tree with priorities, `outParam` modes and default instances. LOGOS's is a linear scan of a `Vec` taking the first unifying entry. Priorities, backtracking and default instances have no carrier at all (T07-006, T07-007, T07-008).

METHOD_IS_A_PROJECTION. A class method becomes `Class_method params inst`, an ordinary definition whose body is a `Term::Match` (context.rs:341-362). It is not special, it is not reducible-by-attribute, and it is not resolved by class membership — only by the flat name `{Class}_{method}` (elaborate.rs:1285).

cases.title: Strict positivity violation — must be refused *before* `add_constructor`
cases.lean: inductive with a negative occurrence (`Bad := mk : (Bad → False) → Bad`), Lean's "(non-)positive occurrence" error
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:413-428 (`add_constructor` — **UNCHECKED**. It is a `HashMap::insert` plus a push onto `constructor_order`; no positivity, no universes, no typecheck of `ty` at all); kernel/src/context.rs:538-560 (`add_constructor_checked` — the *only* path that calls `positivity::check_positivity` and `check_constructor_universes`); kernel/src/positivity.rs:29-47 (`check_positivity` / `check_positivity_mutual`, and the doc: "This prevents paradoxes like `Inductive Bad := Cons : (Bad -> False) -> Bad`", context.rs:538-544); kernel/src/positivity.rs:54-85 (the rule: in `Π(x:A).
