B`, if `A` is not a recursive argument and a block member occurs in `A`, it is a `PositivityViolation`); kernel/src/context.rs:562-594 (`add_mutual_inductives` checks positivity over the whole block up front and is transactional — the mutual path is safe by construction, the single path is not); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:321-343 (the termination guard protects `Fix`, not declarations — a negative inductive needs no `Fix` to produce `False`)
guards: **The primary guard: never call `add_constructor`.** It is the ergonomic API — it is what `add_structure` itself uses internally (context.rs:306) — and it performs no check whatsoever. A translator that registers constructors with it has silently disabled the kernel's only defence against the Girard/Hurkens family of paradoxes. `Bad := mk : (Bad → False) → Bad` registered this way yields a closed inhabitant of `False`, and every certificate minted afterwards is worthless while still reporting `verified == true` (verify.rs:31-43).

Catches "Lean already checked it, so we can use the fast path". Lean checked the *Lean* declaration. What reaches LOGOS is the translator's rendering of it, and a rendering bug — a dropped arrow, a `Pi` whose domain and codomain were swapped, a parameter telescope reattached in the wrong place — can turn a positive declaration into a negative one. The check must be re-run on the emitted term, which is exactly what `add_constructor_checked` is for.

Catches routing a *mutual* block member through `add_constructor_checked`. That checks positivity against **one** inductive name (positivity.rs:29-35), so a sibling in a negative position — `Even`'s constructor storing `Odd n → False` — passes. Mutual blocks must go through `add_mutual_inductives`, which calls `check_positivity_mutual` over the whole block before mutating anything (context.rs:575-580).

Catches confusing "positive" with "appears only to the right of arrows in the final result". LOGOS's rule (positivity.rs:54-85) is per-`Π`: a member may appear as an *argument type* (`Π(x : I …). …` — a recursive argument), but must not appear *inside* a non-recursive argument type. `(Nat → Bad) → Bad` is fine; `((Bad → Nat) → Nat) → Bad` is not.
Catches degrading instead of rejecting. There is no loss record that makes an inconsistent context acceptable.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_POSITIVITY_VIOLATION and registers nothing. For every inductive it *does* register, the registration went through `add_constructor_checked` (single) or `add_mutual_inductives` (block) — never `add_constructor`. Independently: re-running `positivity::check_positivity` over the emitted constructor types must succeed for all of them.
diag: E_POSITIVITY_VIOLATION — must name the inductive, the constructor, and the argument position in which the inductive occurs negatively, and must state that no declaration was registered. The diagnostic must be produced by the *translator*, not delegated to the kernel: LOGOS has an unchecked registration path and a translator that reaches it has already lost.
note: Lean 4.14.0 refuses every declaration this case is about, so none of them can appear as compiling source. Each is reproduced verbatim in the comment block below, together with Lean's exact diagnostic. The compiling declarations that follow are the **nearest legal neighbours** — the strictly-positive variants that differ from the illegal ones by a single arrow — so the file still exercises exactly the discrimination `check_positivity` has to make, from the accepting side.

cases.title: Inductive propositions (`And`, `Or`, `Exists`) — map onto the prelude, do not re-declare
cases.lean: And, Or, Exists, Iff, True, False as inductive `Prop`s
cases.target: the **existing** prelude globals `And`/`conj`, `Or`/`left`/`right`, `Ex`/`witness`, `True`/`I`, `False` — no new registration; user-defined `Prop` inductives go through Context::add_inductive(name, Sort(Prop)) + Context::add_constructor_checked
evidence: kernel/src/prelude.rs:1815 (`add_inductive("And", and_type)` at `Prop`), :1858 (`Or`), :1925 (`Ex`), :723-724 (`True`/`I`), :730 (`False`); kernel/src/term.rs:169-176 (`Universe::Prop` is its own constructor — `Prop` is **not** `Type 0` in LOGOS's representation); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1688-1714 (`is_subsingleton_prop`: zero constructors, or exactly one whose non-arity arguments all live in `Prop`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:277-290 (the large-elimination gate — a `Prop` inductive may be eliminated into a larger sort only if it is a subsingleton); kernel/src/context.rs:545-560 (`add_constructor_checked` exempts `Prop` inductives from the universe constraint — "Impredicative Prop: no constraint on argument universes", type_checker.rs:556-561)
guards: Catches re-declaring `And`/`Or`/`Ex` instead of mapping onto the prelude's. The names are already taken, `add_inductive` is a silent `HashMap::insert` (context.rs:253-255), and the prelude's *own* definitions reference them by name — `decide`, `Decidable_rec`, the `Int` order axioms (prelude.rs:329) and the `auto` tactic's certifier all mention `Or`, `And` and `False` as `Term::Global`s. Overwriting any of them re-points that machinery at the new declaration, and if the constructor order differs (`Or.inr` before `Or.inl`) every positional `Match` in the prelude silently takes the wrong branch. See T02-020.

Catches emitting a user `Prop` inductive at `Type 0` "because it has no computational content". LOGOS is cumulative (`Prop ≤ Type 0`, type_checker.rs:1330-1360) so almost everything still typechecks — but the large-elimination gate stops firing, proof irrelevance (`proof_irrelevant`, type_checker.rs:1547-1567) no longer applies, and a `Match` can now extract data from what the source called a proof.

Catches the constructor **order** of `Or`. LOGOS's prelude registers `left` then `right` (prelude.rs:1858ff); Lean's is `Or.inl` then `Or.inr`. Both orders are "natural", the two branches of a disjunction elimination have the same type whenever the motive is constant, and `Match` is positional (type_checker.rs:253-266) — so a mismatched mapping swaps every `Or` elimination in the development with no type error at all.

Catches translating `Exists` as a `Sigma`/`Subtype`. LOGOS has neither (T10-013), and the two are not interchangeable: `Ex` is a `Prop` and is **not** a subsingleton when its witness is data, so it cannot be large-eliminated. A translator that reaches for a `Type`-valued pair to model `∃` has changed the proposition into data.

Catches `Iff`. It is a *structure* in Lean (two fields), not a primitive, and LOGOS's prelude does not register it — so it must be emitted, and at `Prop`, which `add_structure` cannot reach (T03-012). The translator must build it as a plain `Prop` inductive with hand-written projections and accept the eta loss.
oracle: Every occurrence of Lean's `And`, `Or`, `Exists`, `True`, `False` resolves to the corresponding prelude global with the prelude's constructor order; no prelude name is re-registered; every user `Prop` inductive is registered with `Sort(Prop)`; and `is_subsingleton_prop` agrees with Lean's `recursor.isK`/large-elimination verdict for each.

cases.title: The large-elimination gate — `Acc`, `Eq`, `False`, `And` may cross the `Prop`/`Type` line; `Or` may not
cases.lean: `Prop` inductives eliminated into `Type`, Lean's `InductiveVal.isRec`/`recursor` large-elimination criterion, `Acc.rec`, `Eq.rec`, `False.elim`, subsingleton elimination
cases.target: Context::add_inductive(name, Sort(Prop)) + Context::add_constructor_checked, with the *subsingleton* property preserved exactly, so that `type_checker::is_subsingleton_prop` returns the same verdict LOGOS needs
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1683-1714 (`is_subsingleton_prop`: zero constructors ⇒ true; exactly one constructor ⇒ true iff every argument **beyond the inductive's arity** has sort `Prop`; two or more ⇒ false); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:271-290 (the non-indexed gate: if the discriminant's type is a `Prop` and the return type is not, refuse unless the inductive is a subsingleton — "large-eliminating `Or` would let a *proof* pick a `Type`-level value"); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:667-677 (the identical gate on the indexed path); kernel/src/prelude.rs:1379 (`Acc` at `Prop`, `num_params = 2`), :1400ff (`Acc_rec` is the **auto-derived** dependent eliminator, not an axiom); kernel/src/prelude.rs:1439-1460 (`Eq` at `Prop`, `num_params = 2`, one index; `Eq_rec_dep` is a kernel-checked derived definition — LOGOS *derives* J rather than axiomatising it); kernel/src/recursor.rs:59-71 (`derive_recursor`'s motive target is `Sort(Prop)` for a non-subsingleton `Prop` inductive and `Sort(Type 0)` otherwise — so the derived recursor is itself gated)
guards: Catches getting `is_subsingleton_prop`'s *arity* offset wrong. The criterion skips the inductive's arity (parameters **and** indices, `pi_param_count` of the inductive's own type, type_checker.rs:1699-1702) and inspects only the constructor's remaining arguments. A translator that registers an indexed `Prop` family with the wrong `num_params`/arity — the T03-005 bug — shifts that offset, so a constructor argument that should have been skipped is tested for `Prop`-ness, or vice versa. The result is a subsingleton verdict that disagrees with Lean's, in either direction: either `Eq` stops large-eliminating (and `Eq.rec` becomes underivable, taking most of the development with it), or `Or` starts (and a proof can produce data).

Catches assuming the verdict is about the *number of constructors* alone. `And` has one constructor and is a subsingleton; a one-constructor `Prop` inductive that stores a `Nat` is **not** — Lean refuses to generate its projections at all (T03-012) and LOGOS's criterion rejects it at the `infer_sort(param_type) != Prop` test. Both conditions matter.

Catches relying on cumulativity to paper over a mis-sorted inductive. If a `Prop` inductive is registered at `Type 0`, the gate never fires (the discriminant's type does not infer to `Sort(Prop)`, type_checker.rs:277) and **every** elimination into `Type` is permitted, including `Or`'s. Because LOGOS is cumulative (type_checker.rs:1330-1360), the resulting terms typecheck. That is the single easiest way to turn a translated development into one that can extract data from proofs.

Catches translating `Acc.rec`/`Eq.rec` as axioms. LOGOS **derives** both (prelude.rs:1400ff, :1462-1470) and the derived terms are kernel-checked. Emitting them as `add_declaration` enlarges the trusted base for no reason and loses their computation rules, so `Eq.rec … (refl …)` no longer reduces.

Catches forgetting that the derived recursor's motive target is *fixed* (recursor.rs:59-71). Even for a subsingleton, `derive_recursor` gives a motive into `Sort(Type 0)` — not `Type 1`, not a universe variable. A Lean proof that eliminates `Eq` into `Type 1` has no derived recursor available (T01-007, T01-014).

Catches assuming the two systems' subsingleton criteria coincide. They do not. `is_subsingleton_prop` skips the first `arity` constructor binders **positionally** (type_checker.rs:1699-1712); Lean permits a non-`Prop` field wherever it sits, so long as the indices determine it. The file below contains one declaration on which LOGOS is stricter (a large elimination Lean grants and LOGOS refuses — a lost theorem) and one on which LOGOS is **more permissive** (a large elimination Lean refuses and LOGOS grants — a proof yielding the data it was built from, while proof irrelevance says the two proofs are equal). A translator must compute Lean's verdict and refuse, or report a loss, wherever the two disagree. See T11-020 and T01-014.
oracle: For every `Prop` inductive emitted, `is_subsingleton_prop` agrees with Lean's large-elimination verdict; `Acc`/`Eq` map onto the prelude's entries rather than being re-declared; every elimination of a `Prop` into `Type` present in the source typechecks after translation; and no elimination Lean refused is accepted.

cases.title: `noConfusion` / `injection` — the constructor-disjointness principles are not generated by LOGOS
cases.lean: `Foo.noConfusion`, `Foo.noConfusionType`, the `injection` tactic, `Nat.succ.inj`, `cases h` on an equation between constructors, `Foo.rec` auxiliaries
cases.target: (none — no sound translation of a term that *mentions* `noConfusion`)
evidence: the string `noConfusion` does not occur anywhere in `crates/logicaffeine_kernel/src` — there is no generator, no auxiliary-declaration pass, and no name for it; kernel/src/context.rs:253-255, :419-428, :545-560, :562-614, :623-652 (the complete set of inductive-registration entry points: each adds a header and constructors and *nothing else* — no `.rec`, no `.casesOn`, no `.noConfusion`, no `.injEq`); kernel/src/recursor.rs:36 (`derive_recursor` is the only auxiliary LOGOS can synthesise, and it must be requested explicitly and `add_definition`ed by the caller); kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term` has `Match` but no equation-hypothesis form — see T04-012 — so a match cannot even *observe* which constructor it took); kernel/src/prelude.rs:1439-1470 (`Eq` and its derived eliminators `Eq_rec_dep` / `Eq_rec`: J and substitution are available, **disjointness and injectivity are not** — neither follows from J alone without a large elimination that builds a discriminating family)
guards: Catches axiomatising the principle. `add_declaration("Nat_noConfusion", …)` is one line and makes everything compile. It is also an unaudited extension of the trusted base with a statement whose *own* proof is exactly what is missing, and LOGOS has no `#print axioms` — the `declarations` map is the only record (context.rs:517-522). A translator that does this converts every `injection`-based proof in the source into an assumption.

Catches the "obvious" hand-proof. Constructor disjointness (`Zero ≠ Succ n`) *is* provable in LOGOS, but only by **large elimination**: build a `Match` on the discriminant returning `True` for one constructor and `False` for the others, then transport along the equation. That requires the inductive to admit elimination into `Type`/`Prop` with a *varying* motive — which is fine for a `Type 0` inductive but is refused for a non-subsingleton `Prop` inductive by the large-elimination gate (type_checker.rs:277-290). So the principle is available for `Nat` and `Bool` and **unavailable** for the propositions where `injection` is most often used in Lean. A translator must know which side of that line each inductive falls on.

Catches the injectivity half. `Succ n = Succ m → n = m` needs a *projection* out of the constructor — again a `Match`, this time returning the argument, with a default for the other constructors. For a constructor whose argument type is not inhabited in the other branches there is no default to give, because LOGOS's `Match` requires one case per constructor with no wildcard and no impossible-case elimination (type_checker.rs:253-266, :631-638). Injectivity for a constructor storing a value of an *empty-in-that-branch* type is therefore not constructible.

Catches translating a Lean *tactic* proof that used `injection`, `cases h` on an equation, `simp` with `injEq`, or `omega`'s constructor reasoning, by reproducing the tactic. None of those exist on any LOGOS surface; the only thing that may be translated is the elaborated proof **term**, and that term mentions `Foo.noConfusion` explicitly.

Catches assuming `Foo.rec` brings disjointness with it. It does not: LOGOS's `derive_recursor` (recursor.rs:36) synthesises an eliminator only, and it is not even registered unless the caller `add_definition`s it.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NO_CONFUSION_UNAVAILABLE for any term mentioning a `noConfusion`, `noConfusionType`, `injEq` or `.inj` constant, and writes no declaration — in particular no `add_declaration` naming any of them. Where the translator instead *constructs* the principle by large elimination, it must first check the target inductive against `is_subsingleton_prop` and refuse when the gate would block it.
diag: E_NO_CONFUSION_UNAVAILABLE — must name the inductive whose `noConfusion`, `noConfusionType`, `injEq` or `.inj` lemma the source term mentions, and state that LOGOS generates no such declaration. Must emit no LOGOS output for the term, and in particular must not axiomatise the principle.

cases.title: Impossible case in an indexed match — LOGOS has **no index unification**
cases.lean: dependent pattern matching on an indexed family, automatic discharge of index-contradictory constructors, `Vect α 0` / `Fin 0` / `Even 1`
cases.target: Term::Match whose `cases` vector has **one entry per constructor**, including an explicitly synthesised inhabitant for every constructor Lean ruled out; plus a loss record
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:602-611 (the doc for `infer_indexed_match`: the return type is the motive applied to the discriminant's own index arguments, "each constructor's case is checked against `motive` applied to THAT constructor's result indices"); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:631-638 (**the whole coverage rule**: `if cases.len() != constructors.len() { WrongNumberOfCases }` — a bare count. There is no unifier, no `K`, no `noConfusion`-driven discharge, and no way to mark a branch unreachable); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:685-714 (`compute_indexed_case_type` builds each branch's expected type from the constructor's *declared* result indices — so an impossible branch's expected type is a perfectly well-formed type that simply has no natural inhabitant); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:253-266 (the non-indexed path has the identical count rule — no wildcards anywhere); kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Match { discriminant, motive, cases }` — `cases` is a positional `Vec<Term>`; there is no pattern language and no absurd-branch marker)
guards: Catches omitting the impossible branch. `cases.len() != constructors.len()` is a hard `WrongNumberOfCases` error (type_checker.rs:631-638), so this fails loudly — which is the *good* outcome. The bad outcome is the translator noticing the error and patching it by the next three guards.

Catches filling the branch with `Term::Hole`. `types_equal` treats `Hole` as matching **anything** (type_checker.rs:1594-1597) and that leniency leaks into `is_subtype`'s fast path (`:1314`), so a `Hole` branch typechecks against every expected case type. The `Match` then carries an unchecked subterm into the context, and every later conversion involving it succeeds vacuously. This is the single most dangerous filler.

Catches filling the branch with an axiom (`add_declaration("absurd_case", …)`) or with `sorryAx`. Both make the branch typecheck and both extend the trusted base with a statement the translator did not prove; LOGOS has no axiom audit (T02-003).

Catches filling the branch with a *plausible but wrong* value of the right type — `Zero` for a `Nat`-valued branch. It typechecks, it reduces, and if the "impossible" case turns out to be reachable after a *different* mistranslation (notably the T03-005 params/indices collapse, which makes `Vect.cons` inhabit `Vect α 0`), the function silently returns the filler instead of failing. The two bugs compose into a function that answers wrongly with no diagnostic anywhere.

Catches assuming the motive can dodge the issue. The motive is applied to the **constructor's** declared result indices for each branch (type_checker.rs:685-714), so a motive that returns `True` on the impossible index changes the branch type — but it also changes the *result* type, which is the motive applied to the discriminant's indices. There is no motive that makes one branch trivial and leaves the others alone.

So the honest filler, "derive `False` from the index mismatch and use `False.elim`", is generally unavailable; the translator falls back to an *arbitrary* inhabitant of the branch type.

TOTALITY_ILLUSION. Once an arbitrary inhabitant is supplied, the translated function is total in a way the Lean source was not: `vhead` applied to a `Vect α 0` reduces to the filler instead of being ill-typed. Any downstream reasoning that relied on "this case cannot occur" no longer has a kernel-enforced basis.

Catches translating `Foo.rec` **as a `Match`** at each use site. That is the right *shape* for `casesOn` and wrong for `rec`: the recursor supplies induction hypotheses (the results of the recursive calls) to each minor premise, and a bare `Match` does not. Substituting one for the other changes the arity of every branch, and for a non-recursive inductive — where the two coincide — it will typecheck, so the bug only surfaces on the first recursive type.

Catches the inverse: translating every `match` in the source *through* the derived recursor. LOGOS's `Match` is the primitive; routing matches through a derived recursor means every pattern match carries a `Fix` and is subject to the termination guard, so a perfectly non-recursive match can be rejected for failing to descend.

Catches naming collisions in the derived recursor. The translator chooses the flat name; the prelude already owns `Acc_rec`, `Eq_rec`, `Eq_rec_dep`, `Decidable_rec` (prelude.rs:1400ff, :1462-1470). Overwriting any of them silently replaces a kernel-checked derived term (T02-020).

Reduction therefore takes more steps (delta, then fix-unfold, then iota) against the fixed 10000-step `normalize` fuel (reduction.rs:52-69), and the recursor can be unfolded in places Lean would keep it opaque.

It is **not** universe-polymorphic — `Universe::Type` takes a concrete `u32` (term.rs:169-191) and an inductive cannot carry level parameters at all (T01-007). Every Lean use of `Foo.rec` at `Type 1` or at a level variable is therefore outside the derived recursor's type, and cumulativity (`Prop ≤ Type 0 ≤ Type 1`, type_checker.rs:1330-1360) only helps in the *downward* direction.

Lean's `casesOn` (non-recursive), `brecOn`/`below` (course-of-values), `binductionOn` and the `.rec` auxiliaries are separate constants, none of which LOGOS generates. A term mentioning `brecOn` is a T04-016 rejection, not a degrade.

cases.title: Constructor universe constraint violation — the Girard/Hurkens door
cases.lean: inductive at `Type k` storing a field whose sort exceeds `Type k`; Lean's "invalid universe level in constructor … it must be smaller than or equal to the inductive datatype universe level"
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:539-580 (`check_constructor_universes`: "every VALUE argument's sort must be `≤` the inductive's result sort — so a `Type 0` inductive cannot store a `Type 0`-typed field (which lives in `Type 1`), the universe inconsistency that opens Girard/Hurkens paradoxes"; the leading `num_params` arguments are exempted, and a `Prop` inductive is exempted entirely); kernel/src/context.rs:545-560 (`add_constructor_checked` — the **only** caller of that check); kernel/src/context.rs:413-428 (`add_constructor` — **unchecked**: no positivity, no universes, no typecheck); kernel/src/context.rs:271-306 (`add_structure` registers its constructor through the unchecked `add_constructor`, so **no structure's fields are universe-checked at all**); kernel/src/context.rs:581-594 (`add_mutual_inductives` *does* run the check, in a temp environment carrying the block's headers, before mutating — the mutual path is safe, the single and structure paths are not); kernel/src/term.rs:169-191 (`Universe::Type(u32)`, and `succ`: `Prop → Type 1`, `Type n → Type (n+1)` — so a field of type `Type 0` has sort `Type 1`)
guards: **The primary guard: never call `add_constructor` directly.** It is the path `add_structure` itself uses, and it performs no universe check. `Bad : Type 0` with `mk : Type 0 → Bad` registered this way is a `Type 0` type that quantifies over `Type 0` — the impredicativity that Girard's paradox exploits. Nothing downstream notices; the context is simply inconsistent.

Catches trusting Lean's check to have covered it. Lean checked the Lean declaration. What LOGOS receives is the translator's rendering, and the check is sensitive to the **parameter count**: `check_constructor_universes` exempts the leading `inductive_num_params(ind)` binders (type_checker.rs:561-564). Register the inductive with too *many* parameters — the T03-005 `add_inductive` default — and a genuinely offending field is exempted as if it were a parameter, so even `add_constructor_checked` lets it through. The two bugs compose.

Catches the `Prop` exemption being applied to the wrong thing. A `Prop` inductive is exempt (impredicative `Prop`, type_checker.rs:556-561) — but only if it is *registered* at `Prop`. A translator that re-sorts a `Type 0` inductive to `Prop` to get past the check has not fixed anything; it has made a data type into a proposition (T03-012) and turned off the gate that was protecting it.

Catches the opposite over-correction: bumping the inductive's sort to `Type 1` to satisfy the check. That is often the *right* declaration — it is what Lean itself would infer — but it is a different type from the one the source declared, and every downstream use site that expected `Type 0` must be re-checked. Cumulativity (`Type 0 ≤ Type 1`, type_checker.rs:1330-1360) makes the *uses* typecheck in the permissive direction, hiding the change. If the bump was not in the Lean source, it must be reported, not performed silently.

Catches structures specifically. `add_structure` never universe-checks its fields (context.rs:306 calls the unchecked `add_constructor`) **and** hard-codes the structure's sort to `Type 0` (context.rs:300). So a Lean structure with a `Type`-valued field is doubly unrepresentable: the sort is wrong and the check that would have caught it does not run. See T03-012.

For every inductive it does emit, the registration went through `add_constructor_checked` or `add_mutual_inductives`, and re-running `check_constructor_universes` against the emitted `num_params` succeeds.

Must register nothing: `add_inductive` and `add_constructor` are both unchecked, so a translator that "registers and lets the kernel complain" has already put an inconsistent declaration in the context.
note: Lean 4.14.0 refuses every offending declaration, so none can appear as compiling source. Each is reproduced verbatim in the comment block below with Lean's exact diagnostic. The compiling declarations are the **nearest legal neighbours** — the same records, one universe higher, which Lean accepts — so the file exercises the exact discrimination `check_constructor_universes` has to make, from the accepting side.

Decidable (Eq T a b)`, registered with Context::add_definition and Context::add_instance; plus a loss record for every type where that construction is not available

Decidable (Eq Bool a b)`, written out by hand); kernel/src/prelude.rs:1023-1186 (`decEqNat`, a hand-written structural recursion on `a`); kernel/src/prelude.rs:781 (`Decidable` is an *indexed* inductive, `add_indexed_inductive("Decidable", Π(p:Prop). Because `decide`'s result is a `Bool` and the instance's *type* still says `Decidable (Eq Foo a b)`, nothing type-errors; every proof by `decide` downstream is then a proof of a false statement. `decEqNat` decides equality of `Nat` and of nothing else.

Decidable (Eq Foo a b))` typechecks everything and computes nothing: `decide` is defined through `Decidable_rec` (prelude.rs:798-812), so an opaque instance leaves every `decide` stuck, and every `by decide` proof in the source fails to reduce.

Catches `Decidable`'s params/indices split. The prelude registers it with `num_params = 1` (prelude.rs:781) over the arity `Π(p : Prop). Type 0` — so there are zero indices and `p` is a parameter. A translator that re-registers `Decidable` (rather than mapping onto the prelude's) with the `add_inductive` default gets the same count by luck; one that decides `p` is an index gets `num_params = 0` and every `Match` on a `Decidable` takes the indexed path with a motive of the wrong arity.

Catches deriving `DecidableEq` for a type whose fields are not themselves decidable in LOGOS — a field of type `Int` (opaque, prelude.rs:92-340), `Text`, `Float` (completely inert), or a function type. Lean may still derive it (or refuse); LOGOS has no decision procedure to call, and the instance cannot be built at all.
oracle: Each derived `DecidableEq` becomes a LOGOS *definition* of type `Π(a b : T). Decidable (Eq T a b)` plus a matching `add_instance`; `decide (a = b)` reduces to `true` exactly when `a` and `b` are the same constructor applied to pointwise-equal arguments; no emitted instance body mentions `decEqNat` or `decEqBool` for a type other than `Nat`/`Bool`; and the loss report contains NO_DERIVATION_MECHANISM.

TERM_SIZE. Lean's generated decision procedure uses nested pattern matching with wildcards; LOGOS's `Match` has no patterns and no wildcard (type_checker.rs:253-266), so an n-constructor type needs n² explicit branches. Against the fixed 10000-step `normalize` fuel (reduction.rs:52-69) and O(size)-per-binder substitution (type_checker.rs:1088), `decide` on a moderately-sized enum can exhaust the fuel and **silently return a partially reduced term**.

DISJOINTNESS_DEPENDENCY. Every "different constructors ⇒ not equal" branch must produce a proof of `Eq T a b → False`. That is constructor disjointness, which LOGOS does not generate (T03-018); it has to be built by large elimination through a discriminating `Match`, which is available for `Type 0` inductives and blocked for non-subsingleton `Prop`s (type_checker.rs:277-290).

cases.lean: def by structural recursion on List, `| [] => .. | x :: xs => ..`
cases.target: A locally-declared list inductive (Lean's `List` is NOT in the LOGOS prelude) plus Term::Fix { name: "len", body: Lambda{"l", App(Global("TList"), Global("Nat")), Match { discriminant: Var("l"), motive: .., cases: [<TNil>, <TCons: λh.λt. Succ (len t)>] }}}
evidence: kernel/src/prelude.rs:606-613 (the prelude's only list types are the monomorphic `EList`/`ENil`/`ECons` over `Entity` and the parametric `TList`/`TNil`/`TCons`; Lean's `List` is absent — see LOGOS_FACTS "Absent entirely"); kernel/src/termination.rs:166-174 (`extract_inductive_name` peels an application spine, so `TList A` is recognised as the inductive `TList`); kernel/src/termination.rs:403-440 (`check_match_cases_guarded` counts the constructor's Π-telescope with `count_pi_params` and marks *every* λ-binder of the case as smaller — including the PARAMETER binders); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:255-259 (positional case coverage)
guards: Catches the translator marking the wrong λ-binders as the constructor's fields. `TCons : Π(A:Type 0). A → TList A → TList A` has THREE Π binders, so `count_pi_params` is 3 and `extract_lambda_params` (termination.rs:410-415) peels three λs from the case. A translator that emits the `TCons` case as `λh.λt. …` (two binders, parameter dropped because Lean's `List.cons` shows the parameter as an implicit) has its case arity disagree with the constructor's, and the third peel silently reaches into the case *body* — so a variable that is not a constructor field gets marked structurally smaller, and a non-decreasing recursive call on it is accepted. That is a soundness hole, not a type error.

Catches emitting Lean's `List` as `Global("List")` and assuming the prelude provides it. `Context::get_global` (context.rs:449) returns `None`, so `extract_inductive_name` fails and the `Match` is rejected with `NotAnInductive` — or, worse, a translator that "helpfully" calls the UNCHECKED `add_inductive` + `add_constructor` (context.rs:253,419) registers a list type with no positivity or universe check at all.

Catches confusing `List α` with the prelude's `EList`. `EList` is monomorphic over `Entity` (prelude.rs:561-577); silently retargeting `List Nat` at it makes every element `Entity`-typed, and because LOGOS is cumulative many downstream terms still typecheck.
oracle: The emitted `Fix` typechecks against the translated Lean type, and `normalize(len (TCons Nat 1 (TCons Nat 2 (TNil Nat))))` is `Lit(Nat 2)`.

cases.title: `mutual` recursive definitions — one `MutualFix` block, one shared Giménez guard
cases.lean: mutual def ... end, mutually recursive functions and mutual structural recursion
cases.target: Term::MutualFix { defs: [("isEven", <λn. Match ..>), ("isOdd", <λn. Match ..>)], index: 0 }   -- and `index: 1` for the sibling's reference
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:511-525 (`Term::MutualFix { defs, index }` — a block plus the index of the member this occurrence denotes); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:341-372 (`MutualFix` inference: every member's type is inferred structurally, then `check_termination_mutual`, then every body is re-checked with ALL siblings bound); kernel/src/termination.rs:79-110 (`check_termination_mutual` computes each member's structural ARGUMENT POSITION first, then checks every body so that a call to ANY member passes, at that member's position, something smaller than the CURRENT body's structural parameter); kernel/src/termination.rs:218-232 (`fix_positions.get(name)` — the position is per-callee, not per-caller)
guards: Catches emitting two *separate* `Term::Fix`es, one per Lean definition. Each would then be checked by `check_termination` (termination.rs:49) against a `fix_positions` map containing only its own name, so the sibling call's head is not recognised as a recursive name at all — it falls through to the generic `App` arm (termination.rs:205-242) and is never checked for decrease. Two mutually recursive functions that loop forever would both pass. This is the exact soundness hole `check_termination_mutual` exists to close, and a naive translator walks straight into it because Lean's `Expr` presents the two definitions as two separate constants.

Catches emitting the block but referring to a sibling by `Term::Global` instead of `Term::Var`. The guard only recognises a recursive call when the application head is `Term::Var(name)` with `name ∈ fix_positions` (termination.rs:216-220); a `Global` head is a plain constant, so the call is unguarded — and it will also fail to resolve, because the sibling is not in the context yet.

Catches getting `index` wrong. `MutualFix { defs, index }` returns `types[index]` (type_checker.rs:371); with `defs` in a different order than the translator assumed, `isEven` gets `isOdd`'s type. Both here are `Nat → Bool`, so the kernel accepts it and every use site is silently the other function.

Catches the differing-structural-parameter trap: `check_termination_mutual` recomputes the structural parameter per member (termination.rs:88-94) but checks each body against the CURRENT member's parameter, so a block where one member recurses on argument 0 and another on argument 1 is fine — but a translator that normalises all members to "position 0" (a tempting simplification) makes the check inspect the wrong argument of the sibling call.
oracle: The emitted `MutualFix` typechecks (so `check_termination_mutual` passed), its `defs` has exactly the Lean block's members in a fixed, recorded order, and `normalize` of member `index` applied to `Lit(Nat 4)` matches Lean's `isEven 4`.

cases.title: `termination_by` — a measure-based termination argument has no LOGOS carrier
cases.lean: termination_by, well-founded recursion compiled by Lean's `WF` elaborator
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:493-525 (`Term::Fix` and `Term::MutualFix` carry ONLY a name and a body: there is no measure, no relation, no well-foundedness proof field); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:336 and :363 (every `Fix`/`MutualFix` is gated on `termination::check_termination{,_mutual}` — there is no alternative admission path); kernel/src/termination.rs:1-14 and :378-400 (the guard is the purely SYNTACTIC Giménez structural condition: the recursive argument must be a variable bound by matching on the structural parameter, or an application headed by one); kernel/src/termination.rs:378-395 (`verify_structural_arg_smaller` — anything that is not headed by a `smaller_than` variable is a `TerminationViolation`)
guards: The tempting wrong move is to **drop the `termination_by` clause and emit the `Fix` anyway**, reasoning that "LOGOS will re-check termination, so if it is wrong the kernel catches it". It does catch it — with a `TerminationViolation` — which means the translator has converted a *perfectly good Lean theorem* into a hard error at some later, unrelated point in the build, with no pointer back to the source. Worse is the variant that emits the `Fix` into a context where the guard accidentally passes: `extract_structural_param` falls back to "the first inductive-typed binder" (termination.rs:145-149), so a function whose real decreasing measure is `n - m` but whose first binder happens to be matched on can be admitted with a *different* recursion than the source had.

Catches "translate the measure into a fuel parameter". Adding a `Nat` fuel argument and recursing on it produces a LOGOS `Fix` that passes the guard and is a DIFFERENT function: it returns a junk value when the fuel runs out. Every Lean theorem about the original is then false about the translation, and — because LOGOS is cumulative and the junk value has the right type — nothing in the kernel notices.

Catches "route it through `Acc`". `Acc`/`Acc_intro`/`Acc_rec`/`WellFounded` DO exist in the LOGOS prelude (prelude.rs:1354-1418), which makes this look available. But `WellFounded` is only the abbreviation `Π(x:A). Acc A R x` (prelude.rs:1407-1418) — there is no `WellFounded.fix`, and the recursion still has to be written as a `Fix` that the syntactic guard must accept. See T04-015.

Catches a translator that silently succeeds because the Lean function *happens* to also be structurally recursive and `termination_by` was only an optimisation hint. The verdict is still `reject`: the translator cannot know that in general, and emitting output for some `termination_by` functions and not others makes the conformance report unreliable. Recognising the structural subcase is allowed only as a separate, explicitly-recorded path.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NO_MEASURE_TERMINATION for each of the four definitions below and writes no declaration into the LOGOS context.
diag: E_NO_MEASURE_TERMINATION — must name the function, quote its `termination_by` measure, and state that LOGOS admits recursion only through the syntactic structural guard. Must NOT emit a `Fix`.

cases.title: `decreasing_by` — the termination *proof* has no carrier and cannot be replayed
cases.lean: decreasing_by, decreasing_tactic, the `WF` elaborator's proof obligations
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:493-509 (`Term::Fix { name, body }` has exactly two fields: there is nowhere to attach a proof term); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:328-339 (`Fix` inference runs `check_termination` and then a sanity `infer_type`; the termination argument is never a *term* the kernel checks, it is a decision procedure over syntax); kernel/src/termination.rs:378-400 (`verify_structural_arg_smaller` accepts exactly two shapes — a `smaller_than` variable, or an application headed by one — and takes no proof, no hypothesis, and no context of assumptions); kernel/src/termination.rs:19-43 (`GuardContext` holds only names and a `HashSet<String>` of smaller variables — there is no proof state at all)
guards: Catches the "just discharge it on the LOGOS side" move — translating the `decreasing_by` script into a LOGOS tactic script and attaching it somewhere. There is nowhere to attach it: the `Fix` rule never produces a goal. A translator that emits the `Fix` *plus* a separate LOGOS theorem `n % m < m` has produced a true theorem and an unrelated `Fix` that the guard will reject on its own terms — the theorem does not license the recursion.

Catches the subtler variant: emitting the `Fix` and a `Term::Lit`/axiom "termination certificate" as an extra argument. Because the guard only inspects the argument at the recorded structural POSITION (termination.rs:218-232), padding the call with an extra argument SHIFTS that position — a translator that appends a certificate argument can make the guard inspect the certificate instead of the real recursive argument. If the certificate happens to be a match-bound variable the guard passes and a non-terminating fixpoint is admitted. That inhabits every type.

Catches assuming `decreasing_by omega` means "LOGOS's `omega` can do it too". The LOGOS `omega` is a *proof script* tactic on the vernacular surfaces (LOGOS_FACTS, Surface A/C tactic lists); it is not part of the kernel's `Fix` rule and cannot be invoked from term elaboration.

Catches dropping a `decreasing_by` that used `simp_wf` or `Nat.sub_lt`: these make the *Lean* definition legal, and after they are dropped the surviving `Expr` still looks like an ordinary recursive definition. The translator must key the rejection off the presence of well-founded recursion in the Lean declaration (`WellFounded.fix`/`WF` in the compiled value), not off surface syntax.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NO_TERMINATION_PROOF_CARRIER for each definition below and writes no declaration into the LOGOS context.
diag: E_NO_TERMINATION_PROOF_CARRIER — must name the function and state that LOGOS's termination check is a syntactic guard that accepts no proof obligation, so the `decreasing_by` script is unreplayable. Must NOT emit a `Fix`.

cases.title: `Nat.rec` applied directly — the recursor is primitive in Lean, derived in LOGOS
cases.lean: Nat.rec, Nat.casesOn, @Nat.rec with an explicit motive
cases.target: Either (a) `Global("Nat_rec")` after the translator has itself called `recursor::derive_recursor(ctx, "Nat")` and `Context::add_definition`ed the `(type, term)` pair, or (b) the `Fix` + `Match` the recursor would unfold to.
evidence: kernel/src/recursor.rs:36-48 (`derive_recursor` SYNTHESISES `(recursor_type, recursor_term)`; it does not register anything — "the caller must add_definition it"); kernel/src/recursor.rs:60-72 (the motive target is HARD-CODED: `Sort(Prop)` for a non-subsingleton `Prop` inductive, `Sort(Type 0)` for everything else); kernel/src/term.rs:487-492 (`Term::Match` is the primitive — the inverse of Lean 4, where `.rec` is primitive and `match` is compiled away); kernel/src/context.rs:449 (`get_global` precedence: inductives → constructors → definitions → declarations; a derived recursor is an ordinary *definition*, hence delta-transparent)
guards: Catches emitting `Global("Nat_rec")` without having registered it. `get_global` returns `None` and the term fails to typecheck — but only at the point of USE, which may be many declarations later, so the error blames the wrong source file.

Catches the opposite: registering `Nat_rec` as an `add_declaration` AXIOM (context.rs:434) to make the name resolve. That makes the recursor opaque, so `Nat_rec P z s (Succ k)` never reduces to `s k (Nat_rec P z s k)` — every `rfl` proof in the source that relied on the iota rule silently stops holding, and a translator that then "fixes" the proofs with more axioms has axiomatised arithmetic.

Catches translating `Nat.rec` at a `Sort u` motive by instantiating `u := 0` (i.e. `Prop`) to make it fit. The resulting term typechecks by cumulativity but computes nothing: a `Prop`-motive recursion cannot produce the `Type`-level data the Lean source built.

Catches assuming `Nat.casesOn`, `Nat.recAux`, `Nat.noConfusion`, `Nat.brecOn` are equally derivable. `derive_recursor` produces ONE eliminator; `casesOn`/`noConfusion` /`brecOn` have no LOGOS generator at all (LOGOS_FACTS: "no `casesOn`/`brecOn`/ `noConfusion`/`injection`"). See T03-018 and T04-016.
oracle: The emitted term typechecks, and the loss record contains RECURSOR_PRIMITIVITY; if any Lean occurrence instantiates `Nat.rec`'s motive above `Type 0`, the loss record must additionally contain MOTIVE_UNIVERSE_PINNING (or the case must be rejected).
loss: RECURSOR_PRIMITIVITY. In Lean, `Nat.rec` is a kernel constant with an iota rule. In LOGOS it is an ordinary, delta-transparent definition whose body is a `Fix` over a `Match`. Consequences the translator must record: (a) `Nat_rec` unfolds during `normalize`, so terms that mention it do not stay in recursor form and proof scripts keyed on its shape break; (b) it participates in the 10000-step `normalize` fuel (reduction.rs:52-69) like any other definition; (c) it is not available unless the translator explicitly derived and registered it.

MOTIVE_UNIVERSE_PINNING. `derive_recursor` gives `Nat_rec`'s motive the target `Sort(Type 0)` (recursor.rs:64-71). Lean's `Nat.rec` is universe-polymorphic: `{motive : Nat → Sort u}`. Any Lean use of `Nat.rec` at `Sort u` for `u ≥ 2` — in particular building a `Type 1`-valued family by recursion — has no translation. A `Prop` motive still passes by LOGOS cumulativity (type_checker.rs:1330-1360), so only the *large* end of the range is lost.

cases.title: `match` on several discriminants — LOGOS `Match` is unary, so it must be nested
cases.lean: match e₁, e₂ with | p₁, p₂ => ..., multi-column equation compiler
cases.target: Nested unary matches: Match { discriminant: a, motive: <λx:Bool. Bool → Bool>, cases: [ Match { discriminant: b, motive: .., cases: [.., ..] },   -- a = false Match { discriminant: b, motive: .., cases: [.., ..] } ] } -- a = true
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:487-492 (`Term::Match` has ONE `discriminant` — there is no multi-scrutinee form); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:172-200 (the `Match` rule infers a single discriminant's type and extracts a single inductive name); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:268-272 (the result type is `motive` applied to the discriminant and then BETA-REDUCED — "without beta reduction … causes type mismatches in NESTED matches", the kernel's own comment about exactly this case); kernel/src/termination.rs:262-280 (only a match whose discriminant IS the structural parameter marks variables smaller; an inner match on a different scrutinee does not)
guards: Catches the outer motive being wrong. In a nested encoding the OUTER match's motive must have type `Bool → (Bool → C)`, i.e. it must still abstract the remaining scrutinees. A translator that computes the motive as though the match were the last thing in the term emits `λ_:Bool. C`, and then the outer case bodies — which are themselves `Bool → C` functions — fail to check. Where `C` is itself an arrow the two are confusable and the kernel may accept the wrong one.

Catches scrutinee-order inversion. Lean's `match a, b with` columns are ordered, and the equation compiler may internally reorder them; the LOGOS nesting order fixes which variable is bound where. For a function like `sub2` below, swapping the nesting silently computes `sub2 b a`. Both have type `Nat → Nat → Nat`, so nothing complains.

Catches the termination interaction. In `zipLen` the recursion decreases on the FIRST list, so the OUTER match must be on that list: `termination.rs:264-272` marks constructor binders smaller only when the discriminant is the structural parameter. Nesting the other way round leaves the recursive call's argument unmarked and the whole definition is rejected with a `TerminationViolation` — a correct Lean function turned into a build error purely by a choice of nesting order.

Catches "flatten the product": encoding `match a, b with` as a match on a pair. `Prod` is **absent** from the LOGOS prelude (LOGOS_FACTS, "Absent entirely"), so this requires declaring a product inductive, and then the structural guard sees the recursion running on the pair rather than on the list — which breaks termination for `zipLen`.
oracle: The emitted term typechecks; `normalize` agrees with Lean on all four `Bool × Bool` inputs of `eqBool` and on `zipLen` for at least one asymmetric pair of lists; and the emitted outer `discriminant` is the translation of Lean's FIRST column.

cases.title: Nested constructor patterns — LOGOS `Match` has **no patterns at all**
cases.lean: nested patterns (`(a, b) :: t`, `n + 2`, `.cons (.node f) t`), the equation compiler
cases.target: A TREE of unary, positional `Term::Match`es — one match per constructor layer the Lean pattern inspected, each with exactly one case per constructor of that layer's inductive, in registration order, and each case a λ-telescope binding that constructor's fields.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:487-492 (`Term::Match { discriminant, motive, cases }` — `cases: Vec<Term>` carries NO pattern, NO constructor name, NO binder list); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:255-259 (`cases.len()` must equal the constructor count); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:262-265 (cases are zipped against `ctx.get_constructors(..)` positionally, so the i-th case IS the i-th constructor); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:268-272 (the beta-reduction of `motive disc` exists specifically so NESTED matches typecheck); kernel/src/termination.rs:403-440 (each case's constructor fields are its leading λ-binders, counted by `count_pi_params` on the constructor's type)
guards: Catches emitting a single flat `Match` with one case per *equation*. For `classify` below Lean has three equations but `Nat` has two constructors, so `WrongNumberOfCases { expected: 2, found: 3 }` fires — visibly. The dangerous version is `sumPairs`, where the Lean equation count (2) coincidentally equals the `List` constructor count (2): the flat match then TYPECHECKS with the `(a,b) :: t` equation body installed as the `cons` case, and the pair is never destructured — except that the body refers to `a` and `b`, which are now free `Term::Var`s. If any enclosing binder happens to be named `a` or `b`, the named representation CAPTURES them and the term both typechecks and computes the wrong answer.

Catches dropping the inner layer's exhaustiveness. `| 0 => .. | 1 => .. | n+2 => ..` becomes `Match n [c0, λk. Match k [c1, λj. c2 j]]` — the INNER match needs two cases too. A translator that emits the inner match with only the `Succ` case fails `cases.len()`; one that emits the `Zero` case as a `Term::Hole` produces a term where `types_equal` matches the hole against ANYTHING (type_checker.rs:1594-1597), so the hole survives into the library.

Catches binder-count mismatch in a case. The `TCons`-style constructor's case must bind every Π binder of the constructor's type *including parameters* (termination.rs:410-415 peels `count_pi_params` λs). Binding only the value fields makes the guard peel into the body and mark a non-field variable as structurally smaller — a termination-soundness hole, not a type error.

Catches reusing one binder name across sibling cases. Lean's de Bruijn bodies make `| .cons a t` and `| .cons a t'` interchangeable; LOGOS's named `Var` means a case body that mentions `a` must be under a λ that actually binds `a` at that position.
oracle: The emitted term typechecks; every `Match` node in it satisfies `cases.len() == ctor_count` for its own inductive; the emitted term contains no `Term::Hole`; and `normalize` agrees with Lean on every example below. The loss record must contain PATTERN_STRUCTURE.
loss: PATTERN_STRUCTURE. The source's pattern language — which columns were inspected, in what order, with what binder names, and which equations were written by the user versus synthesised by the compiler — is not recoverable from the emitted match tree. Concretely: `| 0 => .. | 1 => .. | n+2 => ..` and the two-level nested match that encodes it are the same LOGOS term, so error messages, `simp` lemma shapes and equation lemmas (T04-017) cannot be reconstructed. This is acceptable because the *denotation* is preserved: every input reduces to the same value.

ARITY_FLATTENING. A Lean pattern binds a variable at an arbitrary depth (`(a, b) :: t` binds `a` two layers down). In LOGOS the variable is bound by an inner case's λ, so its scope is narrower and its name may have to be freshened (`Term::Var` is NAMED — term.rs:450). The source binder names survive only as hints.

cases.title: Overlapping patterns with first-match semantics — unrecoverable positionally
cases.lean: overlapping match equations, `match`'s top-to-bottom first-match rule
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:487-492 (`Term::Match { discriminant, motive, cases }` — `cases` is indexed by CONSTRUCTOR, not by source equation: there is no pattern, no guard, and no notion of order among alternatives for one constructor); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:255-259 (`cases.len()` must equal the constructor count — so N overlapping equations cannot even be represented as N cases); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:262-265 (the i-th case is checked against the i-th constructor's case type, positionally); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:612-678 (`infer_indexed_match` — still exactly one case per constructor; there is no index unifier and no residual-pattern machinery)
guards: This is the highest-value Tier-4 rejection. The tempting wrong move is **take the first equation for each constructor and drop the rest**, because that always produces a well-typed `Match` of exactly the right arity. For `pick` below that yields `pick 0 0 = 1`, which happens to be right, and `pick 0 5 = 1`, also right — but `pick 5 0` becomes `3` where Lean says `2`. The term typechecks, reduces, and is silently a different function. Nothing in the LOGOS kernel can detect this, because the kernel never saw the discarded equations.

Catches the mirror-image move: **take the LAST equation for each constructor** (natural if the translator folds the equation list left-to-right into a case vector). That is exactly last-match semantics, the opposite of Lean's, and again produces a well-typed term.

Catches "compile it myself": expanding the overlap into disjoint cases by hand. That is a correct *strategy* in principle — it is what Lean's equation compiler does — but doing it in the translator means reimplementing the equation compiler, including its splitting heuristics and its treatment of `Nat` literal patterns, and any divergence is silent. The corpus therefore requires rejection unless the translator works from the ALREADY-COMPILED `Expr` (Lean's `matcher` application), in which case the source has no overlapping patterns left and this case does not arise. A translator that reads surface `Syntax` is exactly the one that gets this wrong: **translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.**

Catches ignoring overlap that is only visible through *literal* patterns. In `bucket` the equations `| 0 => ..`, `| 1 => ..`, `| _ => ..` overlap the wildcard; the `Nat` literal/Peano bridge (reduction.rs:329-346) means the LOGOS scrutinee may be a `Literal::Nat`, so a translator that "specialises on literals" still has to decide an order and has nowhere to record it.

Catches treating a *non-overlapping* multi-column match as overlapping (and thus over-rejecting). `T04-007`'s `eqBool` and `sub2` have disjoint equations and MUST translate. The diagnostic must be driven by an actual overlap witness, not by the mere presence of more equations than constructors.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_OVERLAPPING_PATTERNS and writes no declaration. The diagnostic must include a concrete witness value matched by two equations — e.g. `pick 0 0`, matched by both `| 0, _` and `| _, 0`.
diag: E_OVERLAPPING_PATTERNS — must name the function, list the pair of equations that overlap and at least one value matched by both, and state that LOGOS matching is positional-by-constructor so first-match order has no carrier. Must NOT emit a `Match`.

cases.title: Wildcard `_` pattern — must be expanded to every remaining constructor
cases.lean: `_` catch-all pattern, `| _ => e`, wildcard in one column of a multi-column match
cases.target: A `Term::Match` whose `cases` vector has exactly one entry per constructor, with the wildcard's body REPLICATED (as a λ-telescope of the right arity) into every constructor slot the wildcard covered.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:487-492 (`Term::Match` has no wildcard, no default, no fall-through case); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:253-259 (`let constructors = ctx.get_constructors(..)` ; `cases.len() != constructors.len()` is `WrongNumberOfCases`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:262-265 (positional zip against the constructor list); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:778-830 (`compute_case_type` — each case's expected type is the constructor's remaining Π-telescope ending in `motive (ctor args…)`, so each replicated body must be re-wrapped with THAT constructor's field binders)
guards: Catches emitting one case for the enumerated patterns plus ONE case for the wildcard. For `isRed` below, `Color` has five constructors and the Lean source has two equations, so this gives `cases.len() == 2` against `expected: 5` — caught. But for `isNil`, `List` has exactly two constructors and the source has exactly two equations, one of which is a wildcard: the naive vector has the right LENGTH, and if the wildcard equation was written FIRST the two cases land in swapped constructor slots. The term typechecks (both branches are `Bool`) and `isNil [] ` returns `false`. Silent.

Catches forgetting to re-abstract the wildcard body over each constructor's fields. `compute_case_type` (type_checker.rs:778-830) expects the `cons` case to be `λhd. λtl. body`, and the `nil` case to be a bare `body`. Copying the same bare term into both slots fails for `cons` — or, if the body happens to already be a function of the right type, typechecks and means something else.

Catches expanding against the *Lean* constructor order rather than the LOGOS registration order. `get_constructors` returns them in the order `add_constructor` was called (context.rs:419), which is the translator's own choice; the expansion and the registration must use one single recorded order.
Catches wildcards in a non-leading column of a multi-column match (`| _, true => ..`) being expanded only at the outer layer. Each nesting level needs its own full expansion.
oracle: The emitted term typechecks; for each `Match` node `cases.len()` equals the constructor count of its own inductive; `normalize` agrees with Lean on EVERY constructor of each scrutinised inductive (not merely on the enumerated ones); and the loss record contains DEFAULT_BRANCH_SHARING with the pinned constructor list.
loss: DEFAULT_BRANCH_SHARING. Lean's `Expr` for a compiled wildcard shares one body (Lean's matcher lifts it into an auxiliary `match_i` constant or a `let`). The LOGOS `Term` is a TREE (LOGOS_FACTS: "LOGOS `Term` is a tree; sharing is lost"), so the body is duplicated k times. For a k-constructor inductive with a large default branch this multiplies term size by k, and since substitution is O(size) per binder comparison (type_checker.rs:1088) the cost is superlinear. Acceptable because the denotation is unchanged; must be recorded because it is how a translated file becomes unbuildable.

CATCH_ALL_STABILITY. The expansion is computed against the constructor list AT TRANSLATION TIME. If the Lean inductive later gains a constructor, Lean's `_` silently keeps covering it while the emitted LOGOS term does not — it simply has the wrong arity and stops typechecking. The loss record must pin the constructor list (names and order) the expansion was computed from.

cases.title: Dependent `match` with an explicit motive — LOGOS motive inference is Miller-only
cases.lean: match ... with (return clause / `(motive := ..)`), dependent elimination
cases.target: Term::Match { discriminant, motive: <an EXPLICIT `Term::Lambda` motive, never `Term::Hole`>, cases } — the translator must compute the motive itself from Lean's `Expr.app (matcherApp motive) ..` and emit it, not rely on LOGOS to infer it.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:487-492 (`motive` is a mandatory `Box<Term>` field of every `Match` — there is no "no return clause" form); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:204-250 (the motive must be either a `Π` whose domain is the discriminant's type, or a bare `Sort`, which is silently wrapped as the CONSTANT motive `λ_:I. T`); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:578-636 (`fill_match_motives` fills a `Term::Hole` motive only, and only by calling `infer_match_motive`); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:638-700 (`infer_match_motive` solves `?P disc =?= T` by ABSTRACTING the discriminant out of the EXPECTED type — the Miller-pattern solution — and errors with "cannot infer the motive of this `match`" when there is no expected type and the first case is a λ); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:294-340 (`try_pattern`: a Miller pattern requires the metavariable's arguments to be DISTINCT bound variables; a repeated or non-variable argument makes it `None`)
guards: Catches emitting `motive: Term::Hole` and hoping the LOGOS elaborator fills it. Two failure modes. (a) `fill_match_motives` is part of `elaborate`, NOT of the kernel: a `Hole` that reaches `infer_type` is `CannotInferHole` (type_checker.rs:313). (b) Worse, a `Hole` that survives into an emitted TYPE is matched against **anything** by `types_equal` (type_checker.rs:1594-1597), and that leniency leaks into `is_subtype`'s fast path (:1314) — so a translated theorem can typecheck against a type it does not have.

Catches relying on inference where the Miller condition fails. `infer_match_motive` abstracts the discriminant out of the expected type; when the discriminant is NOT a bare variable (e.g. `match f n with`), `try_pattern` (elaborate.rs:294-340) rejects the non-variable argument and the solution falls back to replacing occurrences syntactically. A discriminant that occurs in the expected type only up to definitional unfolding is then missed, and the inferred motive is constant where the source's was dependent — silently generalising the statement.

Catches computing the motive at the wrong sort. `derive_recursor` pins motive targets (recursor.rs:64-71) but `Match` does not — yet the large-elimination gate (type_checker.rs:275-288) *does*: a `Prop` discriminant may only eliminate into a larger sort if the inductive is a subsingleton per `is_subsingleton_prop` (type_checker.rs:1688-1716). A dependent match on a `Prop` whose motive lands in `Type` is accepted by Lean for `Acc`/`Eq`/`False` and must be checked against LOGOS's own, differently-implemented, subsingleton rule.

Catches emitting an indexed family's motive with the wrong arity. For an indexed inductive the motive must be `Π(indices…). Π(z : I params indices). Sort` (type_checker.rs:602-611); a motive that abstracts only the scrutinee gets the indices applied to it anyway (`:648-652`) and fails — or, if the index happens to be a `Sort`, typechecks meaninglessly.
oracle: The emitted `Match` has a non-`Hole` motive; the whole term contains no `Term::Hole`; it typechecks; and for each `Match` the inferred result type is the translation of Lean's. The loss record contains MOTIVE_PROVENANCE.
loss: MOTIVE_PROVENANCE. Lean's elaborated matcher carries the user's `return` clause (or the motive Lean synthesised) as a first-class argument, together with the information that it was user-written. In LOGOS the motive is just a term in the `Match` node; whether it came from the source or was reconstructed is not recorded, so a later re-elaboration may silently substitute a *different* motive that happens to typecheck (a constant one, say) and quietly weaken the definition's type.

CONSTANT_MOTIVE_COLLAPSE. `type_checker.rs:236-245` accepts a bare `Sort`-typed motive by wrapping it as `λ_:I. T`. A dependent Lean match whose motive *happens* to be constant on the emitted cases is therefore indistinguishable from a non-dependent one after translation. Acceptable (the terms are definitionally the same) but must be recorded, because the round-trip does not preserve dependency.

cases.title: `match h : e with` — the equation hypothesis has no carrier in LOGOS `Match`
cases.lean: match h : e with, `Expr` matchers whose motive is generalised over an `Eq` proof
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:487-492 (`Term::Match { discriminant, motive, cases }` — three fields; there is no hypothesis binder, no per-case proof argument, and no place to record that a case body is under an assumption); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:262-265 and :778-830 (`compute_case_type`: a case's expected type is exactly the constructor's remaining Π-telescope ending in `motive (ctor args…)` — the case binds the CONSTRUCTOR'S FIELDS and nothing else, so an extra `h : Eq I e (ctor …)` binder makes the case's arity wrong); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:612-678 (`infer_indexed_match` — same one-case-per- constructor discipline, and there is **no index unifier**: `:632-638` demands a case for every constructor even when its indices cannot match); kernel/src/prelude.rs:1440-1460 (`Eq` is an indexed inductive with two parameters and one index — it exists, but nothing in the `Match` rule ever builds an `Eq` proof and hands it to a case)
guards: The tempting wrong move is to **drop the hypothesis and emit the plain match**, because `h` is often unused. That is exactly backwards: when `h` IS used — as in `findSub` below, where the returned subtype value is `⟨y, h⟩` — dropping it leaves a free `Term::Var("h")` in the case body. LOGOS's representation is NAMED (term.rs:450), so that free variable is not a dangling de Bruijn index the kernel will notice; it resolves against whatever `h` is in scope. If an enclosing binder is also called `h` (very common — `h` is the universal hypothesis name), the term typechecks with a completely unrelated proof substituted in. That is a proof-library corruption, not a crash.

Catches "generalise the motive and pass `refl`". The sound-looking encoding is to use the motive `λx. Eq I e x → C` and apply the resulting match to `refl I e`. It does not work in LOGOS: the motive's domain must be the discriminant's type (type_checker.rs:213-219), which it still is, but the *cases* now have to produce functions `Eq I e (ctor …) → C`, and the discriminant `e` is generalised in the motive while the `Eq`'s left-hand side is not. There is no index unifier (type_checker.rs:612-678) to relate the two, so what the translator gets back is `Eq I e disc → C` applied to `refl I e` — which only typechecks when `disc` is definitionally `e`, i.e. only in the cases where the hypothesis is useless. Emitting it anyway produces a term that typechecks on the trivial instances and fails, opaquely, on exactly the ones that motivated the feature.

Catches "replace `h` with a `Term::Hole`". `types_equal` treats `Hole` as matching **anything** (type_checker.rs:1594-1597) and that leniency leaks into `is_subtype` (`:1314`), so the hole is accepted and the emitted declaration is a hole-carrying term in the library.

Catches "replace `h` with an axiom `Eq I e (ctor …)` via `add_declaration`" (context.rs:434). That axiom is FALSE for every other constructor of the same inductive, so the library becomes inconsistent — and `add_declaration` performs no check at all.

Catches over-rejection: a `match h : e with` whose `h` is provably unused in every case body is still `reject` under this case's verdict, because the translator cannot decide "unused" reliably after the equation compiler has run. A translator may degrade such a match only on a separate, explicitly-recorded path that proves `h` does not occur in the elaborated `Expr`.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_MATCH_EQUATION_HYPOTHESIS for each definition below and writes no declaration into the LOGOS context.
diag: E_MATCH_EQUATION_HYPOTHESIS — must name the function, name the hypothesis binder, and state that LOGOS's `Match` gives each case only the matched constructor's fields. Must NOT emit a `Match`.

cases.title: Incomplete `match` — LOGOS requires `cases.len() == constructor count`, always
cases.lean: non-exhaustive match, `nomatch`, `Empty.elim`, matches Lean accepts with fewer branches than the type has constructors
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:253-259 (`let constructors = ctx.get_constructors(..)`; `if cases.len() != constructors.len() { WrongNumberOfCases { expected, found } }`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:630-638 (`infer_indexed_match` repeats the same check and documents it: "Coverage: exactly one case per constructor, in registration order"); kernel/src/term.rs:487-492 (`cases: Vec<Term>` has no optionality and no default); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:313 (`Term::Hole` reaching `infer_type` is `CannotInferHole`) and :1593-1597 (`types_equal` treats `Hole` as matching ANYTHING)
guards: The tempting wrong move is to **pad the case vector with `Term::Hole`** so the length check passes. That is the single worst outcome in this tier: `types_equal` matches `Hole` against anything (type_checker.rs:1593-1597) and the leniency leaks into `is_subtype`'s fast path (:1314), so the padded term can typecheck against a type it does not have, and the hole is now inside a declaration in the library.

Catches padding with a *fabricated* inhabitant instead — e.g. `Lit(Nat 0)` for a missing `Nat`-valued case. It typechecks, it reduces, and it is a different function: `headBad`'s `nil` branch would return `0` where the Lean source had no branch at all, so a theorem proved about the Lean function is false about the translation. Nothing in the kernel can notice.

Catches padding with an `add_declaration` axiom (context.rs:434) of the branch's type. `add_declaration` is unchecked and produces an opaque constant, so the branch type gets an inhabitant by fiat — for a `Prop`-valued branch that is an outright inconsistency.

Catches the inverse over-rejection: `nomatch`/`Empty.elim` (zero constructors) and `False.elim` must **translate**, because `cases.len() == 0` genuinely equals the constructor count. A translator that rejects every "fewer branches than expected" match loses `ex falso`, which every proof library needs.

Catches mis-counting constructors after flattening. `get_constructors` is keyed on the FLAT `String` name (context.rs:419, LOGOS_FACTS "no namespaces"), so two Lean inductives whose names collide after flattening share one constructor list and the arity check compares against the wrong count — passing an incomplete match or failing a complete one. See T02-020.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_INCOMPLETE_MATCH on `vheadRefined`/`headBad`; emits no declaration for them; and does NOT reject `nomatchEmpty`, `absurdElim` or `vnilOnly`, all of which have `cases.len() == ctor count`.
diag: E_INCOMPLETE_MATCH — must name the inductive, list the constructors with no case, and state the required `cases.len()`. Must NOT emit a `Match` with a padded or placeholder case.
note: Lean itself refuses a genuinely non-exhaustive `match`, so the offending form cannot appear as live code in a file that must compile. It is given below as a comment, and the file provides the closest COMPILING neighbours: (a) `nomatch` / `Empty.elim`, where Lean supplies *zero* branches because the type has no constructors — which LOGOS accepts, since `cases.len() == 0 == ctor count`; and (b) `Vect`'s index-refined match, where Lean supplies *fewer* branches than `Vect` has constructors because index unification rules one out — which LOGOS does **not** accept, because `infer_indexed_match` has no index unifier (type_checker.rs:612-678 and LOGOS_FACTS). (b) is the live, compiling witness for this rejection. The overlap with T04-014 is deliberate and the two differ in obligation: T04-014 is `degrade` because the translator can SYNTHESISE the missing case (the indices make it unreachable, so any well-typed body will do); this case is `reject` for the situation where no such body can be built — see `headBad` below, whose missing `nil` case would have to inhabit `α` out of nothing.

cases.title: Impossible-case discharge — LOGOS has no index unification, so the case must be synthesised anyway
cases.lean: index-refined match, omitted constructor branches, `Nat.noConfusion`-style discharge, `absurd` in an unreachable branch
cases.target: A `Term::Match` with the FULL case vector: the Lean branches in constructor registration order, plus a SYNTHESISED, well-typed body for every constructor Lean ruled out by index unification.
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:612-678 (`infer_indexed_match`; :630-638 "Coverage: exactly one case per constructor, in registration order" — and there is no index unifier anywhere in the function); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:685-740 (`compute_indexed_case_type`: a case's expected type is the motive applied to THAT constructor's *declared* result indices, not to the discriminant's — so the "impossible" case is given a perfectly well-formed type and simply has to be inhabited); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:653-666 (the result type must infer to a `Sort`; this is the only soundness backstop, and it does not notice unreachable branches); kernel/src/context.rs:374 (`add_indexed_inductive(name, sort, num_params)` — the params/indices split is a declaration-time number, not a unifier)
guards: Catches synthesising the filler as `Term::Hole`. `types_equal` matches `Hole` against **anything** (type_checker.rs:1593-1597) and the leniency leaks into `is_subtype` (:1314), so the padded `Match` typechecks and a hole lands in the library. Never emit a `Hole`.

Catches synthesising the filler by recursion — the lazy fix of copying the *other* branch's body. In `vzipWith` below the other branch contains the recursive call, so the filler's argument is not a match-bound smaller variable of the guarding match and `verify_structural_arg_smaller` (termination.rs:378-395) rejects the whole definition. A correct Lean function becomes a build error.

Catches the case where the filler is NOT constructible. For a `Vect α (n+1) → α` the synthesised `nil` body must inhabit `α`, which is an arbitrary type. There is no sound filler, so the translator must fall back to rejection (T04-013) rather than inventing an axiom via `add_declaration` (context.rs:434) — an axiom of type `Π(α:Type 0). α` is a global inconsistency.

Catches getting the filler's TYPE wrong. `compute_indexed_case_type` (type_checker.rs:685-740) instantiates the constructor's leading `num_params` binders from the DISCRIMINANT's parameters and applies the motive to the CONSTRUCTOR's own result indices. A translator that applies the motive to the discriminant's indices instead builds the filler at the wrong type; for `vnilFill` that is `motive 0 nil` versus `motive (n+1) …`, and the two coincide only when `n` happens to be a literal — so the bug hides on small tests.

Catches setting `num_params` wrong on the inductive. `infer_indexed_match` is only reached when `disc_args.len() > num_params` (type_checker.rs:193-201); with the default "all arity is parameters" (`add_inductive`, context.rs:253) the indexed path is never taken, the plain `Match` rule requires the motive's domain to equal the discriminant's type, and the index is silently treated as a fixed parameter. See T03-005.
oracle: The emitted `Match` has `cases.len() == ctor count` for every node; the emitted term contains no `Term::Hole` and introduces no new axiom; it typechecks; `normalize` agrees with Lean on every reachable input; and the loss record contains UNREACHABILITY with the discharged constructor named.
loss: UNREACHABILITY. Lean's elaborated matcher records that a constructor is impossible at the scrutinee's indices; LOGOS's `Match` records only a case term. After translation the emitted body is indistinguishable from a reachable one, so (a) any later consistency audit cannot tell a synthesised filler from real code, and (b) if the indices are ever weakened the filler silently becomes live. The loss record must name the constructor, the index equation Lean discharged, and the filler's provenance.

NOCONFUSION_ABSENCE. Lean discharges such branches with `noConfusion`/`injection`, which LOGOS does not generate at all (LOGOS_FACTS: "no `casesOn`/`brecOn`/ `noConfusion`/`injection`"). The discharge *proof* is therefore dropped, not translated; only the filler term survives.

cases.title: `WellFounded.fix` / `Acc.rec` recursion — `Acc` is a type, recursion *through* it is not a LOGOS construct
cases.lean: WellFounded.fix, WellFounded.fixF, Acc.rec, Acc.ndrec, WellFoundedRecursion
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/prelude.rs:1354-1418 (`register_acc`: `Acc` is registered by `add_indexed_inductive("Acc", acc_ty, 2)` at :1379, `Acc_intro` at :1398, and `Acc_rec` is the AUTO-DERIVED eliminator `add_definition`ed at :1403-1405; `WellFounded` at :1407-1418 is a plain **abbreviation** `λA. λR. Π(x:A). Acc A R x`, not a recursion combinator); there is **no `WellFounded_fix`, no `WellFounded_fixF`, no `Acc_ndrec`** anywhere in the prelude — `Acc_rec` is the only elimination form; kernel/src/recursor.rs:60-72 (`derive_recursor` hard-codes the motive target; `Acc` is a one-constructor `Prop` whose only field is propositional, so `is_subsingleton_prop` (type_checker.rs:1688-1716) holds and the target is `Sort(Type 0)` — `Acc_rec` therefore **cannot eliminate into `Type 1+`**); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:328-339 (every `Fix` is gated on `check_termination`); kernel/src/termination.rs:378-400 (`verify_structural_arg_smaller` accepts a `smaller_than` variable or an APPLICATION HEADED BY ONE — the applied-smaller rule that makes recursion over an `Acc` proof terminate *when written as a `Fix` whose guarding `match` is on the `Acc` proof itself*)
guards: The distinction this case exists to make crisp: **`Acc` as a TYPE is fine; recursion THROUGH it is not.** `Acc Nat Nat.lt n` translates — it is an ordinary indexed inductive in the prelude. A *proof* of `WellFounded Nat.lt` translates — it is a term of the abbreviation's type. What does not translate is `WellFounded.fix wf F x`, because there is no `WellFounded_fix` global to apply and no way to add one: its body would itself have to be a well-founded recursion.

Catches the "just call `Acc_rec`" move. `Acc_rec` exists, so `Global("Acc_rec")` resolves and an application of it typechecks. But Lean's `WellFounded.fix F x` is `Acc.rec` at the motive `fun x _ => C x` with a step function that recurses through the accessibility *hypothesis*, and Lean's `Acc.rec` is universe-polymorphic in that motive. The LOGOS-derived `Acc_rec`'s motive target is pinned to `Sort(Type 0)` (recursor.rs:64-71), so a Lean well-founded definition producing anything in `Type 1+` has no counterpart — while one producing `Type 0` data typechecks and is a *different, delta-transparent* term that unfolds during `normalize` and burns the 10000-step fuel (reduction.rs:52-69) on every use.

Catches the "reconstruct it as a `Fix` over the `Acc` proof" move. This is the one encoding that can be made to pass the guard — `termination.rs:378-400` explicitly supports `rec (h y hr)` where `h` is `Acc_intro`'s match-bound functional field — but it is a *hand-written LOGOS proof*, not a translation: the translator would have to synthesise the accessibility argument `hr : R y x` at every call site, and that argument is exactly the `decreasing_by` obligation LOGOS has no carrier for (T04-005). Emitting the `Fix` without it leaves a free variable or a `Hole` in the recursive call.

Catches silently dropping the well-foundedness proof and emitting a structural `Fix` on whatever binder happens to be inductive. `extract_structural_param` falls back to "the first inductive-typed binder" (termination.rs:145-149), so `wfDiv` below — whose first binder is a `Nat` — would be checked as a structural recursion on that `Nat` and rejected with a confusing `TerminationViolation` pointing at the wrong argument.

Catches treating `WellFounded` as an inductive. It is an `add_definition` (prelude.rs:1407-1418), so it is delta-TRANSPARENT: `Match`ing on a `WellFounded` value fails with `NotAnInductive` after normalisation exposes the `Π`.
