oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NO_WELL_FOUNDED_RECURSION for every definition below that *recurses*, and writes no declaration for them. It must NOT reject `accIsAType` or `ltWf`, which merely mention `Acc`/`WellFounded` as types.
diag: E_NO_WELL_FOUNDED_RECURSION — must name the function, name the combinator it used (`WellFounded.fix` / `Acc.rec`), and state that LOGOS provides `Acc` as an inductive and `Acc_rec` as a derived eliminator but has no fixpoint combinator over a well-foundedness proof. Must NOT emit a `Fix` or an `Acc_rec` application.

cases.title: `brecOn` / `below` — Lean's course-of-values machinery has no LOGOS generator
cases.lean: Nat.brecOn, Nat.below, List.brecOn, binductionOn, the auto-generated course-of-values recursors Lean uses to compile structural recursion
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/recursor.rs:36-48 (`derive_recursor(ctx, ind)` is the ONLY generator in the kernel and it produces exactly one thing: `(recursor_type, recursor_term)` for `I_rec`. There is no `derive_brec_on`, no `derive_below`, no `derive_cases_on`); kernel/src/recursor.rs:60-72 (even that single recursor's motive target is hard-coded, so it is not a drop-in for Lean's universe-polymorphic `brecOn`); kernel/src/context.rs:253,374,419,545 (the only inductive-registration entry points — nothing generates auxiliary eliminators); kernel/src/term.rs:487-509 (`Match` is the primitive and `Fix` the only recursion form: course-of-values recursion has to be re-expressed, not translated); kernel/src/termination.rs:403-440 (`check_match_cases_guarded` marks only the DIRECT constructor fields of the guarding match as smaller — there is no notion of "every subterm reachable below", which is exactly what `below` packages)
guards: This case fires on almost every real Lean file, because `brecOn` is what the equation compiler EMITS: a translator reading `Expr`s sees `Nat.brecOn` wherever the source wrote `| 0 => .. | n+1 => ..`. The correct response is not to translate `brecOn` but to recognise the pattern and emit `Fix` + `Match` (T04-001). A translator that instead emits `Global("Nat_brecOn")` produces a term referring to a name `get_global` (context.rs:449) cannot resolve — and the failure surfaces at the first USE, not at the declaration, so the diagnostic blames the wrong file.

Catches "just declare `Nat_brecOn` as an axiom" to make the name resolve. `add_declaration` (context.rs:434) is unchecked and opaque, so the constant never reduces: every `rfl` in the source that relied on the recursion computing silently stops holding, and the translator has axiomatised the recursion scheme itself. For `below`, whose type is a *Sort*-valued family, the axiom additionally asserts a type former with no constructors, so nothing can ever inhabit it.

Catches "synthesise `below` as a nested product". `below` for `Nat` is `fun n => PProd (motive n) (Nat.below n)`-shaped — a recursively defined type family built from `PProd`/`PUnit`, and **`Prod`, `PProd`, `Sigma`, `PSigma` and `Unit`'s Lean counterparts are all absent from the LOGOS prelude** (LOGOS_FACTS, "Absent entirely"). Declaring them opens T03-022/T11-013 (unchecked `add_inductive`) and the universe questions of T01-007, none of which this case is licensed to answer.

Catches `casesOn` being lumped in. `I.casesOn` is *also* not generated, but it is a strictly easier problem: it is a `Match` with a constant motive and no recursion, so a translator may handle it — as a separately recorded path — while still rejecting `brecOn`. Rejecting both with the same diagnostic makes the conformance report uninformative.

Catches the "strong induction" form. `Nat.strongRecOn` / `Nat.strongInductionOn` are `brecOn`-derived in Lean and are the usual way a Mathlib-style proof recurses; they carry the same rejection, and a translator that special-cases `brecOn` but not these lets them through as unresolvable globals.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NO_COURSE_OF_VALUES_RECURSOR for every definition below, emits no declaration for them, and emits no `Global` whose name contains `brecOn`, `below`, or `binductionOn` anywhere in its output for the whole corpus.
diag: E_NO_COURSE_OF_VALUES_RECURSOR — must name the Lean constant (`I.brecOn`, `I.below`, `I.binductionOn`) and state that LOGOS generates only `I_rec` via `derive_recursor`. Must NOT emit a `Global` referring to a `brecOn`/`below` name.

cases.title: Equation lemmas (`f.eq_def`, `f.eq_1`) — not generated by LOGOS
cases.lean: f.eq_def, f.eq_1 … f.eq_n, `simp [f]`, `rw [f]`, `unfold f`
cases.target: The `Fix` + `Match` definition alone (T04-001). Every Lean proof step that cited an equation lemma must be re-expressed as an appeal to LOGOS's *definitional* unfolding — `add_definition` is delta-transparent (context.rs:442) and `Fix`/`Match` reduce in `normalize` — i.e. as `refl`/`simp`/`decide` rather than as a rewrite by a named lemma.
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:442 (`add_definition(name, ty, body)` — a delta-TRANSPARENT definition; nothing else is recorded and no auxiliary lemma is produced); kernel/src/context.rs:434 (`add_declaration` is the only other declaration form, and it is an axiom); there is no equation-lemma generator anywhere in `crates/logicaffeine_kernel/src` — `recursor::derive_recursor` (recursor.rs:36) is the sole derived-artifact producer and it emits only `I_rec`; kernel/src/reduction.rs:48-69 (`normalize` is the unfolding mechanism, with a hard fuel of 10000 and a SILENT partial return when it is exhausted); LOGOS_FACTS, Surface A tactic list (`simp`/0 — **no lemma-list argument**; `rewrite`/1 takes a named hypothesis and rewrites EVERY occurrence)
guards: Catches emitting `Global("dbl_eq_def")` because the Lean `Expr` mentioned `dbl.eq_def`. `get_global` (context.rs:449) returns `None` and the failure lands at the use site, arbitrarily far from the definition.

Catches the "fix it with an axiom" move: `add_declaration("dbl_eq_def", <the equation's type>)`. `add_declaration` is unchecked (context.rs:434), so this asserts an equation nobody verified. For a correct equation it is merely redundant; for a mis-translated one it *entrenches the mistranslation as an axiom*, and every later proof that "works" is evidence of nothing.

Catches assuming a LOGOS `simp` can take the definition as a lemma. The script `simp` is **arity 0** and has no lemma-list argument (LOGOS_FACTS, Surface A); the literate surface's `simp` likewise. `rw`/`rewrite` takes a **named hypothesis**, not a term and not a global. So `rw [dbl]` has no mechanical counterpart — it must become `simp`, `decide`, or `refl` relying on delta/iota, and whether that succeeds is a property of the goal, not a mechanical rewrite.

Catches relying on unfolding without budgeting for it. Because there are no equation lemmas, every appeal to a definition's behaviour goes through `normalize`, which has a hard fuel of 10000 and **silently returns a partially reduced term** when it runs out (reduction.rs:52-69). A Lean proof that used one targeted `rw [f]` becomes a full normalisation in LOGOS, and on a large term it can silently fail to close.

Catches treating `f.eq_def` and `f.eq_1` as interchangeable. `eq_def` unfolds to the whole `match`; `eq_i` is one branch, possibly with side conditions. Only the former has a definitional counterpart.
oracle: The emitted term typechecks; the translator's output contains no `Global` whose name ends in `_eq_def` or `_eq_<n>` and introduces no axiom for one; every Lean proof step citing an equation lemma is either re-expressed definitionally or reported; and the loss record contains EQUATION_LEMMA_NAMES.
loss: EQUATION_LEMMA_NAMES. Lean's `f.eq_def` and per-equation `f.eq_1 … f.eq_n` are real constants with real statements, citable by name from any other module. After translation they do not exist. Any Lean proof of the form `rw [f]`, `simp [f]`, `unfold f`, or `exact f.eq_2 ..` has no name to cite. This is acceptable because the *content* survives definitionally — `f args` and its unfolding are definitionally equal in LOGOS, so the facts remain provable — but the proof text must change, and a translator that leaves the citation in place emits an unresolvable `Global`.

EQUATION_GRANULARITY. Lean generates one lemma per *source equation*; LOGOS's unfolding is per *constructor case*. A Lean source with overlapping or nested patterns has equation lemmas whose statements carry side conditions (`n ≠ 0`, "and the earlier patterns did not match"). Those side conditions have no LOGOS counterpart at all, because the pattern structure they refer to was compiled away (T04-008). Where the source cites such a conditional equation lemma, the case is `reject`, not `degrade`.

cases.title: Recursion Lean accepts structurally that the Giménez guard rejects
cases.lean: structural recursion through nested patterns (`| n+2 => f n`), through a `let` alias of a smaller variable, and with the recursive function used as a value
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/termination.rs:262-280 (`check_guarded`'s `Match` arm: constructor binders are marked structurally smaller **only** when the discriminant is the structural parameter and `struct_param_live` holds; a match on any other scrutinee falls through to ":274 Not matching on structural param - just recurse normally", which does NOT extend `smaller_than`); kernel/src/termination.rs:378-395 (`verify_structural_arg_smaller`: the recursive call's structural argument must be headed by a variable in `smaller_than` — nothing else is accepted); kernel/src/termination.rs:316-327 (the `Let` arm: "The value is NOT registered as smaller (the conservative v1 guard — a `fix` whose recursive call passes a let-alias of a smaller variable is rejected)"); kernel/src/termination.rs:329-347 (a bare occurrence of the recursive name is a `TerminationViolation`: "recursive name '{}' occurs as a first-class value, not applied to a structurally-smaller argument"); kernel/src/termination.rs:182-196 (`enter_binder`: an inner binder that shadows the structural parameter sets `struct_param_live = false`, so a later match on that name stops guarding); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:336 (there is no admission path around the guard)
guards: This is the case that makes "Lean accepted it, so it is structural" false. `halve` below is *textbook* structural recursion in Lean — `brecOn` gives it every subterm of `n` at once. Translated literally it becomes `Match n [c0, λm. Match m [c1, λk. … rec k …]]`, and the inner match is on `m`, not on the structural parameter `n`. Per termination.rs:265-272 the inner match does not extend `smaller_than`, so `k` is unmarked and the whole definition is rejected with a `TerminationViolation`. Every `| n+2 => …` function in a Lean library hits this.

Catches the "helpfully hoist it into a `let`" move — binding the smaller variable to a name for readability. The `Let` arm (termination.rs:316-327) deliberately does not propagate smallness, so `letAlias` below is rejected where the identical inline form would pass. A translator that introduces `let`s during lowering (for sharing, say — see T00-022) can turn a *passing* definition into a failing one.

Catches passing the recursive function as a value. Lean's nested recursion over a container — `| .node ts => 1 + (ts.map roseSize).foldl (·+·) 0`, shown commented below — hands the recursive name to `List.map`. The `Var` leaf at termination.rs:334-347 rejects a bare occurrence of a block member outright, so the literal translation is refused; and the tempting workaround, eta-expanding to `fun x => roseSize x`, does not help, because the eta-expanded occurrence is still a bare `Var` under a λ whose argument is not a smaller variable. The only LOGOS-legal shape is the mutual `Tree`/`Forest` pair of T04-003, which is a *re-expression*, not a translation, and must be reported as such.

Catches the *shadowing* failure, which is the silent one and is entirely self-inflicted. `enter_binder` (termination.rs:182-196) clears `struct_param_live` when an inner binder reuses the structural parameter's name, and termination.rs:265-272 then refuses to treat the guarding match as guarding. Because LOGOS `Var`s are NAMED (term.rs:450) while Lean's are de Bruijn, a translator that reuses Lean's binder-name *hints* can emit two nested binders called `n` from a Lean term that had no collision at all. The recursion is then rejected and the cause — a name collision the translator introduced — appears nowhere in the diagnostic. Binders must be freshened at emit time (see T00-004).
Catches "just wrap it with `termination_by`". There is no measure-based path (T04-004); the guard is the only admission rule.

Catches over-rejection: a translator that responds by rejecting ALL nested-pattern recursion loses T04-001's `double` and T04-002's `len`, which are single-level and must translate. The diagnostic must name the specific unmarked variable.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_GIMENEZ_GUARD_STRICTER for every definition below, naming the failing variable, and writes no declaration. It must NOT reject the single-level structural definitions of T04-001/T04-002.
diag: E_GIMENEZ_GUARD_STRICTER — must name the function, name the argument the recursion runs on, and state which of the guard's conditions fails (not marked smaller / let-aliased / first-class occurrence / shadowed structural parameter). Must NOT emit a `Fix`.

cases.title: `if then else` — `Bool` branching is a `Match`; `Prop` branching goes through `Decidable`
cases.lean: if c then a else b, `cond`, `ite`, Decidable instance resolution
cases.target: For a `Bool` condition: `Match { discriminant: <cond>, motive: <λ_:Bool. C>, cases: [<false case>, <true case>] }` in `Bool`'s registration order. For a `Prop` condition: a `Match` on the resolved `Decidable p` instance, `cases: [<isTrue case, λhp. a>, <isFalse case, λhnp. b>]` — LOGOS has **no `ite` global**, so the branch must be emitted as a match on the instance itself.
evidence: kernel/src/prelude.rs:777-794 (`Decidable : Π(p:Prop). Type 0` is registered by `add_indexed_inductive("Decidable", .., 1)` at :781, with `isTrue : Π(p:Prop). p → Decidable p` at :783 and `isFalse : Π(p:Prop). Not p → Decidable p` at :786); kernel/src/prelude.rs:791-794 (`Decidable_rec` is the auto-DERIVED eliminator, `add_definition`ed — not a primitive); kernel/src/prelude.rs:796-815 (`decide : Π(p:Prop). Decidable p → Bool`, defined as a `Decidable_rec` application — `isTrue ↝ true`, `isFalse ↝ false`); kernel/src/prelude.rs:923-1021 and :1023-1160 (`decEqBool` and `decEqNat` are the ONLY `Decidable` instances in the prelude); kernel/src/context.rs:184 (`add_instance` is a flat `Vec<(Term, Term)>`; resolution is first-match-wins); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:255-259 (positional, two-case coverage for `Bool`); there is **no `ite` and no `cond` global anywhere in prelude.rs** — the branch has no combinator to call
guards: Catches emitting the cases in the wrong order. `Bool` is registered `true` then `false` (LOGOS_FACTS, prelude inductive list), and `Decidable` is registered `isTrue` then `isFalse` (prelude.rs:783,786). Lean's surface `if c then a else b` puts the "then" branch first, which HAPPENS to agree with both registration orders — so a translator that copies source order looks correct. It stops being correct for `if ¬c then …`, for `cond`'s `Bool`-first argument convention, and for any inductive whose LOGOS registration order the translator chose differently. Both branches have the same type, so the kernel accepts the swap and the function is silently negated.

Catches emitting `Global("ite")`. There is no `ite` in the LOGOS prelude; `get_global` (context.rs:449) returns `None` and the failure appears at the use site. The `Decidable` instance must be scrutinised directly, or `decide p inst` must be used to get a `Bool` and then matched.

Catches conflating the two branchings. `if (b : Bool) then …` matches on `b`; `if (p : Prop) [inst : Decidable p] then …` matches on `inst`. Emitting a match on `decide p inst` instead of on `inst` loses the proofs `hp : p` and `hnp : ¬p` that `isTrue`/`isFalse` carry — which is exactly what T04-020's `dite` needs. It also inserts an extra delta step through `decide`'s `Decidable_rec` body (prelude.rs:796-815), which counts against `normalize`'s 10000 fuel (reduction.rs:52-69).

Catches assuming Lean's `Decidable` instance translates. The prelude has exactly TWO instances, `decEqBool` and `decEqNat` (prelude.rs:923-1021, :1023-1160). A Lean `if x < y then …` on `Nat` needs `Nat.decLt`, which has no LOGOS counterpart; the translator must either emit a `Decidable` instance of its own or reject. And because `add_instance` is a flat `Vec` resolved first-match-wins (context.rs:184), registering a second instance for an already-covered type silently shadows or is silently shadowed, with no coherence check — see T07-008.

Catches losing the `Decidable` *argument*. `Decidable p` is an indexed inductive with ONE parameter (prelude.rs:781), so a `Match` on an instance takes the indexed path (type_checker.rs:193-201) and each case's type is computed by `compute_indexed_case_type` (:685-740) against the constructor's own result index. A case emitted as a bare term instead of `λh. body` fails, and a case emitted with the wrong arity may typecheck when `p` is itself a function type.
oracle: The emitted term typechecks; `normalize` agrees with Lean on both truth values of each condition; the emitted `Match` on a `Bool` has its cases in LOGOS's `Bool` registration order; and the output contains no `Global("ite")` or `Global("cond")`.

cases.title: `dite` — `if h : c then … else …` binds the decision's proof in each branch
cases.lean: dite, `if h : c then a h else b h`, Decidable.byCases
cases.target: Match { discriminant: <the resolved `Decidable p` instance>, motive: <λ_ : Decidable p. C>, cases: [ λhp  : p.     <then branch, with `h := hp`>, λhnp : Not p. <else branch, with `h := hnp`> ] } — in `Decidable`'s registration order `isTrue`, `isFalse` (prelude.rs:783,786).
evidence: kernel/src/prelude.rs:781-786 (`Decidable` is an indexed inductive with ONE parameter; `isTrue : Π(p:Prop). p → Decidable p` carries the PROOF of `p`, and `isFalse : Π(p:Prop). Not p → Decidable p` carries the refutation — these fields are precisely the `h` that `dite` binds); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:612-678 (`infer_indexed_match`) and :685-740 (`compute_indexed_case_type`: each case's expected type is the constructor's remaining Π-telescope — here `Π(hp : p). motive …` and `Π(hnp : Not p). motive …` — so the branch bodies must be λ-abstractions, not bare terms); kernel/src/prelude.rs:820-910 (`of_decide_eq_true`, PROVEN from `Decidable_rec`, is the only bridge back from a `Bool` to a proof — the long way round that `dite` avoids by matching on the instance directly); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:275-288 (large elimination: `Decidable` is `Type 0`-valued (prelude.rs:781), NOT a `Prop`, so eliminating it into `Type` is unrestricted — which is exactly why `dite` can return data); kernel/src/context.rs:184 (`add_instance`: flat `Vec`, first-match-wins)
guards: Catches erasing the proof binder. A translator that lowers `dite` the same way it lowers `ite` (T04-019) emits case bodies as bare terms instead of `λhp. …` / `λhnp. …`. `compute_indexed_case_type` then reports an arity mismatch — unless the branch body happens to already be a function, in which case the term typechecks and the binder `h` in the source body becomes a FREE `Term::Var`. Because LOGOS `Var`s are NAMED (term.rs:450), that free `h` silently resolves against any enclosing binder called `h`, and `h` is the most common hypothesis name in existence. The result is a well-typed declaration whose proof obligation was discharged by an unrelated hypothesis.

Catches routing through `decide`. `decide p inst : Bool` (prelude.rs:796-815) throws away both `hp` and `hnp`; a translator that matches on the `Bool` then has no proof to give the `then` branch and must recover one via `of_decide_eq_true` (prelude.rs:820-910) — which needs an `Eq Bool (decide p inst) true`, i.e. exactly the `match h : e with` equation hypothesis that LOGOS cannot express (T04-012). So the `Bool` route is a dead end, not merely a slower one.

Catches branch-order inversion. `Decidable` registers `isTrue` first (prelude.rs:783), matching Lean's then-first surface order — so a source-order copy is accidentally right here and wrong the moment the translator registers the constructors in a different order or meets `Decidable.byCases`, whose argument order is the opposite. The two cases have *different* types (`p → C` vs `¬p → C`), so a swap usually fails loudly — but when `p` is itself a negation (`¬q`) the two become confusable and the swap typechecks.

Catches dropping the `Not p` case's argument type. `Not p` must be emitted as `Π(_:p). False`, not as an opaque global: there is no `Not` primitive, and `isFalse`'s field type (prelude.rs:786) is what the case must be checked against.

Catches assuming the instance exists. The prelude has exactly two `Decidable` instances, `decEqBool` and `decEqNat` (prelude.rs:923-1021, :1023-1160). `safeDiv` below needs a decision for `m = 0` on `Nat` (available via `decEqNat`) but `firstBig` needs one for `<` (not available). Resolution is first-match-wins over a flat `Vec` (context.rs:184) with no coherence check, so registering a competing instance silently changes which proof term ends up in the branch — and since the proof is a `Prop` inhabitant, definitional proof irrelevance (type_checker.rs:1547-1567) will often hide the difference.
oracle: The emitted term typechecks; both case bodies are `Term::Lambda`s whose binder types are the translations of `p` and `Not p`; the emitted term contains no free `Term::Var` for the source's `h`; `normalize` agrees with Lean on both truth values; and the output contains no `Global("dite")`.

cases.title: Implicit binders `{x : A}` — a `ParamKind`, not a term-level distinction
cases.lean: {x : A} implicit binder, implicit argument insertion, `binderInfo`
cases.target: An ordinary `Term::Pi { param: "α", .. }` — implicitness is NOT in the term — plus `Context::set_binder_kinds("idf", vec![ParamKind::Implicit, ParamKind::Explicit])`.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:464-469 (`Term::Pi { param, param_type, body_type }` — there is no binder-info field; implicit and explicit Pis are the same term); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1016-1027 (`ParamKind::{Explicit, Implicit, Instance}` — "how a function parameter is supplied during elaboration"); kernel/src/context.rs:199-206 (`set_binder_kinds(name, kinds)` / `binder_kinds(name)` — a per-GLOBAL, positional `Vec<ParamKind>`); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1029-1045 (`elaborate_app`: a fresh metavariable is inserted for each `Implicit` position; `Instance` positions are DEFERRED until the explicit arguments have been unified); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:137-139 (metavariables are `Term::Var` names beginning with `?`, and must be fully instantiated before the kernel sees the term)
guards: **Translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** After Lean elaborates, every implicit argument is already present in the `Expr` as an ordinary `app`. A translator working on `Syntax` has to re-derive which positions were implicit and re-run insertion; a translator working on `Expr` gets them for free and only needs `set_binder_kinds` so that *LOGOS-side* elaboration of hand-written terms behaves. This case is the simplest instance of that rule and the rest of Tier 5 is variations on it.

Catches omitting `set_binder_kinds` entirely. Nothing breaks immediately, because the emitted `Expr`-derived applications are fully explicit. It breaks later: any LOGOS-side term that applies the global with only its explicit arguments — a proof script, a hand-written lemma, another translated declaration that went through `elaborate` — gets `binder_kinds(name) == None` (context.rs:206), no metavariables are inserted, and the first explicit argument is checked against the IMPLICIT parameter's type. For `idf` that means `α` receives a value instead of a type.

Catches recording the kinds with the wrong ARITY or in the wrong ORDER. `binder_kinds` is a positional `Vec` (context.rs:201) with no names attached; Lean's `{α : Type} (a : α)` and `(a : α) {α : Type}` differ only in that vector. An off-by-one silently makes an explicit parameter implicit, and then `elaborate_app` inserts a metavariable where the caller's argument should have gone, shifting every later argument by one.

Catches leaving a metavariable in the output. If the translator lets LOGOS's own elaborator solve an implicit and does not call `instantiate` (elaborate.rs:143-186) before handing the term to the kernel, a `Term::Var("?m0")` reaches `infer_type` and is treated as an ordinary free variable — it will either fail lookup or, if some binder is literally named `?m0`, resolve to it.

Catches conflating implicit-ness with erasure. Lean's implicits are *inferred*, not *erased*: `@idf Nat 3` and `idf 3` elaborate to the same `Expr`. A translator that drops implicit arguments from the emitted application produces a `Term::App` spine of the wrong length, and `infer_type`'s `Pi` rule (type_checker.rs:156-167) then substitutes the wrong argument into the body type.
oracle: The emitted `Pi` chain matches the translation of Lean's type exactly (implicitness is invisible); `ctx.binder_kinds(name)` equals the Lean declaration's binder-info vector, position for position; the emitted term contains no `Term::Var` whose name starts with `?`; and a LOGOS-side `elaborate_app` of the global with only its explicit arguments reproduces the fully-applied term.

cases.title: Strict implicit `⦃x : A⦄` — LOGOS has no strict-implicit `ParamKind`
cases.lean: ⦃x : A⦄ / {{x : A}} strict implicit binder, BinderInfo.strictImplicit
cases.target: `ParamKind::Implicit` for the strict-implicit position, plus a loss record. The TERM is unaffected: `Term::Pi` carries no binder info at all.
evidence: kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1016-1027 (`pub enum ParamKind { Explicit, Implicit, Instance }` — exactly three variants; there is no `StrictImplicit`); kernel/src/term.rs:464-469 (`Term::Pi` has no binder-info field, so the distinction cannot live in the term either); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1029-1045 (`elaborate_app` inserts a fresh metavariable for EVERY `Implicit` position unconditionally — there is no "only if a later explicit argument follows" condition, which is precisely what strict-implicit means); kernel/src/context.rs:199-206 (`set_binder_kinds` stores the `Vec<ParamKind>`; a strict implicit has nowhere to be recorded)
guards: **Translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** Strict implicit is a pure *elaboration* annotation: after Lean has elaborated, the `Expr` contains the argument explicitly, and `Expr.forallE`'s `BinderInfo` is only a hint. A translator on `Syntax` must reimplement Lean's "insert only before an explicit argument" rule; a translator on `Expr` only has to decide what to write into `set_binder_kinds` and record the loss.

Catches promoting `⦃⦄` to `Explicit` instead of `Implicit` "to be safe". That changes the ARITY every LOGOS-side caller must supply: `elaborate_app` (elaborate.rs:1029-1045) consumes `explicit_args` positionally against the kinds vector, so the caller's first real argument is checked against the promoted parameter's type. For `memOf` below that means a `Nat` is checked against `Type`.

Catches silently succeeding. `Term::Pi` is identical either way (term.rs:464-469), so the emitted term typechecks and round-trips perfectly; the ONLY observable difference is in `binder_kinds`. A translator that compares emitted terms to decide whether information was lost will conclude nothing was lost. The loss record is the only evidence, which is exactly why `degrade` requires it.

Catches losing the distinction between the *two* Lean spellings `⦃x : A⦄` and `{{x : A}}`, which are the same binder — a translator that treats them as different kinds emits two different `ParamKind` vectors for the same declaration depending on how it was written.

Catches demoting in a dependent telescope and breaking solvability. In `memPair` the strict implicit `β` is mentioned by a LATER explicit binder's type; once promoted to eager `Implicit`, `elaborate_app` inserts `?β` before that binder has been seen, and `?β` is only solved if the expected-type pass (`elaborate_app_against`, elaborate.rs:1046-1080) runs — which it does only when an expected type is supplied. Unapplied occurrences leave `?β` unsolved.
oracle: The emitted `Pi` chain is identical to what T05-001's eager-implicit translation would produce; `binder_kinds` records `Implicit` at the strict-implicit position; and the loss record contains STRICT_IMPLICIT_DEMOTION naming the declaration and the position.
loss: STRICT_IMPLICIT_DEMOTION. Lean distinguishes `{x : A}` (insert eagerly) from `⦃x : A⦄` (insert only when a later explicit argument is supplied). LOGOS has one implicit kind, which behaves like `{x : A}`. Demoting `⦃⦄` to `{}` changes the ELABORATION BEHAVIOUR of partially-applied occurrences: `f` alone now has its strict implicit solved by a metavariable that nothing constrains, instead of remaining a function awaiting the argument. This is acceptable for the *fully applied* occurrences that dominate a translated library — they are already fully explicit in the `Expr` — and unacceptable for any LOGOS-side term that mentions the global unapplied, which the loss record must flag.

ETA_SENSITIVITY. The classic use of `⦃⦄` is on a coercion-like or membership-like function so that `f` used as a value does not eagerly instantiate. After demotion, `Term::Var("?m")` appears where the source had a genuine binder, and `unify_in`'s eta rule (elaborate.rs:254-268) may then unify it with something the source would have kept abstract.

cases.title: Instance implicit `[Foo A]` — `ParamKind::Instance` and a flat, first-match instance list
cases.lean: [Foo A] instance-implicit binder, typeclass instance synthesis, `inferInstance`
cases.target: An ordinary `Term::Pi` for the instance parameter (no binder info in the term), plus `set_binder_kinds(name, [.., ParamKind::Instance, ..])` and one `Context::add_instance(<class type>, <instance value>)` per Lean `instance`.
evidence: kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1016-1027 (`ParamKind::Instance` — "resolved from the Context's instance database, but only AFTER the explicit arguments have been processed, so any metavariable in the class type is solved first"); kernel/src/context.rs:184-188 (`add_instance(ty, value)` pushes onto a flat `Arc<Vec<(Term, Term)>>`) and :211-214 (`instances()` returns the slice — resolution is a linear scan, FIRST MATCH WINS, with no priority and no coherence check); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1046-1080 (`elaborate_app_against`: the expected-type pass runs BEFORE instance resolution, so the class's type variable can be fixed by the surrounding context); kernel/src/term.rs:464-469 (the term itself is just a `Pi`); kernel/src/context.rs:271-369 (`add_structure` — a Lean `class` is a structure plus an instance registration; see T07-001)
guards: **Translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** After elaboration the instance argument is an ordinary `Expr.app` carrying the *resolved* instance term. A translator on `Syntax` must re-run instance synthesis against LOGOS's flat list — which has different resolution semantics (first-match, no priorities, no coherence) — and will pick a different instance whenever more than one matches. Taking the resolved instance from the `Expr` sidesteps the whole question for the translated declarations; `add_instance` is then only needed so LOGOS-side terms elaborate.

Catches recording the position as `Implicit` instead of `Instance`. Both insert a metavariable, so simple cases work — but `Implicit` positions are solved by unification ONLY, so an instance that no argument's type pins (`defaultOf` below, where the class's type variable comes from the expected type) is left as an unsolved `Term::Var("?inst")`. `Instance` positions are deliberately deferred (elaborate.rs:1016-1027) so that resolution runs after the explicit arguments and the expected type have constrained the class type.

Catches instance-order sensitivity. `add_instance` appends to a flat `Vec` (context.rs:184-188) and resolution is first-match-wins with no priority mechanism. Lean resolves by priority and by most-recently-declared-first within a priority. A translator that registers instances in *source* order therefore reverses Lean's preference wherever two instances overlap. The emitted term typechecks either way, because both instances have the class type — the difference only shows up in what the function COMPUTES. `Sizeable Nat` versus an overlapping `Sizeable Nat` below is exactly that.

Catches forgetting that a Lean `class` needs `add_structure` (context.rs:271-369) before `add_instance` can mention its type. `add_structure` hard-codes the structure's sort to `Type 0` (context.rs:300-303), so a class in `Type u` for `u ≥ 1` or in `Prop` cannot be registered at all — see T03-012 and T07-011. A translator that registers the instance without the class silently has an instance whose type mentions an unresolvable `Global`.

Catches dropping the instance argument from the emitted application because "it is implicit". The `Expr` has it; the `Pi` expects it; omitting it makes the spine one argument short and `infer_type`'s `Pi` rule (type_checker.rs:156-167) substitutes the next argument into the wrong binder.

Catches an instance parameter whose class type mentions a LATER explicit binder. Because instance resolution is deferred to after the explicit pass, that works in LOGOS — but only if the kinds vector positions it correctly; an off-by-one makes the deferral apply to the wrong slot.
oracle: The emitted `Pi` chain matches the translation of Lean's type; `binder_kinds` has `Instance` at exactly the instance-implicit positions; each Lean `instance` produced one `add_instance` call, in a recorded order; the emitted term contains no `?`-named `Term::Var`; and `normalize` of each example agrees with Lean.

cases.title: `@f` — explicit-all application is a surface notation that vanishes in the `Expr`
cases.lean: @f, @id, explicit-all application, `Expr.app` spines
cases.target: The same left-nested `Term::App` spine that the non-`@` form produces: `App(App(Global("idf"), Global("Nat")), Lit(Nat 3))`. There is nothing to emit for the `@` itself.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:478 (`App(Box<Term>, Box<Term>)` — binary and left-nested; an application carries no record of how its arguments were supplied); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:144-170 (the `App` rule: the function's type is whnf'd to a `Pi`, the argument is checked against `param_type`, and the result is `substitute(body_type, param, arg)` — the same rule for every argument regardless of binder kind); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1029-1045 (`elaborate_app` is what CONSUMES `binder_kinds`; an already-explicit spine never goes through it); kernel/src/context.rs:199-206 (`binder_kinds` is per-global and is not consulted by the kernel at all)
guards: **Translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** `@f a b` and `f b` elaborate to the *same* `Expr`; the `@` exists only to suppress insertion. A translator on `Expr` has literally nothing to do for this case — which is the point: it is the cheapest demonstration that the `Syntax`-level surface of Tier 5 is noise. A translator on `Syntax` must implement `@` as a mode flag threaded through its own reimplementation of argument insertion, and every divergence from Lean's rules is a silent mistranslation.

Catches emitting `set_binder_kinds` as though `@` changed the DECLARATION. `@` is a property of a use site, not of the definition; a translator that records `[Explicit, Explicit]` for `idf` because it saw `@idf Nat 3` makes every *other* call site in the library wrong, since LOGOS-side elaboration will then refuse to insert the type argument.

Catches spine-direction errors. `Term::App` is binary and LEFT-nested (term.rs:478), so `@f a b c` is `App(App(App(f,a),b),c)`. A translator that folds the argument list right-nested produces `App(f, App(a, App(b,c)))`, which fails `infer_type` with `NotAFunction` — but only when `a` is not itself a function. For `@compose` below, where several arguments ARE functions, a right-nested fold can typecheck and mean something entirely different.

Catches `@` on a UNIVERSE-polymorphic constant. Lean's `@f.{u}` supplies levels too. In LOGOS only `Term::Const { name, levels }` (term.rs:458) instantiates levels, and it resolves ONLY against `Context::universe_polys` — i.e. only for definitions registered with `add_universe_poly` (context.rs:218). `@List.nil.{0}` has no LOGOS counterpart for an *inductive* constructor at all (T01-007). A translator must not quietly drop the level arguments and emit a plain `Global`.

Catches `@` on a constant with an INSTANCE parameter. `@sizeOf' Nat inst 5` supplies the instance positionally; the emitted spine is the same as the synthesised one only if the translator takes the instance term from the `Expr` rather than re-resolving it against LOGOS's flat, first-match instance list (context.rs:184-188), which may pick a different instance.

Catches partial application. `@idf Nat` is a well-typed value of type `Nat → Nat`; the emitted `App(Global("idf"), Global("Nat"))` must typecheck on its own, so the translator must not eta-expand or complete the spine.
oracle: The emitted term for `@f …` is byte-identical to the emitted term for the corresponding non-`@` application; it typechecks; `binder_kinds` for the callee is unchanged by the presence of `@`; and the emitted `App` spine is left-nested.

cases.title: Named arguments `f (x := 1)` — resolved into positional order before translation
cases.lean: named arguments, `f (y := 2) (x := 1)`, named arguments that skip explicit parameters and thereby eta-expand
cases.target: A positional, left-nested `Term::App` spine in the DECLARATION's parameter order — never in the source's writing order. There is no named-argument form in LOGOS.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:478 (`App(Box<Term>, Box<Term>)` — positional, binary, left-nested; arguments carry no names); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:144-170 (the `App` rule substitutes the argument for the `Pi`'s `param` — the binder's name comes from the FUNCTION's type, never from the call site); kernel/src/context.rs:199-206 (`binder_kinds` is a positional `Vec<ParamKind>` with no names; there is no named-parameter table anywhere in `Context`); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1029-1045 (`elaborate_app` takes `explicit_args: &[Term]` — a positional slice)
guards: **Translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** This is the cleanest case for that rule. Lean resolves named arguments during elaboration, so the `Expr` is already positional; a translator on `Expr` does nothing. A translator on `Syntax` must reimplement Lean's resolution — including the rule that a named argument which SKIPS a preceding explicit parameter causes Lean to eta-expand the call into a lambda over the skipped parameter (`mkLambda` around the remaining application). That is not a reordering; it is a different term. See `skipping` below, whose `Expr` is `fun a => sub3 a 2 9`, not a three-argument application.

Catches translating the arguments in SOURCE order. `f (y := 2) (x := 1)` written with `y` first must still emit `App(App(f, 1), 2)`. Because `sub3`'s parameters all have the same type (`Nat`), the source-ordered spine typechecks perfectly and computes a different number. Nothing in the kernel can notice: `Term::App` has no names to compare against.

Catches resolving names against the WRONG telescope. Lean's parameter names come from the declaration's signature, including binders introduced by `variable` and by auto-bound implicits (T05-008). A translator that reads names off the *body's* lambda binders, or off a `Syntax` signature that has not yet had `variable`s inserted, resolves `(x := ..)` to a different position.

Catches named arguments naming an IMPLICIT parameter. `idf (α := Nat) 3` supplies an implicit by name; the resulting `Expr` is the same as `@idf Nat 3`, so the emitted spine must include the type argument. A translator that treats "named argument" as "explicit argument" and appends it at the end of the explicit spine puts `Nat` where the value should go.

Catches named arguments combined with DEFAULTS. `withDefaults (c := 9)` supplies the third parameter by name and leaves the first two to their defaults; the `Expr` contains the default *values* inlined (T05-006), so the emitted spine has three arguments even though the source wrote one.

Catches the dependent case. In `depNamed` the named argument's value determines a later parameter's TYPE, so the reordering must respect the Pi telescope's dependency order; emitting the arguments in any other order makes `substitute(body_type, param, arg)` (type_checker.rs:166) substitute into a type that does not yet mention the binder.
oracle: The emitted spine equals, term for term, the spine emitted for the same call written positionally; it typechecks; `normalize` agrees with Lean on every example; and for `skipping` the emitted term is a `Term::Lambda`, not an `App` spine.

cases.title: Default arguments `(n : Nat := 3)` — the default value must be inlined at every call
cases.lean: optional parameters with default values, `optParam`, structure field defaults
cases.target: At each call site, the default's translated VALUE inlined as an ordinary positional argument. For the declaration itself, an ordinary `Term::Pi` — `optParam` is erased, because LOGOS has no optional-parameter form and no `optParam` wrapper.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:464-469 (`Term::Pi { param, param_type, body_type }` — three fields, no default slot); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1016-1027 (`ParamKind` has exactly `Explicit`, `Implicit`, `Instance` — there is no `Optional` kind, so a parameter with a default cannot be marked as fillable); kernel/src/context.rs:199-206 (`set_binder_kinds` is the only per-parameter metadata `Context` holds; nothing stores a default term); kernel/src/context.rs:271-369 (`add_structure(name, params, fields)` takes fields as name/type pairs — a structure field's default has nowhere to go either, and `add_structure` generates a single `{name}_mk` constructor of full arity); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1029-1045 (`elaborate_app` consumes `explicit_args` positionally and never fills a missing one)
guards: **Translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** Lean has already inserted every default by the time the `Expr` exists — including defaults that are themselves elaborated terms mentioning earlier parameters. A translator on `Syntax` must re-elaborate the default expression *in the call site's context*, which means reimplementing the elaborator. This is the same failure the auto-param case (T05-007) makes fatal.

Catches emitting the declaration's `Pi` with `optParam` still wrapped. Lean's type for `withDefault` is `Nat → optParam Nat 3 → Nat`, and `optParam` is a real constant in Lean's environment. Emitting `Global("optParam")` gives an unresolvable name; and declaring it as an axiom (context.rs:434, unchecked) gives an opaque type former that nothing inhabits, so every call site stops typechecking.

Catches dropping the default argument from the call site's spine rather than inlining it. The spine is then one argument short, and `infer_type`'s `Pi` rule (type_checker.rs:156-167) substitutes the *next* argument into the defaulted binder. For `withDefault` the following argument is also a `Nat`, so this typechecks and silently shifts every later argument by one.

Catches defaults that MENTION earlier parameters. `sized n (m := n * 2)` has a default whose value depends on `n`; the inlined term must be the default with `n` substituted by the call site's actual argument, not the default's open term with a free `Term::Var("n")` — which, in LOGOS's NAMED representation (term.rs:450), will silently capture any enclosing binder called `n` instead of failing.

Catches structure-field defaults. `{ val := 1 }` for a structure with a defaulted `tag` must emit `Wrap_mk 1 0`, not `Wrap_mk 1`. `add_structure`'s constructor has full arity (context.rs:271-369), so the short form fails — unless the omitted field type happens to make the partial application well-typed.
oracle: The emitted spine for a call that omitted a default has the same arity as the fully-explicit call and is term-for-term identical to it; the output contains no `Global("optParam")`; and the loss record contains DEFAULT_VALUE_INDIRECTION with the defaulted parameter named.
loss: DEFAULT_VALUE_INDIRECTION. Lean's `optParam` keeps the default as part of the function's TYPE, so it is one shared definition that every call site refers to. After translation it is a value copied into each call site. Consequences: (a) term size grows with call-site count, and since substitution is O(size) per binder comparison (type_checker.rs:1088) that is a real cost on a large library; (b) the defaults are frozen at translation time, so changing the Lean default no longer changes existing translated call sites; (c) a call site that a human later reads in LOGOS cannot tell which arguments the Lean author actually wrote.

STRUCTURE_FIELD_DEFAULTS. `add_structure` (context.rs:271-369) emits one `{name}_mk` constructor taking every field. A Lean structure-instance literal that omits a defaulted field must be emitted with that field's default value supplied explicitly. The knowledge that it *was* a default is lost. Lean's `..` is a SEPARATE mechanism — it supplies `_`, not the default (T05-016) — so the two must not share a translation path.

cases.title: Auto params `(h : P := by tac)` — the tactic must be RUN by Lean before translation
cases.lean: autoParam, `(h : P := by decide)`, `(h : P := by simp)`, auto-bound proof obligations
cases.target: (none — no sound translation from the surface form)
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (the `Term` enum has no tactic, no `Syntax`, no delayed elaboration, and no metavariable variant — `Hole` is the only unknown and it is not a suspension); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:137-139 (`is_meta`: metavariables are `Term::Var` names beginning with `?`, and LOGOS_FACTS records that they "must be fully instantiated before the kernel sees the term"); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1016-1027 (`ParamKind` has no `AutoParam` variant, so the parameter cannot even be marked as tactic-filled); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:313 (`Term::Hole` reaching `infer_type` is `CannotInferHole`) and :1593-1597 (`types_equal` treats `Hole` as matching **anything**); LOGOS_FACTS, Surface A tactic grammar (`crates/logicaffeine_proof/src/ tactic_script.rs`) — the LOGOS tactic language is a proof-script surface with a fixed primitive list; it is not reachable from term elaboration, and `exact` takes a **named hypothesis only, not a term**
guards: **This is the case that makes the Tier-5 rule load-bearing: translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** An auto param is a `Syntax` object stored in the function's TYPE (`autoParam P (Syntax.ident ``decide)`) and run by Lean at each call site. Reading `Syntax` therefore gives the translator a tactic block and no proof; reading the elaborated `Expr` of the CALL SITE gives it the finished proof term, which translates like any other. The rejection is against translating the auto param *as such*; a translator that elaborates each call site and translates the resulting proof term is doing the right thing and this case's declarations will then never reach the rejection path — the diagnostic must fire only when the unelaborated form is met.

Catches emitting `Term::Hole` for the auto-param argument. `types_equal` matches a `Hole` against **anything** (type_checker.rs:1593-1597) and that leniency leaks into `is_subtype`'s fast path (:1314), so a declaration carrying the hole can typecheck against a type it does not have. For an auto param the hole stands where a PROOF should be, so this is the difference between a proof library and a pile of assertions.

Catches emitting an axiom of the auto param's type via `add_declaration` (context.rs:434), which is unchecked. `predOf`'s auto param is `n ≠ 0`; axiomatising it asserts `Π(n:Nat). Not (Eq Nat n Zero)`, from which `0 ≠ 0` and then `False` follow. One convenience axiom, whole library inconsistent.

Catches translating the tactic BLOCK into a LOGOS proof script. The LOGOS script surface is a separate vernacular (LOGOS_FACTS, Surface A) that does not interoperate with kernel terms; there is no way to attach a script to an argument position, the primitive list is fixed and small, and `exact` accepts only a named hypothesis. Even where a LOGOS script could prove the same proposition, the resulting `VerifiedProof` is a separate object — not a term that can sit in an application spine.

Catches assuming the tactic is deterministic across call sites. `by decide` on `n ≠ 0` produces a DIFFERENT proof term for each `n`, because it reduces a `Decidable` instance at that `n`. A translator that elaborates the auto param once, at the declaration, and reuses the term at every call site emits a proof of the wrong proposition — and since proofs are `Prop` inhabitants, definitional proof irrelevance (type_checker.rs:1547-1567) may hide the mismatch until the type itself disagrees.

Catches the `autoParam` wrapper leaking into the emitted type. Lean's type for `safeDiv` literally mentions the constant `autoParam`; emitting `Global("autoParam")` is an unresolvable name, and declaring it as an axiom gives a type former nothing inhabits.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_AUTO_PARAM_UNELABORATED for each declaration below when it meets the unelaborated form; writes no declaration; emits no `Term::Hole`, no new axiom, and no `Global("autoParam")`. If the translator instead elaborates call sites, the emitted proof term for each call must be the translation of the term Lean's tactic produced AT THAT CALL SITE.
diag: E_AUTO_PARAM_UNELABORATED — must name the declaration, the auto-param binder, and the tactic block, and state that the tactic must be executed by Lean and its resulting proof term translated. Must NOT emit a `Hole`, an axiom, or a LOGOS tactic script.

cases.title: Auto-bound implicits — Lean invents binders the source never wrote
cases.lean: autoBound implicits (`relaxedAutoImplicit`), `Type*`-style auto-bound universes, free lowercase Greek/single-letter identifiers in a signature
cases.target: The FULL `Term::Pi` telescope, including every binder Lean auto-bound, plus a `set_binder_kinds` vector whose auto-bound positions are `ParamKind::Implicit`, plus a loss record naming each auto-bound binder.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:464-469 (`Term::Pi` has no notion of a binder's origin — a binder the user wrote and one Lean invented are the same term); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1016-1027 (`ParamKind` records only how a parameter is supplied, not where it came from); kernel/src/context.rs:199-206 (`set_binder_kinds` is the only per-parameter metadata in `Context`); kernel/src/term.rs:458 and kernel/src/context.rs:218 (an auto-bound UNIVERSE has no counterpart at all: `Term::Const { name, levels }` resolves only against `universe_polys`, i.e. only for `add_universe_poly` DEFINITIONS — an auto-bound universe on an inductive is T01-007, a rejection); kernel/src/term.rs:167-191 (`Universe::Type(u32)` takes a concrete `u32`, so a level VARIABLE can only be `Universe::Var` and only where a level parameter list exists)
guards: **Translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** Auto-bound implicits exist *only* in the elaborated signature: the `Syntax` for `def idf (a : α) : α := a` contains no binder for `α` at all. A `Syntax`-level translator must reimplement Lean's auto-binding rules — which identifiers qualify, whether `relaxedAutoImplicit` is on, where the binders are inserted, and how they are sorted — and any divergence changes the declaration's arity. This is the case where the `Syntax` surface is not merely inconvenient but actively missing information.

Catches emitting the telescope WITHOUT the auto-bound binders, on the theory that "the source did not write them". The emitted type is then `α → α` with `α` a free `Term::Var`, which in LOGOS's named representation is not a detectable error — it resolves against whatever `α` is in scope at the use site, or fails lookup far from the declaration.

Catches getting the auto-bound binder's SORT wrong. With `autoImplicit` on, Lean binds `α` at `Sort u` for a fresh auto-bound universe `u`, not at `Type 0`. Pinning it to `Type 0` is a silent monomorphisation with exactly the failure mode of T01-007: because LOGOS is CUMULATIVE (type_checker.rs:1330-1360) while Lean is not, the monomorphised declaration still typechecks at most use sites and is wrong wherever the source instantiated it above `Type 0`.

Catches auto-bound UNIVERSES specifically. `sortId` below is auto-bound at `Sort u`; if the declaration is a `def`, `add_universe_poly` (context.rs:218) can carry it and `Term::Const { levels }` can instantiate it. If the same auto-binding happens on an `inductive` or a `structure`, there is no carrier at all and the case becomes a rejection (T01-007, T03-012) — a translator must not silently degrade those.

Catches name collision between an auto-bound binder and a user binder. `collide` below has a user binder named `α` in an inner scope; the auto-bound outer `α` shadows or is shadowed depending on emit order, and `substitute_avoiding` (type_checker.rs:1088) only alpha-renames when the REPLACEMENT's free variables collide — not when two binders merely share a name. Freshening is the translator's job.
oracle: The emitted `Pi` telescope has exactly the arity of Lean's elaborated signature, binder for binder and in Lean's order; `binder_kinds` marks each auto-bound position `Implicit`; the emitted term has no free `Term::Var`; and the loss record contains BINDER_PROVENANCE listing each auto-bound binder by name and position.
loss: BINDER_PROVENANCE. After translation there is no way to tell that `α` in `idf`'s type was auto-bound rather than written. Consequences: (a) a round-trip back to Lean cannot reproduce the source, (b) a later edit to Lean's `autoImplicit` setting changes the declaration's arity while the translated one is frozen, and (c) an auto-bound binder's NAME is chosen by Lean from the identifier the user happened to type, so it participates in LOGOS's NAMED `Var` representation (term.rs:450) and can collide with a user binder of the same name elsewhere in the telescope.

AUTO_BOUND_ORDERING. Lean inserts auto-bound implicits at the FRONT of the telescope, in first-occurrence order, and re-sorts them by dependency. That order is not derivable from the surface text. The emitted `Pi` telescope must be Lean's, and the loss record must pin it, because `binder_kinds` is positional (context.rs:201) and any later re-derivation that orders them differently makes every call site's argument land in the wrong slot.

cases.title: Anonymous constructor `⟨…⟩` — resolved to a named constructor before translation
cases.lean: ⟨a, b⟩ anonymous constructor notation, nested and right-associated ⟨…⟩
cases.target: A fully-applied `Term::App` spine headed by the resolved constructor's `Term::Global` — `⟨1, 2⟩ : Point` becomes `App(App(Global("Point_mk"), Lit(Nat 1)), Lit(Nat 2))`, with the structure's PARAMETERS supplied first.
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:271-369 (`add_structure(name, params, fields)` generates the inductive, ONE constructor named `{name}_mk`, and one projection definition per field — the anonymous-constructor notation resolves to that `{name}_mk`); kernel/src/context.rs:419 (`add_constructor(name, inductive, ty)` — constructors are ordinary flat `String` globals); kernel/src/term.rs:453 and :478 (`Global(String)` plus left-nested binary `App` is the whole of application — there is no anonymous-constructor term); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1029-1080 (`elaborate_app`/`elaborate_app_against` — the expected-type pass is what lets a constructor's implicit parameters be solved from the surrounding type, which is exactly what `⟨…⟩` relies on); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:144-170 (the `App` rule; a spine of the wrong length fails only if the types disagree)
guards: **Translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** `⟨…⟩` has no meaning until the expected type is known: the same `⟨1, 2⟩` is a `Point`, a `Prod Nat Nat`, an `And`, or a `Subtype` depending on context. Lean has resolved it by the time the `Expr` exists. A translator on `Syntax` must re-run expected-type-driven resolution, and since LOGOS's `Prod`, `Sigma`, `Subtype` and `Option` are **absent from the prelude** (LOGOS_FACTS, "Absent entirely") it would have to invent them too.

Catches the RIGHT-ASSOCIATION rule. Lean flattens `⟨a, b, c⟩` for a 3-field structure but nests it as `⟨a, ⟨b, c⟩⟩` for a 2-field one whose second field is itself a structure. For `Triple` and `NestedPair` below the source text is identical and the elaborated terms have different shapes. A translator that always flattens emits `Nested_mk a b c` against a 2-argument constructor; a translator that always nests emits `Triple_mk a (?_ b c)`. Both are arity errors — except when the field types line up, in which case one of them typechecks and is wrong.

Catches omitting the structure's PARAMETERS. `add_structure`'s field projections take the parameters before the receiver (context.rs:310-362, LOGOS_FACTS), and the constructor likewise takes them first. `⟨1, true⟩ : Pair Nat Bool` must become `Pair_mk Nat Bool 1 true`, not `Pair_mk 1 true`. Since `Nat` is a `Type 0` and the first field's type is the parameter, a two-argument spine can typecheck against a four-argument constructor's prefix and yield a partially-applied value.

Catches `⟨…⟩` for a `Prop`. `⟨h1, h2⟩ : A ∧ B` resolves to the LOGOS prelude's `conj`, and `⟨w, hw⟩ : ∃ x, P x` to `witness` — both present, but under LOGOS's own names (LOGOS_FACTS prelude list: `And`/`conj`, `Ex`/`witness`). Emitting `Global("And.intro")` or `Global("Exists.intro")` is an unresolvable name.

Catches `⟨…⟩` for a type with no LOGOS counterpart. `⟨1, true⟩ : Nat × Bool` and `⟨n, h⟩ : { x // P x }` resolve to `Prod.mk` and `Subtype.mk`, and neither `Prod` nor `Subtype` is in the LOGOS prelude — the translator must declare them (T10-013) or reject, never emit a dangling `Global`.
Catches `⟨…⟩` with a trailing `..` (T05-016), which supplies `_` — not defaults — for the remaining fields; the emitted spine must still be full-arity and must contain no `Term::Hole`.
oracle: The emitted term is a fully-applied `App` spine headed by the resolved constructor's `Global`, with the structure's parameters first; it typechecks; it is term-for-term identical to the translation of the same value written with the explicit constructor name; and `normalize` of each projection agrees with Lean.

cases.title: Dot notation and generalized field notation — `elaborate_dot` and the `H_field` convention
cases.lean: x.f dot notation, generalized field notation (`xs.map f`), `.ctor` anonymous constructor dot notation
cases.target: `H_field <the receiver's type arguments…> <receiver>` — the LOGOS convention implemented by `elaborate::elaborate_dot`, e.g. `p.fst` with `p : Pair A B` becomes `Pair_fst A B p`.
evidence: kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1262-1299 (`elaborate_dot(ctx, mctx, receiver, field)`: the receiver's type is normalised, its head must be a `Term::Global` `H`, the projection name is `format!("{hname}_{field}")`, and the result is `H_field params… receiver` — the parameters are read off the RECEIVER'S TYPE and applied BEFORE the receiver); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1284-1289 (an unknown projection is a hard error: "dot notation: no projection `{proj}` for field `{field}` of `{hname}`"); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1297 (`crate::infer_type(ctx, &applied)?` — the result is certified, so an arity slip is caught here rather than later); kernel/src/context.rs:271-369 (`add_structure` is what creates `{name}_{field}` as an ordinary *definition* whose body is a `Term::Match`); kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (there is **no `Term::Proj`** — dot notation has no term-level counterpart, only this encoding)
guards: **Translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** Lean's dot notation is resolved against the receiver's *elaborated* type, and generalized field notation (`xs.map f`) resolves to a function in the receiver's type's namespace with the receiver inserted at the first argument of that type — a rule involving namespace search and argument-position search. After elaboration the `Expr` is a plain application of a fully-resolved constant. A translator on `Syntax` has to reimplement both searches; one on `Expr` only has to map the resolved constant's flat name.

Catches the PARAMETERS-FIRST convention. `elaborate_dot` applies the structure's parameters, taken from the receiver's type, before the receiver (elaborate.rs:1290-1296). A translator that emits `Pair_fst p` — natural, since Lean's `p.fst` looks unary — produces a term whose first argument is checked against the parameter `α : Type 0`. When the receiver's own type is a `Type 0` (a `Pair Type Type`, say) that can typecheck.

Catches the flat-name convention. LOGOS keys are flat `String`s with no namespaces (LOGOS_FACTS; context.rs:419,442), and `elaborate_dot` looks up exactly `format!("{hname}_{field}")`. Lean's `Pair.fst` must therefore be emitted as `Pair_fst`, and a Lean declaration literally named `Pair_fst` collides with it — see T02-020.

Catches generalized field notation on a NON-structure. `xs.length` with `xs : List Nat` resolves to `List.length xs`, an ordinary function, not a projection. `elaborate_dot` would look for `List_length` and, if the translator registered `List.length` under that name, find it — but the receiver is inserted at the END of the parameter list by `elaborate_dot`, whereas Lean inserts it at the first argument whose type is headed by `List`. For `List.append` (`xs.append ys`) those are different positions, so the arguments are silently swapped.

Catches `.ctor` dot notation (`.nil`, `.cons a t`, `.red`). That is anonymous CONSTRUCTOR notation resolved against the expected type, not field access; it must become `Global("List_nil")`-style constructor application (T05-009), not a projection lookup.

Catches dot notation on a receiver whose type is a REDEX. `elaborate_dot` normalises the receiver's type first (elaborate.rs:1274); a translator that reads the head off the un-normalised type gets a `Lambda` or an `App` and hits the "not headed by an inductive" error, or worse, picks the wrong `H`.
oracle: The emitted term is `Global("{H}_{field}")` applied to the receiver's type arguments and then the receiver, in that order; it typechecks; and `normalize` of the emitted projection of a literal constructor value equals the corresponding field.

cases.title: `Coe` coercions and `↑` — LOGOS's coercion table is a flat, unordered list
cases.lean: Coe, CoeTail, CoeHead, CoeT, ↑x, automatic coercion insertion, transitive coercion chains
cases.target: The COERCION FUNCTION applied explicitly, taken from the elaborated `Expr`: `App(Global("boolToNat"), b)`. Plus one `Context::add_coercion(from, to, coe)` per Lean `Coe` instance, so LOGOS-side elaboration can insert it too.
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:190-196 (`add_coercion(from: Term, to: Term, coe: Term)` pushes onto a flat `Arc<Vec<(Term, Term, Term)>>`; `coercions()` returns the slice); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1301-1330 (`resolve_coercion(ctx, mctx, from, to)` scans `ctx.coercions()` linearly and returns the FIRST triple that unifies — "a match commits the unification"); kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (there is no coercion term, no `mdata`, and no marker of any kind: an inserted coercion is indistinguishable from a function the user wrote); kernel/src/context.rs:184-188 (`add_instance` is a separate, equally flat list — LOGOS does not model `Coe` as a typeclass, so Lean's instance-resolution search does not carry over)
guards: **Translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** Coercion insertion is decided by Lean's unifier: `(b : Nat)` where `b : Bool` inserts `boolToNat b` only because the expected type forced it. The `Syntax` contains no coercion at all. A translator on `Syntax` must reimplement `CoeT`'s search — head, body, tail, and the `Coe` output-parameter rules — and get the same answer Lean did, including where Lean chose NOT to coerce.

Catches the order sensitivity of the flat list. `resolve_coercion` takes the FIRST unifying triple (elaborate.rs:1305-1330). Two coercions `Bool → Nat` registered in either order both typecheck; only one of them is the one Lean chose. Because both produce a `Nat`, nothing downstream disagrees — the translated program simply computes different numbers. There is no priority mechanism and no coherence check.

Catches relying on transitivity. `Bit → Bool → Nat` below is two Lean instances and one automatic chain. Registering the two one-step triples and expecting `resolve_coercion` to compose them silently fails: the scan finds no `(Bit, Nat, _)` triple and the argument is left un-coerced, so the type mismatch surfaces at the kernel — or, if LOGOS's CUMULATIVITY (type_checker.rs:1330-1360) happens to bridge the gap at a sort, does not surface at all.

Catches dropping the coercion because "the types look close enough". LOGOS is cumulative where Lean is not, so `Prop ≤ Type 0 ≤ Type 1` is admitted (LOGOS_FACTS). A translator that decides a coercion is unnecessary on the basis that `is_subtype` accepts the term has just produced a term that means something different from the Lean source — this is the T11-001 trap reached through Tier 5.

Catches the `from`/`to` argument ORDER of `add_coercion`. The signature is `add_coercion(from, to, coe)` (context.rs:190); registering it reversed makes the scan look for the wrong direction. For a coercion between two types that both appear on both sides elsewhere in the table, the reversed triple can still unify against a different query and be applied backwards.

Catches a coercion into a FUNCTION or a SORT. `CoeFun`/`CoeSort` have no analogue at all (T05-012); they must not be registered as ordinary `add_coercion` triples, which would make `resolve_coercion` return a function used as if it were the coerced value.
oracle: The emitted term contains the coercion function applied explicitly, matching the elaborated `Expr` application for application; `ctx.coercions()` contains one triple per Lean `Coe` instance plus any synthesised composite, in a recorded order; the emitted term typechecks; and the loss record contains COERCION_TRANSITIVITY listing every synthesised composite.
loss: COERCION_TRANSITIVITY. Lean's coercion resolution is a typeclass search: `CoeT` chains `CoeHead`, `Coe` and `CoeTail`, so a path `A → B → C` is found automatically from two one-step instances. `resolve_coercion` (elaborate.rs:1301-1330) is a single linear scan over `(from, to, coe)` triples with NO transitive closure. Every composite path the Lean source relied on must be pre-composed and registered as its own triple, and the loss record must list which composites were synthesised — they are new definitions that did not exist in the source.

COERCION_INVISIBILITY. Lean marks an inserted coercion in the `Expr` (it is a recognisable application of a `Coe`-family constant, and Lean's delaborator can hide it again). LOGOS has no marker at all, so after translation an inserted coercion and a user-written function application are the same term. A round-trip cannot restore the `↑`, and a reader cannot tell where the source relied on coercion.

cases.title: `CoeFun` / `CoeSort` — no analogue: LOGOS coercions go between two `Term`s, not into a function or a sort position
cases.lean: CoeFun, CoeSort, a structure used as a function, a structure used as a type
cases.target: (none — no sound translation of the mechanism)
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:190-196 (`add_coercion(from: Term, to: Term, coe: Term)` — a coercion is a triple of TERMS; there is no "coerce when used in head position" and no "coerce when used in type position" form); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1301-1330 (`resolve_coercion` is called when an ARGUMENT's type does not match an expected PARAMETER type — that is the only insertion site; nothing consults the coercion table when a non-function is applied or when a non-sort appears as a type); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:144-170 (the `App` rule: the head's type is whnf'd and must be a `Term::Pi`, else `KernelError::NotAFunction` — no coercion hook); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:172-200 (the `Match` rule requires the discriminant's type to be headed by a registered inductive, else `NotAnInductive`); kernel/src/context.rs:271-369 and :300-303 (`add_structure` hard-codes the structure's sort to `Type 0`, so a `CoeSort` target cannot even be a general sort)
guards: **Translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** In the elaborated `Expr`, `f x` where `f : Fn` is already `Fn.f f x` — the `CoeFun` projection is applied. So a translator reading `Expr` gets a perfectly ordinary application and this case never fires for translated *call sites*. What is rejected is translating the `CoeFun`/`CoeSort` INSTANCE itself, which is what a `Syntax`-level translator (or one that tries to make LOGOS-side elaboration behave the same) would attempt. The diagnostic must fire on the instance declaration, not on the uses.

Catches registering a `CoeFun` instance via `add_coercion` (context.rs:190). The triple would be `(Fn, Nat → Nat, Fn_f)`, and `resolve_coercion` would then fire at ARGUMENT positions — so passing an `Fn` where a `Nat → Nat` is expected would silently be coerced, which Lean's `CoeFun` does NOT do. The translated program accepts terms the source rejects.

Catches emitting the un-coerced application `App(Global("f_value"), x)`. `infer_type`'s `App` rule (type_checker.rs:144-170) whnfs the head's type; a structure type is headed by a `Global`, not a `Pi`, so this is `NotAFunction` — a clean failure, except when the structure is a one-field wrapper around a function AND the translator registered the structure with `add_structure`, whose eta rule (`try_structure_eta`, type_checker.rs:1391-1417) can make the wrapper and its field definitionally equal inside `def_eq`. Then the error moves somewhere unrelated.

Catches `CoeSort` specifically. The Lean idiom `(t : Ty)` used as a TYPE requires coercing a VALUE into a sort position. LOGOS has no rule that consults the coercion table when a term appears as a type: `infer_sort` simply demands a `Term::Sort`. And `add_structure` pins the structure's own sort to `Type 0` (context.rs:300-303), so even a hand-rolled encoding cannot target `Type 1+` or `Prop` — see T03-012.

Catches "just unfold it". Replacing `Fn` by its field type everywhere is sound for `CoeFun` on a one-field wrapper and unsound in general: a multi-field structure with a `CoeFun` carries data the function type does not, and any Lean theorem quantifying over `Fn` is no longer expressible. A translator that unfolds must do so only where it can prove the structure is a single-field wrapper, and record it as a separate, explicitly-named transformation — not as a coercion.

Catches over-rejection of ordinary `Coe`. `Coe A B` between two ordinary types is `degrade`, not `reject` (T05-011); the diagnostic must distinguish the `CoeFun`/ `CoeSort` classes from `Coe`/`CoeTail`/`CoeHead`.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NO_COE_FUN_COE_SORT on the `CoeFun` and `CoeSort` instance declarations below; writes no declaration for them; adds no entry to `ctx.coercions()` for them; and does not reject the ordinary `Coe` instance in T05-011.
diag: E_NO_COE_FUN_COE_SORT — must name the instance (`CoeFun`/`CoeSort`), the source type, and the use site, and state that LOGOS inserts coercions only at argument positions. Must NOT emit a `Term::App` whose head is the un-coerced structure, and must NOT register the instance with `add_coercion`.

cases.title: `_` holes resolved by unification — must be fully instantiated before the kernel
cases.lean: `_` placeholder, `(_ : T)`, holes solved by unification against the expected type
cases.target: The SOLVED term, with every hole replaced. `idf _ 3` becomes `App(App(Global("idf"), Global("Nat")), Lit(Nat 3))`. The emitted term must contain **no `Term::Hole`** and **no `Term::Var` whose name begins with `?`**.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:540-544 (`Term::Hole` — "implicit argument"; it is the only unknown in the term language and it is not a metavariable); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:313 (`Term::Hole => Err(KernelError::CannotInferHole)` — a hole reaching `infer_type` is a hard error); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1593-1597 (`types_equal` returns **true** whenever either side is a `Hole` — a hole matches ANYTHING) and :1314 (that leniency leaks into `is_subtype`'s fast path); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:456-470 (`check_type` special-cases `Hole` on both the term and the expected side, which is what lets holes survive `check_type` while failing `infer_type`); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:137-139 (`is_meta`: elaborator metavariables are `Term::Var` names beginning with `?`, NOT a `Term` variant); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:143-186 (`instantiate` substitutes every solved metavariable, transitively — this is the call that must precede handing the term to the kernel)
guards: **Translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** A `_` has no meaning in `Syntax`; Lean's unifier decides what it is. After elaboration the `Expr` holds the solution. A translator on `Syntax` must run its own unifier against LOGOS's — whose `unify_in` (elaborate.rs:216-292) is a *different* algorithm with Miller-pattern restrictions (T05-014) and an eta rule — and will diverge from Lean wherever the two disagree.

Catches emitting `Term::Hole` for an unsolved `_` "to be filled in later". This is the single most dangerous output in the corpus. `types_equal` treats a `Hole` as matching **anything** (type_checker.rs:1593-1597), and `is_subtype`'s fast path inherits that (:1314) — so a declaration whose TYPE contains a hole will typecheck against any type at all, and every theorem stated with it proves nothing. See T00-016 and T11-004.

Catches the asymmetry between `check_type` and `infer_type`. `check_type` accommodates holes (type_checker.rs:456-470) while `infer_type` rejects them (:313). A translator that validates its output with `check_type` against an expected type it also emitted will therefore *pass* on hole-carrying terms, and only fail later when something calls `infer_type` — typically inside a `Match` motive or a `Fix` sanity check, far from the source of the hole.

Catches leaving an elaborator METAVARIABLE in the output. These are not `Hole`s: they are `Term::Var("?m0")` (elaborate.rs:137-139). The kernel has no idea they are special — it treats `?m0` as an ordinary free variable, so it either fails lookup or, in LOGOS's NAMED representation (term.rs:450), resolves against a binder that happens to share the name. `instantiate` (elaborate.rs:143-186) must be called, and its result must be checked to contain no `?`-prefixed `Var`.

Catches a `_` in a POSITION Lean solved from a later constraint. In `viaLater` below the hole's solution comes from the expected type of the whole expression, not from any argument — so a translator that solves left-to-right and gives up when an argument does not pin the hole emits a hole where Lean had an answer.

Catches `_` standing for a PROOF. In `holeProof` the `_` is filled by a proof term; because proofs are `Prop` inhabitants, definitional proof irrelevance (type_checker.rs:1547-1567) will accept almost anything there — including a hole — so nothing downstream complains.
oracle: The emitted term contains no `Term::Hole` and no `Term::Var` whose name starts with `?`; `infer_type` (not merely `check_type`) succeeds on it; and it is term-for-term identical to the translation of the same expression written with every `_` filled in by hand.

cases.title: Higher-order pattern unification — Miller patterns only, on both sides
cases.lean: motive inference for `Eq.mpr`/`▸`/`Eq.subst`, `congrArg`, `?m x y =?= t`, dependent `match` motive synthesis
cases.target: The SOLVED term with every motive written out as an explicit `Term::Lambda` — `h ▸ e` becomes an application of the translated `Eq` eliminator to a motive the translator took from Lean's `Expr`, never a `Hole` for LOGOS to re-solve.
evidence: kernel/src/elaborate.rs:216-292 (`unify_in(ctx, mctx, lctx, a, b)`: metavariable assignment, then `try_pattern` in BOTH directions, then the η rule, then structural congruence — first-order unification is `unify` with an empty local context); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:294-340 (`try_pattern`: the head must be an UNSOLVED metavariable; EVERY argument must be a DISTINCT bound variable of `lctx`; a repeated argument returns `None`, a non-variable argument returns `None`, an occurs-check failure returns `Some(false)`, and an out-of-scope free variable on the right returns `Some(false)`); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:638-700 (`infer_match_motive` is the Miller solution of `?P disc =?= T`, by abstracting the discriminant out of the expected type); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:137-139,143-186 (metavariables are `?`-prefixed `Term::Var`s and must be `instantiate`d away before the kernel sees the term)
guards: **Translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** Lean's unifier has already solved these motives; the `Expr` contains them explicitly. A translator on `Syntax` must re-solve them with LOGOS's unifier — which is a strictly weaker algorithm (pattern fragment only, no postponement, no unfolding heuristics) — and will fail on the cases below where Lean succeeded by a non-pattern approximation.

Catches relying on LOGOS to solve a NON-pattern constraint. `try_pattern` (elaborate.rs:294-340) returns `None` for a repeated argument (`?M x x =?= t`) and for a non-variable argument (`?M (f y) =?= t`), so unification falls through to structural congruence and simply FAILS. Lean solves both cases — by picking a canonical solution among several, which is why they are outside the pattern fragment. A translator that emits a `Hole` and expects LOGOS to fill it gets a hard error here, and a `CannotInferHole` (type_checker.rs:313) if the hole survives.

Catches the difference in what "distinct bound variables" means. `try_pattern` checks membership in the LOCAL CONTEXT `lctx` (elaborate.rs:313-325), and the top-level `unify` runs with an EMPTY `lctx` (elaborate.rs:216-219) — so at top level NO higher-order pattern is solvable at all, only first-order unification. A translator that calls `unify` rather than `unify_in` with a populated context gets first-order behaviour and silently different answers.

Catches the η rule's reach. `unify_in` (elaborate.rs:254-268) η-expands a λ against a non-λ, so `?M =?= fun x => t` and `?M x =?= t` can both succeed and assign DIFFERENT solutions depending on which side was tried first. Lean's answer is one specific one; the emitted term must be Lean's.

Catches an occurs-check difference. `try_pattern` returns `Some(false)` when the metavariable occurs in the right-hand side (elaborate.rs:327-329), aborting the unification rather than falling through — so a constraint Lean solved by unfolding a definition first will fail in LOGOS with no fallback.
