cases.title: Mathlib's algebraic hierarchy — the case that explains why Mathlib as a whole does not port
cases.lean: class Mul/One/Semigroup/Monoid/Group and their `extends` chain, universe-polymorphic algebraic structures, `Monoid.{u}` instantiated at more than one level
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:271-369 (`add_structure` is the ONLY record-declaring API); kernel/src/context.rs:300 (`let ind_type = pis(params, Term::Sort(Universe::Type(0)))` — the structure's sort is HARD-CODED to `Type 0`; there is no sort argument and no universe-parameter list); kernel/src/context.rs:253,374 (`add_inductive(name, sort)` / `add_indexed_inductive(name, sort, num_params)` take a single FIXED `sort: Term` — an inductive cannot carry universe parameters either); kernel/src/context.rs:218 (`add_universe_poly(name, params, ty, body)` — universe polymorphism exists for DEFINITIONS ONLY, and requires a `body`, which a type declaration does not have); kernel/src/term.rs:458 (`Term::Const { name, levels }` is the only universe-instantiating form, and kernel/src/type_checker.rs:70-85 plus kernel/src/reduction.rs:82-91 resolve it ONLY against `Context::universe_polys`); kernel/src/term.rs:167-191 (`Universe::Type(u32)` takes a CONCRETE `u32`, not a level expression); kernel/src/recursor.rs:64-71 (`derive_recursor` hard-codes the motive target to `Sort(Type 0)` for a non-`Prop` inductive, so a structure's eliminator cannot eliminate into `Type 1+` either); kernel/src/context.rs:71,184-186 (the instance database is a flat `Vec<(Term,Term)>` with no priorities and no coherence checking — T07-005, T07-008, T07-013)
guards: THIS IS THE CASE THAT SETTLES THE MATHLIB QUESTION, and it is a CONJUNCTION of three independent walls. A translator that works around any one of them still hits the other two: 1. UNIVERSE POLYMORPHISM. `Monoid.{u} (M : Type u)` needs a universe parameter on a TYPE. `add_structure` hard-codes `Type 0` (context.rs:300); `add_inductive` takes one fixed sort (context.rs:253); `add_universe_poly` handles DEFINITIONS only and needs a body (context.rs:218). There is no third option. See T01-007. 2. THE `extends` CHAIN. Mathlib's hierarchy is ~15 levels of `extends` with deliberate diamonds (`CommRing` reaches `AddCommMonoid` by several paths) whose coherence is maintained by hand and checked by Lean. LOGOS's instance database cannot express a priority, cannot express a scoped instance, and resolves first-match-wins on insertion order (elaborate.rs:1331-1340) — so the diamond resolves to whichever path the translator happened to emit first, undetectably. See T07-005 and T07-013. 3. `outParam`. `HMul`/`HAdd`/`SMul` — the classes that carry Mathlib's notation — have `outParam` positions, which LOGOS has no concept of. See T07-006.

THE TEMPTING WRONG MOVE: monomorphise every class at `Type 0` and carry on. It compiles. It typechecks. And it is wrong the moment the source instantiates a class at two different levels — which Mathlib does constantly, because a `Module R M` has `R : Type u` and `M : Type v` with `u ≠ v` in general, and because `CategoryTheory` quantifies over `Type (u+1)`. The two instantiations collapse to ONE flat LOGOS global (keys are flat `String`s, context.rs:449), so `Monoid` at level 0 and `Monoid` at level 1 share a declaration whose projections and derived eliminator can only land in `Type 0` (recursor.rs:64-71). Every downstream proof is then checked against a type that is not the one the Lean source meant. And because LOGOS is CUMULATIVE (`Prop ≤ Type 0 ≤ Type 1`, type_checker.rs:1330-1360) while Lean is not, the resulting terms very often STILL TYPECHECK — so the kernel will not catch this for you. See T01-007 and T11-019.

Catches per-instantiation monomorphisation (`Monoid@0`, `Monoid@1`). It is sound-ish for the types but breaks the moment a universe-polymorphic LEMMA quantifies over `u` — `mul_assoc` in Mathlib is `∀ {M : Type u} [Monoid M]`, and there is no level variable to bind on the emitted structure. The translator must then reject any declaration whose universe parameters are not fully determined at every use site, which is most of the library. See T01-008.

Catches "declare the classes as `Prop`-valued mixins instead". Mathlib's `Monoid` carries DATA (`mul`, `one`), not just laws, so it cannot be a `Prop`; and `add_structure` would put it in `Type 0` regardless (context.rs:300).

Catches the partial-success failure mode, which is the realistic one. A translator will happily emit `Mul`, `One` and `Semigroup` at `Type 0` — they LOOK fine — and then fail on `Module` or on a `Type (u+1)` category. At that point the context already contains a dozen monomorphised classes and their instances, and the certificate minted from it claims `PRELUDE_VERSION = "logos-coc-1"` (certificate.rs:28) while describing a hierarchy that does not mean what its source meant. The rejection must happen at the FIRST universe-polymorphic class, not at the first one that fails to typecheck.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NO_UNIVERSE_POLYMORPHIC_STRUCTURE at `Mul` (the first universe-polymorphic class in the file) and writes NO declaration into the LOGOS context — in particular, zero `add_structure` calls. A harness additionally asserts that the translator does not emit a `Type 0` monomorphisation of any class declared with a universe parameter.
diag: E_NO_UNIVERSE_POLYMORPHIC_STRUCTURE — must name the class, list its universe parameters, cite `add_structure`'s hard-coded `Type 0` (context.rs:300), and state that neither the structure nor a replacement inductive can carry a universe parameter. Must NOT suggest monomorphisation at `Type 0` as a fix.

cases.title: Bundled vs unbundled structures — the same mathematics, two very different LOGOS encodings, and only one of them resolves
cases.lean: bundled structure (`structure Mon where carrier; mul; …`) vs unbundled class (`class Monoid (α : Type) where mul; …`), `CoeSort` on a bundled carrier
cases.target: UNBUNDLED (`class C (α : Type)`): `add_structure("C", &[("a", Sort(Type 0))], <fields>)` + `set_binder_kinds` with `ParamKind::Instance` at each `[C α]` + one `add_instance` per instance. Method calls resolve. BUNDLED (`structure Mon where carrier : Type; …`): `add_structure("Mon", &[], &[("carrier", Sort(Type 0)), …])` — a PARAMETERLESS structure whose first field is a type. Nothing about it is an instance; `Mon_carrier m` is an ordinary projection and every use site must pass `m` explicitly. Plus a loss record, because the bundled form loses the `CoeSort` that makes `(m : Mon)` usable as a type.
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:271-369 (`add_structure(name, params, fields)` — `params` become the inductive's arity and are bound BEFORE the receiver in every projection's type, :310-362; so the unbundled/bundled distinction is exactly "is the carrier a param or a field"); kernel/src/context.rs:300 (both forms land in `Type 0`, so a bundled structure whose `carrier : Type` field makes it morally `Type 1` is mis-sorted — see the guard below); kernel/src/context.rs:184-186 and kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1174-1189 (`class_heads` is derived from registered instances' conclusion heads, so a bundled structure — which is never registered as an instance — is never a "class" and its fields are never resolved automatically); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1267-1299 (`elaborate_dot` looks up `format!("{hname}_{field}")` — the same mechanism for both forms, which is why they look interchangeable and are not); a grep for `CoeSort` in `crates/logicaffeine_kernel/src` returns NOTHING (see T05-012)
guards: Catches translating a bundled structure AS a class — i.e. calling `add_instance` on a bundled value. Its type is `Mon`, whose head `Global("Mon")` then enters `class_heads` (elaborate.rs:1178-1189), and from that moment EVERY parameter of type `Mon` anywhere in the development is classified as an instance PREMISE by `try_instance` (elaborate.rs:1365) and resolved automatically — silently substituting the first registered `Mon` for whichever one the caller meant to pass. This is the worst bug in this case, because the resulting term typechecks and computes a plausible answer.

Catches the reverse: translating an unbundled class as a bundled structure by moving the carrier into the field list. The projections' telescopes change (context.rs:310-362 binds `params` before the receiver), so `C_mul α inst a b` becomes `C_mul inst a b`, and every emitted call site must agree. A translator that chooses per-declaration rather than per-CLASS will emit both spellings for one class.

Catches dropping the `CoeSort`. `(m : Mon)` used in type position is `Mon_carrier m`; there is no `CoeSort` in LOGOS (T05-012) and `add_coercion` (context.rs:190) is a flat `(from, to, coe)` list over TERMS, not sorts, so it cannot express this. The translator must insert `Mon_carrier` explicitly at every type-position occurrence, and must record that it did.
oracle: Each form is emitted with a consistent carrier position across the whole class; no `add_instance` is emitted for a bundled structure; every type-position use of a bundled value is rewritten to an explicit `_carrier` projection; and the loss record names CARRIER_POSITION and NO_RESOLUTION_FOR_BUNDLED.
loss: CARRIER_POSITION. In the unbundled form the carrier is a PARAMETER, so `C_mul α inst a b`; in the bundled form it is a FIELD, so `Mon_mul m a b` where `a b : Mon_carrier m`. These are different terms with different telescopes, and a development that mixes the two — as Mathlib does, with `Monoid M` unbundled and `MonCat` bundled — needs an explicit bridge in both directions. LOGOS has no `CoeSort`, so the bundled-to-unbundled direction cannot be implicit: every `(m : Mon)` used as a type must become `Mon_carrier m` by hand.

NO_RESOLUTION_FOR_BUNDLED. A bundled structure's "instance" is a VALUE the user passes. Nothing resolves it, because resolution only scans `ctx.instances()` (elaborate.rs:1331) and a bundled value is not registered there. So the translation of a bundled development is correct but every call site grows an explicit argument — which is exactly what the Lean source used the bundling to avoid, and which changes the arity of every function. Downstream, `set_binder_kinds` for those functions must mark that argument `Explicit`, not `Instance`.

BUNDLED_SORT. A bundled structure whose first field is `carrier : Type` morally lives in `Type 1`, because it quantifies over `Type 0`. `add_structure` declares it at `Type 0` regardless (context.rs:300). LOGOS's cumulativity (type_checker.rs:1330-1360) hides the error at most use sites — `Type 0 ≤ Type 1` holds, so terms typecheck — while Lean would have rejected the same declaration at that sort. This is the T11-019 shape: a universe constraint only Lean's non-cumulative check catches.

cases.title: Instance diamond INCOHERENCE — two resolution paths that disagree, which LOGOS cannot detect
cases.lean: two `extends` paths to one parent carrying DIFFERENT parent data, non-defeq diamond, `set_option structureDiamondWarning true`
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:71 (`instances: Arc<Vec<(Term, Term)>>` — no key, no priority, no coherence metadata, and no room for any); kernel/src/context.rs:184-186 (`add_instance` is an unconditional `push`: it performs no lookup, so it cannot notice that an entry with a unifiable conclusion is already present); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1331-1340 (`resolve_instance_at` returns at the FIRST candidate that fully resolves — `return Some(result)` — and never enumerates the rest, so the SECOND path is never even constructed, let alone compared); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1190-1197 (doc: "The first instance that fully resolves wins"); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1391-1417 (`try_structure_eta` — the only rule that could relate two differently-built dictionaries of the same structure, and it is reachable only from `def_eq_normalized` at :1473-1478, never from `normalize`, and only for structures in the `structures` registry); kernel/src/type_checker.rs: 1536-1541,1547-1567 (proof irrelevance fires only for `Prop`s — a dictionary carrying DATA is not a `Prop`, so two incoherent dictionaries are genuinely unequal)
guards: THE TRAP, and it is the subtlest one in Tier 7: the translator emits both paths' instances, LOGOS resolves the first, and EVERYTHING TYPECHECKS. There is no error, no warning, and no artefact recording that a choice was made. The Lean source may have been relying on the two paths being definitionally equal — Mathlib maintains exactly this invariant by hand across its whole hierarchy — and if the translation breaks it, the breakage shows up as a later proof mysteriously failing `def_eq`, arbitrarily far from the diamond.

Catches "LOGOS will catch it because the two dictionaries are not `def_eq`". It will not, because the two dictionaries are never COMPARED. Resolution returns at the first success (elaborate.rs:1334-1339); the alternative is never built. The only way a comparison happens is if the Lean source explicitly writes both paths' parent projections into one statement — which is exactly what `bothPaths` below does, and which real code does not do.

Catches relying on structure eta. `try_structure_eta` (type_checker.rs:1391-1417) relates `Foo_mk α x` to a variable `f` when `f`'s fields reconstruct to the same thing; it does NOT relate `Foo_mk α 0` to `Foo_mk α 1`. Eta makes coherent diamonds work; it does nothing for incoherent ones. And it is unavailable under `normalize` anyway (gated at :1473-1478), so a proof that reaches the comparison through normalization fails even in the COHERENT case.

Catches translating a diamond that is coherent IN LEAN but whose coherence depends on Lean's structure-flattening choice. Lean decides per-declaration which parent becomes a subobject and which is flattened (see T07-005: `Qux.mk` there takes `[toBar]` and a bare `right`, having flattened `Baz`). The resulting definitional equalities are a consequence of that choice. A LOGOS translation that flattens differently — and `add_structure` gives it no choice, since there is no subobject notion at all (context.rs:271-369) — can turn a coherent Lean diamond into an incoherent LOGOS one WITHOUT the Lean source containing any incoherence. So the translator must check coherence itself, on the emitted encoding, not merely trust Lean's check.

Catches emitting only ONE path "to avoid the ambiguity". That silently drops an instance the source declared, so a goal that Lean discharged via the dropped path fails with `no typeclass instance found` (elaborate.rs:1147-1152) somewhere else entirely.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_INSTANCE_DIAMOND_INCOHERENT, names both paths, and emits NO `add_instance` for the incoherent class. A harness additionally asserts that for every class the translator DOES emit, no two entries in the emitted instance vector have unifiable conclusions with non-`def_eq` values.
diag: E_INSTANCE_DIAMOND_INCOHERENT — must name the class reached by more than one path, list the paths, exhibit the two resulting parent dictionaries, and state that LOGOS resolution is first-match-wins with no coherence check. Must NOT emit either path.

cases.title: Typeclass method projection — a method call is a structure projection applied parameters-first, then the dictionary
cases.lean: class method call, `C.method`, dot notation on a dictionary, generalized field notation, method with its own explicit arguments
cases.target: `C.method (α := α) (self := inst) a b` ⟼ `App(App(App(App(Global("C_method"), <α>), <inst>), <a>), <b>)`. The projection is the ordinary DEFINITION that `add_structure` emitted — body a `Term::Match` on the dictionary — and it takes the structure's PARAMETERS first, then the receiver, then the method's own arguments. There is no `Term::Proj`.
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:271-369 (`add_structure` — "a projection `{name}_{fieldᵢ} : Π(params). Π(s:{name} params). Tᵢ` for each field (its body a `match` on `s`)", :265-267; the projection type is built by `pis(params, pi("s", s_applied, …))` at :330-362, so params come BEFORE the receiver); kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (the complete `Term` enum — there is NO `Proj` variant); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1267-1299 (`elaborate_dot` resolves `x.field` by looking up `format!("{hname}_{field}")` at :1284, where `hname` is the head `Global` of `x`'s type); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1391-1417 (`try_structure_eta`, gated by the `structures` registry at context.rs:153-167 and reachable only from `def_eq_normalized` at :1473-1478 — never from `normalize`); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1136-1153 (the dictionary argument itself is a deferred instance obligation, solved after the explicit arguments)
guards: Catches emitting the projection with the receiver FIRST. `add_structure` binds the structure's parameters before the receiver (context.rs:330-362), so a two-parameter class's method is `C_method α β inst a b`, not `C_method inst α β a b` and not `C_method inst a b`. `twoParams` below is the discriminating case. Getting the order wrong produces a term whose `infer_type` fails — which is the GOOD outcome; the bad outcome is a class whose parameters happen to have the same type as its first method argument, where the mis-ordered application typechecks and computes nonsense.

Catches emitting the method as an opaque axiom. If `C_method` were an `add_declaration` (context.rs:434) rather than the `Match`-bodied definition `add_structure` produces, then `C_method α (C_mk α f) a ≡ f a` would NOT hold, and every `rfl` that computes through an instance — which is most of them — fails. `computesThroughInstance` below is the case.

Catches inlining the `Match` at each use site instead of calling the projection definition. The term typechecks, but (a) it blows up term size, and LOGOS's `Term` is a tree with no sharing (term.rs:443-545) while substitution is O(size) per binder (type_checker.rs:1088), so this is quadratic; and (b) `try_structure_eta` is gated on the `structures` registry entry (context.rs:159-167), which records the PROJECTION NAMES — an inlined `Match` is not recognised as a projection, so eta silently stops firing and `C_mk α (C_method α c) ≡ c` becomes unprovable.

Catches losing the flat-name collision. Projections are named `format!("{name}_{field}")` (context.rs:310-362) into a flat `String` keyspace (context.rs:449), so Lean's `Pointed.point` and a user's `def Pointed_point` both key to `"Pointed_point"` and the second silently replaces the first. `Pointed_point` below is declared deliberately to exercise this. See T02-020.

Catches the method whose own arguments include ANOTHER instance premise. The dictionary is resolved as a deferred obligation AFTER the explicit arguments (elaborate.rs:1016-1027,1136-1140), so a method taking `[D β]` has two obligations resolved in one pass, and their order matters if one pins the other's type variable. `nestedPremise` below exercises it.

Catches assuming eta holds under `normalize`. It does not: `try_structure_eta` is reached only from `def_eq_normalized` (type_checker.rs:1473-1478). A tactic or a translator step that compares two dictionaries by normalizing both and testing syntactic equality will report a mismatch that `def_eq` would have accepted. See T03-011.
oracle: Every emitted method call is `Global("{Class}_{field}")` applied parameters-first, then the dictionary, then the method's arguments; `computesThroughInstance` reduces under `normalize`; the reconstruction in `etaRoundTrip` is accepted by `def_eq`; and no emitted term contains an inlined projection `Match`.

cases.title: `intro` / `intros` — the one script tactic whose arity and goal shapes nearly match
cases.lean: intro, intro (several binders), intros, intro on ¬p, rintro-free core usage
cases.target: LOGOS script atom `intro <name>` — canonical name `intro`, arity 1, aliases `assume`, `suppose`, `let`, `introduce`, `given`, `fix` (proof/src/tactic_script.rs:276, :310) → `combinators::intro` (proof/src/tactic.rs:988-991) → `ProofState::intro` (proof/src/tactic.rs:313-356)
evidence: proof/src/tactic_script.rs:310 (`canonical`: "intro"|"assume"|"suppose"|"let"| "introduce"|"given"|"fix" ⟼ "intro"); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:264-274 (`arg()` — an atom's argument is exactly ONE `Tok::Word`; a missing one is the hard error "tactic `intro` expects an argument"); proof/src/tactic.rs:313-356 (`ProofState::intro` handles EXACTLY two goal shapes, `ProofExpr::Implies` and `ProofExpr::ForAll`, and returns `TacticError::DoesNotApply` for every other, tactic.rs:352-354); proof/src/tactic.rs:329-340 (the ∀ case *renames* the bound variable to the supplied name by capture-unaware `apply_subst_to_expr`, with a special case when the name already IS the binder); proof/src/lib.rs:199-238 (`ProofExpr` — `Not` is its OWN constructor, NOT sugar for `Implies(p, False)`)
guards: Catches mapping Lean's `intro h` on a `¬ p` goal to LOGOS `intro h`. In Lean `Not p` unfolds to `p → False` and `intro` succeeds. In LOGOS `ProofExpr::Not` is a distinct constructor (lib.rs:230) and `ProofState::intro` matches only `Implies`/`ForAll` (tactic.rs:315-355), so the script step fails with `DoesNotApply` — at the FIRST step of a proof whose remaining steps were all emitted on the assumption that it succeeded. The translator must either re-express the goal as `Implies(p, ⊥)` before emitting, or refuse.

Catches emitting Lean's zero-argument `intro` (which names the hypothesis inaccessibly, `h✝`) as a bare LOGOS `intro`. `arg()` (tactic_script.rs:264-274) peeks for a `Tok::Word` and errors if the next token is a separator — so bare `intro` followed by `.` is a PARSE error, and the whole script is rejected before any step runs. The translator must synthesise a name. It must further ensure the synthesised name cannot collide: `ProofState::intro` on a ∀ goal substitutes the new name into the body (tactic.rs:332-337), so choosing a name that already occurs free in the body captures it silently.

Catches emitting Lean's multi-binder `intro a b c` verbatim. The script grammar's atom is `NAME ARG?` — exactly one argument (tactic_script.rs:16, :275-292) — so `intro a b c` parses as `intro a`, and then `b` is read as the next ATOM, i.e. a tactic name; `canonical("b")` is `None` and the script dies with "unknown tactic `b`". Lean's `intro a b c` must become `intro a . intro b . intro c`.

Catches the alias trap in the other direction. `let` is an `intro` alias (tactic_script.rs:310). A translator that emits a LOGOS `let`-binding step spelled `let x` while meaning a local definition gets ∀/→ introduction instead, silently. Likewise `fix` and `given` — `given` is also the surface keyword for a PREMISE (`Given:`), so the two readings must not be conflated.
oracle: For each theorem below the emitted script is a `;`-separated sequence of `intro <name>` atoms whose count equals the number of Lean binders introduced, every `<name>` is a single `[A-Za-z0-9_]+` word, and `ProofState::run_script` on the translated goal leaves `open_goals() == 1` with the expected residual target. The `¬`-goal theorem must NOT be emitted as `intro`.

cases.title: `exact` takes a NAMED HYPOTHESIS in LOGOS, never a term — `exact (f h)` has no image
cases.lean: exact, exact with an applied term, exact up to definitional unfolding
cases.target: LOGOS script atom `exact <name>` — canonical `exact`, aliases `from`, `because` (proof/src/tactic_script.rs:277, :311) → `combinators::exact` (proof/src/tactic.rs:1017-1021) → `ProofState::exact` (proof/src/tactic.rs:377-391)
evidence: proof/src/tactic_script.rs:277 (`"exact" => Ok(c::exact(&arg()?))` — the argument is a `String`, lexed as one `Tok::Word`, and is used as a HYPOTHESIS NAME); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:89-100 (the script lexer produces only `Word`/`Semi`/ parens/brackets/`|`/`<;>` — there is no application, no parenthesised term, no operator, so a term argument cannot even be TOKENISED); proof/src/tactic.rs:377-391 (`exact` looks the name up in `g.hyps` by `h.name == name` and then demands `h.prop == g.target` — STRUCTURAL equality of `ProofExpr`, with no normalisation, no unfolding and no unification); proof/src/tactic.rs:183-186 (`direct_hyp` — the only way a name enters `hyps` is a premise, an `intro`, or a `cases` branch)
guards: THE CENTRAL TIER-8 TRAP FOR THIS TACTIC. Lean's `exact e` takes an arbitrary TERM. `exact (h₁ h₂)`, `exact ⟨a, b⟩`, `exact Nat.le_refl n`, `exact fun x => f x` are all ordinary Lean. NONE of them has a LOGOS script image: `arg()` reads exactly one word (tactic_script.rs:266-271) and anything else is a parse error, or — far worse — `exact f h` parses as `exact f` followed by the ATOM `h`, so the translator's term silently becomes "close the goal with hypothesis `f`, then run the tactic `h`", which fails with "unknown tactic `h`" AFTER `exact f` may already have committed.

Catches assuming `exact` is up to definitional equality. Lean's `exact` elaborates the term against the goal with full defeq (delta, iota, beta, eta, proof irrelevance). LOGOS's is `h.prop == g.target` (tactic.rs:380) — derived `PartialEq` on `ProofExpr`. `hp : p ∧ q` does not close the goal `q ∧ p`; `hp : ¬¬p` does not close `p`; a hypothesis stated with the arguments in a different but equivalent spelling does not close anything. A translator that emits `exact h` wherever Lean wrote `exact h` will produce scripts that fail on goals Lean accepted, and the failure is reported as `DoesNotApply`, i.e. as if the hypothesis were the wrong one.

Catches confusing `exact` with `assumption`. LOGOS's `exact` fails with `NoSuchHypothesis` when the NAME is absent and `DoesNotApply` when the name is present but the proposition differs (tactic.rs:385-390); `assumption` (tactic.rs:361-373) searches all hypotheses. Since LOGOS hypothesis names are MACHINE-CHOSEN in several places (`hp0`, `hp1`, … for premises, tactic.rs:211; `h_1`/`h_2`/`h_l`/`h_r`/`h_w` after `cases`, tactic.rs:516-541), a translator that carries Lean's user-written names into `exact` will name hypotheses that do not exist. `assumption` is the robust emission; `exact` is only safe for a name the translator itself created.

Catches the alias `from`/`because` (tactic_script.rs:311) being emitted as prose. `from h` means `exact h`, and `from` is also a Lean keyword in `show T from e` — a translator that passes `show … from …` through as script text produces a LOGOS `exact` applied to whatever word follows `from`.
oracle: Every emitted `exact` atom's argument is a single word that names a hypothesis the translator itself introduced (a premise name, an `intro` name, or a `cases`-generated `h_1`/`h_2`/`h_l`/`h_r`/`h_w`), and `ProofState::exact` closes the goal. Any Lean `exact` whose argument is not a bare free variable of the local context must NOT be emitted as `exact`; the harness asserts the translator either restructured the proof or emitted a diagnostic.

cases.title: `apply` — no script spelling exists; the Rust `apply` is single-antecedent modus ponens
cases.lean: apply, apply with several arguments, apply with implicit unification, apply at
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: proof/src/tactic_script.rs:308-327 (`canonical` — the COMPLETE alias table. There is no arm producing "apply", so the word `apply` in a script reaches tactic_script.rs:261-262 and dies with `ScriptError("unknown tactic \`apply\`")`); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:275-292 (`parse_primitive`'s dispatch — fifteen arms, none of them `apply`; an unmatched canonical name is itself an error at :291); proof/src/tactic.rs:984-1147 (module `combinators` — the COMPLETE set of tactic VALUES: intro, assumption, simp, decide, omega, crush, exact, split, left, right, exists, cases, rewrite, induction, induction_over, auto, seq, first, try_, repeat, all_goals, then_all. There is no `combinators::apply`, so `apply` is not even composable from Rust the way every other primitive is); proof/src/tactic.rs:467-484 (`ProofState::apply`, the only entry point, exists as an inherent method — and it is modus ponens on ONE `ProofExpr::Implies(ant, con)`: it requires the rule to be a top-level implication, unifies only its CONCLUSION against the goal, and emits exactly one subgoal, the antecedent)

The script parser's failure is a `ScriptError`, which `compile_theorem` surfaces as a proof failure rather than as a translation failure, so the bug is reported against the user's theorem instead of against the translator.

Catches the plausible re-spelling `exact` for `apply`. `apply f` leaves subgoals; `exact f` must close the goal. A translator that maps `apply h` to `exact h` produces a script that fails whenever `h` is not literally the goal, and — in the one case where `h`'s conclusion IS the goal syntactically — closes the goal WITHOUT ever discharging the antecedent, because `ProofState::exact` only compares `h.prop` to `g.target` (tactic.rs:380). For `hpq : p → q` and goal `q` that comparison fails, so this particular slip is caught; but see `applyConclusionIsGoal` below, where the rule's conclusion and the goal coincide and the mis-emission is much harder to see.

Catches "just use `auto`". `ProofState::auto` (tactic.rs:901-914) runs the whole backward chainer over every hypothesis; it either closes the goal outright or fails. It is not a step-wise `apply`: it produces NO subgoals, so a Lean proof of the shape `apply f; <proof of the antecedent>` becomes `auto; <proof of the antecedent>` where the second half now runs against whatever goal remained — usually none, making the rest of the script a `NoOpenGoals` error, or, if `auto` failed, the first half is a hard failure. Neither is a translation.

Catches the scale error. Even reaching `ProofState::apply` through the Rust API is not enough: Lean's `apply f` handles a rule with an arbitrary TELESCOPE of arguments (`f : ∀ a b, P a → Q b → R`), instantiates implicit arguments by unification, and spawns one goal per unfilled argument. LOGOS's takes a single `Implies(ant, con)` and spawns exactly one goal (tactic.rs:469-479). The multi-premise rules below are outside that fragment even with full Rust access.

A harness additionally asserts that no emitted script, anywhere in the corpus, contains a word whose `canonical` image is `None` — i.e. every emitted atom is one of the fifteen primitives.

Must NOT emit a script.
