cases.lean: assumption, assumption against a defeq hypothesis, assumption with metavariables
cases.target: LOGOS script atom `assumption` — canonical `assumption`, arity 0, aliases `done`, `trivial`, `established`, `hypothesis` (proof/src/tactic_script.rs:281, :315) → `combinators::assumption` (proof/src/tactic.rs:993-995) → `ProofState::assumption` (proof/src/tactic.rs:361-373)
evidence: proof/src/tactic.rs:361-373 (`assumption` scans `g.hyps` for the FIRST `h` with `h.prop == g.target` — derived structural `PartialEq` on `ProofExpr`, no normalisation — and closes the goal with THAT hypothesis's recorded `DerivationTree`, so a conjunct extracted by `cases` re-emits its `ConjunctionElim` projection rather than a dangling name); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:315 ("assumption"|"done"|"trivial"|"established"| "hypothesis" ⟼ "assumption"); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:281 (arity 0 — `arg()` is never called, so a trailing word after `assumption` is parsed as the NEXT atom); proof/src/tactic.rs:183-186 (`direct_hyp` — every in-scope hypothesis carries a `PremiseMatch` leaf as its proof, which is what the certifier resolves)
guards: Catches assuming Lean's search strength. Lean's `assumption` matches a hypothesis against the goal up to REDUCIBLE definitional unfolding and instantiates the goal's metavariables while doing so. LOGOS's is `h.prop == g.target` on an untyped FOL `ProofExpr` (tactic.rs:363). `h : ¬ p` does not close the goal `p → False` — those are `Not(p)` and `Implies(p, False)`, different constructors (lib.rs:224, :230). `h : p ∧ q` does not close `q ∧ p`. A translator that emits `assumption` wherever Lean wrote it will produce scripts that fail on goals Lean discharged, and the reported error is `NoSuchHypothesis`, which reads like a naming bug.

Catches the alias `trivial` (tactic_script.rs:315). Lean's `trivial` is a DIFFERENT tactic: it proves `True`, closes `rfl` goals, and runs `assumption` among other things. LOGOS's `trivial` IS `assumption` and nothing else — so Lean's `trivial` on the goal `True` becomes a LOGOS `assumption` that fails unless `True` is literally a hypothesis. Emitting the English word instead of the canonical name is how this slips through: the alias table makes the wrong word parse.

Catches the alias `done` (tactic_script.rs:315). Lean's `done` SUCCEEDS iff there are no goals left and proves nothing; LOGOS's `done` closes the focused goal from a hypothesis. A translator that emits `done` to assert "the proof is finished" instead discharges a goal — and if it happens to succeed, the script is now one step short of where the translator thought it was, so every subsequent step targets the wrong goal.

Catches losing the PROJECTION. `assumption` closes with `h.proof`, not with a fresh leaf (tactic.rs:364-365). For a conjunct introduced by `cases` the recorded proof is a `ConjunctionElim` node over the parent (tactic.rs:505-517), so the certified term is the projection applied to the parent's proof. A translator that "optimises" by re-emitting a `PremiseMatch` leaf for the conjunct name produces a derivation whose leaf cites a hypothesis the certifier's context does not bind, and `check_derivation` fails with an unbound reference far from the `cases` that caused it.
oracle: `ProofState::run_script` on the translated goal closes it, `qed()` returns a `VerifiedProof` with `verified == true`, and for `conjunctViaCases` the assembled derivation's closing node is a `ConjunctionElim`, not a bare `PremiseMatch`.

cases.title: `rfl` has no script spelling — it must be routed through `simp` or `decide`
cases.lean: rfl, rfl up to delta/iota, Eq.refl, rfl on a non-Eq reflexive relation
cases.target: LOGOS script atom `simp` (canonical `simp`, arity 0, aliases `simplify`, `normalize`, `simplification` — proof/src/tactic_script.rs:282, :316) whose closing branch emits `InferenceRule::Reflexivity` (proof/src/tactic.rs:806-816), or `decide` (canonical `decide`, aliases `compute`, `evaluate`, `calculate` — tactic_script.rs:283, :317) for a ground goal
evidence: proof/src/tactic_script.rs:308-327 (`canonical` — there is NO arm mapping any word to "rfl"; the word `rfl` in a script is `unknown tactic \`rfl\``); proof/src/tactic.rs:806-816 (`simp`'s closing attempt: if the normalised target is `ProofExpr::Identity(l, r)` with `l == r` it closes with a `InferenceRule::Reflexivity` leaf — this is the reflexivity route); proof/src/tactic.rs:820-826 (`simp` FAILS with `DoesNotApply` when it neither rewrote nor closed — so `simp` is not a no-op and cannot stand in for a `rfl` that had nothing to do); proof/src/decide.rs:1-12, :64 (`decide_expr` — a router over ground `Int` identities, ground comparisons and `Bool` equalities, with propositional structure recursing through the intro rules; it declines on anything open); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1473-1493 (`def_eq_normalized` — the kernel's own definitional equality, which is what Lean's `rfl` corresponds to, and which the SCRIPT layer never calls: the script layer compares `ProofExpr`s, not kernel `Term`s)
guards: Catches emitting the word `rfl`. It is not in the alias table (tactic_script.rs: 308-327), so the script dies at parse time — before any step runs — with "unknown tactic `rfl`". Because `parse_script` is called from `run_script` (tactic_script.rs:358-362) and the state is left unchanged on a parse error, the failure is total: a single stray `rfl` anywhere in a long script discards the whole proof.

Catches assuming `simp` reproduces Lean's `rfl`. Lean's `rfl` succeeds up to FULL definitional equality in the kernel — delta-unfolding every transparent definition, iota-reducing every recursor application, beta, eta, and structure eta. LOGOS's reflexivity route is a SYNTACTIC `l == r` check on `ProofExpr` after simp-set rewriting (tactic.rs:808-816), and the simp set is only the in-scope hypotheses that orient as rules (tactic.rs:264-272). So `rfl` proving `2 + 2 = 4` by iota becomes `decide`; `rfl` proving `f x = g x` by unfolding `f` becomes NOTHING, because there is no delta step at the script layer at all.

Catches routing a NON-`Eq` reflexivity through this path. Lean's `rfl` closes any goal whose head is a relation tagged `@[refl]`, which in Mathlib includes `LE.le`. LOGOS's reflexivity branch matches only `ProofExpr::Identity` (tactic.rs:808), and `n ≤ n` translates to a `le` shape, not an `Identity`. The correct target there is the `le_refl` axiom (kernel/src/prelude.rs:202-340) reached through `auto`, not `simp` — and `simp` on such a goal fails outright (tactic.rs:820-826) rather than leaving it open, so the mis-route is at least loud.

Catches the silent-success inversion. `decide` DECLINES a false goal rather than erroring (decide.rs:8-11: "A false, open, or unsupported goal yields `None` — decide declines, it never guesses"), and `simp` fails when it has nothing to do. So a translator cannot distinguish "the goal was already closed" from "the tactic did not apply" by exit status alone; it must inspect `open_goals()`.
oracle: No emitted script contains the token `rfl`. For each `Eq`-shaped theorem the emitted atom is `simp` or `decide` and `run_script` leaves `open_goals() == 0`; the assembled derivation's closing rule is `Reflexivity` (simp route) or `ArithDecision`/ `NativeDecide` (decide route, decide.rs:1-12). For `leRefl` the emitted atom must NOT be `simp`.
note: `LE.le` is NOT `@[refl]` in bare Lean 4.14 — `by rfl` on `n ≤ n` errors with "no @[refl] lemma registered for relation LE.le". Since this corpus forbids `import Mathlib`, `leRefl` below is written `Nat.le_refl n`; the Mathlib spelling `by rfl` is the construct the guard is about.

cases.title: `constructor` on `∧` ⟼ `split` — but LOGOS's `split` is ∧-only and the word `constructor` is its ALIAS
cases.lean: constructor, exact ⟨_, _⟩, constructor on ∨, constructor on Iff, refine ⟨_, _⟩
cases.target: LOGOS script atom `split` — canonical `split`, arity 0, aliases `constructor`, `both`, `conjunction` (proof/src/tactic_script.rs:286, :320) → `combinators::split` (proof/src/tactic.rs:1022-1025) → `ProofState::split` (proof/src/tactic.rs:395-410), emitting `InferenceRule::ConjunctionIntro`
evidence: proof/src/tactic_script.rs:320 ("split"|"constructor"|"both"|"conjunction" ⟼ "split" — the Lean word `constructor` is accepted, and it means ∧-introduction REGARDLESS of the goal); proof/src/tactic.rs:395-410 (`ProofState::split` matches ONLY `ProofExpr::And(a, b)` and returns `DoesNotApply` for every other shape, :408); proof/src/tactic.rs:401-405 (two subgoals, left conjunct FIRST, certified by `InferenceRule::ConjunctionIntro`); proof/src/tactic.rs:280-298 (`refine` pushes the new subgoals to the FRONT of `open`, in order — so the step after `split` targets the LEFT conjunct); proof/src/lib.rs:217-231 (`ProofExpr` — `And`, `Or` and `Iff` are three distinct constructors; there is no generic "apply the inductive's first constructor")
guards: THE ALIAS TRAP. A translator that passes Lean's tactic word through unchanged gets the right answer for `∧` by luck and the WRONG tactic everywhere else: the script word `constructor` is hard-wired to ∧-introduction (tactic_script.rs:320), so Lean's `constructor` on an `∨` goal — where Lean picks `Or.inl` — becomes LOGOS `split`, which reports `DoesNotApply` ("split expects ∧, got Or(..)"). The error names `split`, a tactic the translator never wrote, so the diagnostic points at the wrong place.

Catches `constructor` on an `Iff` goal. Lean's `constructor` applies `Iff.intro` and leaves the two implications. LOGOS has `ProofExpr::Iff` (lib.rs:227) and `InferenceRule::BicondIntro` in the rule set, but `split` does not handle it (tactic.rs:397-409) and NO script atom introduces an `Iff`. An `Iff` goal therefore has no step-wise script proof at all; the only route is `auto`.

Catches `constructor` on a general inductive. Lean's `constructor` applies the first constructor of ANY inductive whose conclusion matches — `Exists.intro`, `Or.inl`, `Nat.succ`, a user structure's `mk`. LOGOS's script layer works on FOL `ProofExpr`, which has exactly three introduction atoms (`split`, `left`/`right`, `exists`); a `constructor` on a user structure has no image, and its `⟨…⟩` sugar is equally unreachable because `exact` takes only a name (see T08-002).

Catches the ORDER of the residual goals. `split` pushes the left conjunct to the front of `open` (tactic.rs:401-404 then :296-297), matching Lean's `constructor`. A translator that reverses them — natural if it folds a goal list — produces a script whose subsequent steps are applied to the wrong conjunct and which, for a symmetric conjunction like `p ∧ p`, still SUCCEEDS while proving the goals in the wrong order. That is undetectable downstream.

Catches emitting `both` (tactic_script.rs:320) from prose. The alias exists so an English proof can read "…and both…"; a translator that emits the English rendering of a Lean `And.intro` gets ∧-introduction, which is right — but `both` is also a plausible rendering of a two-branch case analysis, which is `cases`, not `split`.
oracle: Every `∧`-goal theorem emits `split` (or the alias `constructor`) and `run_script` leaves exactly two open goals with the LEFT conjunct focused. The `∨` and `Iff` theorems must NOT emit `split`; the translator must emit `left`/`right` for the former and a diagnostic (or `auto`) for the latter.

cases.title: `left` / `right` — the names coincide, the goal shapes they accept do not
cases.lean: left, right, Or.inl / Or.inr, left on a general two-constructor inductive
cases.target: LOGOS script atoms `left` and `right` — canonical `left` / `right`, arity 0, NO aliases (proof/src/tactic_script.rs:287-288, :321-322) → `combinators::left` / `combinators::right` (proof/src/tactic.rs:1026-1033) → `ProofState::left` / `right` → `ProofState::disjunct` (proof/src/tactic.rs:413-439), emitting `InferenceRule::DisjunctionIntro`
evidence: proof/src/tactic_script.rs:321-322 ("left" ⟼ "left", "right" ⟼ "right" — these are the only two entries in `canonical` with a single spelling and no English alias); proof/src/tactic.rs:422-439 (`disjunct` matches ONLY `ProofExpr::Or(a, b)`, picks `a` or `b` by the `take_left` flag, emits ONE subgoal, and returns `DoesNotApply` for every other goal shape, :435-437); proof/src/tactic.rs:428-432 (both branches emit the SAME rule, `InferenceRule::DisjunctionIntro` — the choice of disjunct is recorded only in the subgoal's target, not in the rule); proof/src/certifier.rs (the `DisjunctionIntro` arm must recover which side was taken by matching the child's conclusion against the conclusion's two disjuncts)
guards: Catches `left`/`right` on a non-`Or` goal. Lean's `left` applies the FIRST constructor of any two-constructor inductive: `Sum.inl`, `Bool.false`... and on an `Iff` goal `left` is an error in Lean too, but on `Decidable p` it picks `isTrue`. LOGOS's is `ProofExpr::Or`-only (tactic.rs:425). Anything else is `DoesNotApply`.

Catches the rule-level ambiguity. Because both branches emit `InferenceRule::DisjunctionIntro` with no side marker (tactic.rs:428-432), a derivation for `p ∨ p` is IDENTICAL whichever branch ran. That is harmless for `p ∨ p`, but it means a translator cannot round-trip a derivation back to the tactic that produced it, and a harness that checks "the translator emitted `left`" must compare the SUBGOAL, not the rule.

Catches the absent aliases. Every other tactic in the table has English synonyms (tactic_script.rs:310-326); `left` and `right` have none. A translator rendering Lean's `left` as prose — "take the first disjunct", "choose the left" — produces words `canonical` does not know, and the script dies with `unknown tactic`. The canonical spelling must be emitted verbatim.

Catches the FILLER-WORD collision. `parse_atom` calls `skip_filler` before every atom, and the filler list (tactic_script.rs:298-303) includes `the`, `on`, `a`, `of`, `to`, `and`. A translator emitting "right on" or "and left" has those words silently discarded — which happens to work — but emitting `left of h` discards `of` and then reads `h` as the NEXT ATOM, so the script fails with "unknown tactic `h`" rather than with anything about disjunctions.

Catches the one-subgoal shape. Lean's `left` leaves one goal; so does LOGOS's. But a translator that models `∨`-introduction as "split then discard" (there being a `split` atom right next to `left` in the table) would emit `split`, which on an `Or` goal is `DoesNotApply` — see T08-006.
oracle: Each `∨`-goal theorem emits exactly one of `left` / `right`, `run_script` leaves `open_goals() == 1`, and the residual target is the corresponding disjunct. The non-`Or` theorems must not emit `left` or `right`.

cases.title: `cases` / `obtain` — LOGOS binder names are FIXED (`h_1`,`h_2`,`h_l`,`h_r`,`h_w`) and the ∃-witness name depends on unrelated earlier tactics
cases.lean: cases, cases … with | intro a b, obtain ⟨a, b⟩ := h, rcases, ∃-elimination
cases.target: LOGOS script atom `cases <name>` — canonical `cases`, arity 1, aliases `destruct`, `consider`, `casework` (proof/src/tactic_script.rs:278, :312) → `combinators::cases` (proof/src/tactic.rs:1038-1042) → `ProofState::cases` (proof/src/tactic.rs:495-554)
evidence: proof/src/tactic.rs:486-494 (the doc comment fixing the three shapes and the naming scheme); proof/src/tactic.rs:516-517 (`∧`: pushes `format!("{name}_1")` and `format!("{name}_2")`, each backed by a `ConjunctionElim` projection of the parent); proof/src/tactic.rs:523, :526 (`∨`: `format!("{name}_l")` and `format!("{name}_r")`, two subgoals, LEFT first, `InferenceRule::DisjunctionCases`); proof/src/tactic.rs:536-541 (`∃`: a fresh witness CONSTANT from `fresh_witness`, and the hypothesis `format!("{name}_w")`); proof/src/tactic.rs:228-231 (`fresh_witness` — `self.fresh += 1; format!("W{}", self.fresh)`, a counter on the WHOLE proof state); proof/src/tactic.rs:571 (`ProofState::induction` ALSO bumps `self.fresh`, and tactic.rs:651 shows `induction_over` bumping it once per constructor argument); proof/src/tactic.rs:515-518 (the `∧` branch CLONES `g.hyps` and pushes — the parent `h` REMAINS in scope); proof/src/tactic.rs:550-552 (every other hypothesis shape — a `Nat`, a list, a user inductive — is `DoesNotApply`: "cases expects ∧/∨/∃ hypothesis")
guards: THE WITNESS-NAME TRAP, and the most dangerous part of this case. `cases h` on an `∃` introduces a fresh constant named `W{n}` where `n` is `ProofState::fresh` (tactic.rs:228-231) — a counter shared with `induction` (tactic.rs:571) and `induction_over` (tactic.rs:651). The witness's name therefore depends on HOW MANY EARLIER TACTICS IN THE SAME PROOF bumped the counter, not on anything local. A translator that predicts `W1` by looking at the `∃`-elimination in isolation is right only when no induction preceded it. Because the witness constant appears inside the residual goal, a wrong prediction makes every later `exact`/`rewrite` reference the wrong term — and since `ProofExpr` is untyped, the mismatch surfaces as a structural inequality, not as a name error.

Catches assuming `cases` CLEARS the scrutinee. Lean's `cases h` consumes `h`. LOGOS's `∧` branch clones the hypothesis list and pushes the two projections (tactic.rs:515-518), so `h` is still there. A translator that emits `cases h` twice — e.g. because it re-destructures in a later branch — gets `h_1`/`h_2` pushed a SECOND time, and `exact h_1` then resolves against whichever copy `find` reaches first (tactic.rs:379, `iter().find`), i.e. the earlier one. Silent, and correct only by accident.

Catches the `∨` branch's goal ORDER and its effect on a flat script. `cases h` on a disjunction produces TWO goals, left first, pushed to the front of `open` (tactic.rs:528-532 then :296-297). The script language has no focusing (see T08-025), so the tactics after `cases` run on the left branch until it closes and then continue into the right branch. A translator that emits Lean's two `·` blocks concatenated gets the right behaviour ONLY if the first block closes its goal exactly; if it closes two or leaves one open, the blocks silently misalign.

Catches mapping `rcases h with ⟨a, b⟩ | c` (an alternation pattern) to anything. LOGOS `cases` dispatches on the hypothesis's shape alone; there is no pattern language, so a mixed ∧/∨ pattern must be decomposed into a `cases` per level with the machine-chosen names threaded through.
oracle: The emitted script contains one `cases` atom per destructuring level, every downstream hypothesis reference uses the LOGOS-generated name, and the emitted loss record names BINDER_NAMING and (for nested patterns) DESTRUCTURING_DEPTH. For `existsElim` the harness asserts the translator did not hard-code `W1` but read the witness name back from the resulting `ProofState`, or else refused.
loss: BINDER_NAMING. Lean's `obtain ⟨a, b⟩ := h` / `cases h with | intro a b` name the components; LOGOS names them `h_1`/`h_2` after the PARENT. The translator must rewrite every downstream reference from the Lean name to the LOGOS name, and must record that the user's chosen names are gone. Acceptable because the names are not semantically load-bearing — but only if the rewrite is total: one missed reference becomes `NoSuchHypothesis` in the middle of a script.

DESTRUCTURING_DEPTH. Lean's `obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, c⟩ := h` destructures in one step. LOGOS needs `cases h . cases h_1`, and the inner components are then `h_1_1` / `h_1_2`. Every nesting level costs an atom and lengthens the generated name.

SCRUTINEE_CLASS. LOGOS's `cases` eliminates a HYPOTHESIS of propositional shape. `cases n` for `n : Nat`, `cases xs` for a list, `cases c` for a user inductive are all outside it (tactic.rs:550-552); the generic route is `induction_over` (tactic.rs:623-695), which is Rust-only — see T08-010 and T08-020.

cases.title: `induction n` ⟼ zero-argument `induction`, which consumes the goal's OUTERMOST `∀`
cases.lean: induction n, induction n with | zero | succ k ih, induction on a context variable
cases.target: LOGOS script atom `induction` — canonical `induction`, arity **0**, alias `induct` (proof/src/tactic_script.rs:290, :324) → `combinators::induction` (proof/src/tactic.rs:1047-1050) → `ProofState::induction` (proof/src/tactic.rs:561-607), emitting `InferenceRule::StructuralInduction { variable, ind_type: "Nat", step_var }`
evidence: proof/src/tactic_script.rs:290 (`"induction" => Ok(c::induction())` — `arg()` is NEVER called, so the atom takes no argument and a following word is read as the next ATOM); proof/src/tactic.rs:562-570 (`induction` reads the target and requires `ProofExpr::ForAll { variable, body }`; anything else is `DoesNotApply` — so the variable inducted on is whatever the goal's OUTERMOST binder happens to be); proof/src/tactic.rs:601 (`ind_type: "Nat".to_string()` — hard-coded); proof/src/tactic.rs:583-586 (base target is `body[variable := Constant("Zero")]`, step target is `body[variable := Function("Succ", [Constant(step_var)])]`); proof/src/tactic.rs:571, :577 (`self.fresh += 1` then `step_var = format!("K{}", self.fresh)` — uppercase so the search treats it as a rigid eigenconstant); proof/src/tactic.rs:593 (the induction hypothesis is named `"ih"`, hard-coded, and placed FIRST in the step's hypothesis list); proof/src/tactic.rs:604 (children are `[base_goal, step_goal]`, base first); proof/src/tactic.rs:916-941 (`assemble` remaps the eigenconstant back to a bound `Variable` via `eigen_to_var_tree`, which is what the certifier's `Match` arm binds)
guards: Catches emitting `induction n`. The atom's arity is zero (tactic_script.rs:290), so the trailing `n` is parsed as the NEXT ATOM and `canonical("n")` is `None`: the whole script fails at PARSE time with "unknown tactic `n`", discarding the proof (`run_script` leaves the state unchanged on a parse error, tactic_script.rs:358-362). This is the single most likely mechanical slip in Tier 8 and it is at least loud.

Catches inducting on the WRONG variable. With a goal `∀ m n, P m n`, Lean's `induction n` inducts on the inner binder; LOGOS's argumentless `induction` takes `m`, the outermost. Both produce a base case and a step case, both typecheck, and the resulting theorem is a DIFFERENT theorem — proved, certified, and wrong. Nothing downstream can detect it, because the FOL layer is untyped and the substitution `m := Zero` is perfectly well-formed. A translator MUST verify that the outermost binder is the one Lean named.

Catches the `fresh`-counter coupling. `induction` increments `ProofState::fresh` (tactic.rs:571), the same counter that names `∃`-elimination witnesses `W{n}` (tactic.rs:228-231). Emitting an induction changes the name of every later witness in the same proof. See T08-008.

Catches assuming the step variable is a `Variable`. It is a `Constant` named `K{n}` during the search (tactic.rs:572-577) and only becomes a `Variable` when `assemble` runs (tactic.rs:926-930). A translator that emits a step-case reference as `Variable("K1")` will not match the goal, which holds `Constant("K1")`.
oracle: The emitted script contains a bare `induction` atom with NO argument; the goal it runs against has the Lean-named variable as its outermost `∀`; every step-case hypothesis reference is `ih`; and the loss record names TARGET_SELECTION and CASE_NAMING. For `innerBinder` the harness asserts the translator either reordered the binders or emitted a diagnostic rather than an `induction` atom.
loss: TARGET_SELECTION. Lean's `induction n` names its target and works on a variable already in the local context; it REVERTS every hypothesis depending on `n`, generalises, and re-introduces. LOGOS's `induction` has no argument: it can only induct on the goal's outermost `∀`. A Lean proof that does `intro n; …; induction n` must be re-ordered so the `∀ n` is the outermost connective at the moment the atom runs — i.e. the translator must perform Lean's `revert` itself, at the script level, where there is no `revert` atom to perform it with. If any hypothesis mentions `n`, the generalisation is not expressible at all and the case escalates to `reject`.

CASE_NAMING. `induction n with | zero => … | succ k ih => …` names both the cases and the step variable and the IH. LOGOS fixes all three: the cases are positional (base then step, tactic.rs:604), the step variable is `K{fresh}` (tactic.rs:577), and the IH is `ih` (tactic.rs:593). Every reference in the translated step block must be rewritten to `ih`, and every reference to Lean's `k` to the generated `K{n}`.

IH_PLACEMENT. The IH is pushed to the FRONT of the step's hypothesis list deliberately (tactic.rs:590-594), so `assumption`/`auto` prefer it over a base fact and keep the step variable symbolic. Lean places it last. Any translated step that relies on `assumption` picking a particular hypothesis changes meaning.

cases.title: `induction xs` on a list — the script `induction` is hard-wired to `Nat` and will silently substitute `Zero` / `Succ K` into a list-typed goal
cases.lean: induction on List, induction on a user inductive, induction using a custom eliminator
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: proof/src/tactic.rs:599-603 (`InferenceRule::StructuralInduction { variable, ind_type: "Nat".to_string(), step_var }` — the inductive type is a HARD-CODED string literal, not derived from the goal); proof/src/tactic.rs:583-586 (the base target is `body[variable := Constant("Zero")]` and the step target is `body[variable := Function("Succ", [Constant(step_var)])]` — the two Peano constructors, by name, unconditionally); proof/src/tactic.rs:556-560 (the method's own doc comment: "Nat only for now — `List`/general inductives need the dependent `InductionScheme`"); proof/src/tactic.rs:623-695 (`induction_over` — the generic scheme, one subgoal per `CtorSpec`, IHs for the recursive arguments — which is exactly what a list induction needs); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:275-292 (`parse_primitive`'s dispatch — `induction_over` has NO arm, and `canonical` (:308-327) has no word mapping to it, so it is unreachable from script text; cf. T08-020); proof/src/lib.rs:199-238 (`ProofExpr` is UNTYPED first-order logic: a `ProofTerm` carries no type, so substituting `Zero` for a list-valued variable is well-formed at this layer and raises nothing); kernel/src/prelude.rs (the LOGOS prelude registers `EList`/`ENil`/`ECons` and `TList`, but Lean's `List` is ABSENT — see T10-012 — so even the generic scheme needs the inductive to be declared first)
guards: THE HIGHEST-VALUE TIER-8 REJECTION. The tempting wrong move is to emit the bare `induction` atom and let the goal shape sort itself out. It will not fail. LOGOS's `induction` requires only that the goal be a `ProofExpr::ForAll` (tactic.rs:563-570) — it never looks at the variable's type, because there are no types at that layer. Against `∀ xs, length (append xs nil) = length xs` it produces the base goal `length (append Zero nil) = length Zero` and the step goal `length (append (Succ K1) nil) = length (Succ K1)`. Those are syntactically well-formed `ProofExpr`s. `auto`, `simp` and `crush` will all happily try to prove them, and for a statement whose predicate is insensitive to the substituted term — a reflexivity, a tautology, anything the backward chainer closes structurally — they will SUCCEED. The resulting `StructuralInduction` node claims a `Nat` induction for a `List` statement, and the failure, if it comes at all, surfaces in `check_derivation` as a kernel type error about `Nat` in a theorem that never mentioned `Nat`.

Catches "map `List` onto `Nat` by length". Inducting on `xs.length` instead of `xs` is a real proof technique, but it is a DIFFERENT proof: the induction hypothesis is `∀ ys, length ys = k → P ys`, not `P tail`. A translator that silently performs this reindexing has rewritten the user's proof, and the generalisation it must insert (over all lists of that length) is not expressible with the script atoms available.

Catches "use `induction_over`". It is the right scheme — but it is a Rust API (tactic.rs:623-695) with no script spelling, and it requires the caller to supply a `Vec<CtorSpec>` listing each constructor and which of its arguments are recursive (proof/src/tactic.rs:40-58). A translator that produces `ProofStrategy::Script` text cannot reach it, and one that drives `ProofState` from Rust must ALSO have declared the inductive in the kernel context first, since Lean's `List` is not in the LOGOS prelude. Claiming `induction_over` as the target without doing both is a phantom translation.

Catches `induction … using <custom eliminator>` and strong/two-step induction. Even the Rust `induction_over` is plain structural induction, one IH per recursive argument (tactic.rs:668-675); `Nat.strong_induction_on`, `List.reverseRecOn` and friends have no analogue, and LOGOS has no well-founded recursion at all (kernel/src/termination.rs — syntactic Giménez guard only).
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_INDUCTION_NOT_NAT for every theorem below and emits no script containing the atom `induction`. A harness additionally asserts that no emitted `StructuralInduction` rule anywhere in the corpus carries `ind_type` other than `"Nat"`, and that every goal an `induction` atom runs against has a `Nat`-typed outermost binder in the Lean source.
diag: E_INDUCTION_NOT_NAT — must name the variable, name its Lean inductive type, state that the script-level `induction` is `Nat`-only (tactic.rs:601) and that the generic `induction_over` is not reachable from script text (tactic_script.rs:275-292), and must NOT emit an `induction` atom. If the translator has Rust-level access it may instead emit `induction_over` with an explicit `Vec<CtorSpec>` and downgrade this case to `degrade` — see the @note.
note: The index records this as `reject`, which is correct for a translator that emits script TEXT — the only surface a Lean tactic block can be compiled to. A translator that drives `ProofState` through the Rust API may legitimately emit `induction_over` with an explicit constructor list; for that translator this case is `degrade` with loss SCHEME_SELECTION (case names, IH names and IH placement are all machine-chosen, as in T08-009). The rejection stands for the script surface.

cases.title: `rw` ⟼ `rewrite`: all-occurrences Leibniz on a GROUND equation, no direction, no `at`, no ∀-instantiation, and no binder protection
cases.lean: rw [h], rw [← h], rw [h] at h', rw with a ∀-quantified equation, subst
cases.target: LOGOS script atom `rewrite <name>` — canonical `rewrite`, arity 1, aliases `rw`, `substitute`, `subst` (proof/src/tactic_script.rs:279, :313) → `combinators::rewrite` (proof/src/tactic.rs:1043-1047) → `ProofState::rewrite` (proof/src/tactic.rs:702-737), emitting `InferenceRule::Rewrite { from: rhs, to: lhs }` over an `EqualitySymmetry` premise
evidence: proof/src/tactic.rs:710-717 (the hypothesis must be `ProofExpr::Identity(l, r)`; a `ProofExpr::ForAll` wrapping an equality is `DoesNotApply` — "rewrite expects an equality hypothesis"); proof/src/tactic.rs:718 (`replace_in_expr(&g.target, &lhs, &rhs)` — the direction is fixed lhs→rhs, and the SCRUTINEE is `g.target`: the goal, never a hypothesis); proof/src/tactic.rs:113-128 and :130-156 (`replace_in_term` / `replace_in_expr` — "Replace EVERY occurrence", recursing through `Predicate` args, `Identity` sides, every connective, and — critically — into `ForAll`/`Exists` BODIES at :148-153 without consulting the binder); proof/src/tactic.rs:719-723 (fails when `lhs` does not occur); proof/src/tactic.rs:724-736 (the certified shape: the equality premise proves `rhs = lhs`, the open child is the rewritten goal — so `rewrite` NEVER closes the goal itself); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:313 ("rewrite"|"rw"|"substitute"|"subst" ⟼ "rewrite")
guards: THE CAPTURE BUG, and the reason this case exists. `replace_in_expr` recurses into `ForAll`/`Exists` bodies (tactic.rs:148-153) and `replace_in_term` compares `t == from` structurally (tactic.rs:115) — with NO check that `from` is the binder. `ProofExpr` binders are NAMED strings (lib.rs:235-238). So rewriting with `h : x = 0` inside a goal `∀ x, P x` replaces the BOUND occurrences of `x`, yielding `∀ x, P 0`: a different, usually stronger, statement, silently. Lean's `rw` cannot do this — `kabstract` abstracts only occurrences valid in the motive and reports "motive is not type correct" instead. A translator must prove the rewritten LHS does not collide with any binder name in the goal before emitting `rewrite`.

Catches the "all occurrences" assumption running the WRONG way. On a GROUND equation the two languages agree — Lean's `rw [h]` with `h : a = b` on `f a a = f b b` rewrites both `a`s and closes by the trailing `rfl` (verified). The divergence is entirely in the quantified and occurrence-selected cases, so a translator that tests only ground rewrites will see perfect agreement and ship the bug.

Catches the ALIAS `subst` (tactic_script.rs:313). Lean's `subst h` is a DIFFERENT tactic: it requires one side to be a local free variable, substitutes it everywhere INCLUDING in all hypotheses, and clears it. LOGOS's `subst` is `rewrite` — goal-only, no clearing. A translator that passes Lean's tactic word through gets a strictly weaker step that leaves the hypotheses untouched, and every later reference to a hypothesis Lean had rewritten now mismatches.

Catches occurrence selection. `conv ... => rw [h]` and Mathlib's `nth_rewrite` exist precisely to rewrite ONE occurrence. LOGOS's rewrite is all-or-nothing, so those have no image at any granularity — see T08-023.
oracle: Every emitted `rewrite` atom names a hypothesis whose LOGOS proposition is a `ProofExpr::Identity` (not a `ForAll`), its `lhs` is not equal to any binder name occurring in the goal, the rewrite direction matches the Lean source, and the loss record names QUANTIFIED_REWRITE / DIRECTION / LOCATION as applicable. A harness re-runs the rewritten goal through `types_equal` against the translation of Lean's post-`rw` goal and requires them equal.
loss: QUANTIFIED_REWRITE. Lean's `rw [h]` with `h : ∀ x, f x = g x` finds the FIRST match, fixes `x` from it, and rewrites only the occurrences of THAT instance (verified: on `f 1 = g 1 ∧ f 2 = g 2` the goal becomes `g 1 = g 1 ∧ f 2 = g 2`). LOGOS's `rewrite` refuses a quantified hypothesis outright (tactic.rs:710-717). The translator must pre-instantiate — which means computing Lean's first match itself, i.e. reimplementing `kabstract`'s traversal order. Acceptable only because the translator can read the instantiation off the ELABORATED `Expr` (the `Eq.mpr`/motive application Lean already built) instead of re-deriving it from the surface syntax: **translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.**

DIRECTION. There is no `← h`. `rewrite` is lhs→rhs only (tactic.rs:718). The symmetric hypothesis would have to be constructed — and the script surface has no term language to construct it with (`exact` takes a name, T08-002), so `rw [← h]` has no script image at all unless the ORIGINAL theorem is restated with the equation reversed.
LOCATION. `rw [h] at h'` rewrites in a hypothesis. `ProofState::rewrite` reads and writes only `g.target` (tactic.rs:718, :730). No `at` clause exists.

TRAILING_RFL. Lean's `rw` attempts `rfl` after rewriting and frequently closes the goal outright. LOGOS's `rewrite` always leaves the rewritten subgoal open (tactic.rs:730-735). A translator that maps `rw [h]` to `rewrite h` and then expects zero goals emits the rest of its script against a goal that is still there — and because `refine` pushes subgoals to the front (tactic.rs:296-297), the following atom runs on it and usually fails with a confusing shape error.

cases.title: `simp only [foo, bar]` — LOGOS's `simp` takes NO lemma list and silently uses every hypothesis in scope instead
cases.lean: simp, simp only [..], simp [..], simp at h, simp with a default @[simp] set
cases.target: LOGOS script atom `simp` — canonical `simp`, arity **0**, aliases `simplify`, `normalize`, `simplification` (proof/src/tactic_script.rs:282, :316) → `combinators::simp` (proof/src/tactic.rs:996-1002), whose rule set is `ProofState::scope_simp_set()` (proof/src/tactic.rs:261-272) → `ProofState::simp` (proof/src/tactic.rs:750-827)
evidence: proof/src/tactic_script.rs:282 (`"simp" => Ok(c::simp())` — `arg()` is never called; the atom is nullary and a following word is read as the NEXT atom); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:51-105 (the script lexer has `[` and `]` tokens, but `parse_atom` (:212-243) accepts a bracket ONLY after the keyword `first` (:221-231), so `simp only [h]` cannot be parsed at all); proof/src/tactic.rs:261-272 (`scope_simp_set` — the rule set is built by `register_lemma` over EVERY in-scope hypothesis, with no way to select); proof/src/simp.rs:83-91 (`register_lemma` peels the ∀-prefix and refuses a lemma with a shadowed binder, returning `false` — so some hypotheses silently do NOT become rules and there is no report of which); proof/src/tactic.rs:750-756 (`const BUDGET: usize = 1000` plus a seen-goal set, so the fixpoint is bounded and may stop mid-normalisation); proof/src/tactic.rs:806-826 (the closing attempts — reflexivity, then `assumption`; and `DoesNotApply` when it neither rewrote nor closed); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:385-396, :421-437 (`ScriptedTheorem::simp` and the `simp_pool` — the ONLY `[simp]`-attribute analogue, and it exists only inside `prove_scripted_library`, never for a standalone `## Theorem` script)
guards: THE CENTRAL TRAP. A translator that maps `simp only [Nat.add_zero]` to `simp` produces a step that is *stronger and differently-shaped*. If the extra rewrites happen to close the goal, the proof "works" and the translated script no longer corresponds to the Lean proof at all — a later step that expected the `simp only` residue now runs against `NoOpenGoals`. If they do not close it, the residue differs and every downstream `exact`/`rewrite` misses structurally. Both outcomes are silent at translation time.

Catches emitting the lemma list anyway. `simp only [h]` written verbatim parses as the atom `simp`, then the atom `only` — `canonical("only")` is `None` — so the whole script dies at parse time with "unknown tactic `only`". A translator must strip the list, and stripping it is exactly the loss above, so the stripping MUST be recorded.

Catches the silently-dropped rules. `simp::register_lemma` returns `false` for a lemma whose ∀-prefix shadows a binder (simp.rs:87-90) and `scope_simp_set` (tactic.rs:264-272) IGNORES the return value. So a hypothesis the translator supplied as a rewrite rule may simply not be in the set, with no diagnostic, and the `simp` then fails for reasons invisible from the script.

Catches relying on the `[simp]` POOL. `ScriptedTheorem { simp: true }` puts a proved conclusion into a pool that later theorems in the SAME `prove_scripted_library` call see (tactic_script.rs:392-395, :432-437). It is not an environment attribute: it does not persist, it is not visible to a `## Theorem` block, and it is keyed on proof order within one Rust call. A translator that maps Lean's `@[simp]` attribute onto it has changed a global, persistent fact into a call-local one.

Catches the budget. 1000 steps plus a seen-goal set (tactic.rs:751-754, :767) means `simp` can stop with the goal PARTIALLY normalised and still report success, because it returns `Ok` whenever `progress` is true (tactic.rs:820-821). The residual shape is then neither the input nor the Lean normal form.
oracle: No emitted script contains a `[` outside a `first [...]` construct. Every Lean `simp only [...]` maps to a `simp` atom accompanied by a loss record naming RULE_SET_SELECTION, and the harness asserts that the goal after `run_script`'s `simp` is `types_equal` to the translation of Lean's post-`simp` goal — failing the case if LOGOS normalised further.
loss: RULE_SET_SELECTION. `simp only [foo, bar]` names its rules precisely; LOGOS's `simp` cannot name any. The loss runs in the dangerous direction: LOGOS uses MORE rules than asked for, not fewer. Two `simp only` calls in the same Lean proof that deliberately normalise to different shapes both become the same LOGOS `simp`, which normalises past the first one's intended stopping point.

DEFAULT_SET. Lean's bare `simp` runs the global `@[simp]` set — thousands of core lemmas. LOGOS's bare `simp` runs the LOCAL hypotheses only (tactic.rs:264-272). The two spellings are identical and mean almost disjoint things. Every arithmetic identity Lean's `simp` discharges from the default set (`Nat.add_zero`, `List.append_nil`, …) must be supplied as an explicit premise or a cited lemma, or the LOGOS `simp` fails with `DoesNotApply`.
LOCATION. `simp at h` and `simp_all` normalise hypotheses. `ProofState::simp` reads and rewrites only `g.target` (tactic.rs:757, :766). No location clause exists.

cases.title: `omega` — the name maps 1:1, but LOGOS's `omega` only REFUTES hypotheses; it never decides the goal
cases.lean: omega on Nat/Int linear goals, omega from contradictory hypotheses, omega with no arithmetic hypotheses
cases.target: LOGOS script atom `omega` — canonical `omega`, arity 0, aliases `arithmetic`, `linarith`, `integers` (proof/src/tactic_script.rs:284, :318) → `combinators::omega` (proof/src/tactic.rs:1008-1011) → `ProofState::omega` (proof/src/tactic.rs:852-878), closing the goal with `InferenceRule::ExFalso`
evidence: proof/src/tactic.rs:852-860 (`omega` FIRST calls `omega_solve::has_arith_facts` on the hypotheses and returns `DoesNotApply` — "omega: no arithmetic (≤ / <) hypotheses in scope" — when there are none. The GOAL is never inspected for arithmetic content); proof/src/tactic.rs:861-873 (`omega_close(&known)` searches for a refutation of the hypotheses; on success the goal — ANY goal — is closed by `InferenceRule::ExFalso` over the `⊥` derivation); proof/src/tactic.rs:874-877 (`DoesNotApply` when the hypotheses have an integer model: "the integer hypotheses are satisfiable (no refutation)"); proof/src/linarith_solve.rs:1-8 (the decision core: Fourier-Motzkin producing a FARKAS CERTIFICATE — multipliers `λᵢ ≥ 0` with `Σ λᵢ·constraintᵢ` a positive constant `≤ 0`); proof/src/tactic.rs:846-851 (the doc comment: "linear INTEGER arithmetic … using discreteness (`a < b ⟹ a+1 ≤ b`) … Mirrors the REFUTATION HALF of Lean's `omega`"); kernel/src/prelude.rs:202-340 (the eight `Int` order axioms the Farkas certificate is reconstructed against: `le_refl`, `le_trans`, `le_add_mono`, `le_mul_nonneg`, `le_sub`, `lt_succ_le`, `lt_add1_le`, `le_total`, where `a ≤ b ≔ Eq Bool (le a b) true`)
guards: THE HALF-TACTIC TRAP. Lean's `omega` is a DECISION PROCEDURE for the goal: it proves `n + 0 = n`, `x < 1 → x = 0`, `2 * n ≥ n` from nothing. LOGOS's proves nothing from nothing — with no `≤`/`<` hypotheses in scope it declines at tactic.rs:856-859 before looking at the goal at all, and with satisfiable hypotheses it declines at :874. A translator that maps every Lean `omega` to a LOGOS `omega` gets a script that fails on the majority of real uses, and the failure message ("no arithmetic hypotheses in scope") describes the HYPOTHESES when the problem is that LOGOS has no way to attack the goal.

Catches assuming the goal is negated first. A complete `omega` would negate the goal, add it to the hypothesis set, and refute. LOGOS's does not: `known` is built from `g.hyps` alone (tactic.rs:861-862) and the goal appears only as the `ExFalso` conclusion. So `x ≤ 3 ⊢ x ≤ 4` — trivially valid, and refutable only after negating the goal — is DECLINED, because `x ≤ 3` alone is satisfiable.

Catches the `Nat` / `Int` conflation. LOGOS's order axioms are stated for `Int` (prelude.rs:202-340), and `Int` in LOGOS is an OPAQUE type with axiomatised laws while `Nat` is an inductive with a literal bridge (see T10-004). Lean's `omega` handles both, and crucially knows `Nat` subtraction truncates and that every `Nat` is `≥ 0`. Neither fact is available to `omega_close`, which works over ℤ. A `Nat` goal whose validity depends on non-negativity or on truncated subtraction is outside the fragment even when hypotheses are present.

Catches over-trusting the ex-falso closure. When `omega` succeeds it closes ANY goal (tactic.rs:866-871) — including a FALSE one, soundly, because the hypotheses were contradictory. That is correct, but it means a successful `omega` is NO evidence that the goal was arithmetic or even meaningful. A harness must not treat "omega closed it" as "the arithmetic content was translated".
oracle: Every emitted `omega` atom runs against a goal whose LOGOS hypothesis set satisfies `omega_solve::has_arith_facts` and is integer-unsatisfiable; `run_script` closes the goal and `qed()` returns `verified == true` with an `ExFalso` root over a Farkas certificate. For the `positiveGoal*` theorems the translator must either emit a loss record or a diagnostic — emitting a bare `omega` is a failure.
note: The index records `translate`, and the script-level name maps exactly: `omega` in, `omega` out, aliases included. This file keeps that verdict because the REFUTATION fragment corresponds one-for-one. There is a defensible argument for `degrade` with loss OMEGA_REFUTATION_ONLY, since the `positiveGoal*` theorems below have no LOGOS image whatever — Lean proves them, LOGOS declines. A translator that chooses `degrade` and emits the loss record is behaving better than one that chooses `translate` and emits nothing; the harness should accept either, and must reject a translator that emits `omega` for a positive goal with no loss record at all.

cases.title: `decide` — LOGOS's is a hard-wired evaluator router, not a `Decidable`-instance driven tactic
cases.lean: decide, decide on a DecidableEq enum, decide on a bounded quantifier, native_decide
cases.target: LOGOS script atom `decide` — canonical `decide`, arity 0, aliases `compute`, `evaluate`, `calculate` (proof/src/tactic_script.rs:283, :317) → `combinators::decide` (proof/src/tactic.rs:1004-1007) → `ProofState::decide` (proof/src/tactic.rs:833-844) → `decide::decide_expr` (proof/src/decide.rs:64), closing with `InferenceRule::ArithDecision` or `InferenceRule::NativeDecide`
evidence: proof/src/decide.rs:1-12 (the module header fixing the whole fragment: "ground `Int` identities" via `ArithDecision`, "ground comparisons and Bool equalities" via `NativeDecide`, "propositional structure recurses through the ordinary intro rules", and "A false, open, or unsupported goal yields `None` — decide DECLINES, it never guesses"); proof/src/decide.rs:16-20 (`eval_int` — numeric constants and `add`/`sub`/`mul`/ `div`/`mod` trees, CHECKED arithmetic, and "overflow declines": the evaluator is `i64`, so a goal outside `i64` is not decided even though `kernel/src/term.rs:13-44` has a `Literal::BigInt`); proof/src/tactic.rs:840-843 (`DoesNotApply` — "decide: not a closed decidable goal (or it is false)", one message for two very different situations); kernel/src/prelude.rs (the trusted base registers `Decidable`/`isTrue`/`isFalse` and exactly two decision procedures, `decEqBool` and `decEqNat` — there is no instance SYNTHESIS, no `DecidableEq` derivation, and no way to register a new one from a script); kernel/src/prelude.rs:1195-1219 (`reduceBool` / `ofReduceBool` — Lean's `native_decide` pair, which is a DIFFERENT route, see T06-014)
guards: THE INSTANCE-SYNTHESIS TRAP. Lean's `decide` works for ANY proposition with a `Decidable` instance — a derived `DecidableEq` on a user enum, `List.all`, a bounded `∀ x < 10`, a structural equality on a record. LOGOS's `decide` is a hard-coded router over ground `Int`/`Bool` arithmetic (decide.rs:1-12); there is no instance resolution in the script layer at all. A translator that maps `decide` to `decide` produces a step that fails for every user-defined decidable proposition, and the message ("not a closed decidable goal (or it is false)") is indistinguishable from the message you get for a FALSE goal.

Catches the decline/failure conflation in the dangerous direction. `decide_expr` returns `None` both when the goal is unsupported and when it is FALSE (decide.rs:8-11). A translator that treats a `DoesNotApply` from `decide` as "try another tactic" will keep searching past a goal that is actually false, and may eventually close it with `auto`'s classical reductio or with `omega`'s ex-falso from some unrelated contradiction — producing a certified proof of a statement the Lean source never asserted. The decline must be surfaced, not swallowed.

Catches the `i64` boundary. `eval_int` is checked `i64` arithmetic and declines on overflow (decide.rs:16-20), while the kernel's `Literal` has `BigInt` and `Nat` (`BigInt`) variants (term.rs:13-44) and `Nat` literals are definitionally `Succ^n Zero` (reduction.rs:330-345). So a `decide` that Lean discharges on a large numeral has no LOGOS image, and the boundary is at `i64`, not at the kernel's representable range — a limit invisible from both the Lean source and the kernel.

Catches routing `native_decide` here. It is a separate trusted path through `reduceBool`/`ofReduceBool` (prelude.rs:1195-1219) with a different TCB; mapping Lean's `native_decide` to LOGOS's `decide` silently narrows it to the evaluator router, and mapping LOGOS's `NativeDecide` inference rule back to Lean's `decide` silently widens the TCB. See T06-014.

Catches the alias `compute`/`evaluate`/`calculate` (tactic_script.rs:317). These are natural renderings of `norm_num`, `native_decide`, `rfl`-by-computation and `simp arith` too. Emitting an English rendering rather than the canonical `decide` lands on whichever tactic the alias table happens to point at.
oracle: Every emitted `decide` atom runs against a goal that `decide::decide_expr` accepts — closed, `i64`-representable, built only from `Int` identities, comparisons, `Bool` equalities and propositional structure over them — and `run_script` closes it with an `ArithDecision` or `NativeDecide` leaf. For the enum, bounded-quantifier and large-numeral theorems the translator must emit a diagnostic rather than a `decide` atom.

cases.title: `ring` exists only on the LITERATE surface, is `Int`/`Nat`-only, and reports failure by REDUCING to an error derivation rather than by failing
cases.lean: ring, ring_nf, ring over a general CommRing
cases.target: Surface C (literate kernel theorem) proof tactic `ring.`, parsed at `kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:626-636` into `Term::App(Global("try_ring"), <goal as Syntax>)`, declared at `kernel/src/prelude.rs:2966-2991` (`try_ring : Syntax → Derivation`, plus the `DRingSolve : Syntax → Derivation` constructor) and reduced by `kernel/src/reduction.rs:579-582` → `try_try_ring_reduce` (`kernel/src/reduction.rs:2282-2316`)
evidence: proof/src/tactic_script.rs:308-327 (`canonical` — there is NO arm mapping any word to "ring"; `ring` in a Surface-A `Proof:` script is `unknown tactic \`ring\``. The tactic-script surface and the literate surface DO NOT INTEROPERATE); kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:626-636 (the `ring` arm of `parse_proof_tactic`); kernel/src/prelude.rs:2984-2990 (`try_ring`'s type is `Syntax → Derivation` — it consumes a REIFIED goal, not a proposition); kernel/src/reduction.rs:2282-2316 (`try_try_ring_reduce`: extract `Eq T a b`, require `is_ring_type(T)`, reify both sides with ONE shared `VarInterner`, compare `canonical_eq`, and emit `DRingSolve goal` on success); kernel/src/reduction.rs:2352-2357 (`is_ring_type` — `name == "Int" || name == "Nat"`, and nothing else); kernel/src/reduction.rs:2290-2292, :2296-2315 (EVERY failure path returns `Some(make_error_derivation())` — the reduction SUCCEEDS, producing `DAxiom (SName "Error")`, rather than getting stuck or returning `None`); kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:867-870 (literate `induction` is hardcoded to `Nat`); LOGOS_FACTS §Surface C (there is NO `forall` in the `Statement:` grammar — free variables are effectively universally closed)
guards: THE ERROR-DERIVATION TRAP, and the reason this case is in the corpus. When `ring` cannot prove the goal, `try_try_ring_reduce` does not fail: it returns `make_error_derivation()` (reduction.rs:2290, :2294, :2299, :2315). A `Term` of type `Derivation` is produced, the reduction step reports success, and the difference between "proved" and "not proved" is a `DAxiom (SName "Error")` sitting inside an otherwise well-typed term. A translator that checks only "did the kernel accept the term" will record a proof where there is none. The check must be on the derivation's HEAD CONSTRUCTOR: `DRingSolve` means proved, `DAxiom (SName "Error")` means not.

Catches emitting `ring` into a Surface-A script. The three LOGOS vernacular surfaces do not interoperate (LOGOS_FACTS §"The three vernacular surfaces"), and `ring` is reachable only from Surface C. A Lean theorem proved `by ring` must therefore be emitted as a LITERATE theorem — which in turn means its statement must fit the literate `Statement:` grammar, which has no `forall` (literate_parser.rs:1223-1270). A `ring` proof of a UNIVERSALLY QUANTIFIED identity is expressible only because the literate surface universally closes free variables implicitly; a translator that emits an explicit quantifier will not parse.

Catches the CARRIER. `is_ring_type` admits exactly `Int` and `Nat` (reduction.rs:2352-2357). Lean's `ring` works in any `CommSemiring`/`CommRing`, which is most of Mathlib's algebra. Translating a `ring` call over an abstract `CommRing R` to LOGOS's `ring` silently changes the carrier to `Int`, and since LOGOS's `Int` is OPAQUE with eight axiomatised ring laws (prelude.rs:92-191) rather than a derived structure, the resulting statement is about a different object than the Lean source's.

Catches losing the SHARED INTERNER. `try_try_ring_reduce` reifies both sides with ONE `VarInterner` (reduction.rs:2295-2306) precisely so the two sides agree on which named global is which polynomial variable. A translator that reifies the sides separately — natural if it normalises subterms independently — produces polynomials whose variables are numbered differently and whose `canonical_eq` then fails on a true identity.
oracle: Each theorem is emitted as a Surface-C literate theorem whose `Proof:` is `ring.`; the reduced derivation's head is `DRingSolve`, NOT `DAxiom (SName "Error")`; the statement's `Eq` type argument is `Int` or `Nat`; and no Surface-A script anywhere in the corpus contains the token `ring`.
