cases.title: `linarith` is an ALIAS for `omega` — an ordered-field goal silently becomes integer-linear, and integer discreteness is unsound over ℚ
cases.lean: linarith, linarith over ℚ/ℝ, linarith with rational coefficients, nlinarith
cases.target: LOGOS script atom `omega` — reached through the alias `linarith` (proof/src/tactic_script.rs:318: `"omega" | "arithmetic" | "linarith" | "integers" => Some("omega")`) → `combinators::omega` (proof/src/tactic.rs:1008-1011) → `ProofState::omega` (proof/src/tactic.rs:852-878) → `omega_solve::omega_close` over `linarith_solve`'s Fourier-Motzkin core
evidence: proof/src/tactic_script.rs:318 (the alias itself — `linarith` and `omega` are THE SAME canonical tactic; there is no separate rational solver reachable from a script); proof/src/tactic.rs:846-851 (the doc comment, which states the divergence outright: "linear INTEGER arithmetic. When the in-scope `≤`/`<` hypotheses are jointly unsatisfiable over ℤ — using DISCRETENESS (`a < b ⟹ a+1 ≤ b`), the fact rational solvers lack — refute them … Proves `x < y ∧ y < x+1 ⊢ Q`, WHICH `linarith` CANNOT (that system is rationally satisfiable)"); proof/src/linarith_solve.rs:1-8, :13-20 (`LinExpr` — coefficients are `i64`, the constant is `i64`; there is no rational coefficient type anywhere in the solver); proof/src/lib.rs:199-238 (`ProofExpr` is UNTYPED: a `Predicate`'s arguments are `ProofTerm`s carrying no carrier information, so nothing in a translated goal records that the Lean source was about ℚ or ℝ); kernel/src/prelude.rs:202-340 (the eight order axioms, all stated for `Int`, where `a ≤ b ≔ Eq Bool (le a b) true` — there is no ordered-field structure in the trusted base at all, and no `Rat`/`Real` type: see LOGOS_FACTS §"Absent entirely")
guards: THE SOUNDNESS TRAP, and the most dangerous alias in the table. `x < y` and `y < x + 1` are jointly UNSATISFIABLE over ℤ and perfectly SATISFIABLE over ℚ. LOGOS's `omega` refutes them (tactic.rs:846-851 says so explicitly) and then discharges ANY goal by `ExFalso` (tactic.rs:866-871). If the Lean source was about ℚ, the translated theorem is FALSE and LOGOS has certified it — and nothing in the LOGOS artefact records the carrier, because `ProofExpr` is untyped. The kernel cannot catch this: it is checking a correct ℤ proof of a statement that was never about ℤ. The translator is the only place this can be caught, and it must be caught before emission.

Catches the mitigation that looks sufficient. "LOGOS has no ℚ, so a ℚ goal would fail earlier" is false in exactly the case that matters: the ORDER PREDICATES translate fine (`le`/`lt` are prelude primitives, prelude.rs:352-515), the variables translate to bare `ProofTerm`s, and only the TYPE — which the FOL layer discards — was carrying the field-ness. A translator that erases types before choosing the tactic has already lost the information it needs to refuse.

Catches the alias reaching the script by accident. `arithmetic` and `integers` are also aliases (tactic_script.rs:318). A translator that renders a Lean `linarith` into prose ("by arithmetic") lands on `omega` too. There is no spelling of "linear arithmetic over an ordered field" anywhere in the grammar.

Catches `nlinarith` and `polyrith`. Neither has an alias; the words are unknown to `canonical` and the script dies at parse time. That is the correct outcome and must not be "fixed" by mapping them onto `omega` or `crush`.
oracle: Every emitted `omega` atom that originated from a Lean `linarith` carries a loss record naming FIELD_TO_INTEGER, and the translator has recorded a proof obligation that the goal's carrier is `Int` or `Nat`. For `ratFieldSatisfiable` the harness asserts the translator emitted NO tactic — a certified LOGOS proof of that goal is a corpus failure, not a pass.
loss: FIELD_TO_INTEGER. A `linarith` call over ℚ, ℝ, or any `LinearOrderedField` becomes an integer-linear refutation. The coefficients are `i64` (linarith_solve.rs:13-20), so rational multipliers are unrepresentable, and the solver's use of discreteness makes it prove strictly MORE than `linarith` does. Acceptable ONLY when the translator has independently established that the carrier is `ℤ` or `ℕ`; otherwise it must escalate — see the second guard.

DIRECTION_OF_STRENGTH. Ordinary degrades lose power. This one GAINS it: LOGOS's `omega` refutes hypothesis sets that Lean's `linarith` correctly leaves alone. So the usual safety argument ("a weaker target just fails louder") does not apply, and a loss record is not optional.
note: Bare Lean 4.14 has NO `linarith` (Mathlib). Every theorem below carries the Mathlib invocation in a comment and is proved with the core equivalent — `omega` for the integer-linear goals, explicit lemmas elsewhere. The ℚ/ℝ cases are written against a LOCALLY declared ordered-field-like class rather than `import Mathlib`, which is also the honest model of the situation: the field structure is a typeclass the LOGOS side has no counterpart for.

A defensible reading makes the ℚ/ℝ cases `reject` rather than `degrade`, since no sound translation of them exists at all. The index records `degrade`, which this file keeps: the degrade is correct for the ℤ/ℕ fragment, and the ℚ/ℝ cases are the boundary the loss record must refuse to cross. A translator that emits `omega` for `ratField*` below without a carrier proof must be failed.

cases.title: `use (n+1)` has no image — the LOGOS witness is always a bare `ProofTerm::Constant`, even when the Lean witness was a local VARIABLE
cases.lean: exists, use, use with an applied term, refine ⟨w, ?_⟩, Exists.intro
cases.target: LOGOS script atom `exists <word>` — canonical `exists`, arity 1, aliases `use`, `witness`, `choose`, `provide` (proof/src/tactic_script.rs:280, :314) → `combinators::exists` (proof/src/tactic.rs:1034-1037) → `ProofState::exists` (proof/src/tactic.rs:443-463), emitting `InferenceRule::ExistentialIntro { witness, witness_type: "Entity" }`
evidence: proof/src/tactic_script.rs:280 (`"exists" => Ok(c::exists(ProofTerm::Constant(arg()?)))` — the argument word is wrapped in `ProofTerm::Constant` UNCONDITIONALLY, with no lookup against the local context and no alternative term shape); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:264-274 (`arg()` accepts exactly one `Tok::Word`; the lexer (:89-100) produces a `Word` only for a run of `is_alphanumeric() || '_'`, so a parenthesis, an operator, or a second word is not an argument); proof/src/tactic.rs:443-463 (`exists` substitutes the witness into the `∃` body and leaves the instantiated goal OPEN — it never attempts `rfl`); proof/src/tactic.rs:333 (`ProofState::intro` binds an introduced ∀-variable as `ProofTerm::Variable(name)` — a DIFFERENT constructor from `Constant`); proof/src/lib.rs (`ProofTerm::Constant` vs `ProofTerm::Variable` are distinct variants compared by derived `PartialEq`, which is what `assumption` (tactic.rs:363) and `exact` (tactic.rs:380) use); proof/src/formula.rs:437-445 (`ident_to_term` — the FOL surface's own convention: uppercase- or digit-leading ⟹ `Constant`, lowercase-leading ⟹ `Variable`. The script `exists` atom does NOT follow it)
guards: THE VARIABLE-BECOMES-CONSTANT TRAP, and the subtlest failure in Tier 8. When the Lean witness is a variable already in scope — `intro n; use n` — the translator naturally emits `exists n`. That produces `ProofTerm::Constant("n")` (tactic_script.rs:280), while the `intro n` that bound it produced `ProofTerm::Variable("n")` (tactic.rs:333). The instantiated goal therefore mentions `Constant("n")` and the hypotheses mention `Variable("n")`; `assumption` and `exact` compare with derived `PartialEq` (tactic.rs:363, :380) and find no match. The script fails at a step AFTER the `exists`, with a message about the wrong hypothesis, and the two terms PRINT IDENTICALLY — `Display` renders both as `n` — so the difference is invisible in every diagnostic the user sees.

Catches the `∃`-elimination round trip. `cases h` on an existential introduces a fresh witness `ProofTerm::Constant("W{n}")` (tactic.rs:536-541), which IS a `Constant`. So `obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := h; use w` translates correctly only if the translator emits the LOGOS-generated `W{n}` rather than Lean's `w` — and only because both sides are `Constant`s. The same emission pattern is right here and wrong in the previous guard, which is why the translator must track the PROVENANCE of every witness name, not just its spelling.

Catches emitting a numeral and assuming the `Nat` bridge. `exists 0` yields `ProofTerm::Constant("0")` — a constant whose NAME is the digit zero, not a `Literal::Nat` and not the kernel's `Zero` constructor. Whether that matches the goal depends on how the translator rendered numerals elsewhere in the same goal; if it rendered them as `Constant("Zero")` or as a literal, the witness will not match. One numeral convention must be chosen and applied everywhere.

Catches the `witness_type` field. `ExistentialIntro` records `witness_type: "Entity"` unconditionally (tactic.rs:455) — `Entity` being the LOGOS prelude's opaque zero-constructor entity type. The recorded type is therefore never the Lean witness's type, and a translator must not read it back as one.
oracle: Every emitted `exists` atom's argument is a single `[A-Za-z0-9_]+` word; for a witness that was a Lean local variable the translator has either emitted a global definition naming it or refused; a follow-up atom discharging the instantiated goal is always present; and the loss record names WITNESS_TERM_SHAPE and TRAILING_DISCHARGE. The harness asserts `run_script` leaves `open_goals() >= 1` immediately after every `exists`.
loss: WITNESS_TERM_SHAPE. Lean's witness is an arbitrary term: `use (n + 1)`, `use (f x)`, `use ⟨a, b⟩`, `use 0`. LOGOS's is one identifier. The translator must either (a) name the witness as a fresh global definition first — which the script surface cannot do, so it means emitting a kernel `add_definition` alongside the script — or (b) refuse. Acceptable only with (a) done explicitly and recorded.

TRAILING_DISCHARGE. Lean's `use` closes the residual goal with `rfl`/`trivial` when it can, so `use 0` often finishes the proof. LOGOS's `exists` always leaves the instantiated goal open (tactic.rs:450-458). Every translated `use` needs an explicit follow-up atom that the Lean source did not contain.

MULTIPLE_WITNESSES. `use a, b` supplies witnesses for nested `∃`s in one step. The script's `,` is a step SEPARATOR (tactic_script.rs:61-64), so `exists a , b` parses as `exists a` followed by the atom `b`, which is an unknown tactic. Nested existentials need one `exists` atom per binder.
note: `use` is a MATHLIB tactic; bare Lean 4.14 has only the core `exists`, which accepts the same comma-separated witness list and also discharges the residual goal. Since this corpus forbids `import Mathlib`, the live code below uses `exists` throughout and each `use` spelling is named in the doc comment. The LOGOS alias table maps the WORD `use` onto the same `exists` atom (tactic_script.rs:314), so the two spellings are interchangeable on the target side regardless.

cases.title: `<;>` — same spelling, but LOGOS applies the right-hand tactic to EVERY open goal, not only to the ones the left-hand tactic produced
cases.lean: t1 <;> t2, chained <;>, <;> after a tactic that leaves several goals
cases.target: LOGOS script `chain := atom ('<;>' atom)*`, left-associative (proof/src/tactic_script.rs:202-210) → `combinators::then_all` (proof/src/tactic.rs:1138-1146)
evidence: proof/src/tactic_script.rs:85-88 (the lexer's only multi-character token: `'<' if src[i..].starts_with("<;>")` ⟹ `Tok::ThenAll`); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:202-210 (`parse_chain` — left-associative `c::then_all(acc, rhs)`, binding TIGHTER than the `;`/`.`/`,`/`then` separators handled by `parse_seq` at :177-199, exactly as in Lean); proof/src/tactic.rs:1138-1146 (`then_all(t1, t2)` = `t1(st)?; all_goals(t2)(st)` — note that `all_goals` is applied to the state AFTER `t1`, with no record of which goals `t1` created); proof/src/tactic.rs:1124-1136 (`all_goals` iterates `st.open` — the COMPLETE open-goal deque — focusing each in turn and propagating failure with `t(st)?`); proof/src/tactic.rs:280-298 (`refine` pushes new subgoals to the FRONT of `open`, so after `split` the deque is [left, right, …any goals that were already there]); proof/src/tactic.rs:1091-1099, :1104-1119 (`try_` and `repeat` speculate on a CLONE and commit only on success — `then_all` does NOT, so a failure inside `t2` leaves whatever `t1` committed)
guards: THE OPEN-SET LEAK, and the only real semantic difference in this case. Lean's `<;>` applies `t2` to exactly the goals `t1` produced. LOGOS's `then_all` applies it to `st.open` in full (tactic.rs:1126-1133), which also contains any goal that was already waiting from an EARLIER branching step. So in a script like `split . left <;> assumption`, Lean's `<;>` touches only the single goal `left` produced, while LOGOS's also touches the right conjunct that `split` left behind. When `assumption` happens to discharge it, the script succeeds and is now one goal further along than the translator believes, so every subsequent atom targets the wrong goal. When it does not, `all_goals` propagates the failure (`t(st)?`, tactic.rs:1130) and the whole chain fails — for a goal the Lean source never asked `t2` to look at.

Catches the "it usually works" corollary. The leak is invisible whenever `<;>` is the FIRST branching step of a proof, because `st.open` then contains only `t1`'s output. Almost every textbook use of `<;>` has that shape, so a translator can pass a large test suite and still be wrong in exactly the nested proofs where it matters.

Catches the ASSOCIATIVITY assumption. `parse_chain` folds left (tactic_script.rs:204-208), matching Lean, so `a <;> b <;> c` is `(a <;> b) <;> c`. But because `then_all`'s second stage is `all_goals`, the middle `b` has already spread across the whole open set before `c` runs, and `c` then spreads across the result of that. The fan-out compounds. A translator that models `<;>` as a simple pairing of goals will mispredict the goal count after two chained `<;>`s.

Catches PRECEDENCE against the separators. `<;>` binds tighter than `;`/`.`/`,`/the word `then` (tactic_script.rs:177-199 vs :202-210) — the same as Lean. But the LOGOS separators include the PERIOD, so a translator that emits prose punctuation inside a chain (`split . left <;> assumption`) gets a different tree from one that emits `split ; left <;> assumption` only by accident of where it put the period. The period is a separator, not decoration.

Catches assuming `<;>` backtracks. `try` and `repeat` clone the state before speculating (tactic.rs:1091-1119); `then_all` does not (tactic.rs:1141-1145). A `t1 <;> t2` whose `t2` fails on the third goal leaves `t1`'s effects and `t2`'s effects on the first two goals committed. Lean's `<;>` is atomic. A translator relying on all-or-nothing semantics to recover from a failed chain will read a half-applied state.
oracle: Every Lean `<;>` maps to a `<;>` token in the emitted script with the same associativity. The harness runs `run_script` and asserts that the open-goal count after the chain equals the open-goal count Lean reports after the corresponding `<;>`; for `leakAfterSplit` below it asserts the translator did NOT emit a bare `<;>` but either restructured or recorded the divergence.

cases.title: `first` / `try` / `repeat` — the three combinators are LOWERCASE-ONLY keywords and `first` uses brackets, not Lean's leading bar
cases.lean: first | t1 | t2, try t, repeat t, repeat' , nested combinators
cases.target: LOGOS script atoms `first [ s1 | s2 | … ]`, `try <atom>`, `repeat <atom>` (proof/src/tactic_script.rs:221-239) → `combinators::first` (proof/src/tactic.rs:1076-1090), `combinators::try_` (:1091-1099), `combinators::repeat` (:1104-1119)
evidence: proof/src/tactic_script.rs:221 (`Some(Tok::Word(w)) if w == "first"` — an EXACT, case-SENSITIVE byte comparison, unlike `canonical` which lowercases at :309); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:232, :236 (same for `try` and `repeat`); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:222-230 (`first` requires `[`, then `script ('|' script)*`, then `]` — brackets and bars, where Lean writes `first | t1 | t2` with no brackets); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:233, :237 (`try` and `repeat` each take a single ATOM, not a sequence — `try a ; b` is `(try a) ; b`, and a multi-step body needs parentheses, which `parse_atom` accepts at :215-220); proof/src/tactic.rs:1076-1090 (`first` speculates on `st.clone()` per alternative and commits the first that succeeds — genuine backtracking); proof/src/tactic.rs:1091-1099 (`try_` — clone, attempt, commit on success, ALWAYS `Ok`); proof/src/tactic.rs:1104-1119 (`repeat` — bounded at 100_000 iterations, stops early when `st.open.is_empty()`, ALWAYS `Ok`); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:169-173, :298-303 (`skip_filler` runs before every atom and discards `by`, `the`, `on`, `that`, `now`, `with`, `we`, `it`, `a`, `an`, `of`, `to`, `and`)
guards: THE CASE-SENSITIVITY TRAP. Every PRIMITIVE tactic name is matched case-insensitively (`canonical` lowercases at tactic_script.rs:309), so `Assume h` and `assume h` are the same atom. The three COMBINATORS are not: `parse_atom` compares the raw word (tactic_script.rs:221, :232, :236). A translator that capitalises the first word of a sentence — the obvious thing to do when emitting an English-esque `Proof:` line — turns `try simp` into `Try simp`, which falls through to `parse_primitive`, `canonical("Try")` returns `None`, and the whole script dies with "unknown tactic `Try`". The failure is at parse time, so nothing runs.

Catches emitting Lean's `first` syntax. Lean writes `first | t1 | t2`; LOGOS requires `first [ t1 | t2 ]` (tactic_script.rs:222-229). Emitting the Lean form gives `expected LBracket, found Bar` — or worse, if the leading bar is dropped, `first` consumes `t1` as the bracket it wanted and reports a mismatch about a token the user never wrote.

Catches the ATOM/SEQUENCE distinction. `try` and `repeat` each take one atom (tactic_script.rs:233, :237). Lean's `try (t1; t2)` and LOGOS's `try (t1 ; t2)` agree only because both need the parentheses; but a translator that emits `try t1 ; t2` from Lean's `try t1 <;> t2` has silently moved `t2` outside the `try`, so a failure in `t2` now fails the whole script instead of being swallowed.

Catches `repeat`'s bound and its early exit. It iterates at most 100_000 times and breaks as soon as `st.open.is_empty()` (tactic.rs:1106-1116). It ALWAYS returns `Ok`, like Lean's `repeat`. But a non-progressing tactic that nevertheless SUCCEEDS — `try assumption`, say — will run the full 100_000 iterations, cloning the entire `ProofState` each time (tactic.rs:1107). `repeat (try t)` is therefore a performance trap a translator can easily emit while "being safe".

Catches the FILLER words. `skip_filler` discards thirteen words before every atom (tactic_script.rs:298-303). A translator emitting readable prose — "first try the simp" — has `the` silently removed, which happens to work, but `first try a simp` loses `a` too and `try on h` loses `on` and then reads `h` as an atom. The filler list makes malformed scripts parse into DIFFERENT well-formed scripts rather than failing, so the translator must emit the canonical spelling with no connective words.

Catches assuming `first` is left-biased in the same way. LOGOS's `first` clones the state per alternative (tactic.rs:1078-1087), so an alternative that partially applies and then fails leaves no trace — same as Lean. But the alternatives are full `parse_seq`s (tactic_script.rs:224-228), so `first [ intro h ; exact h | assumption ]` commits the whole first branch or none of it, whereas Lean's `first | (intro h; exact h) | assumption` needs the parentheses to mean that.
oracle: Emitted combinator keywords are byte-for-byte lowercase `first` / `try` / `repeat`; every `first` is bracketed with `[` … `]` and bar-separated; every multi-step `try` or `repeat` body is parenthesised; and no emitted script contains a filler word from `is_filler` (tactic_script.rs:298-303) in a position where it would be consumed.

cases.title: `all_goals` / `any_goals` — `all_goals` is Rust-only and `any_goals` does not exist at all
cases.lean: all_goals, any_goals, focus, iterate
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: proof/src/tactic_script.rs:308-327 (`canonical` — no arm maps any word to "all_goals"; the lexer WILL produce a single `Tok::Word("all_goals")`, since `_` is an identifier character at :89-93, so the failure is the generic `ScriptError("unknown tactic \`all_goals\`")` at :262, not a lexing error); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:275-292 (`parse_primitive`'s dispatch — fifteen arms, none of them `all_goals`); proof/src/tactic.rs:1124-1136 (`combinators::all_goals` DOES exist as a Rust value: it snapshots `st.open`, focuses each goal in turn, runs `t`, and collects the resulting goals in original order — but nothing in the script grammar constructs it directly); proof/src/tactic.rs:1138-1146 (`then_all`, the `<;>` combinator, is the ONLY script-reachable consumer of `all_goals` — and it always runs `t1` first, so `all_goals t` standing alone has no spelling); a grep of `crates/logicaffeine_proof/src` for `any_goals` returns NOTHING — the combinator does not exist in Rust either; proof/src/tactic.rs:1130 (`all_goals` propagates failure with `t(st)?` — it is strictly `all_goals`, never `any_goals`, and there is no `try`-wrapped variant)
guards: THE `<;>` SUBSTITUTION TRAP. `all_goals t` is *almost* `<;> t`, and a translator will be tempted to synthesise `something <;> t`. It cannot, because `<;>` needs a left-hand tactic and `all_goals` has none — the goals it acts on were produced by an EARLIER, already-emitted step. Splicing `t` onto that earlier step changes the script's structure: the earlier step's own effects are now inside a chain, and — per T08-018 — LOGOS's `then_all` spreads `t` over the WHOLE open set, which may include goals from steps before that. The rewrite is not local and is not sound.

Catches substituting `repeat t`. `repeat` (tactic.rs:1104-1119) applies `t` to the FOCUSED goal over and over; `all_goals` applies it ONCE to each of many goals. On a state with three open goals and a `t` that closes the focused one, `repeat t` closes all three — by accident, because closing one refocuses the next — and on a `t` that does not close its goal, `repeat t` applies `t` to the same goal 100_000 times. The two combinators coincide only in the special case where `t` closes every goal it touches, which is exactly the case a translator's tests will cover.

Catches emitting `t` alone. Dropping `all_goals` leaves `t` acting on the focused goal only. The remaining goals stay open, `qed()` fails with `TacticError::GoalsRemain` (tactic.rs:967-968), and the reported count points at the end of the proof rather than at the dropped combinator.

Catches conflating `any_goals` with `all_goals`. Lean's `any_goals t` succeeds if `t` succeeds on at least one goal; `all_goals t` requires all. LOGOS's combinator is `all_goals` (failure propagates at tactic.rs:1130) and there is no `try`-wrapped variant, so even a Rust-level translator cannot express `any_goals` without writing new Rust. A translator that emits `all_goals` for Lean's `any_goals` turns a permissive step into a strict one and fails proofs Lean accepted.

Catches `focus` and `iterate`. Neither has a script spelling either; `focus` is additionally meaningless in LOGOS because there is no focusing bracket at all (see T08-025), and `iterate n t` has no bounded-repetition form — `repeat` is unbounded-until-failure.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_TACTIC_NOT_IN_SCRIPT_GRAMMAR for every theorem below and emits no script. A harness asserts that no emitted script contains the substrings `all_goals`, `any_goals`, `focus` or `iterate`, and that every emitted `<;>` in the corpus corresponds to a `<;>` in the Lean source rather than to a synthesised one.
diag: E_TACTIC_NOT_IN_SCRIPT_GRAMMAR — must name the tactic (`all_goals` or `any_goals`), state that the script primitive set is closed (tactic_script.rs:275-292), and for `any_goals` additionally state that no Rust combinator exists either, so it is not reachable at any level. Must NOT emit a script.

cases.title: `calc` — no chaining form exists on any LOGOS surface, and the intermediate terms are unwritable on the two that could host it
cases.lean: calc with =, calc with mixed relations (Trans), calc as a term, calc in tactic mode
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: a grep of `crates/logicaffeine_proof/src` and `crates/logicaffeine_kernel/src` for `calc` returns NOTHING outside unrelated identifiers (`polycalc`), so there is no `calc` construct, no `Trans` class, and no transitivity-chaining combinator anywhere in LOGOS; proof/src/tactic_script.rs:308-327 (`canonical` — no arm for `calc`); proof/src/lib.rs:488-728 (`InferenceRule` — `EqualityTransitivity` and `LeTrans` exist as individual STEPS, but nothing composes a chain of them from a list of intermediate terms); proof/src/formula.rs:427-432 (Surface B's `parse_term` accepts ONLY a bare identifier, so `a * (b + c)` — a typical `calc` waypoint — cannot be written as a term on that surface at all); LOGOS_FACTS §Surface A ("No term arithmetic exists on this surface" — the English theorem block's `Given:`/`Prove:` lines go through the natural-language parser); kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:1223-1270 (Surface C DOES have infix terms — `<= ≤ >= ≥ < > + - *` and the word `equals` — but its `Proof:` grammar is a single tactic (`ring`, `refl`, `lia`, `cc`, `simp`, `omega`, `auto`, `induction`), with no step-list form); kernel/src/prelude.rs:202-340 (the only order facts in the trusted base are the eight `Int` axioms; there is no generic `Trans` instance mechanism to mix `=` and `<` in one chain)
guards: THE `rewrite`-EXPANSION TRAP. A pure-`=` `calc` chain `a = b := h₁; _ = c := h₂` looks like `rewrite h1 . rewrite h2`, and for a goal `a = c` that expansion sometimes works. It is not sound in general for two reasons, both from T08-011: LOGOS's `rewrite` replaces EVERY occurrence of the LHS (tactic.rs:130-156), so a waypoint that occurs elsewhere in the goal is rewritten too; and `rewrite` requires a GROUND `ProofExpr::Identity` hypothesis (tactic.rs:710-717), so a `calc` step justified by a quantified lemma has no image. A translator that performs the expansion has silently chosen a different proof, and for a chain whose waypoints repeat, a different theorem.

Catches MIXED RELATIONS. `calc a = b := h₁; _ < c := h₂; _ ≤ d := h₃` is ordinary Lean — the `Trans` typeclass composes the relations and computes the chain's overall relation. LOGOS has no `Trans`, no relation composition, and the eight order axioms (prelude.rs:202-340) are individual `Int` facts stated over `a ≤ b ≔ Eq Bool (le a b) true`. There is nothing to compose them with, so a mixed chain cannot even be expanded step-by-step: the translator would have to synthesise the `lt_succ_le`/`le_trans` plumbing itself, i.e. write the proof rather than translate it.

Catches the TERM/TACTIC split. `calc` is an EXPRESSION in Lean 4, usable outside `by`. The translator therefore meets it while translating a term, not a tactic block, and must reject at that point — before the script surface is even chosen. A translator that only inspects tactic blocks will pass a `calc`-proved theorem through as an opaque term and then fail to translate its `Expr`, producing a diagnostic about `Trans.trans` rather than about `calc`.

Catches "put the waypoints in a Surface-C literate theorem". Surface C is the only LOGOS surface with infix arithmetic (literate_parser.rs:1223-1270), so it is the only place the intermediate terms can be spelled — but its `Proof:` is one tactic, not a list of justified steps, and there is no `forall` in its `Statement:` grammar (LOGOS_FACTS §Surface C). Each `calc` step would become its own literate theorem, and the composition of those theorems back into the original statement has no surface at all. The three surfaces do not interoperate.

Catches the degenerate one-step `calc`. `calc a = b := h` is just `exact h` and DOES translate. The diagnostic must be driven by a chain of length ≥ 2, or by the presence of a relation other than `=`, so that a translator is not over-rejecting.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NO_CALC_CHAIN for `chainEq`, `chainMixed`, `chainAsTerm` and `chainWithQuantifiedStep`, and emits no script for any of them. It must NOT reject `oneStep`. A harness additionally asserts that no emitted script anywhere in the corpus contains a `rewrite` atom that the translator synthesised from a `calc` step.
diag: E_NO_CALC_CHAIN — must name the theorem, report the number of `calc` steps and the relations used, and state that no LOGOS surface has a chaining form. If the chain is pure `=` it must additionally say that the expansion into `rewrite` steps was considered and why it was refused (see the guards). Must NOT emit a script.

cases.lean: by_contra, by_contra!, push_neg, not_not, negation normal form
cases.target: LOGOS script atom `auto` — canonical `auto`, arity 0, aliases `tauto`, `automatically`, `automation`, `trivially`, `directly` (proof/src/tactic_script.rs:289, :323) → `combinators::auto` (proof/src/tactic.rs:1059-1062) → `ProofState::auto` (proof/src/tactic.rs:901-914) → `BackwardChainer::prove`, whose Strategy 8 emits `InferenceRule::ClassicalReductio` (proof/src/engine.rs:2337-2350), certified as `dne G (λ hng. <⊥-proof>)` (proof/src/certifier.rs:1447-1473) against the single classical axiom `dne` (kernel/src/prelude.rs:78)
evidence: proof/src/engine.rs:2337-2350 (Strategy 8, verbatim: "Classical reductio (proof by contradiction) — LAST RESORT at the top level for a POSITIVE goal G: assume ¬G and search for ⊥". The guard is `if depth == 0 && !is_falsum(&goal.target) && !matches!(goal.target, ProofExpr::Not(_))`); proof/src/certifier.rs:1449-1473 (the `ClassicalReductio` arm builds `dne G (λ(hng : ¬G). <False proof>)` — the ONLY use of `dne` in the whole certifier); kernel/src/prelude.rs:78 (`ctx.add_declaration("dne", dne_type)` — the whole classical fragment of the trusted base is this one axiom; there is no `Classical.choice`, no `propext`, no `funext`); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:308-327 (`canonical` — no arm for `by_contra`, `contrapose`, `push_neg`, or any negation-normalisation word); proof/src/tactic.rs:901-914 (`auto` either CLOSES the goal or fails with `TacticError::AutoFailed` — it never produces a subgoal, so it cannot be a step in a longer script); proof/src/tactic.rs:264-272 and :750-826 (`simp`'s rule set is the in-scope hypotheses only — there are no De Morgan lemmas in the LOGOS prelude, so `simp` cannot normalise negations either)
guards: THE `depth == 0` GATE, and the reason a naive mapping fails in the middle. Because Strategy 8 fires only at `depth == 0` (engine.rs:2340), classical reductio is NOT available for any subgoal the chainer generates internally. A Lean proof whose `by_contra` sits under an `intro` translates to a script whose `auto` runs on the post-`intro` goal — which IS depth 0 for that `auto` call, so it works — but a Lean proof whose `by_contra` is needed for a subgoal of a larger automatic search will never reach it. The difference is invisible from the script text: both spellings are the word `auto`.

Catches emitting `crush` instead. `crush` (tactic.rs:884-896) is e-matching plus congruence closure; it has no reductio strategy at all. A translator that tries `first [ auto | crush ]` to "be safe" will silently prefer whichever succeeds, and `crush` succeeding means the proof went through WITHOUT the classical axiom — a different, constructively-weaker derivation than the Lean source's, which is a difference a `#print axioms`-style audit is supposed to be able to see.

Catches the ALIAS `tauto` (tactic_script.rs:323). Lean's `tauto` is a propositional decision procedure; LOGOS's `tauto` is `auto`, the full backward chainer WITH classical reductio. Emitting the word `tauto` therefore silently enables the `dne` axiom for a proof the Lean source intended to be propositional. The axiom footprint of the translated theorem is larger than the original's, and nothing records it.

Catches treating `auto`'s success as a proof. `ProofState::auto` closing the goal produces a DERIVATION; only `qed()` → `check_derivation` (tactic.rs:966-972) turns it into a `VerifiedProof`, and `verified == false` is a possible outcome (proof/src/verify.rs:31-43) that `compile_theorem` reports as "derivation found but NOT kernel-certified (this is not a proof)" (compile.rs:1163). A reductio derivation is exactly the kind that can fail certification, because the `ClassicalReductio` arm must reconstruct `¬G` as a kernel type (certifier.rs:1456-1458) and a `ProofExpr` that does not translate to a `Prop` will fail there.
oracle: Every Lean `by_contra` maps to a single `auto` atom that is given the ENTIRE remaining subproof, accompanied by a loss record naming REDUCTIO_IS_NOT_A_STEP; the resulting derivation's root (or some node) is `InferenceRule::ClassicalReductio`; and `qed()` returns `verified == true`. For `pushNegForall` the translator must record NNF_UNAVAILABLE, and the harness asserts no emitted script contains `push_neg`.
loss: REDUCTIO_IS_NOT_A_STEP. Lean's `by_contra h` is a STEP: it adds `h : ¬G` and leaves `False` as the goal, and the rest of the tactic block proves it. LOGOS's reductio is a SEARCH STRATEGY inside `auto` — it is tried only when the backward chainer has exhausted everything else, only at `depth == 0`, and only for a positive non-`False` goal (engine.rs:2340). A Lean proof of the shape `intro x; by_contra h; <20 steps>` has no step-wise image: the whole subproof must be handed to `auto` as one opaque call, and if `auto` cannot find the contradiction, there is no way to help it.

NNF_UNAVAILABLE. `push_neg` rewrites `¬∀`, `¬∃`, `¬(p ∧ q)`, `¬(a < b)` into positive form. LOGOS has no De Morgan rewriting: `simp`'s rules are the scope's hypotheses (tactic.rs:264-272), and the prelude registers no propositional lemmas. Every `push_neg` must be discharged by `auto` on the un-normalised goal, or the translator must supply the De Morgan equivalence as an explicit premise — which changes the theorem's hypothesis set.
note: `by_contra` and `push_neg` are MATHLIB tactics; bare Lean 4.14 has neither (`by_contra` reports "unknown tactic"). Each theorem below carries the Mathlib invocation in a comment and is proved with core Lean — `intro`/`exact` against `Classical.byContradiction`, or explicit `Decidable`/`Classical.em` reasoning. The CONSTRUCT under test is the commented Mathlib call.

cases.title: `conv` — positional rewriting is exactly what LOGOS's all-occurrences `rewrite` cannot express
cases.lean: conv => lhs; rw [..], conv at h, conv in <pattern>, nth_rewrite
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: a grep of `crates/logicaffeine_proof/src` and `crates/logicaffeine_kernel/src` for `conv` returns NOTHING — there is no conversion-mode state, no zipper, no subterm navigator anywhere in LOGOS; proof/src/tactic_script.rs:308-327 (`canonical` — no arm for `conv`, `lhs`, `rhs`, `enter`, `congr` or `nth_rewrite`); proof/src/tactic.rs:113-128 (`replace_in_term` — the ONLY rewriting primitive: `if t == from { return to.clone() }` then recurse into every argument, with no position argument, no occurrence counter, and no way to stop early); proof/src/tactic.rs:130-156 (`replace_in_expr` — same, over the whole formula); proof/src/tactic.rs:702-737 (`ProofState::rewrite` calls `replace_in_expr` once on `g.target` and fails only if NOTHING changed, :719-723 — there is no "rewrite the second occurrence" mode and no way to observe how many occurrences changed); proof/src/tactic.rs:750-826 (`simp` — the other rewriting tactic — likewise rewrites through `replace_in_expr` at :766, so it is all-occurrences too); proof/src/lib.rs:488-728 (`InferenceRule::Rewrite { from, to }` carries only the two TERMS — there is no position, path, or occurrence index in the certified record, so even a Rust-level translator has nowhere to write one)
guards: THE CENTRAL POINT, and the reason this case sits next to T08-011. `conv` exists in Lean *because* `rw` is not positional enough. Translating a `conv` block by dropping the navigation and emitting the inner `rw` as a LOGOS `rewrite` produces exactly the behaviour the user wrote `conv` to avoid: every occurrence is rewritten. The result is a well-typed term, a well-formed derivation, and a different goal. Nothing in the kernel can object, because the kernel sees only the finished `Rewrite` node and its two terms.

Catches the "it's the same when there is one occurrence" rationalisation. A `conv` block whose target occurs exactly once IS equivalent to a plain rewrite — and the translator cannot know that in general, because deciding it requires counting occurrences in the TRANSLATED goal, after every earlier step has run. A translator that counts occurrences in the LEAN goal instead is counting in a different term: Lean's `Expr` has `mdata`, implicit arguments, and instance arguments that LOGOS's `ProofExpr` does not, so occurrence counts differ. If a translator wants to admit the single-occurrence case it must count on the LOGOS side, at emission time, and record the check.

Catches `conv at h`. Conversion mode can target a HYPOTHESIS; `ProofState::rewrite` reads and writes `g.target` only (tactic.rs:718, :730). Both the positional aspect and the location aspect are missing, and a translator that "fixes" only one of them has fixed nothing.

Catches Mathlib's `nth_rewrite n [h]`. It is the compact spelling of the same request and must be rejected by the same rule. A translator that special-cases `nth_rewrite 1 [h]` as "the first occurrence, which is what `rw` does anyway" is wrong twice: Lean's `rw` rewrites all occurrences of the instantiated pattern (verified in T08-011), not the first, and LOGOS's does the same — so `nth_rewrite 1` is NOT the default behaviour of either.

Catches `conv` used for its OTHER purpose — entering under a binder to rewrite inside a `∀`/`λ` body. LOGOS's `replace_in_expr` already recurses into `ForAll`/`Exists` bodies (tactic.rs:148-153), so the navigation is unnecessary there — and, per T08-011, it does so WITHOUT binder protection, which is a capture bug rather than a feature. A translator must not read "LOGOS already rewrites under binders" as "the `conv` was redundant".
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NO_CONVERSION_MODE for every theorem below and emits no script containing a `rewrite` atom derived from a `conv` block. A harness additionally asserts that every emitted `rewrite` in the corpus corresponds to a Lean `rw`/`subst` whose pattern occurs exactly once in the translated goal, or carries the T08-011 loss record.
diag: E_NO_CONVERSION_MODE — must name the theorem, report the conversion path the `conv` block navigates (`lhs`, `rhs`, `enter [2]`, a pattern), and state that LOGOS's only rewriting primitive is all-occurrences `replace_in_expr` (tactic.rs:113-156) with no positional form in the certified `InferenceRule::Rewrite` either. Must NOT emit a `rewrite` atom.

cases.lean: tauto, aesop, trivial-by-automation, simp-driven closure

A translator that reports success when the script RAN — rather than when `verified == true` — will mark theorems proved that are not. Because `auto` is the tactic most likely to be emitted for a hard goal, it is also the one most likely to produce an uncertifiable derivation.

Catches the DEAD-RULE failure mode. Seven of the 46 `InferenceRule` variants are emitted by no engine and have no certifier arm (lib.rs:488-728); a derivation carrying one fails with `KernelError::CertificationError`. A translator that constructs derivation trees directly — rather than letting `auto` build them — must never emit a modal or temporal rule. See T11-021.

Catches the Z3 ORACLE. Strategy 9 (engine.rs:2352-2356) falls back to an external SMT solver at the top level, certified as `InferenceRule::OracleVerification`. That moves the trust boundary outside the LOGOS kernel for that step. A translator that reports "kernel-certified" for a theorem whose derivation contains an `OracleVerification` node is overstating the guarantee, and must record it.

Catches the ALIAS SPRAY. `trivially`, `directly`, `automatically` and `automation` all mean `auto` (tactic_script.rs:323), while `trivial` means `assumption` (tactic_script.rs:315) and `grind`/`blast` mean `crush` (tactic_script.rs:319). Four near-synonyms, three different tactics. A translator that renders Lean tactics into English prose will hit the wrong one; the canonical names must be emitted.
oracle: Every Lean `tauto`/`aesop` maps to a single `auto` atom with a loss record naming SEARCH_SHAPE, AXIOM_FOOTPRINT and NONDETERMINISM; `qed()` is called and `verified == true` is asserted (not merely that `run_script` returned `Ok`); and the assembled derivation contains no dead `InferenceRule` variant. If it contains an `OracleVerification` node, the translator must say so in its report.
loss: SEARCH_SHAPE. Lean's `tauto` is a propositional decision procedure and `aesop` is a configurable best-first search with a rule set, `simp` integration, and safe/unsafe rule phases. LOGOS's `auto` is a backward chainer over untyped FOL `ProofExpr` whose knowledge base is the in-scope hypotheses (tactic.rs:904-906). The three succeed on overlapping but different goal sets, and none of them is a subset of another. Every translated `aesop` is a bet that the LOGOS search happens to find A proof.

AXIOM_FOOTPRINT. `auto`'s Strategy 8 uses the `dne` axiom (engine.rs:2346, certifier.rs:1449-1473). Lean's `tauto` on a constructively provable goal produces a constructive term. So translating `tauto` to `auto` can turn an axiom-free Lean proof into one that depends on LOGOS's single classical axiom — a change a `#print axioms`-style audit is supposed to be able to see, and which the script text does not record. The loss record must name it.

NONDETERMINISM. `auto` returns whichever derivation the search finds first. Adding an unrelated hypothesis to the theorem changes the knowledge base (tactic.rs:904-906) and can change the derivation — so the translated artefact is not a function of the Lean proof alone, and two runs over a slightly-edited source produce different certified terms for the same theorem.

cases.title: `·` focusing, `case`, `next` — the script's separators are FLAT and goals have no names or brackets
cases.lean: · focus dot, case <tag> => …, next => …, case' , focus
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: proof/src/tactic_script.rs:177-199 (`parse_seq` — a script is a FLAT list of chains separated by `;`/`.`/`,`/the word `then`; there is no block, no indentation sensitivity, and no goal selector in the grammar at :9-17); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:215-220 (parentheses group a SUB-SCRIPT — `'(' script ')'` — but grouping is not focusing: the inner script still runs against `st.open` as it finds it, and leaves whatever it leaves); proof/src/tactic.rs:280-298 (`refine` — new subgoals are pushed to the FRONT of the `open` deque, in order, so execution is depth-first on the first subgoal and the following atoms simply continue into the next one when it closes); proof/src/tactic.rs:104-111, :83-90 (`ProofState`'s goals are `VecDeque<usize>` indices into a `Vec<Node>` — a `Goal` is `{ hyps, target }` (:around 30-40) with NO name, tag or label field, so there is nothing for `case <tag>` to select on); proof/src/tactic.rs:528-532, :401-405, :604 (`cases`, `split` and `induction` all produce their subgoals positionally, with no constructor tag attached); proof/src/tactic.rs:1124-1136 (`all_goals` — the only goal-selection mechanism in the system, and it selects ALL of them; it is not reachable from script text, see T08-020)
guards: THE FLATTENING TRAP, and the reason this is a rejection rather than a degrade. A translator that strips the `·` bullets and concatenates the blocks with `;` produces a script that WORKS — as long as every block closes exactly the one goal it was written for. Because `refine` pushes subgoals to the front (tactic.rs:296-297), execution is depth-first in exactly the order Lean's bullets appear, so the happy path is indistinguishable. The moment a block leaves a goal open, or closes two, the blocks silently misalign: the second bullet's tactics run against the first bullet's residue. The proof either fails somewhere far from the cause, or — when the tactics are generic enough (`assumption`, `simp`, `auto`) — SUCCEEDS, having proved the goals in an order and a pairing the source never specified. Lean's `·` exists precisely to make that impossible: it is an error for a focused block to leave its goal open.

Catches `case <tag>`. Lean's case tags come from the inductive's constructor names (`inl`, `inr`, `zero`, `succ`, `intro`). LOGOS's `Goal` has no tag field at all, and `cases`/`split`/`induction` attach none (tactic.rs:528-532, :401-405, :604). So `case` cannot be translated even by reordering: there is nothing to reorder BY. A translator that maps `case inr => …` to "the second goal" is assuming the LOGOS ordering matches Lean's constructor order — true today for `∨` (left then right) and `Nat` (base then step), and an undocumented coincidence rather than a guarantee.

Catches `next`. `next => …` focuses the FIRST goal without naming it, which is the closest thing to a flat sequence — and is therefore the case a translator is most likely to flatten silently. It still carries the "must close this goal" obligation that flattening discards.

Catches using PARENTHESES as focusing. `parse_atom` accepts `( script )` (tactic_script.rs:215-220), which looks like a block. It is not: it is precedence grouping. The inner script sees the same `st.open` and can close, open or leave any number of goals. Emitting `( … ) . ( … )` for two bullets changes nothing about which goals the second group runs on.

Catches the "just use `<;>`" alternative. `t1 <;> t2` applies the SAME tactic to every goal (and, per T08-018, to goals from earlier steps as well). Bullets exist because the branches need DIFFERENT tactics. The two are not interchangeable in either direction.

A harness additionally asserts, for every multi-goal step anywhere in the corpus, that the translator recorded how many goals each emitted atom consumed — so that a flattened emission cannot be mistaken for a focused one.

It is only sound for a `have` whose statement is CLOSED. `prove_scripted_library` assembles each theorem's premises as a flat list of `ProofExpr`s before the proof starts (tactic_script.rs:424-437); there is no parameterisation, no context capture, and no way for a cited lemma to refer to the citing theorem's `intro`-bound variables. A translator that lifts a `have` mentioning a local will produce a lemma whose free variables are `ProofTerm::Variable`s that mean nothing in the lemma's own context, and the lemma will either fail to prove or prove something vacuous — and then be cited as though it said what the `have` said.

A translator that passes Lean's tactic word through gets ∀/→ introduction on the goal, which either fails with `DoesNotApply` or — if the goal happens to be an implication — consumes a hypothesis the source never introduced, shifting everything after it.

A translator must compare the translation of `T` with the current LOGOS goal and, if they differ, either refuse or record the divergence — it cannot rely on LOGOS's definitional equality to bridge the gap, because the script layer never calls the kernel's `def_eq` at all (it compares `ProofExpr`s, not kernel `Term`s).

Catches `suffices`. `suffices h : T by tac` REPLACES the goal with `T` and leaves `tac`'s obligation. It is a goal transformation, and the only goal-transforming script atoms are `intro`, `split`, `left`/`right`, `exists`, `cases` and `rewrite` — none of which can substitute an arbitrary new goal. The lift is the same as for `have`, with the same locality restriction, plus the residual proof of `T → original` which must ALSO be lifted.

oracle: Every Lean `have` becomes a distinct `ScriptedTheorem` whose `goal` is closed, is named in the citing theorem's `cites`, and has `simp: false`; every `show` is dropped only after a structural equality check against the current LOGOS goal; and the loss record names LOCALITY, PROOF_TERM_SHAPE and SHOW_ERASURE as applicable. For `haveMentionsLocal` the translator must REFUSE rather than lift.
loss: LOCALITY. A Lean `have` is local: its statement may mention the enclosing theorem's bound variables and hypotheses, and it disappears at the end of the block. A LOGOS `ScriptedTheorem` is global, closed, and citable by name. Lifting therefore requires closing the `have`'s statement over every local it mentions — and the script surface has no way to state a quantified premise that re-binds those locals, because `premises` are `ProofExpr`s fixed at `ProofState::start` (tactic.rs:198-214) and the locals were introduced by `intro` AFTER that. A `have` mentioning an `intro`-bound variable cannot be lifted, and the case escalates to `reject`.

PROOF_TERM_SHAPE. `have h : T := e` supplies a TERM. The script surface has no term language (T08-002), so the lifted theorem must be proved by its own script, and the translator must find one. `have h : T := by tac` is the tractable case: `tac` becomes the lifted theorem's script.

SHOW_ERASURE. `show T` is a no-op up to definitional equality in Lean. LOGOS has no step that changes a goal's spelling without changing the goal, so `show` is dropped. That is sound when `T` is structurally the translation of the current goal, and WRONG when Lean's `show` performed a defeq change — unfolding a definition, reducing an `if`, or eta-expanding — because every later atom then runs against the un-unfolded form and `exact`/`assumption` (which compare structurally, tactic.rs:363, :380) will not match.

cases.title: `refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩` — no `refine` atom, and the obvious term-level encoding puts a `Term::Hole` in the output, which `types_equal` matches against ANYTHING
cases.lean: refine, refine ?_ , refine' , named holes ?h, exact? placeholders
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: proof/src/tactic_script.rs:308-327 (`canonical` — no arm for `refine`; the script grammar's fifteen primitives (:275-292) contain nothing that takes a partial term); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:51-105 (the script lexer has no `?`: the character falls into the `other =>` arm at :101 and the script fails with `unexpected character '?'` — so a `?_` hole cannot even be tokenised); kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term::Hole` — the only placeholder variant; there is NO metavariable variant, no `mvar`, and no assignment map); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1594-1597 (`types_equal` treats `Term::Hole` as MATCHING ANYTHING — the leniency that makes an emitted hole a soundness hole, not merely an incompleteness); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1314 (the same leniency leaks into `is_subtype`'s fast path); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:138 (elaborator metavariables are `Term::Var` names beginning with `?`, NOT a `Term` variant — they exist only inside the elaborator and must be fully instantiated before the kernel sees the term); proof/src/tactic.rs:83-90, :943 (`ProofState`'s own open goals are `Node::Hole(Goal)` — a PROOF-STATE hole, not a term hole; `assemble` refuses to build a derivation while one remains, returning `TacticError::GoalsRemain`)
guards: THE HOLE-IS-NOT-A-METAVARIABLE TRAP, and the reason this is a rejection rather than a "not supported yet". A translator that cannot find a `refine` atom will reach for the term level and emit the partial term directly, filling the `?_`s with `Term::Hole`. That term TYPECHECKS — `types_equal` returns true for a `Hole` against any type (type_checker.rs:1594-1597), and the leniency leaks into `is_subtype` (type_checker.rs:1314). So the kernel accepts a "proof" with a gap in it, and the certificate that results is indistinguishable from a real one. This is the same failure as T00-016 and T11-004, reached from the tactic side.

Catches the `Term::Var("?h")` encoding. LOGOS's elaborator represents metavariables as `Term::Var` names beginning with `?` (elaborate.rs:138) and requires them to be instantiated before the kernel runs. A translator that emits such a `Var` and hands it to the kernel gets an unbound-variable error if it is lucky, and — if a binder anywhere in the term happens to be named `?h` — a CAPTURED variable if it is not, because LOGOS's representation is named (term.rs:449) and substitution alpha-renames only on collision (type_checker.rs:1088).

Catches mapping `refine` onto `split`/`constructor`. `refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩` on a conjunction IS `split` — and only there. `refine` with a partially-applied function, a nested anonymous constructor, or a hole in a non-head position has no correspondence to any of the fifteen primitives. A translator that special-cases the `⟨?_, ?_⟩`-on-`∧` shape must reject every other shape, and must not present the special case as general support.

Catches NAMED holes. `refine ⟨?left, ?right⟩` names the resulting goals, and the names are then used by `case left => …`. LOGOS's `Goal` has no name field at all (see T08-025), so even the goals the special case would produce cannot carry the names forward.

Catches the ORDER of `refine`'s goals. Lean's `refine` produces goals in the order the holes appear in the term, and `refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩` therefore agrees with `constructor`. A translator that assumes this in general will be wrong for `refine f ?a ?b` where `f`'s arguments are not in goal order.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NO_REFINE (or E_HOLE_IN_OUTPUT) for every theorem below and writes NO declaration. A harness additionally asserts the global invariant this case is a member of: **no `Term::Hole` appears anywhere in the translator's output for the entire corpus**, checked by walking every emitted `Term`.
diag: E_NO_REFINE / E_HOLE_IN_OUTPUT — must name the theorem, report the number and names of the `?` holes, state that the script grammar has no `refine` and its lexer rejects `?`, and state that emitting a `Term::Hole` is forbidden because `types_equal` matches it against anything. Must emit NO term and NO script.

cases.title: `sorry` / `admit` — must never become an `add_declaration`, a `Term::Hole`, or a `verified == false` derivation that is reported as a proof
cases.lean: sorry, admit, sorryAx, a proof term containing sorry, a definition using sorry
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: a grep of `crates/logicaffeine_kernel/src` and `crates/logicaffeine_proof/src` for `sorry` / `admit` returns NOTHING outside unrelated prose — there is no `sorryAx`, no admitted-proof marker, and no "incomplete" flag on a declaration anywhere in LOGOS; proof/src/tactic_script.rs:308-327 (`canonical` — no arm for `sorry` or `admit`; the script dies with "unknown tactic `sorry`" at :262); kernel/src/context.rs:434 (`add_declaration(name, ty)` — the AXIOM form: a type with no body, opaque, indistinguishable from a prelude axiom once registered); kernel/src/context.rs:449 (`get_global`'s lookup precedence — inductives, constructors, definitions, declarations: a declaration added this way is found and used like any other global); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1594-1597 (`types_equal` treats `Term::Hole` as matching ANYTHING — so the other obvious encoding is worse than useless); proof/src/verify.rs:31-43 (`VerifiedProof.verified == true` IFF a kernel term was produced AND typechecked — a derivation may exist with `verified == false`); logicaffeine_language/src/compile.rs:1163 ("derivation found but NOT kernel-certified (this is not a proof)"); kernel/src/certificate.rs:28 (`PRELUDE_VERSION = "logos-coc-1"`); kernel/src/certificate.rs:63-75 (`recheck` refuses a mismatched `prelude_version` and then REBUILDS the trusted context itself from `StandardLibrary::register` — "never trust a context the certificate might carry")
guards: THE AXIOM SMUGGLING TRAP, and the highest-value rejection in Tier 8. `ctx.add_declaration("sorryAx", <translated type>)` is one line. It compiles. Every term that uses it typechecks. `get_global` (context.rs:449) resolves it exactly like a prelude axiom, so nothing downstream can tell it apart from `dne` or `le_trans`. And because `Term::Sort(Prop)` is inhabited by fiat once such a declaration exists, the translator has just made LOGOS inconsistent — with no marker, no attribute system to tag it with (LOGOS has none, T02-013), and no `#print axioms` analogue to discover it. The certificate that results still reads `PRELUDE_VERSION = "logos-coc-1"` (certificate.rs:28).

Catches the "it fails at recheck anyway" rationalisation. `certificate::recheck` rebuilds the trusted context from `StandardLibrary::register` alone (certificate.rs:73-75), so a certificate mentioning the invented axiom fails with a bare `KernelError::UnboundVariable("sorryAx")` — a message that looks like a name-resolution bug, not like "this proof was never finished". And that is the GOOD case: a translator that "fixes" it by also patching the prelude gets a passing recheck against an axiom set the version string does not describe. See T11-014.

Catches the `Term::Hole` encoding. Leaving a hole where the proof should be is worse than the axiom: `types_equal` matches `Hole` against anything (type_checker.rs:1594-1597), so the gap does not even localise to one type. See T08-027, T00-016, T11-004.

Catches the `verified == false` encoding. Running the script, letting `qed()` produce a `VerifiedProof` with `verified == false`, and emitting it as the theorem's artefact looks honest — the flag is right there. It is not enough: `compile_theorem` reports such a result as "derivation found but NOT kernel-certified (this is not a proof)" (compile.rs:1163), and a translator that passes the artefact along leaves the "this is not a proof" determination to whoever reads the report. The verdict is `reject`: no output at all.

Catches TRANSITIVITY, and note how quiet Lean itself is about it. A `sorry` in one declaration poisons every declaration that uses it, but the compiler warns ONLY on the declaration whose own elaborated term contains `sorryAx`: `dependsOnSorry` below produces NO warning, and the poisoning is visible only through `#print axioms dependsOnSorry`, which reports `'dependsOnSorry' depends on axioms: [sorryAx]` (verified). A translator that keys its rejection on the compiler WARNING will therefore let the whole downstream cone through. It must key on the axiom closure of the elaborated `Expr` instead, and refuse the cone, not just the `sorry`-bearing declaration. LOGOS offers no second chance here: it has no dependency tracking of this kind at all.

Catches `sorry` in DATA, not just in proofs. `stubbedFunction` is a `Nat`-valued definition whose body is `sorry`. Translating it as `add_declaration` gives an opaque constant of type `Nat` — which is sound as an axiom but is NOT the function the source names, and any later `decide`/`simp` that tries to reduce it will silently get stuck instead of computing.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_INCOMPLETE_PROOF for every declaration below AND for `dependsOnSorry`, performs ZERO `add_declaration` calls, emits no `Term::Hole`, and emits no artefact with `verified == false`. A harness additionally asserts the corpus-wide invariant that the set of `add_declaration` names the translator produces is a subset of the names `StandardLibrary::register` already registers.
diag: E_INCOMPLETE_PROOF — must name the declaration, state that its Lean proof is incomplete (`sorry`/`admit`/`sorryAx` in the elaborated term), and produce NO LOGOS output for it or for anything that depends on it. Must NOT offer an axiom, a hole, or an unverified derivation as a substitute.
note: THIS FILE WARNS, DELIBERATELY. `lean` exits 0 but prints "declaration uses 'sorry'" for SIX of the seven declarations below — that is the construct under test, and a corpus case about `sorry` that did not warn would not contain a `sorry`. No `set_option` is used to suppress it. The seventh, `dependsOnSorry`, is silent, which is the point of the transitivity guard: the warning is a necessary but NOT sufficient signal, and a translator must key its rejection on the axiom closure instead.

cases.title: `notation` — expands before the `Expr` exists, so there is nothing left to translate
cases.lean: notation, notation with precedence, notation binding several arguments
cases.target: The translation of the EXPANDED term. A `notation` command itself produces NO LOGOS declaration; the application it abbreviates translates by the ordinary Tier 0 rules (`Term::App` spine, kernel/src/term.rs:459).
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term` — the COMPLETE kernel term language: there is no `Notation`, no `Syntax`, no parse-tree variant, and no place to record how a term was written); kernel/src/context.rs:20-80 (`Context` — flat `HashMap<String, _>` maps for inductives, constructors, declarations, definitions, universe polys, instances, coercions and binder kinds. There is no notation table, no parser extension, no precedence database); kernel/src/context.rs:201 (`set_binder_kinds` — the closest thing to surface information LOGOS records, and it stores only `ParamKind::{Explicit, Implicit, Instance}`, elaborate.rs:1018-1027); kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:1223-1270 (the ONE fixed infix table LOGOS has — `<= ≤ >= ≥ < > + - *` and the word `equals` — which is hard-coded in the literate parser and not extensible); kernel/src/elaborate.rs (elaboration works on `Term`, never on a surface tree: there is no `Syntax` type in the kernel at all)
guards: THE GOVERNING RULE OF TIER 9, stated here because this is the first case it applies to: **translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** A translator that reads Lean's `Syntax` would have to expand `notation` itself — which means reimplementing Lean's macro expander, including precedence resolution, binder notation, and the interaction with `open`/`local`/`scoped`. Every divergence from Lean's expander is a silent mistranslation, because the resulting term is well-formed and simply means something else. Working from the elaborated `Expr` makes this case vanish: by then `x ⊕ y` is already `myOp x y`.

Catches emitting a LOGOS declaration for the `notation` command. There is no target for it (term.rs:443-545, context.rs:20-80). A translator that tries — say by registering a definition named after the notation token — pollutes the flat global namespace with a name no term will ever reference, and risks colliding with a real declaration (see T02-020).

Catches losing the notation at the REPORTING boundary. The `Expr` carries no record of the surface spelling, so a diagnostic about a term the user wrote as `x ⊕ y` will name `myOp`. That is unavoidable (there is no LOGOS carrier for it), but a translator should keep the Lean-side source position so its own messages can point back. This is the same information loss as T09-010 and T00-009, and must not be confused with a translation failure.

Catches PRECEDENCE-SENSITIVE parses. `notation:65 a " ⊕ " b => myOp a b` and a different precedence produce DIFFERENT `Expr`s for the same character sequence when combined with other operators. A `Syntax`-reading translator must get the precedence right; an `Expr`-reading one cannot get it wrong. `precedenceMatters` below is the witness: the two spellings elaborate to different trees.

Catches notation that is NOT a simple abbreviation. `notation "⟦" x "⟧" => wrap x` introduces brackets that change how the parser reads what is inside them. A translator working from `Syntax` must handle the bracketing; one working from `Expr` sees only `wrap`.
oracle: The `notation` commands below produce ZERO LOGOS declarations. Each theorem's translated term is `types_equal` to the translation of the same theorem written without the notation — i.e. `notationIsTransparent` and `writtenOut` below must translate to the same LOGOS `Term`, up to alpha-renaming.

cases.title: `infixl` / `infixr` / `prefix` / `postfix` — associativity is resolved into the `Expr` spine before translation
cases.lean: infixl, infixr, infix, prefix, postfix, associativity and precedence
cases.target: The translation of the EXPANDED application spine. The command itself produces NO LOGOS declaration; `a ⋄ b ⋄ c` under `infixl` is `App(App(Global("f"), App(App(Global("f"), a), b)), c)` and under `infixr` it is `App(App(Global("f"), a), App(App(Global("f"), b), c))` (kernel/src/term.rs:459, left-nested `App`).
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:459 (`App(Box<Term>, Box<Term>)` — binary and left-nested; a multi-argument application is a SPINE, and the spine shape is the only record of how the arguments were grouped); kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (no `Syntax`, no fixity, no associativity anywhere in the term language); kernel/src/context.rs:20-80 (no fixity table in `Context`); kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:1223-1270 (LOGOS's only infix support is a FIXED table in the literate parser — `<= ≤ >= ≥ < > + - *` plus the word `equals` — with hard-coded associativity and no extension point); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:51-105 (the tactic-script lexer has no operator tokens at all beyond `<;>`, so no user fixity is expressible there either); proof/src/formula.rs:427-432 (Surface B's `parse_term` accepts only a bare identifier — no operators, user-defined or otherwise)
guards: THE ASSOCIATIVITY TRAP, and the reason this case is separate from T09-001. `infixl` and `infixr` produce DIFFERENT `Expr`s for the identical character sequence `a ⋄ b ⋄ c`. A translator that reads surface `Syntax` must carry the fixity declaration forward and apply it; if it guesses left-associativity (the common default), every `infixr` operator in the source is regrouped — and since most interesting operators are not associative, the resulting LOGOS term denotes a different value. It still typechecks. **Translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`** makes the trap unreachable: the spine already has the right shape.

Catches PRECEDENCE between two user operators. `assocDiffers` and `mixedPrecedence` below are the witnesses: the same token sequence groups differently depending on the declared precedences, and only the elaborated `Expr` records the outcome.

Catches `prefix` and `postfix` colliding in the flat namespace. Both expand to an application of a named function; the NAME is what survives into LOGOS's flat `HashMap<String, _>` keys (context.rs:20-80). Two notations for the same function are fine; two functions whose flattened names collide are not — see T02-020.

Catches assuming LOGOS can round-trip the notation. There is no fixity carrier, so a LOGOS term printed back out will use application syntax, not the operator. Any harness that compares printed forms rather than `types_equal` will report spurious failures on every case in this tier.

Catches the SECTION-LOCAL form. `local infixl` and `scoped infixl` are visible only inside a section or namespace; the expansion still happens before elaboration, so the `Expr` is unaffected. A translator that tracks notation scope is doing work it does not need to do, and doing it wrong is a way to mistranslate a term that would otherwise have been fine.
oracle: The fixity commands below produce ZERO LOGOS declarations. `assocLeft` and `assocRight` must translate to STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT LOGOS terms (the harness asserts they are not `types_equal` after erasing names), and each must be `types_equal` to the translation of its written-out counterpart.

cases.title: `macro_rules` — a RECURSIVE, multi-pattern rewriter on `Syntax` that must be run, not reimplemented; its output is ordinary
cases.lean: macro_rules, macro, recursive macro_rules, several alternatives for one syntax
cases.target: The translation of the EXPANDED term. The `macro_rules` command produces NO LOGOS declaration; whatever the expansion elaborates to translates by the ordinary Tier 0 rules.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term` — no `Syntax`, no quotation, no macro variant, no way to record that a term arose from an expansion); kernel/src/context.rs:20-80 (`Context` — no macro table, no syntax-category registry, no expansion history); kernel/src/elaborate.rs (elaboration consumes `Term` and produces `Term`; there is no surface-tree stage in the kernel at all, so nothing downstream of the translator can expand anything); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:113-133, :250-260 (`TacticEnv` — the ONLY user-extension mechanism anywhere in LOGOS: a name-to-script-source map, expanded in place at parse time, DEPTH-BOUNDED at `MAX_TACTIC_DEPTH = 128` (:133) so a recursive definition is refused rather than looped. It is a textual macro over TACTIC SCRIPTS, not over terms, and it cannot pattern-match on anything); kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:1223-1270 (the literate surface's fixed infix table — likewise not extensible)
guards: THE REIMPLEMENTATION TRAP, and the sharpest instance of the governing rule. `macro_rules` is a pattern-matching, potentially RECURSIVE rewriter with several alternatives tried in order, hygiene, and `Syntax`-level antiquotation. A translator that reads surface `Syntax` must therefore implement Lean's macro expander — alternative ordering, recursion, hygiene and all — and any divergence produces a well-formed term with a different meaning. **Translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** After elaboration `nested![a, b, c]` is already `cons a (cons b (cons c nil))` and the macro has left no trace to get wrong.

Catches ALTERNATIVE ORDER. `macro_rules` alternatives are tried in declaration order, and a later `macro_rules` block for the same syntax PREPENDS its alternatives. A translator that collects the alternatives into a set, or that applies them in source order across blocks, expands differently from Lean. `overlappingRules` below has two blocks whose alternatives overlap, so the result depends on this ordering rule.

Catches RECURSION. A recursive `macro_rules` expands until a base alternative matches. A `Syntax`-reading translator needs a termination story of its own; LOGOS offers no help, because its one macro-like facility (`TacticEnv`, tactic_script.rs: 113-133) is depth-bounded at 128 and refuses recursion rather than supporting it.

Catches emitting a LOGOS declaration for the macro. There is no target. In particular, mapping a term-level `macro_rules` onto `TacticEnv::define` (tactic_script.rs:123-125) is a category error: that registry holds TACTIC SCRIPT text, keyed case-insensitively, expanded textually with no pattern matching — it cannot represent a term macro, and registering one there would make a tactic name that expands to nonsense.

Catches HYGIENE. A macro that introduces a binder must not capture a name from the call site. Lean's expander handles this with macro scopes; the resulting `Expr` has already-freshened binder names. A `Syntax`-reading translator that expands naively captures, and since LOGOS's representation is NAMED (`Term::Var(String)`, term.rs:449) and substitution alpha-renames only on collision (type_checker.rs:1088), the capture survives into the kernel as a silently different term. `hygienic` below is the witness: the macro introduces `x` and the call site also has an `x`.
oracle: The `macro_rules` commands below produce ZERO LOGOS declarations. Each theorem's translated term is `types_equal` to the translation of the same theorem written with the expansion inlined by hand — in particular `hygienic` must translate to a term whose inner binder is DISTINCT from the call site's `x`.

cases.title: `syntax` + `elab` — an arbitrary `MetaM` program; the metaprogram is rejected, its OUTPUT is ordinary
cases.lean: syntax + elab, elab_rules, custom term elaborators, custom tactic elaborators
cases.target: (none for the metaprogram — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term` — the complete target language: `Sort`, `Var`, `Global`, `Const`, `Pi`, `Lambda`, `App`, `Match`, `Fix`, `MutualFix`, `Let`, `Lit`, `Hole`. There is no computation-at-elaboration-time construct, no `MetaM`, no tactic-as-term, and no reflection of the `Context` back into the term language); kernel/src/context.rs:20-80 (`Context` holds only inductives, constructors, declarations, definitions, universe polys, instances, coercions and binder kinds — all flat `HashMap<String, _>`. There is no elaborator-extension table and no way to register a Rust closure against a syntactic form); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1016-1027, :1030-1050 (`ParamKind` and `elaborate_app` — LOGOS's elaborator is a FIXED algorithm: insert metavariables for implicits, defer instance resolution until the explicit arguments are unified, then solve. It exposes no registration API); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:113-133 (`TacticEnv` — the ONLY user extension in the system: a `HashMap<String, String>` from a name to SCRIPT SOURCE TEXT, expanded textually and depth-bounded at `MAX_TACTIC_DEPTH = 128`. It cannot run code, inspect a goal, or construct a term); proof/src/tactic.rs:978 (`pub type Tactic = Box<dyn Fn(&mut ProofState) -> Result<(), TacticError>>` — Rust closures ARE first-class tactics, but only inside the Rust process; nothing serialises one, so no LOGOS artefact can carry it)
guards: THE SCOPE-OF-REJECTION GUARD, and the nuance this case exists to fix. It is easy to over-read this rejection as "any file using a custom elaborator is untranslatable". That is wrong, and would make the translator useless on real Lean. What cannot be translated is the METAPROGRAM — the `elab` body, which is Lean code running in `MetaM` with access to the environment, the local context, unification and IO. What the metaprogram EMITS is an ordinary `Expr`, and it translates by the ordinary rules. A translator must therefore reject the `syntax`+`elab` commands and CONTINUE, translating every declaration whose elaborated term happens to have been produced by them. `usesCustomElab` below is the test: its `Expr` is a plain `Nat` literal and must translate.

Catches the over-generalisation running the other way. Inlining the elaborator's output works only because Lean already ran the elaborator. A translator asked to process a Lean FILE rather than an elaborated environment cannot run it — `MetaM` needs the whole Lean runtime — so it must refuse the file rather than guess. **Translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`**: an `Expr`-driven translator never faces this choice.

Catches mapping `elab` onto `TacticEnv::define` (tactic_script.rs:123-125). That registry stores SCRIPT TEXT and expands it textually with a depth bound; an `elab` body is a program. Registering the elaborator's NAME there with some plausible script produces a LOGOS tactic that runs something the Lean source never specified, under a name that suggests it does.

Catches elaborators that are NOT deterministic functions of their syntax. An `elab` body may read the environment (`getEnv`), the local context, the message log, or `IO` — so the same syntax elaborates differently in different positions. `usesEnvReadingElab` below does exactly this. Nothing about it is recoverable from the syntax alone, which is why the rejection is of the metaprogram rather than a deferral.

Catches `elab_rules : tactic`. A custom TACTIC elaborator produces no term at all: it manipulates goals. LOGOS's script surface has a closed set of fifteen primitives (tactic_script.rs:275-292, see T08-003 and T08-020), so even a tactic elaborator whose effect is simple has no spelling — and its EFFECT, the proof term, still translates.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_METAPROGRAM_NOT_REPLAYABLE for each `syntax`/`elab` pair below, emits nothing for them, and DOES emit a correct LOGOS declaration for `usesCustomElab`, `usesEnvReadingElab`, `usesCustomTactic`, `usesBranchingElab` and `usesBranchingElabOdd` — whose elaborated `Expr`s contain no trace of the metaprogram. A translator that refuses those has over-rejected and fails this case.
diag: E_METAPROGRAM_NOT_REPLAYABLE — must name the syntax category and the elaborator, state that the elaborator is an arbitrary `MetaM` program with no LOGOS counterpart, and — importantly — state that the DECLARATIONS THE ELABORATOR PRODUCES are not themselves rejected. Must emit nothing for the `syntax`/`elab` pair.
note: This file opens with `import Lean`, which is part of the Lean 4 CORE distribution (not Mathlib) and is required to write any elaborator at all. Lean requires `import` to be the first command in a file, so the metadata block sits immediately after it rather than on line 1. The same applies to T09-005, T09-006, T09-007 and T09-012.

cases.title: Syntax quotation and antiquotation — `Syntax` is a Lean-runtime data type with no LOGOS representation, and `?` cannot even be lexed by the script surface
cases.lean: `(…) quotation, $x antiquotation, `(tactic| …), Syntax.mkApp, TSyntax
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term` — thirteen variants, none of which is a representation of syntax. `Term::Lit` (term.rs:13-44) holds `Int`, `Float`, `Text`, `Duration`, `Date`, `Moment`, `BigInt`, `Nat` — a quoted `Syntax` tree is none of these, and encoding one as `Literal::Text` would be a string, not a tree); kernel/src/prelude.rs (the registered inductives are `Entity`, `Int`, `Float`, `Text`, `Duration`, `Date`, `Moment`, `Nat`/`Zero`/`Succ`, `EList`/`ENil`/`ECons`, `Bool`, `TList`, `True`/`I`, `False`, `Decidable`, `Eq`, `Acc`, `And`, `Or`, `Ex`, and the hardware types — there is no `Syntax` inductive and no `Name` type); kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:631-635, :2277-2316 (the ONE place LOGOS has something called `Syntax`: `try_ring` has type `Syntax → Derivation` (prelude.rs:2984-2990) and the literate parser REIFIES a goal into it with `term_to_syntax`. That `Syntax` is a fixed reflection of a GOAL for the tactic reducers — `SName`, `SApp` — not a general parse tree, and nothing constructs one from user text); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:51-105 (the script lexer: `is_alphanumeric() || '_'` for words, plus `;.,()[]|` and `<;>`. The character `?` falls to the `other =>` arm at :101 and produces `ScriptError("unexpected character '?'")` — an antiquotation cannot be TOKENISED, let alone represented); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:137-140 (`is_meta` — LOGOS's own `?`-prefixed names are ELABORATOR metavariables in `Term::Var`, a completely different thing from an antiquotation, and they must be fully instantiated before the kernel runs)
guards: THE `?`-COLLISION TRAP. LOGOS uses a `?` prefix on `Term::Var` names for its own elaborator metavariables (elaborate.rs:137-140). A translator that sees Lean's antiquotation `$x` or a named hole `?h` and reaches for that convention produces a `Term::Var("?x")` — which the LOGOS elaborator will then try to SOLVE by unification, and which must be fully instantiated before the kernel sees it. An antiquotation is not a metavariable: it is a splice point in a parse tree. Encoding one as the other means the elaborator will either solve it to something arbitrary or leave it, at which point it reaches the kernel as an unbound named variable.

Catches encoding a quotation as `Literal::Text`. `Term::Lit(Literal::Text(..))` (term.rs:13-44) will hold the source text, and it will typecheck as a `Text`. It is not a syntax tree: nothing can traverse it, splice into it, or elaborate it, and LOGOS has NO string operations at all (see T10-016), so it cannot even be manipulated.
