A translator that does this has smuggled uninterpretable data into a proof term under a type that claims it is a string.

Catches confusing Lean's `Syntax` with LOGOS's. `try_ring : Syntax → Derivation` (prelude.rs:2984-2990) makes it look as though LOGOS has a syntax type to target. It does not have a general one: `term_to_syntax` (literate_parser.rs) reifies a kernel `Term` into a fixed `SName`/`SApp` encoding so the tactic REDUCERS can pattern match on a goal (reduction.rs:2282-2316). It represents propositions, not programs, and there is no constructor for a binder, a tactic block, or an antiquotation.

Catches the scope of the rejection, as in T09-004. A quotation's eventual OUTPUT — the term it builds once spliced and elaborated — is ordinary and translates. What is rejected is any declaration whose TYPE or BODY mentions `Syntax`/`TSyntax` as a value, because that value has no LOGOS counterpart at any stage.

Catches `` `(tactic| …) `` specifically. A quoted TACTIC is a value of type `TSyntax `tactic`, and the LOGOS script language is a STRING parsed at run time (tactic_script.rs:330-353) with no reified form. The nearest analogue, `TacticEnv::define(name, script_source)` (tactic_script.rs:123-125), stores text and re-expands it textually — it cannot be constructed programmatically from parts, and has no antiquotation.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NO_SYNTAX_REPRESENTATION for every declaration below whose type mentions `Lean.Syntax` or `Lean.TSyntax`, and emits no `Term::Lit` whose `Literal::Text` payload is Lean source text. A harness additionally asserts that no emitted `Term::Var` name begins with `?` anywhere in the corpus.
diag: E_NO_SYNTAX_REPRESENTATION — must name the quotation, state that LOGOS has no `Syntax` type in its term language or its prelude, and state that the `Syntax`-typed VALUE is what is unrepresentable (not the term the quotation eventually produces). Must emit no declaration for anything whose type mentions `Lean.Syntax` or `TSyntax`.
note: `import Lean` (core, not Mathlib) is required to write a quotation at all; see the
on T09-004 about the metadata block's position.

cases.title: Custom `deriving` handlers — the handler is a `CommandElabM` program; the declarations it generates are ordinary and must be translated
cases.lean: deriving with a custom handler, registerDerivingHandler, deriving Repr/BEq/Inhabited
cases.target: (none for the handler — no sound translation). The GENERATED declarations translate by the ordinary rules: an instance becomes `Context::add_instance` (kernel/src/context.rs:184), a generated function becomes `Context::add_definition` (kernel/src/context.rs:442).
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:20-80 (`Context` — flat maps only; there is no handler registry, no attribute system, and no hook that fires on an inductive's registration); kernel/src/context.rs:253, :374, :419, :545 (`add_inductive`, `add_indexed_inductive`, `add_constructor`, `add_constructor_checked` — declaring an inductive runs NO user code and generates NO companions); kernel/src/recursor.rs:36 (`derive_recursor(ctx, ind)` — even the RECURSOR, the one thing LOGOS derives, is not created by declaration: it synthesises `(type, term)` and the CALLER must `add_definition` it. That is the whole extent of automatic generation in LOGOS); kernel/src/context.rs:184 (`add_instance(ty, value)` — a flat `Vec<(Term, Term)>`, first match wins: the target for a generated instance); kernel/src/prelude.rs:926, :1027 (`decEqBool` and `decEqNat` — the ONLY two decidable equality procedures in the trusted base; there is no `DecidableEq` synthesis, see T03-023); kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (no `Term` variant can hold a Lean program, so the handler cannot be carried as data either)
guards: THE SAME NUANCE AS T09-004, and it matters more here because `deriving` is common in ordinary Lean. Rejecting the handler must NOT mean rejecting the type that uses it. `deriving Repr, BEq` appears on a large fraction of real Lean inductives; a translator that refuses any inductive carrying a `deriving` clause will refuse most input. The clause is a REQUEST TO RUN A PROGRAM; Lean has already run it, and the resulting instances are ordinary definitions sitting in the environment. The translator reads those, not the clause. This is the index's own note on T02-017: "handler output must be translated, not the `deriving` clause".

Catches translating the generated instance WITHOUT checking it is in a supported fragment. Deriving `BEq` for a recursive inductive generates a structurally recursive function; LOGOS's termination check is a syntactic Giménez guard (kernel/src/termination.rs) with no well-founded recursion, so a generated function Lean accepts may be refused. Deriving `Repr` generates `String`-producing code, and LOGOS has `Literal::Text` but NO string operations at all (T10-016), so `Repr` instances are untranslatable in practice even though the `deriving` clause that asked for them is what gets the diagnostic. The translator must diagnose against the GENERATED declaration, naming it, not against the clause.

Catches deriving `DecidableEq`. The trusted base has exactly `decEqBool` and `decEqNat` (prelude.rs:926, :1027) and no synthesis mechanism, so a generated `DecidableEq` for a user inductive must be emitted as an ordinary definition and registered with `add_instance` (context.rs:184) — a flat `Vec` searched by unification, first match wins. There is no priority and no coherence check, so two derived instances for overlapping types silently resolve to whichever was added first. See T07-008 and T03-023.

Catches the ORDER of emission. `add_instance` is insertion-ordered and first-match wins (context.rs:184). Lean's instance resolution uses priorities and specificity. A translator that emits derived instances in declaration order will get a different resolution than Lean whenever two of them could apply — and derived instances are exactly the ones a user never looks at, so the divergence is invisible.

Catches assuming the handler is deterministic or pure. `registerDerivingHandler` takes a `Array Name → CommandElabM Bool`: it can read the environment, emit several declarations, log messages, and decline (returning `false`) so that another handler runs. None of that is recoverable from the `deriving` clause.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_METAPROGRAM_NOT_REPLAYABLE for the `initialize registerDerivingHandler` command and for each `deriving` clause below, emits nothing for them, and DOES emit LOGOS declarations for `Flag`, `Pair`, `Colour`, `Chain`, their constructors, the `Flag_tag` / `Pair_tag` definitions, the `MyTag` instances, and every instance Lean's built-in handlers generated for `Colour` and `Chain`. A translator that refuses any of those types has over-rejected and fails this case.
diag: E_METAPROGRAM_NOT_REPLAYABLE — must name the handler and the classes it derives, state that LOGOS has no deriving-handler registry and no hook on inductive declaration, and state explicitly that the GENERATED declarations are translated normally. Must emit nothing for the handler itself.
note: `import Lean` (core, not Mathlib) is required to register a handler; see the @note on T09-004 about the metadata block's position. The handler below deliberately does something trivial and visible — it emits a `def` named after the type plus an instance — so a harness can check that the OUTPUT was translated while the handler was rejected.

Lean's `initialize registerDerivingHandler` takes effect only when the module is IMPORTED; a `deriving MyTag` clause in the SAME file fails with "default handlers have not been implemented yet". `Flag` and `Pair` below therefore carry no `deriving MyTag` clause and the handler's output is written out by hand. Nothing is lost for this case — the point is precisely that the translator reads the generated DECLARATIONS and never the clause — and the limitation is direct evidence for T09-007, since it exists because `initialize` mutates a persistent environment extension, which is the thing LOGOS has no counterpart for.

cases.title: `initialize` and environment extensions — LOGOS's `Context` has no extension slot, no attribute system, and no import-time effects
cases.lean: initialize, builtin_initialize, registerSimpAttr, EnvExtension, IO.Ref state, attribute registration
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:20-80 (`Context` — the COMPLETE state: `bindings`, `inductives`, `constructors`, `inductive_params`, `constructor_order`, `declarations`, `definitions`, `hints`, `universe_polys`, `instances`, `coercions`, and per-binder kinds. Every one is a flat `HashMap`/`Vec` of TERMS. There is no extension registry, no attribute map, no user-extensible slot, and no IO); kernel/src/context.rs:434, :442 (the two ways a name enters the environment — `add_declaration` and `add_definition` — both take only a name and terms, so nothing can attach metadata to a declaration); kernel/src/context.rs:449 (`get_global`'s lookup precedence: inductives, constructors, definitions, declarations. Nothing consults an extension); kernel/src/certificate.rs:63-75 (`recheck` REBUILDS the trusted context itself from `StandardLibrary::register`, explicitly refusing to "trust a context the certificate might carry" — so even if a translator did smuggle extra state into a `Context`, the artefact that is supposed to be re-checkable would not carry it); kernel/src/certificate.rs:28 (`PRELUDE_VERSION = "logos-coc-1"` — the ONLY environment-level metadata in the system, a single version string); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:385-396, :421-437 (`ScriptedTheorem::simp` and the `simp_pool` — the nearest thing to an attribute, and it is CALL-LOCAL to one `prove_scripted_library` invocation, not persistent); kernel/src/prelude.rs (the trusted base is built by a fixed sequence of registration calls with no hook for user code to join in)
guards: THE STATE-IS-NOT-A-DECLARATION TRAP. `initialize` does not declare anything: it RUNS `IO` at import time and mutates an environment extension or an `IO.Ref`. There is no term, no type, and no name for the translator to emit. A translator that treats the `initialize` block as an ordinary `def` (it does elaborate to a term of type `IO Unit` or similar) and emits it as a definition produces a LOGOS global of an uninhabited-in-LOGOS type that no one calls — harmless, but it hides the fact that the SIDE EFFECT was silently dropped, and the side effect is the whole point.

Catches dropping an attribute registration and continuing as if nothing happened. `initialize registerSimpAttr` and `attribute [simp] foo` change how LATER declarations elaborate and how tactics behave. LOGOS has no attribute system at all (T02-013), so the effect cannot be carried — and its absence is not local to the `initialize` block: every downstream `simp` now runs a different rule set. The rejection must therefore extend to a REPORT that the affected tactic calls are no longer faithful, not just to the block itself. See T08-012's DEFAULT_SET loss.

Catches the `simp_pool` false friend. `ScriptedTheorem { simp: true }` (tactic_script.rs:392-395) puts a proved conclusion into a pool visible to later theorems in the SAME `prove_scripted_library` call (tactic_script.rs:432-437). That looks like `@[simp]` and is not: it does not persist past the call, it is keyed on proof order within the call, and a `## Theorem` block never sees it. Mapping Lean's `@[simp]` onto it converts a global persistent fact into a call-local one, which changes which theorems are provable depending on how the translator batched them.

Catches `IO.Ref` state. `initialize ref : IO.Ref Nat ← IO.mkRef 0` creates mutable state that later metaprograms read and write. LOGOS's kernel has NO IO — the crate is pure by construction (`logicaffeine_data` carries the "Lamport invariant: NO IO", and `logicaffeine_kernel` the "Milner invariant: NO LEXICON") — so there is not merely no representation for the reference, there is no place for it to exist.

Catches the IMPORT-TIME timing. `initialize` runs when the module is IMPORTED, not where it is written — which is why T09-006's custom deriving handler cannot be used in the file that registers it. A translator processing one module at a time will never observe the effect at all, and one processing a whole build will observe it in an order determined by the import graph. Neither ordering is representable in a LOGOS `Context`, which is built by a linear sequence of `add_*` calls.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NO_ENVIRONMENT_EXTENSION for every `initialize` block and every `attribute`/`@[…]` registration below, emits nothing for them, and — critically — emits a REPORT entry saying which later declarations' elaboration or tactic behaviour depended on the dropped state. The ordinary declarations (`tagged`, `plainDef`) must still translate.
diag: E_NO_ENVIRONMENT_EXTENSION — must name the `initialize` block and the extension or attribute it registers, state that LOGOS's `Context` has no extension slot and no attribute system, and state that the effect is a persistent, import-time mutation that has no artefact to live in. Must emit nothing for the block.
note: `import Lean` (core, not Mathlib) is required for `initialize` and for the extension API; see the @note on T09-004 about the metadata block's position.

cases.title: `set_option` — pragmas are erased, but some of them CHANGE THE ELABORATED TERM, so erasure is only sound after the elaboration they affected
cases.lean: set_option, set_option ... in, per-declaration options, options that change the Expr
cases.target: Nothing is emitted for the pragma itself. The declarations it scopes translate by the ordinary rules.
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:20-80 (`Context` — no options map, no configuration, no reducibility settings, no elaboration flags. Every field is a flat map of terms); kernel/src/type_checker.rs, kernel/src/reduction.rs (the kernel's behaviour is fixed at compile time: `normalize`'s fuel is the CONSTANT 10000 (reduction.rs:52-69) and not a settable option; there is no `maxRecDepth`, no `maxHeartbeats`, no `pp.*`); kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term` — no `mdata` variant, so even Lean's own carrier for per-node configuration has nowhere to go, see T00-009); kernel/src/context.rs:201 (`set_binder_kinds` — the ONLY per-declaration setting LOGOS records, and it stores `ParamKind::{Explicit, Implicit, Instance}` (elaborate.rs:1016-1027), nothing else. In particular there is no reducibility hint, so `@[reducible]`/`@[irreducible]` are equally uncarriable, see T00-013); kernel/src/certificate.rs:28 (`PRELUDE_VERSION = "logos-coc-1"` — the single piece of environment metadata a certificate carries)
guards: THE "ALL PRAGMAS ARE COSMETIC" TRAP. It is tempting to drop every `set_option` with a blanket rule and no record. Most are cosmetic; `autoImplicit` is not. Under `autoImplicit true` (Lean's default) the declaration `def idAuto (x : α) : α := x` elaborates with `α` bound as an implicit universe-polymorphic type argument; under `autoImplicit false` it is an ERROR. The two produce a different declaration and a different arity, and the difference is recorded nowhere except in the pragma. A translator working from the elaborated `Expr` is safe; one that re-derives binders from surface syntax is not.

Catches losing `set_option ... in`'s SCOPE. The `in` form applies to exactly one following declaration; the bare form applies to the rest of the section. A translator that records options at all must get the scope right, and one that does not record them must at least not report that it did.

Catches `set_option maxRecDepth` / `maxHeartbeats` as though they were a fidelity issue. They are not — but their LOGOS analogue is, and it is not settable: `normalize` has a hard fuel of 10000 and SILENTLY RETURNS THE PARTIALLY-REDUCED TERM when exhausted (reduction.rs:52-69). So a Lean declaration that needed a raised heartbeat limit is exactly the one whose LOGOS normalisation will quietly stop early. The translator must record that too; see T00-012 and T11-005.

Catches `set_option linter.unusedVariables false` and friends being treated as semantic. They are not, and a translator that refuses a file because it cannot carry a linter setting has over-rejected. This corpus deliberately prefers RENAMING an unused binder to `_x` over silencing the linter with a pragma, precisely so that no case file's meaning depends on an option.
Catches `set_option` inside a TACTIC block (`set_option ... in tac`). The option affects how the tactic elaborates, and the tactic's output is a term. Same rule: the term is what translates.
oracle: No LOGOS declaration is emitted for any `set_option` below. Every declaration in scope of one translates, and the loss record names PRAGMA_ERASURE — plus ELABORATION_AFFECTING_OPTIONS for the `autoImplicit` section specifically. A harness asserts that `idAuto`'s translated LOGOS arity matches the arity of its elaborated Lean `Expr`, not the arity its surface syntax suggests.
loss: PRAGMA_ERASURE. Every `set_option` is dropped. For the large majority — `pp.*`, `trace.*`, `maxHeartbeats`, `linter.*`, `diagnostics`, `warningAsError` — this is exact, because they affect Lean's presentation, resource limits, or diagnostics, none of which the elaborated `Expr` records. Acceptable, and the loss record exists so the erasure is visible rather than assumed.

ELABORATION_AFFECTING_OPTIONS. A minority of options change the `Expr` itself, and they must be separated from the cosmetic majority. `autoImplicit` and `relaxedAutoImplicit` decide whether an unbound identifier becomes an implicit binder, so they change a declaration's ARITY (compare T01-011 and T05-008); `structureEta` changes which terms are definitionally equal, so it changes which `rfl`s elaborate at all; `bootstrap.*` changes what the elaborator is allowed to assume. For these the erasure is sound ONLY because Lean has already elaborated under them — the governing rule of this tier restated: **translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** A translator that re-elaborates anything must carry the options forward or it will produce a different term.

cases.title: `#check` / `#eval` / `#print` — commands that produce no declaration, and must produce no LOGOS output either
cases.lean: #check, #eval, #print, #print axioms, #reduce, #guard
cases.target: Nothing. These commands add no constant to the Lean environment, so there is nothing to translate and the correct LOGOS output is the empty set of declarations.
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:434, :442 (`add_declaration` and `add_definition` — the ONLY two ways a name enters a LOGOS `Context`; both require a name and a term, and a `#check` has neither); kernel/src/context.rs:20-80 (`Context` — nothing that could hold a query result: no message log, no output buffer, no trace); kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term` — nothing that represents "the type of this expression, printed", so even the RESULT of a `#check` has no representation beyond the type itself, which is an ordinary term); kernel/src/reduction.rs:52-69 (`normalize`'s hard fuel of 10000, silently returning the partially-reduced term — the closest LOGOS analogue of `#reduce`, and the reason a translator must not try to reproduce `#eval`'s answers by normalising); kernel/src/prelude.rs:1195-1219 (`reduceBool`/`ofReduceBool` — the ONE place LOGOS deliberately wires an evaluator into kernel reduction, and it is gated to `Bool`; it is not a general `#eval`)
guards: THE PHANTOM-DECLARATION TRAP. `#check foo`, `#eval e` and `#print bar` look like commands that "do something", and a translator walking the surface command list will be tempted to emit *something* for each — an `add_declaration` for the checked type, a definition holding the evaluated value, a comment. All of these pollute the flat LOGOS namespace (`HashMap<String, _>`, context.rs:20-80) with names the source never declared, and since LOGOS keys are flat strings with no namespaces (T02-011), such a name can COLLIDE with a real declaration (T02-020). The correct output is nothing.

Catches reproducing `#eval`'s ANSWER as a definition. `#eval (2 + 2 : Nat)` prints `4`; emitting `add_definition("evalResult", Nat, Lit(Nat(4)))` records a fact the source never asserted, and one that is only true because Lean's evaluator agreed with the kernel. LOGOS's evaluator is wired into reduction only through `reduceBool` (prelude.rs:1195-1219), for `Bool` only, so there is no general correspondence to reproduce.

Catches `#eval` WITH SIDE EFFECTS. `#eval (IO.println "hi")` runs `IO`. LOGOS's kernel has no IO at all, so this is not merely a no-op command — it is the same rejection as T09-012, reached through a `#`-command. A translator must distinguish `#eval` of a pure term (nothing to emit) from `#eval` of an `IO` action (reject and report), because the second means the source file DID something that the translation does not.

Catches `#print axioms`. Its output is exactly the audit a translator's own report should reproduce — which declarations depend on which axioms — and it is the tool that reveals a `sorryAx` dependency that produces no compiler warning (see T08-028). A translator should compute the same closure itself; it must not emit the `#print` command's textual output as data.

Catches `#reduce` being taken as a specification. `#reduce e` shows Lean's whnf/full reduction. LOGOS's `normalize` has a hard fuel of 10000 and SILENTLY returns the partially-reduced term when exhausted (reduction.rs:52-69), so the two agree only for small terms. A translator that uses `#reduce` output to validate its emission will get false failures on anything large; it must compare with `def_eq`, not with printed normal forms. See T00-012 and T11-005.

Catches over-rejecting. A file full of `#check`s is perfectly translatable — the commands simply contribute nothing. A translator that refuses a file because it contains a command it does not recognise will refuse most real Lean, where `#check` and `#print` are ubiquitous in comments and examples.
oracle: The translator emits ZERO declarations for every `#`-command below, exits zero, and the resulting LOGOS `Context` contains exactly the names declared by `realDef` and `realTheorem` — no more. The `#eval` of an `IO` action must be reported (see T09-012), and `#print axioms` must not appear in the output at all.

cases.title: Doc comments and module docs — no LOGOS carrier, and the erasure is the same one that erases `Expr.mdata`
cases.lean: /-- doc comment -/, /-! module doc -/, @[inherit_doc], add_decl_doc, source positions
cases.target: Nothing is emitted for the documentation. The documented declaration translates by the ordinary rules.
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:20-80 (`Context` — `bindings`, `inductives`, `constructors`, `inductive_params`, `constructor_order`, `declarations`, `definitions`, `hints`, `universe_polys`, `instances`, `coercions`, per-binder kinds. There is no docstring map, no comment store, no source-position table, and no metadata slot of any kind); kernel/src/context.rs:434, :442 (`add_declaration(name, ty)` and `add_definition(name, ty, body)` — the signatures show there is nowhere to put a docstring even if one wanted to); kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term` has NO `mdata` variant — Lean's own carrier for per-node annotations, including some documentation and every source position, has no counterpart. This is exactly the T00-009 erasure, reached from the command level rather than the term level); kernel/src/term.rs:13-44 (`Literal::Text(String)` exists — so a translator CAN smuggle a docstring in as data, which is the trap below); kernel/src/certificate.rs:28 (`PRELUDE_VERSION = "logos-coc-1"` — the only string-valued metadata in a certificate)
guards: THE DOCSTRING-AS-DATA TRAP. `Literal::Text` (term.rs:13-44) makes it possible to emit a docstring as a term — `add_definition("foo_doc", Global("Text"), Lit(Text("…")))`. It typechecks. It also puts a name in the flat global namespace (context.rs:20-80) that the source never declared, which can collide with a real declaration (T02-020); it is invisible to anything that reads documentation; and since LOGOS has NO string operations at all (T10-016), nothing can ever use it. The correct output is no declaration.

Catches the ATTRIBUTE half. `@[inherit_doc]` is an attribute, and LOGOS has no attribute system (T02-013). A translator that handles docstrings but not `@[inherit_doc]` will report different losses for two declarations that differ only in how their documentation was written.

Catches conflating this with a `reject`. Nothing here blocks translation: a fully documented file translates perfectly, minus the documentation. A translator that refuses a declaration because it cannot carry its docstring has over-rejected, and would refuse essentially all library Lean.

Catches the DIAGNOSTIC consequence being reported as a translation success. Once positions are gone, a LOGOS kernel error names a flat string like `"Foo_bar"` and nothing else. If the translator's report says only "translated 40 declarations", the user has no way back to the source. The loss record must be per-declaration, naming the LOGOS key and the Lean position, so the mapping lives in the REPORT even though it cannot live in the artefact.

Catches assuming the module doc is where the corpus metadata lives on the LOGOS side. It is not: this corpus's own `@case`/`@guard` blocks are Lean module docs (TEMPLATE.md), and they are erased by exactly the rule this case describes. The conformance metadata is an input to the harness, never an output of the translator.
oracle: The translator emits ZERO declarations for the documentation below, emits correct declarations for `documented`, `Documented`, `documentedTheorem` and `inheritsDoc`, emits no `Term::Lit(Literal::Text(..))` whose payload is a docstring, and produces a per-declaration loss record naming DOCUMENTATION_ERASURE and SOURCE_POSITION_ERASURE together with the Lean source position it dropped.
loss: DOCUMENTATION_ERASURE. Every `/-- … -/`, `/-! … -/`, `@[inherit_doc]` and `add_decl_doc` is dropped. Acceptable because documentation is not semantic: no Lean term's meaning depends on it, and no LOGOS check consults it. The loss record exists so the erasure is a recorded decision rather than an unnoticed omission, and so a round-trip tool knows it must re-attach documentation from the Lean side rather than expect it back from LOGOS.

SOURCE_POSITION_ERASURE. The same absence of `mdata` (term.rs:443-545) means source positions are gone too, so a LOGOS-side error cannot be pointed at a line of Lean. A translator must keep its OWN name→position map outside the LOGOS artefact; the artefact cannot carry it. This is the practical cost of the erasure, and it is larger than the loss of the prose.

cases.title: Unicode identifiers and `«guillemet names»` — the kernel accepts them, every LOGOS SURFACE does not, and one surface reclassifies them by their first character's case
cases.lean: unicode identifiers (α, β, Γ, ℕ), «guillemet names», subscripts, primes, dotted names
cases.target: `Term::Var(String)` / `Term::Global(String)` (kernel/src/term.rs:449, :452) — the kernel's names are plain Rust `String`s and hold any UTF-8. The degradation is at the three vernacular SURFACES and in the flat namespace, not in the term language.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:449, :452 (`Var(String)` and `Global(String)` — NAMED, not de Bruijn, and `String` is UTF-8, so `α` is a perfectly good kernel name); kernel/src/context.rs:20-80 (every map is keyed by flat `String`: there is no `Name` type, no namespace structure, and no escaping convention — so `Foo.bar` and `Foo_bar` both key to whatever the translator flattens them to, see T02-020); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:89-100 (the script lexer's word rule is `c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '_'`. Rust's `char::is_alphanumeric` IS Unicode-aware, so `α` and `Γ` DO lex as words — but `«`, `»`, `'`, `!`, `?` and every space inside a guillemet name do not, and fall to the `other =>` arm at :101 with `ScriptError("unexpected character …")`); proof/src/formula.rs:158-166 (Surface B's lexer, same rule and the same `unexpected character '{other}'` failure); proof/src/formula.rs:437-445 (`ident_to_term` — THE RECLASSIFICATION: an identifier is a `Constant` iff its first character satisfies `c.is_uppercase() || c.is_ascii_digit()`, otherwise it is a `Variable`. This is `char::is_uppercase`, which is Unicode-aware: `Α` (U+0391 GREEK CAPITAL ALPHA) is uppercase and `α` (U+03B1) is not); base/src/intern.rs:34-39 (`pub struct Symbol(u32)` — the language-side interner is a u32 handle over arbitrary `String`s; interning itself imposes no character restriction)
guards: THE CASE-RECLASSIFICATION TRAP, and the reason this case is not simply "names are strings". On Surface B (`formula.rs:437-445`) an identifier's ROLE is decided by its first character's case: uppercase or digit ⟹ `ProofTerm::Constant`, lowercase ⟹ `ProofTerm::Variable`. Lean's conventional type variables are Greek lowercase — `α`, `β`, `γ` — and `char::is_uppercase('α')` is FALSE, so they become VARIABLES. But `Γ`, `Δ`, `Σ`, equally conventional in Lean for contexts and sums, ARE uppercase and become CONSTANTS. Two names the Lean source treats identically are split into different FOL categories by nothing but their codepoint. Since `assumption` and `exact` compare `ProofExpr`s structurally (proof/src/tactic.rs:363, :380), a `Constant("Γ")` never matches a `Variable("Γ")`, and the resulting failure names a hypothesis rather than a lexical rule. Compare T08-017, where the same `Constant`/`Variable` split bites for a different reason.

Catches guillemet names reaching a surface. `«my theorem»` is a single Lean identifier containing a space. The script lexer (tactic_script.rs:89-101) will lex `my` as a word, `theorem` as another word, and fail on `«` before either. There is no escaping convention in any LOGOS surface, so the only sound handling is to RENAME and record the mapping.

Catches the PRIME. `h'` is overwhelmingly common in Lean (`h`, `h'`, `h''`). The apostrophe is not alphanumeric and is not `_`, so `exact h'` lexes as the atom `exact h` followed by the character `'`, which errors — meaning the script both fails AND, before failing, would have referenced the wrong hypothesis if the lexer had been more permissive. Renaming `h'` to `h_1` is the obvious fix and collides with the name `cases` generates for a conjunct (tactic.rs:516). The renaming scheme must avoid the machine-generated namespace: `h_1`, `h_2`, `h_l`, `h_r`, `h_w`, `W{n}`, `K{n}`, `ih`, `hp{i}`.

Catches Lean's INACCESSIBLE names. A bare `intro` produces `a✝`, and `✝` (U+271D) is not alphanumeric. Those names cannot be referenced from Lean either, but they DO appear in the elaborated `Expr`'s binder names, so a translator that copies binder names through will put a `✝` into a `Term::Var` — legal in the kernel, unusable in any script that must name it. See T08-001.

Catches assuming the kernel is the constraint. It is not: `Term::Var(String)` holds anything. A translator that "fixes" unicode names at the KERNEL level — mangling `α` to `alpha` in emitted terms — has done unnecessary damage and made its output harder to relate to the source, while leaving the actual surface problem unsolved.
oracle: Every name the translator emits into a SCRIPT matches `[A-Za-z0-9_]+` and is not in the machine-generated namespace listed above; the translator publishes a Lean-name → LOGOS-name mapping for every name it renamed; kernel-level `Term::Var` / `Term::Global` names are NOT mangled; and the loss record names SURFACE_LEXICALITY and NAMESPACE_FLATTENING. A harness additionally asserts that no two distinct Lean names map to the same flat LOGOS key.
loss: SURFACE_LEXICALITY. Kernel-level names survive intact. Names that must appear in a SCRIPT — a hypothesis name in `intro h` / `exact h` / `cases h` / `rewrite h`, or a witness in `exists w` — must be `[A-Za-z0-9_]`-shaped plus whatever Unicode letters `is_alphanumeric` admits, and must contain no `«`, `»`, `'`, `?`, `!` or space. Lean names like `h'`, `«my hyp»` and `h✝` therefore have to be RENAMED before they can be referenced from a script, and the renaming must be applied consistently to every later reference.

NAMESPACE_FLATTENING. Lean's hierarchical `Name` becomes a flat `String` key (context.rs:20-80). The separator the translator chooses is a naming convention with no support from LOGOS, and collisions are possible — see T02-011 and T02-020.

cases.title: `run_cmd` and `#eval` of an `IO` action — elaboration-time effects that the LOGOS kernel, which has no IO at all, cannot have
cases.lean: run_cmd, #eval with IO, IO.println, IO.FS.readFile, elaboration-time effects
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term` — thirteen variants, none of which sequences an effect. There is no monadic bind, no `IO`, no world token, and `Term::Let` (term.rs:471) is a pure zeta-transparent binding, not a `do`-step); kernel/src/prelude.rs (the registered inductives and axioms — `Entity`, `Int`, `Float`, `Text`, `Duration`, `Date`, `Moment`, `Nat`, `EList`, `Bool`, `TList`, `True`, `False`, `Decidable`, `Eq`, `Acc`, `And`, `Or`, `Ex`, the quotient primitives, the `Int` ring and order axioms, and `reduceBool`/`ofReduceBool`. There is no `IO`, no `Monad`, no `Bind`, and no `PUnit`/`RealWorld`); kernel/src/prelude.rs:1195-1219 (`reduceBool : Bool → Bool` with `ofReduceBool` — the ONE place LOGOS deliberately wires an evaluator into kernel reduction (reduction.rs:109-115). It is Lean's `native_decide` pair, it is gated to `Bool`, and it is pure: it is NOT an escape hatch for effects. See T06-014); the crate invariants recorded in the repo's own guide — `logicaffeine_kernel` is "Pure CoC type theory — NO LEXICON (Milner invariant)" and `logicaffeine_data` is "WASM-safe data structures + CRDTs — NO IO (Lamport invariant)"; IO lives only in `logicaffeine_system`, which the kernel does not depend on; kernel/src/context.rs:20-80 (`Context` — no effect log, no output buffer; see T09-007 on the absence of any mutable environment state)
guards: THE EFFECT-IS-NOT-A-VALUE TRAP. `#eval (IO.println "hi")` elaborates to a term of type `IO Unit` and then RUNS it. A translator that stops at "it is a term, terms translate" will emit something for the `IO Unit` value — at best an opaque `add_declaration` of a type LOGOS has no inductive for, at worst a definition whose body is a partially-translated monadic chain. Neither records that the source file printed something, read a file, or changed the world. The verdict is `reject` because a translation that silently drops an effect is a translation that claims the source did less than it did.

Catches `run_cmd` that GENERATES DECLARATIONS. This is the important sub-case and the exact mirror of T09-004: `run_cmd elabCommand (← `(def generated : Nat := 5))` is an effect whose visible consequence is an ordinary `def`. The effect is rejected; the `def` it produced is in the environment and must be translated. A translator that refuses the whole file because it saw a `run_cmd` will drop declarations that are perfectly translatable — including, in real Lean, whole families of generated lemmas.

Catches `reduceBool` being read as an IO escape hatch. `reduceBool` runs the CBV evaluator inside kernel reduction (prelude.rs:1195-1219, reduction.rs:109-115) and is the closest LOGOS comes to "running code during checking". It is pure, it is `Bool`-only, and its TCB story is already a degrade of its own (T06-014). Routing an `IO` action through it — encoding a print as a `Bool` computation, say — puts arbitrary evaluation into the kernel's trusted reduction path under a type that claims it is a decision procedure.

Catches NON-DETERMINISM. `IO.FS.readFile` makes the elaborated environment depend on the filesystem, so the same Lean source produces different declarations on different machines. A translator's output would then not be a function of its input, which breaks the one property a conformance corpus needs. The rejection must fire even when the effect looks harmless.

Catches `do` notation generally. Lean's `do` block desugars to `bind`/`pure` applications, and LOGOS has no `Monad`, no `Bind` and no `IO` (see T05-019 and T05-020). A translator that handles `IO` specially but lets other monads through will emit `bind` applications against globals that do not exist.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_ELABORATION_TIME_EFFECT for every `run_cmd` and for every `#eval` of an `IO`-typed term below, emits nothing for them, and DOES emit a correct LOGOS declaration for `generatedByRunCmd` and for the pure declarations. A harness additionally asserts that no emitted `Term::Global` names `IO`, `bind`, `pure` or any other monadic operation, and that no `add_declaration` introduces a type not registered by `StandardLibrary::register`.
diag: E_ELABORATION_TIME_EFFECT — must name the command, state that it performs `IO` during elaboration, and state that the LOGOS kernel has no IO and no monadic structure, so the effect has no representation at any stage. Must emit no declaration. If the effect PRODUCED declarations (a `run_cmd` that elaborates commands), those declarations are ordinary and translate — the same nuance as T09-004 and T09-006.
note: `import Lean` (core, not Mathlib) is required for `run_cmd`; see the @note on T09-004 about the metadata block's position. The `run_cmd` and `#eval`s below print during compilation — that output is expected and is not a warning.

A declaration created by `run_cmd elabCommand` is NOT visible to later commands in the same Lean 4.14 file (its elaboration is asynchronous, and a reference to the new name reports "unknown identifier"). The declaration-generating `run_cmd` below therefore emits a name nothing references, and the declaration it stands for is written out by hand as `generatedByRunCmd`. The case is unaffected: the point is that the EFFECT is rejected while the declaration it produces is ordinary — and the visibility rule is itself a consequence of the same import-time/elaboration-time staging that makes T09-007's `initialize` unrepresentable.

cases.title: Macro expansion ORDERING — the integration case for the whole tier: read the post-elaboration `Expr` and the order stops existing
cases.lean: interleaved notation/macro_rules/infix, redefinition, scoped and local macros, expansion order vs. elaboration order
cases.target: The translation of the final elaborated `Expr` for each declaration. Every command that only extends the PARSER — `notation`, `infixl`/`infixr`/`prefix`/`postfix`, `macro`, `macro_rules`, `syntax` — produces NO LOGOS declaration.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term` — no `Syntax`, no expansion record, no ordering information: two declarations whose surface forms expanded differently are simply two different terms, with nothing marking why); kernel/src/context.rs:20-80 (`Context` — flat maps, populated by a LINEAR sequence of `add_*` calls. There is no notion of "this declaration was elaborated under that notation scope", and no re-elaboration); kernel/src/context.rs:449 (`get_global` — lookup precedence is inductives, constructors, definitions, declarations: a fixed order over a flat namespace, nothing to do with source order); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:1030-1050 (`elaborate_app` — LOGOS elaboration consumes and produces `Term`; there is no surface stage for an ordering to matter in); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:250-260 (the ONE place LOGOS has expansion ordering at all: a user-defined tactic takes PRECEDENCE over a built-in alias and is expanded in place, depth-bounded at 128 (:133). That is a textual tactic macro, and its ordering rule — "an explicit `define` is authoritative, so a user tactic may even shadow a built-in alias" — is LOGOS's own, unrelated to Lean's)
guards: THE TIER'S GOVERNING RULE, stated as its own case: **translate the post-elaboration `Expr`, never the surface `Syntax`.** Every expansion-ordering question in this file — which `macro_rules` alternative wins, whether an `infixr` regroups, whether a `local` notation is in scope, whether a redefinition shadows — is a question about Lean's parser and macro expander. A translator that reads `Expr` never asks any of them. A translator that reads `Syntax` must answer all of them correctly, and every wrong answer produces a well-typed LOGOS term that means something else. This case exists so a conformance report can state which kind of translator is under test.

Catches LATER-BLOCK-WINS. A second `macro_rules` for the same syntax PREPENDS its alternatives, so the later block is tried FIRST. A translator that expands alternatives in source order gets the opposite answer. `laterWins` below is the witness, and it is a plain `Nat` equation, so the wrong answer is not a type error.

Catches REBINDING of a token. `firstMeaning` and `redefinedMeaning` below use the SAME token `⊞` and elaborate to `op` and to `alt` respectively, because each sits in a section with its own `local notation`. In the `Expr` this is simply two different globals with nothing recording the token; in `Syntax` it is a scoping question whose answer depends on where in the file each use sits. (Two notations for one token at the SAME scope level do not shadow in Lean 4 — they overload, and a use is then rejected as "ambiguous, possible interpretations"; the sectioned form above is how a real file rebinds a token, and it is what the translator will actually meet.)

Catches SCOPE. `local notation` inside a `section` is out of scope after `end`, and `scoped notation` inside a `namespace` requires `open`. Neither affects the `Expr` of anything already elaborated. A translator that models notation scope will get it subtly wrong at the `open` boundary; one that reads `Expr` has nothing to model.

Catches ELABORATION order being confused with EXPANSION order. Macros expand during parsing; elaboration happens afterwards and may postpone (instance resolution, `OfNat` literals, coercions — see T05-015, T05-017, T05-011). Two declarations can expand identically and elaborate differently because of a `variable` or an `open` between them. The `Expr` is the only artefact that records the outcome of BOTH stages, which is why it and not the expansion is the translation input.

Catches emitting anything for the parser-extension commands. Each `notation`, `infixl`, `macro` and `syntax` below must produce ZERO LOGOS declarations — see T09-001, T09-002, T09-003. A translator that emits a placeholder per command will produce as many phantom globals as there are notations in the file, in a flat namespace where any of them can collide (T02-020).
oracle: The translator emits declarations for exactly `op`, `alt`, `usesVariable` and the eight theorems below — and for nothing else. For each theorem, the emitted LOGOS term is `types_equal` to the translation of the hand-expanded form given in the same theorem's right-hand side. A harness additionally asserts that the number of emitted declarations is unchanged when every `notation`/`macro`/`infix` command in the file is replaced by its expansion at each use site.

cases.title: Custom BINDER notation — `extBinder`, `binder_predicate` and `∀ x > 0, …` expand to binder structure no LOGOS surface can introduce
cases.lean: notation3-style binders, extBinder, binder_predicate, ∀ x > 0 / ∃ x ∈ s, bounded quantifiers, Σ/Π-style user binders
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:463, :467 (`Pi { param, param_type, body_type }` and `Lambda { param, param_type, body }` — the ONLY binders in the kernel term language. Each binds exactly one NAMED variable with one type, and there is no binder annotation, no telescope form, and no predicate slot); kernel/src/context.rs:201 (`set_binder_kinds` — the only per-binder metadata LOGOS records, and it stores `ParamKind::{Explicit, Implicit, Instance}` (elaborate.rs:1016-1027): three values, none of which encodes a bound); kernel/src/prelude.rs (`Ex`/`witness` — the existential is a `Prop`-valued inductive over a predicate; there is no bounded-existential form and no `∃ x ∈ s`); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:276, :310 (the script's ONLY binder-introducing atom is `intro <name>` — one name, no type, no bound. `ProofState::intro` (proof/src/tactic.rs:313-356) handles `Implies` and `ForAll` and nothing else); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:280 (`exists` takes one bare word wrapped in `ProofTerm::Constant` — so the existential side has no bound either, see T08-017); proof/src/formula.rs (Surface B's formula grammar — `for all`/`∀` and `there exists`/`∃` over a BARE IDENTIFIER, with `parse_term` accepting only an identifier at :427-432: a bounded binder cannot be written); kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:1223-1270 and LOGOS_FACTS §Surface C (the literate `Statement:` grammar has NO `forall` at all — free variables are universally closed implicitly, so there is nowhere to attach a bound)
guards: THE "IT DESUGARS, SO IT TRANSLATES" TRAP. `∀ x > 0, p x` desugars to `∀ x, x > 0 → p x`, which is an ordinary `Pi` over an ordinary implication and DOES translate as a TERM. So a translator reading the elaborated `Expr` will handle the quantified statement fine — and that is correct, and is why this case is about the NOTATION rather than the proposition. What is rejected is the `binder_predicate` / `extBinder` declaration itself, which extends Lean's binder parser: it produces no `Expr`, it has no LOGOS counterpart, and a translator that emits anything for it puts a phantom name into the flat global namespace (T02-020).

Catches the PROOF-SIDE consequence, which is the part that actually breaks. A term may desugar, but a SCRIPT that proves it cannot. `∀ x > 0, p x` desugars to a `Pi` whose body is an implication, so proving it needs `intro x . intro hx` — TWO atoms where the Lean source wrote one binder — and the translator must synthesise the second name, ensure it does not collide with LOGOS's machine-generated namespace (`h_1`, `h_2`, `h_l`, `h_r`, `h_w`, `W{n}`, `K{n}`, `ih`, `hp{i}`), and rewrite every downstream reference. On the existential side it is worse: `∃ x > 0, p x` desugars to `∃ x, x > 0 ∧ p x`, so `exists w` must be followed by a `split`, and LOGOS's `exists` takes a bare `Constant` witness that a bound may not even be stateable about (T08-017).

Catches `∃ x ∈ s, …`. It desugars to `∃ x, x ∈ s ∧ …`, and LOGOS has no `Membership` class, no `Set`, and no `List` in its prelude (T10-012, T10-013). So the desugared form mentions a global that does not exist, and the failure surfaces as an unbound name rather than as "this binder notation is unsupported".

Catches BINDER TELESCOPES introduced by one notation. `notation3`-style binders can bind several variables with one token; `Term::Pi` binds exactly one (term.rs:463). The expansion is a nested telescope, which is fine as a term — and which, per T00-021 and T11-007, makes LOGOS's named, capture-avoiding substitution quadratic in the telescope depth. A translator that generates deep telescopes from compact binder notations should record that cost.

Catches the Surface-B and Surface-C dead ends specifically. Surface B's `∀`/`∃` range over a bare identifier with no domain (formula.rs:427-432), and Surface C has no `forall` in its `Statement:` grammar at all. So a bounded quantifier has no spelling on EITHER of the two surfaces that can state a quantified proposition, and the only route is the kernel term language via the Rust API — where the desugared form works and the notation still does not exist.

Catches over-rejecting the desugared THEOREM. `boundedForallDesugared` and `boundedExistsDesugared` below are ordinary Lean with no custom notation, and must translate. The diagnostic must fire on the notation declaration, not on every theorem whose statement happens to contain a bounded quantifier.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NO_CUSTOM_BINDER for the `binder_predicate` and custom-binder `notation` declarations below, emits nothing for them, and DOES emit correct LOGOS declarations for every theorem — including the ones written with the custom binders, whose elaborated `Expr`s are ordinary. For each such theorem the emitted script introduces one `intro` atom per DESUGARED binder, and the harness asserts none of the synthesised names lies in LOGOS's machine-generated namespace.
diag: E_NO_CUSTOM_BINDER — must name the binder notation, report the binder variable and the predicate or domain it carries, and state that LOGOS's only binders are `Term::Pi` and `Term::Lambda` over one named variable and one type, with the script surface offering only nullary `intro`. Must emit nothing for the notation.
note: `binder_predicate` IS a core Lean 4.14 command and is exercised live below. Mathlib's `notation3`, the other standard way to declare a custom binder, is NOT available in bare Lean 4.14 ("unexpected identifier; expected 'binder_predicate', …"); it is named in a comment and its desugared output is written out, exactly as T08-015 and T08-016 do for Mathlib tactics. The rejection covers both spellings.

cases.title: Small `Nat` literal — `Literal::Nat(BigInt)`, not `Literal::Int(i64)`
cases.lean: Nat numeric literal, OfNat.ofNat, Nat.zero, Nat.succ
cases.target: Term::Lit(Literal::Nat(BigInt::from_i64(n)))
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:38-44 (`Literal::Nat(BigInt)` — "a compact, accelerated form of the unary Peano numeral `Succ^n Zero`"); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:302 (`Literal::Nat(_) => Ok(Term::Global("Nat"))` — a `Nat` literal's inferred type is the inductive `Nat`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:296 (`Literal::Int(_) | Literal::BigInt(_) => Ok(Term::Global("Int"))` — the OTHER literal family infers `Int`, a DIFFERENT type); kernel/src/prelude.rs:529-552 (`register_nat`: `Nat : Type 0` is an inductive with constructors `Zero` and `Succ : Nat → Nat`); kernel/src/reduction.rs:330-345 (`extract_constructor`'s Peano bridge makes `Lit(Nat(n))` constructor-form so `Match` computes on it)
guards: Catches the single most tempting literal bug in the tier: emitting a Lean `Nat` literal as `Literal::Int(n)` because the value fits an `i64` and `Int` is "the integer literal". `infer_type` then reports `Int` (type_checker.rs:296), not `Nat`. `Int` is an OPAQUE inductive with ZERO constructors (prelude.rs:354), so the emitted term can never be matched on, `extract_constructor` returns `None` for it, and every downstream `Match`/recursor over what the Lean source called a `Nat` is stuck. Worse, it is stuck *silently*: `normalize` returns the un-reduced redex rather than erroring (reduction.rs:52-69), so a proof by `rfl` degenerates to a definitional-equality failure at a site far from the literal.

Catches the inverse: emitting a Lean `Int` literal as `Literal::Nat`. A negative `Literal::Nat` is rejected outright by `infer_type` (type_checker.rs:297-301), but a NON-negative `Int` literal mis-emitted as `Nat` typechecks fine and then silently acquires Peano computation it should not have — `mod 4 2` on it will not reduce via the `Int` primitive hook (reduction.rs:444-466) because the operands are the wrong `Literal` variant, and `add`/`mul` become stuck applications of an axiom.

Catches carrying the literal as a spelled-out `Succ (Succ … Zero)` term. That is *definitionally* correct (term.rs:38-44) but is `n` heap nodes; a literal such as `1000000` emitted this way exceeds `normalize`'s 10000-step fuel (reduction.rs:52-69) during any comparison and the kernel then silently answers with a partially reduced term. The accelerated literal exists precisely to avoid this.

Catches assuming Lean's `OfNat` elaboration survives. `(5 : Nat)` is `@OfNat.ofNat Nat 5 (instOfNatNat 5)` in the elaborated `Expr`; the translator must see through the instance to the raw `Nat.lit`, not emit an application of a `OfNat_ofNat` global that LOGOS does not have. See T10-014.
oracle: For each declaration below, the emitted term is `Term::Lit(Literal::Nat(v))` with `v` the source value, and LOGOS `infer_type` returns `Term::Global("Nat")`. A harness additionally asserts that NO `Literal::Int` appears anywhere in the output for this file, and that `def_eq(emitted(3), Succ (Succ (Succ Zero)))` holds.

cases.title: `Nat` literal beyond `i64` — the `BigInt` path and its canonicalisation invariant
cases.lean: Nat literal exceeding 2^63-1, Nat.pow, large numeral elaboration
cases.target: Term::Lit(Literal::Nat(BigInt)) — `Literal::Nat` ALWAYS carries a `BigInt`, so the small and large cases are the same constructor and no widening decision arises
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:38-44 (`Nat(BigInt)` — one arm, arbitrary precision, "the value is non-negative"); kernel/src/term.rs:26-35 (`BigInt` is a PARALLEL *integer* representation and is CANONICAL: "it holds only values `to_i64()` cannot, so every integer has a unique `Literal` … and definitional equality stays sound"); kernel/src/term.rs:50-55 (`int_lit` is the ONLY sanctioned way to build an INTEGER literal from a `BigInt`, demoting to `Int(i64)` when it fits); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1485 (`(Lit(Nat(x)), Lit(Nat(y))) => x == y` — two `Nat` literals are definitionally equal iff their `BigInt`s compare equal); base/src/numeric.rs:354-375 (`BigInt::div_rem`, and the limb representation the comparison runs over)
guards: Catches the canonicalisation bug that breaks definitional equality. For INTEGERS the kernel has two representations — `Literal::Int(i64)` and `Literal::BigInt` — and the soundness of literal `def_eq` rests on `int_lit`'s invariant that a value fitting an `i64` is NEVER stored as a `BigInt` (term.rs:26-35, :50-55). A translator that emits `Literal::BigInt(BigInt::from_i64(3))` for a small `Int` produces a term that is *not* `PartialEq`-equal to `Literal::Int(3)`; `def_eq_normalized`'s literal arms compare by `==` on the `Literal` (type_checker.rs:1485 for `Nat`), so `3` fails to equal `3`. The symptom is an unprovable `rfl` with two identical-looking printouts.

Catches the truncating emitter. Reading a Lean `Nat` literal through `u64`/`i64` and then calling `BigInt::from_i64` silently wraps for any value ≥ 2^63. The resulting term still typechecks (`infer_type` returns `Nat` for any non-negative `Nat` literal, type_checker.rs:302) and still computes — at the WRONG value. Nothing in the kernel can detect it; the translator must read Lean's literal as arbitrary precision end to end.

Catches emitting a negative value into `Literal::Nat`. `infer_type` rejects it (type_checker.rs:297-301), but the more dangerous path is `extract_constructor`, which clamps a negative `Nat(n)` to `Zero` so the `Succ`-peel terminates rather than descending toward −∞ (reduction.rs:337-341). A mis-signed literal therefore does not crash — it silently *computes as zero* inside a `Match`.

Catches "just spell it in Peano". `Succ^n Zero` for `n = 2^64` is not representable at all; even the fuel-bounded normaliser (10000 steps, reduction.rs:52-69) cannot peel it. The accelerated literal is mandatory above a few thousand.
oracle: The emitted `Literal::Nat` payload equals the source value compared as an arbitrary-precision decimal string (not as `i64`), and `infer_type` returns `Global("Nat")`. A harness additionally asserts the `int_lit` invariant over the whole corpus: no emitted `Literal::BigInt` has a `to_i64()` that is `Some`.

cases.title: Negative `Int` literal — `int_lit` canonicalisation and the `negSucc` encoding gap
cases.lean: Int numeric literal, Neg.neg on Int, Int.negSucc, Int.ofNat
cases.target: Term::Lit(int_lit(BigInt)) — i.e. `Literal::Int(n)` when `n` fits an `i64`, else `Literal::BigInt(n)`; type `Global("Int")`
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:50-55 (`int_lit`: `match n.to_i64() { Some(x) => Literal::Int(x), None => Literal::BigInt(n) }`); kernel/src/term.rs:26-35 (the canonicality invariant — one `Literal` per integer value, "so … definitional equality stays sound"); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:296 (`Literal::Int(_) | Literal::BigInt(_)` both infer `Global("Int")`); kernel/src/prelude.rs:354 (`ctx.add_inductive("Int", Sort(Type 0))` — `Int` is an inductive with NO constructors, i.e. opaque); kernel/src/reduction.rs:474-506 (the `Int` primitive reduction hook: literal operands only, `i64` fast path then exact `BigInt` path, result re-canonicalised through `int_lit` at :499)
guards: Catches emitting Lean's *constructor* encoding. Lean's `Int` is a two-constructor inductive `ofNat : Nat → Int` / `negSucc : Nat → Int`, and `(-5 : Int)` elaborates to `Int.negSucc 4`. A structurally faithful translator emits `App(Global("Int_negSucc"), Lit(Nat(4)))`. That compiles — `add_inductive` and `add_constructor` are UNCHECKED (context.rs:253, :419), so nothing stops you declaring `Int_negSucc` — but it is now a DIFFERENT `Int` from the prelude's, which is opaque and zero-constructor. The eight ring axioms and eight order axioms (prelude.rs:92-340) are all stated about the prelude's `Int`, so none of them apply to the shadow type, and the primitive reduction hook (reduction.rs:474-506) fires only on `Term::Lit` operands, so `add (Int_negSucc 4) (Int_ofNat 7)` never computes. The translation typechecks and proves nothing.

Catches the sign dropped at the literal boundary. Lean prints `-5` as a single token but its `Expr` is `Neg.neg (OfNat.ofNat 5)`; a translator that lowers `OfNat.ofNat 5` and then fails to see the enclosing `Neg.neg` emits `Literal::Int(5)`. The term still has type `Int` and still reduces, so every downstream arithmetic fact is off by a sign with no diagnostic anywhere.

Catches breaking `int_lit`'s canonicality in the negative direction. `i64::MIN` (−9223372036854775808) fits an `i64`, so it MUST be `Literal::Int`, while `−9223372036854775809` must be `Literal::BigInt`. An emitter that negates after demoting, or that routes every negative through the wide form, produces two distinct `Literal`s for one value and definitional equality of literals — which is settled by `==` on the `Literal` — silently fails.

Catches assuming `Int` literals behave like `Nat` literals. There is NO Peano bridge for `Int`: `extract_constructor` bridges only `Literal::Nat` (reduction.rs:330-345). An `Int` literal is never constructor-form, so it can never be a `Match` scrutinee. Any Lean proof that case-splits on `Int` must be rejected, not silently re-encoded.
oracle: The emitted term is `Term::Lit` with the `int_lit`-canonical payload for the source value, `infer_type` returns `Global("Int")`, and the emitted term contains no `Int_negSucc`/`Int_ofNat` global. A harness asserts `normalize(add (-5) 3)` reduces to `Lit(Int(-2))`.

cases.title: `Nat`/`Int` conflation — LOGOS's `Nat` is an INDUCTIVE, its `Int` is OPAQUE, and the two compute by completely different mechanisms
cases.lean: Nat, Int, Int.ofNat coercion (↑), Nat.cast, Int.toNat, Int.natAbs
cases.target: (none — no sound translation of a term that treats the two as one type)
evidence: kernel/src/prelude.rs:529-552 (`register_nat`: `Nat : Type 0` inductive, constructors `Zero : Nat` and `Succ : Nat → Nat` — a genuine Peano inductive that `Match` eliminates); kernel/src/prelude.rs:354 (`ctx.add_inductive("Int", Sort(Type 0))` with NO `add_constructor` call anywhere for it — an inductive of arity 0 and zero constructors, i.e. an opaque carrier); kernel/src/prelude.rs:363-381 (`add`, `sub`, `mul`, `div`, `mod` are `add_declaration`s of type `Int → Int → Int` — AXIOMS, not definitions, and there is no `Nat` counterpart anywhere in the prelude); kernel/src/prelude.rs:92-191 (8 ring axioms, all about `Int`); kernel/src/prelude.rs:202-340 (8 order axioms, all about `Int`); kernel/src/reduction.rs:444-506 (`try_primitive_reduce`: `Int` arithmetic computes by a PRIMITIVE HOOK on `Term::Lit` operands); kernel/src/reduction.rs:330-345 (`Nat` computes by the Peano bridge in `extract_constructor`, i.e. by ι-reduction); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:296-302 (`Literal::Int`/`BigInt` infer `Int`; `Literal::Nat` infers `Nat` — two different globals)
guards: THIS IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE REJECTION IN TIER 10. The tempting wrong move is to notice that LOGOS's *arithmetic* lives on `Int` — `add`/`sub`/`mul` are `Int → Int → Int` and there is literally no `Nat` addition in the prelude — and therefore to translate every Lean `Nat` as LOGOS `Int`. That compiles, reduces, and gives the right answers on every non-negative example, which is exactly what makes it lethal: it is wrong precisely at `Nat` subtraction (see T10-017), where Lean truncates at zero and LOGOS's `sub` goes negative, and at induction, where the Lean source's `Nat.rec`/`match` has no LOGOS counterpart on a zero-constructor type.

Catches the mirror move: translating Lean `Int` as LOGOS `Nat` because "the literal bridge is nicer". A negative `Literal::Nat` is refused by `infer_type` (type_checker.rs:297-301) — but only when it is a *literal*. A computed negative value flows into `extract_constructor`, which CLAMPS it to `Zero` so the `Succ`-peel terminates (reduction.rs:337-341). So `-1` silently becomes `0` inside a `Match`, with no error at any point.

Catches translating Lean's coercion `↑n : Int` as the identity. Because the two LOGOS types are distinct globals, the identity is ill-typed and would be caught — UNLESS the translator has already conflated them, in which case the coercion disappears and with it every proof obligation the coercion carried (`Int.toNat_of_nonneg` and friends). The coercion needs a genuine emitted function, and there is no `Nat → Int` primitive in the prelude to build it from.

Catches the "both are literals, so both are `Literal`" reasoning. They are different `Literal` VARIANTS with different typing rules (type_checker.rs:296 vs :302) and different reduction mechanisms: `Literal::Nat` participates in ι-reduction via the Peano bridge and is NOT accepted by `try_primitive_reduce` (which matches only `Literal::Int`/`BigInt`, reduction.rs:459-500); `Literal::Int` participates in the primitive hook and is NOT constructor-form. A term mixing them is stuck in both directions at once and `normalize` reports that as "already normal".
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NAT_INT_DISTINCT for every declaration below and emits no LOGOS output. A harness additionally asserts, over the whole corpus, that no emitted term applies `Global("add")`/`"sub"`/`"mul"`/`"div"`/`"mod"` to a subterm whose inferred type is `Global("Nat")`.
diag: E_NAT_INT_DISTINCT — must name both LOGOS types, state that `Nat` is a two- constructor inductive whose arithmetic must be emitted as `Fix`/`Match` recursion while `Int` is a zero-constructor opaque carrier whose arithmetic is an axiom with a reduction hook, and refuse to identify them. Must NOT offer a coercion.

cases.title: `String` literal — `Literal::Text` carries the bytes and nothing else
cases.lean: String literal, Expr.lit (Literal.strVal), String.mk, List Char
cases.target: Term::Lit(Literal::Text(s)) of type `Global("Text")`
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:19-20 (`Literal::Text(String)` — "UTF-8 string"); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:304 (`Literal::Text(_) => Ok(Global("Text"))`); kernel/src/prelude.rs:356 (`ctx.add_inductive("Text", Sort(Type 0))` — an inductive with ZERO constructors, so `Text` is opaque and cannot be matched on); kernel/src/prelude.rs:352-381 (`register_primitives` declares arithmetic and comparison builtins for `Int` and temporal operations for `Duration`/`Date`/`Moment` — and NOTHING for `Text`); a grep of `crates/logicaffeine_kernel/src/prelude.rs` for `Text` returns only the registration at :356 and its use as the payload type of the reflection constructor `SName` at :2151-2152; kernel/src/reduction.rs:444-506 (`try_primitive_reduce` handles `add/sub/mul/div/mod/le/lt/ge/gt` only — no string operation reduces)
guards: Catches the translator that declares a fresh `String` inductive over an invented `Char` and emits the literal as a spelled-out `Cons c1 (Cons c2 …)`. That typechecks (`add_inductive`/`add_constructor` are UNCHECKED, context.rs:253/:419), but the emitted type is NOT `Text`, so it shares nothing with the prelude, and a literal of any realistic length blows past `normalize`'s 10000-step fuel (reduction.rs:52-69) during comparison — at which point the kernel returns the PARTIALLY reduced term and reports no error, so a disequality can be "proved" by two strings agreeing on their first few thousand steps. See T11-005.

Catches dropping the loss record because "the literal round-trips". It does round-trip; what is lost is every THEOREM about it. A Lean file that proves `"ab".length = 2` must not be reported as translated.

Catches confusing `Text` with the reflection layer. The only other use of `Text` in the kernel is as the payload of `SName : Text → Syntax` (prelude.rs:2151-2152), the name tag of LOGOS's own reified-syntax inductive. A translator that maps Lean `String` onto `SName`'s argument position, or that reuses `Syntax`'s machinery because it is "the thing that handles strings", has attached the user's data to the kernel's metaprogramming representation — where `try_syn_arith_reduce` (reduction.rs:1174-1280) will happily reduce it as if it were a syntax node.

Catches escaping/encoding drift. `Literal::Text` holds a Rust `String`, i.e. valid UTF-8; Lean's `String` is also UTF-8, so the value maps across, but the translator must emit the DECODED characters, not Lean's source-level escape sequence. `"
"` must become a one-byte `Text`, not a two-character one — and since `def_eq` on literals is `==` on the payload, getting this wrong makes `"
" = "
"` fail whenever the two occurrences were spelled differently in the source.
oracle: Emitted term is `Lit(Text(s))` with `s` byte-identical to Lean's decoded literal; `infer_type` returns `Global("Text")`; and the loss record contains STRING_IS_AN_ATOM. A harness asserts that no declaration in the output applies any global to a `Text`-typed argument other than equality.
loss: STRING_IS_AN_ATOM. Lean's `String` is a STRUCTURE wrapping `List Char` (`String.mk : List Char → String`), and every string function in Lean core is defined by recursion over that list; `String` literals are definitionally equal to their `String.mk` spelling and `decide` can compute over them. LOGOS's `Text` is an opaque carrier with a literal injection and no eliminator at all. The translation therefore keeps the VALUE of each literal and loses (a) the character-list structure, (b) every equation about it, and (c) any ability to compute. Two `Text` literals can still be compared by `def_eq` (structural `==` on the `Literal`), so literal equality and disequality survive — that is the entire residual semantics.

NO_CHAR_LAYER. Because `Char` is absent from LOGOS entirely (T10-006), the loss is not recoverable by "just declaring `String` as a list of characters": the element type does not exist and `Char`'s validity invariant is a `UInt32` predicate, and `UInt32` is absent too (T10-009).

cases.title: `Char` — absent from LOGOS, and not reconstructible because its invariant needs `UInt32`
cases.lean: Char, character literal 'a', Char.ofNat, Char.val, Char.valid, Char.isValidCharNat
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/prelude.rs:18-51 (`StandardLibrary::register` — the complete registration list; no `Char` anywhere); kernel/src/prelude.rs:352-381 (`register_primitives` registers exactly `Int`, `Float`, `Text`, `Duration`, `Date`, `Moment` as opaque types — no character type); kernel/src/term.rs:13-44 (the complete `Literal` enum: `Int`, `Float`, `Text`, `Duration`, `Date`, `Moment`, `BigInt`, `Nat` — there is NO character literal variant, so a `Char` cannot even be *injected*); kernel/src/context.rs:271-300 (`add_structure` hard-codes the structure's sort to `Type 0`, and it takes `fields` as plain types — there is no facility for a field whose type is a PROOF about an earlier field, which is exactly what Lean's `Char` needs)
guards: Catches the "a `Char` is just a `Nat`" re-encoding. Emitting `'a'` as `Lit(Nat(97))` typechecks and even computes (the Peano bridge makes it constructor-form, reduction.rs:330-345). It is wrong in two ways that no LOGOS check can see. First, it DROPS THE VALIDITY INVARIANT: Lean's `Char` is a subtype carrying a proof that the code point is a scalar value, so `Char.ofNat 0xD800` is NOT the surrogate — Lean replaces it with `'\0'` — while the `Nat` encoding happily represents it. Second, it makes `Char` and `Nat` the SAME LOGOS type, so a Lean function `Nat → Char` becomes `Nat → Nat` and every use site typechecks even when the arguments are swapped.

Catches encoding `Char` as a one-character `Text`. `Text` is opaque with zero constructors (prelude.rs:356) and has no operations at all (see T10-005), so the encoding is a dead end: `Char.val`, `Char.toNat` and every ordering fact about characters become unstatable, and the translator has quietly turned a decidable type into an atom while reporting success.

Catches the translator that reaches this case only through `String`. Almost no real Lean source mentions `Char` directly; it arrives via `String.data`, `String.toList`, `String.any`, `String.map` or a `for c in s` loop. The rejection must fire on the elaborated `Expr`, where `Char` appears as a constant, not on the surface syntax.

Catches the scale error in the other direction from T06-009: rejecting `Char` is cheap for mathematical Lean and fatal for anything that manipulates text. A translator must report which of the two kinds of input it is looking at, rather than degrading `Char` to keep a success rate up.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_TYPE_ABSENT_FROM_TARGET(Char) for every declaration below, performs zero `add_inductive`/`add_structure` calls, and emits no `Literal` for a character. A harness asserts that `"Char"` never appears as a LOGOS global name anywhere in the corpus output.
diag: E_TYPE_ABSENT_FROM_TARGET(Char) — must name `Char`, state that LOGOS has neither the type nor a character `Literal` variant, and state that the natural encoding (`{ val : UInt32 // val.isValidChar }`) is blocked twice over: `UInt32` is also absent (T10-009) and `Subtype` is also absent (T10-013). Must NOT silently re-encode `Char` as `Nat`.

cases.title: `Float` — the type and the literal exist in LOGOS, and nothing else does
cases.lean: Float, float literal, Float.add / Float.mul, OfScientific, Float.ofNat
cases.target: Term::Lit(Literal::Float(f64)) of type `Global("Float")` — and NO operation
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:17-18 (`Literal::Float(f64)`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:303 (`Literal::Float(_) => Ok(Global("Float"))`); kernel/src/prelude.rs:355 (`ctx.add_inductive("Float", Sort(Type 0))` — a zero- constructor opaque carrier); kernel/src/prelude.rs:363-381 (`register_primitives` declares `add`/`sub`/`mul`/`div`/`mod` at type `Int → Int → Int` and `le`/`lt`/`ge`/`gt` at `Int → Int → Bool` — every one of them is an `Int` operation, NONE is `Float`); kernel/src/prelude.rs:92-340 (the 16 axioms are all about `Int`; there is no `Float` axiom); kernel/src/reduction.rs:444-506 (`try_primitive_reduce` matches `Literal::Int`/`Literal::BigInt` operands only via `lit_bigint`, term.rs:59-63, which returns `None` for `Literal::Float` — so no `Float` expression ever reduces)
guards: Catches the translator that reuses the `Int` primitives for `Float` because their names look generic. `add : Int → Int → Int` (prelude.rs:377) applied to a `Float` is ILL-TYPED and will be caught — but only if the translator does not ALSO emit a coercion or leave a `Term::Hole` in the argument position, because `types_equal` treats `Hole` as matching anything (type_checker.rs:1594-1597) and that leniency leaks into `is_subtype`'s fast path (:1314). With one `Hole`, `add (1.5 : Float) 2` typechecks. See T11-004.

Catches declaring the `Float` operations as fresh axioms to "fill the gap". That is worse than rejecting: the emitted `Float_add` has no reduction rule, so nothing about it computes, AND it has no laws, so nothing about it is provable — yet the translation reports success and the resulting library contains theorems whose proofs are stuck applications. It also enlarges the trusted base, which `certificate::recheck` rebuilds from `StandardLibrary::register` alone (certificate.rs:63-75), so the certificate will fail with an unbound-variable error that reads like a name-resolution bug. Compare T06-009.

Catches silently rounding the literal. Lean's float literals go through `OfScientific`, so `0.1` is a decimal mantissa/exponent pair that Lean resolves to a specific `f64`. The translator must emit the SAME `f64` bit pattern, not re-parse the decimal with different rounding — because literal equality is bitwise-ish `==` and a one-ulp difference makes two occurrences of `0.1` unequal.

Catches assuming Lean can compute with floats in proofs either. Lean's `Float` operations are `@[extern]` opaque constants, so `rfl` does not prove `1.5 + 2.5 = 4.0` in Lean any more than in LOGOS. The degrade record must say what is *additionally* lost — the operations themselves, and `native_decide`'s ability to evaluate them.
oracle: Emitted term for a float literal is `Lit(Float(f))` with `f` bit-identical to Lean's elaborated `f64`; `infer_type` returns `Global("Float")`; the loss record contains FLOAT_IS_INERT; and the translator performs ZERO `add_declaration` calls introducing a `Float` operation.
loss: FLOAT_IS_INERT. The type exists and literals inject into it, so a `Float`-typed signature survives translation and `Float` values can be passed around and compared for literal identity. Everything else is gone: no arithmetic, no comparison, no axiom, no reduction rule. `Float` in LOGOS is strictly less than an axiomatised type — an axiomatised type at least has laws. It is a labelled atom.

NAN_AND_SIGNED_ZERO. `Literal::Float` holds an `f64` and definitional equality of literals is structural `==` on the `Literal` (type_checker.rs:1485 and the surrounding literal arms). Rust's `PartialEq` on `f64` is IEEE-754, under which `NaN != NaN` and `0.0 == -0.0`; the derived `Eq` on `Literal` that the kernel relies on therefore does not agree with Lean's `Float` equality either, and the discrepancy is silent. A translator must record this rather than assume `Float` literals behave like `Int` literals.

cases.title: `Bool` — the one primitive type that maps across cleanly, and the two ways to break it
cases.lean: Bool, Bool.true / Bool.false, cond, Bool.and / Bool.or / Bool.not, decide
cases.target: Global("Bool") with constructors Global("true") / Global("false") — the LOGOS prelude's own registrations, NOT freshly declared ones
evidence: kernel/src/prelude.rs:593-604 (`register_bool`: `Bool : Type 0` via `add_inductive`, then `add_constructor("true", "Bool", Bool)` and `add_constructor("false", "Bool", Bool)` — IN THAT ORDER); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:254-260 (`Match` is POSITIONAL: `cases.len()` must equal the constructor count and the cases are in registration order); kernel/src/prelude.rs:373-381 (`le`/`lt`/`ge`/`gt : Int → Int → Bool` — the comparison primitives land in this exact `Bool`); kernel/src/reduction.rs:449-450 and :466-476 (`try_primitive_reduce` returns `Term::Global("true")`/`Global("false")` literally — the bare constructor names); kernel/src/prelude.rs:202-340 (the `Int` order axioms encode `a ≤ b` as `Eq Bool (le a b) true`, so this `Bool` and these two constructor names are load- bearing for the entire order theory); kernel/src/prelude.rs:761-823 (`register_decidable`: `Decidable`/`isTrue`/`isFalse`); kernel/src/prelude.rs:1195-1219 (`reduceBool : Bool → Bool` and `ofReduceBool`)
guards: Catches the translator that DECLARES ITS OWN `Bool`. `Bool` is one of the very few Lean core types the LOGOS prelude already has, and re-registering it under a namespace-flattened name such as `Bool_Bool`, or re-adding constructors `Bool_true`/`Bool_false`, produces a type that is not the prelude's. Every comparison primitive (`le`, `lt`, `ge`, `gt`) returns the PRELUDE's `true`/`false` (reduction.rs:449-450), and every order axiom is stated about them (prelude.rs:202-340), so the shadow `Bool` silently severs all arithmetic comparison from all arithmetic reasoning. Nothing errors; the proofs just stop going through, at sites far from the declaration.

Catches CONSTRUCTOR ORDER INVERSION. LOGOS `Match` has no patterns: it is a positional list of cases in the inductive's registration order (type_checker.rs:254-260), and the prelude registers `true` FIRST, `false` second (prelude.rs:599-603). Lean's `Bool` also declares `false` first (`inductive Bool | false | true`), so the registration orders are OPPOSITE. A translator that lowers a Lean `match b with | false => x | true => y` by keeping Lean's constructor order emits `Match { cases: [x, y] }`, which LOGOS reads as `true => x, false => y`. Both branches typecheck whenever they have the same type — which is the common case — so the term is accepted and computes the NEGATION of what the source said. This is the most mechanical silent-mistranslation in the corpus and it is invisible to the kernel.

Catches translating `Bool` as `Prop`. LOGOS has both, and `decide`/`Decidable` (prelude.rs:761-823) is the bridge, exactly as in Lean. Collapsing them would make `if` untranslatable and would route through cumulativity (`Prop ≤ Type 0`, type_checker.rs:1330-1334), which Lean does not have — see T11-001.

Catches losing the `true`/`false` names to flattening. The prelude's constructors are keyed by the bare strings `"true"` and `"false"` (prelude.rs:600, :603). A translator that flattens `Bool.true` to `"Bool_true"` produces an unbound global; one that flattens it to `"true"` is correct here but must then reckon with T11-003, where the same flattening collides two distinct Lean declarations.
oracle: Emitted `Bool` terms use `Global("Bool")`, `Global("true")`, `Global("false")` with no new registration; and for every Lean `match` on `Bool` in the file, the emitted `Match`'s `cases[0]` is the Lean `true`-branch and `cases[1]` the `false`-branch. A harness asserts `normalize(le 3 4)` is `Global("true")` and that this is the same global the emitted `Match` dispatches on.

cases.title: `UInt8` / `UInt32` / `UInt64` / `USize` — absent, and wrapping arithmetic has no LOGOS counterpart
cases.lean: UInt8, UInt32, UInt64, USize, UInt64.add (wrapping), UInt32.val, Fin (2^n)
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/prelude.rs:18-51 (`StandardLibrary::register` — no `UInt` of any width); kernel/src/prelude.rs:352-381 (`register_primitives`: the complete list of primitive types is `Int`, `Float`, `Text`, `Duration`, `Date`, `Moment`, and the complete list of arithmetic builtins is `add`/`sub`/`mul`/`div`/`mod : Int → Int → Int` — UNBOUNDED integers, with no modulus anywhere); kernel/src/reduction.rs:455-471 (the `i64` fast path uses `checked_add`/`checked_sub`/ `checked_mul`, which return `None` ON OVERFLOW and fall through to the exact arbitrary-precision path at :486-500 — LOGOS arithmetic deliberately never wraps); kernel/src/term.rs:26-35 (`Literal::BigInt` exists precisely so that "`2.pow(63)` is the value `i64` cannot hold" is representable, base/src/numeric.rs:398-399); kernel/src/prelude.rs:3470-3525 (`register_bvec`: LOGOS's `BVec` — the only fixed-width thing in the kernel — is a hardware bit-vector, not a machine word; see T10-010)
guards: Catches the "`UInt64` is just a `Nat`" re-encoding. It typechecks, it computes, and it is wrong at exactly one place: overflow. `(0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF : UInt64) + 1` is `0` in Lean and `18446744073709551616` in the `Nat` encoding.
