Worse, LOGOS's arithmetic is *designed* not to wrap — `checked_add` failing routes to the exact `BigInt` path (reduction.rs:459, :491) rather than truncating — so there is no configuration of the prelude in which the encoding accidentally agrees. Every theorem about a hash, a checksum, a PRNG or a serialiser translated this way is silently false.

Catches encoding `UIntN` as `Fin (2^N)`, which is Lean's own definition. `Fin` is itself absent from LOGOS (T10-013), and rebuilding it needs `Subtype`, which is also absent — and the bound proof needs a `Nat` `<` relation that LOGOS's order axioms do not provide (they are all about `Int`, prelude.rs:202-340). The encoding is blocked three layers deep, and a translator that pushes through it ends up declaring all three with `add_inductive`/`add_constructor`, which are UNCHECKED (context.rs:253, :419) and will accept an ill-formed family without complaint. See T11-013.

Catches emitting the modulus as an explicit `mod 2^64` wrapper around `Int` arithmetic. That is arithmetically faithful, but `mod` in LOGOS is TRUNCATED toward zero with the remainder taking the DIVIDEND's sign (base/src/numeric.rs:354-375), so it is not the non-negative modulus the encoding needs; on any negative intermediate it produces a negative "unsigned" value. See T10-018.

Catches reaching this case only through `ByteArray`, `String.utf8ByteSize`, `Nat.toUInt64`, or `USize` in an array index. The rejection must fire on the elaborated `Expr`, where the width appears as a constant.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_TYPE_ABSENT_FROM_TARGET for every declaration below, and emits no LOGOS declaration. A harness asserts that no global named `UInt8`, `UInt16`, `UInt32`, `UInt64` or `USize` is ever registered.
diag: E_TYPE_ABSENT_FROM_TARGET(UInt8|UInt32|UInt64|USize) — must name the width, state that LOGOS has no bounded integer type and that its `Int` arithmetic is exact and unbounded by construction (reduction.rs:486-500), and must NOT offer `Int` or `Nat` as a substitute.

cases.title: `BitVec n` — LOGOS's `BVec n` shares the name and nothing else
cases.lean: BitVec n, BitVec.ofNat, BitVec.toNat, BitVec.add (mod 2^n), BitVec.extractLsb, HAnd / HOr / HXor on BitVec
cases.target: (none — `BVec` is a different type, not a re-spelling of `BitVec`)
evidence: kernel/src/prelude.rs:3468-3517 (`register_bvec`: `BVec : Nat → Type 0`, with `BVNil : BVec Zero` and `BVCons : Bit → Π(n:Nat). BVec n → BVec (Succ n)` — a UNARY CONS-LIST of `Bit`s indexed by its length, i.e. a linked list, not a machine word); kernel/src/prelude.rs:3450-3457 (`Bit`/`B0`/`B1` — the element type is a two-constructor inductive, not a boolean bit of a word); kernel/src/prelude.rs:3826-3849 (the COMPLETE set of `BVec` operations: `bv_and`, `bv_or`, `bv_xor`, `bv_not` — bitwise only. There is NO `bv_add`, `bv_mul`, `bv_shl`, `bv_ushr`, no `toNat`, no `ofNat`, and no modular arithmetic of any kind); kernel/src/prelude.rs:3477 (`ctx.add_inductive("BVec", …)` — NOT `add_indexed_inductive`, so per context.rs:249-253 the whole arity is treated as uniform PARAMETERS and `BVec` is registered with ZERO indices even though its constructors plainly index it by `Zero`/`Succ n`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:612-678 (`infer_indexed_match` has no index unifier and no impossible-case elimination)
guards: THE NAME IS THE TRAP. `BVec n` and `BitVec n` have the same arity, the same kind (`Nat → Type`), and nearly the same name, so a name-directed translator maps one to the other and every SIGNATURE typechecks. The semantics are unrelated: Lean's `BitVec n` is `structure BitVec (w : Nat) where toFin : Fin (2^w)` — a NUMBER with modular arithmetic — while `BVec n` is `BVNil`/`BVCons`, a list. `BitVec.add` is addition mod 2^n; there is no `BVec` addition at all (prelude.rs:3826-3849), so `x + y` translates to nothing, and if the translator supplies its own it must decide bit ordering, carry propagation and endianness with no specification to check against.

Catches the endianness/ordering silent flip. `BVCons : Bit → Π(n:Nat). BVec n → BVec (Succ n)` (prelude.rs:3492-3516) puts the NEW bit first and the length index SECOND, after the element — an argument order that no Lean constructor has. A translator that emits `BVCons n b v` rather than `BVCons b n v` produces an ill-typed term (caught), but one that emits the bits in Lean's LSB-first order into a structure the LOGOS `bv_*` definitions read MSB-first produces a well-typed term that computes the bit-reversal of the intended value (not caught).

Catches inheriting the prelude's own params/indices misdeclaration. `BVec` is registered with `add_inductive` (prelude.rs:3477), which per context.rs:249-253 treats its entire arity as uniform parameters — so LOGOS believes `BVec` has one PARAMETER and zero indices, while its constructors target `BVec Zero` and `BVec (Succ n)`. Matching on a `BVec` therefore goes through the parametric path, not `infer_indexed_match`, and the length index is not related to the scrutinee at all. Any translation that relies on the index to rule out a case is unsound here; see T03-005 and T11-010.

Catches the "it's fine, I only need bitwise ops" rationalisation. Even restricted to `&&&`/`|||`/`^^^`/`~~~`, Lean's operations are on a `Fin (2^w)` and LOGOS's are `Match`-bodied recursions over a list (prelude.rs:3826-3849), so the two agree on values but not on any lemma: nothing in LOGOS states `bv_and x x = x`, and nothing can be proved about a `BVec` of symbolic length without a recursor that `derive_recursor` pins to a `Type 0` motive (recursor.rs:64-71).
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_TYPE_ABSENT_FROM_TARGET(BitVec) for every declaration below and emits no LOGOS declaration. A harness asserts that `Global("BVec")` never appears in output translated from a Lean `BitVec`.
diag: E_TYPE_ABSENT_FROM_TARGET(BitVec) — must name `BitVec`, must state that LOGOS's `BVec` is a `Bit` cons-list with four bitwise operations and no arithmetic, and must NOT propose `BVec` as the translation. Must also refuse any proposal routed through `UInt*` (T10-009) or `Fin (2^n)` (T10-013).

cases.title: `Array` — absent, and the `List` encoding changes the complexity *and* the proofs
cases.lean: Array, #[…] literal, Array.get / getElem, Array.push, Array.size, Array.data, Array.foldl, USize indexing
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/prelude.rs:18-51 (`StandardLibrary::register` — no `Array`); kernel/src/prelude.rs:609-652 (`register_tlist`: the only parametric sequence in the prelude is `TList : Type 0 → Type 0` with `TNil`/`TCons`, a CONS-LIST); kernel/src/prelude.rs:564-592 (`register_monolist`: `EList` is a monomorphic list of `Entity`, and its own doc comment explains it exists because "the kernel's parametric `TList A` carries a type argument, so its constructors are `Π(A:Type)…`" — i.e. even the prelude works around its own list); kernel/src/term.rs:13-44 (the `Literal` enum has no array/vector variant, so `#[1,2,3]` cannot be injected as a literal); kernel/src/reduction.rs:444-506 (`try_primitive_reduce` — no indexing, no `get`/`push`/`size` primitive exists); kernel/src/prelude.rs:3468-3477 (`BVec` is the only length-indexed container, and it is a `Bit` list — see T10-010)
guards: Catches the silent `Array ↦ TList` substitution. The two have the same INTERFACE for `foldl`/`map`/`size`, so most Lean sources translate without a type error. What changes is (a) `Array.get a i` is O(1) and total given a bound proof, while a list lookup is O(i) recursion that must be written and must handle the out-of-range case, (b) `Array.set` is destructive-with-sharing while a list update rebuilds, and most importantly (c) EVERY LEMMA. `Array.size_push`, `Array.get_push_eq`, `Array.getElem_set_eq` and friends do not hold of a cons-list by construction; the translator must re-prove each one, and if it instead re-declares them with `add_declaration` it has enlarged the trusted base with statements about a type the prelude does not have (compare T06-009).

Catches the `GetElem` bound proof being dropped. `a[i]` in Lean is `@getElem _ _ _ _ a i h` where `h : i < a.size`. In a `TList` encoding the bound proof has no target — LOGOS has no `Nat` order relation at all (the order axioms at prelude.rs:202-340 are every one of them about `Int`) — so the tempting move is to translate `a[i]` as a total lookup with a default. That is a DIFFERENT FUNCTION, and it makes `a[i] = a[j] → i = j`-style reasoning unsound at out-of-range indices while still typechecking.

Catches translating the array literal `#[1,2,3]` as a `Literal`. There is no array literal variant (term.rs:13-44); it must become nested `TCons` applications, each carrying the `Type 0` parameter explicitly (prelude.rs:637-651 — `TCons`'s first argument is the element type). An emitter that omits the type argument, or that leaves it as `Term::Hole`, produces a term that `types_equal` accepts because `Hole` matches anything (type_checker.rs:1594-1597) — see T11-004.

Catches `TList`'s `Type 0` pinning. `TList : Type 0 → Type 0` (prelude.rs:613-619), so an array of `Prop`s, of types, or of anything in `Type 1` is not encodable — and because LOGOS is cumulative (`Prop ≤ Type 0`, type_checker.rs:1330-1334) an `Array Prop` may well typecheck as a `TList Prop` anyway, which Lean would reject. See T11-001.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_TYPE_ABSENT_FROM_TARGET(Array) for every declaration below and emits no LOGOS declaration. A harness asserts that no `Global("TList")` appears in output translated from a Lean `Array`.
diag: E_TYPE_ABSENT_FROM_TARGET(Array) — must name `Array`, state that LOGOS has no array type, no array literal, and no indexing primitive, and must NOT silently substitute `TList`. If the translator offers a `TList` encoding it must do so as an explicit, user-approved rewrite with a loss record, never as a translation.

cases.title: `List` — Lean's `List` is not in the LOGOS prelude, and the nearest neighbour `TList` is pinned to `Type 0`
cases.lean: List, [], ::, [1,2,3] literal, List.append, List.map, List.length, List.rec
cases.target: A translator-emitted inductive. The nearest prelude neighbour is `TList : Type 0 → Type 0` with `TNil : Π(A:Type 0). TList A` and `TCons : Π(A:Type 0). A → TList A → TList A`, plus a `derive_recursor` result the caller must `add_definition`.
evidence: kernel/src/prelude.rs:609-652 (`register_tlist` — the exact shape above, and note `add_inductive("TList", Π(A:Type 0). Type 0)` at :619, so the parameter is a `Type 0` parameter, not a level-polymorphic one); kernel/src/prelude.rs:564-592 (`register_monolist`'s doc comment: `EList` exists because `TList`'s `Π(A:Type)…` constructors do not fit the generic `InductionScheme`, and the `E`-prefixed names "deliberately avoid the user-space `List`/`Nil`/`Cons` a REPL program defines (typically a parametric `List A`)" — i.e. the prelude EXPECTS the user to declare their own `List`); kernel/src/recursor.rs:36 and :64-71 (`derive_recursor` synthesises `(type, term)` and the caller must `add_definition` it; the motive target is HARD-CODED to `Sort(Type 0)` for a non-`Prop` inductive — so the derived `List` recursor cannot eliminate into `Type 1`, and cannot be universe-polymorphic); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:254-260 (`Match` is positional over the constructor registration order); kernel/src/context.rs:253 (`add_inductive` is UNCHECKED)
guards: Catches the constructor-order flip. Lean declares `List` as `nil` then `cons`; a translator that registers `Cons` before `Nil` produces a `Match` whose positional cases (type_checker.rs:254-260) are swapped. Both branches of a `List` match frequently have the same type — `length`, `sum`, `any` all do — so the term typechecks and computes the wrong answer with no diagnostic. Compare T10-008.

Catches forgetting that `TNil`/`TCons` take the element TYPE as an explicit leading argument (prelude.rs:637-651). Lean's `[]` and `a :: as` have the type implicit, so the elaborated `Expr` has it as an implicit argument that must be turned into an EXPLICIT first argument, or the binder kind recorded with `set_binder_kinds(name, [ParamKind::Implicit, …])` (context.rs:201). Omitting it and leaving a `Term::Hole` in its place typechecks, because `types_equal` treats `Hole` as matching anything (type_checker.rs:1594-1597). See T11-004.

Catches reusing the prelude's `TList` as if it were Lean's `List`. It is a different global with different constructor names; any Lean lemma name-mapped onto it is a claim about a type the source never mentioned. And `EList` is worse: it is MONOMORPHIC in `Entity` (prelude.rs:564-592), so `EList` is `List Entity` and nothing else.

Catches emitting the inductive but not the recursor. `derive_recursor` does not register anything — "the caller must `add_definition` it" (recursor.rs:36). A translator that emits `List` and its constructors and then translates `List.rec` as an unbound `Global("List_rec")` produces a term whose `infer_type` fails with `UnboundVariable`, which reads like a name-resolution bug rather than a missing elimination principle.
oracle: The emitted declaration set contains exactly one inductive with two constructors in `nil`-then-`cons` order plus an `add_definition`-registered recursor; `infer_type` accepts every term below; and the loss record contains LIST_IS_REDECLARED and LIST_IS_MONOMORPHISED_AT_TYPE_0. A harness asserts the emitted `Match` case order matches the registration order.
loss: LIST_IS_REDECLARED. The emitted `List` is a fresh LOGOS inductive that happens to have the same shape as Lean's. It carries none of Lean's ~900 `List` lemmas, none of its `@[simp]` set, and no `DecidableEq`; every fact the source relies on must be re-translated from its Lean proof or the declaration must be rejected. "The types line up" is not evidence that a `List` theorem survives.

LIST_IS_MONOMORPHISED_AT_TYPE_0. Lean's `List : Type u → Type u` is universe- polymorphic; LOGOS inductives carry a single fixed sort (context.rs:253, :374) and `derive_recursor` pins the motive to `Type 0` (recursor.rs:64-71). So the emitted list is `Type 0 → Type 0`. `List Prop` survives only via LOGOS's cumulativity (`Prop ≤ Type 0`, type_checker.rs:1330-1334), which Lean does not have; `List Type` and `List (List α)` at two different levels do not survive at all. This is the `reject` of T01-007 showing through a `degrade` case: the loss record must name it, and if the source instantiates the list at two distinct levels the case escalates to T01-007's rejection.

cases.title: `Option` / `Prod` / `Sum` / `Sigma` / `Subtype` / `Fin` — none is registered; each must be emitted, and each emission is a fresh, lemma-free type
cases.lean: Option, Prod (α × β), Sum (α ⊕ β), Sigma (Σ x, β x), Subtype ({x // p x}), Fin n, and their anonymous-constructor / projection notation
cases.target: One translator-emitted declaration per type. `Prod`, `Sigma` and `Subtype` are records and should go through `Context::add_structure` (which also gives eta); `Option` and `Sum` are plain inductives via `add_inductive` + `add_constructor`; `Fin` needs `Subtype` first, so it is emitted last.
evidence: kernel/src/prelude.rs:18-51 (`StandardLibrary::register` — the complete registration list; none of these six appears); kernel/src/context.rs:271-369 (`add_structure` desugars a record into an inductive + `{name}_mk` + one DEFINITION per field whose body is a `Term::Match`, and registers the `StructInfo` that gates eta); kernel/src/context.rs:300 (`add_structure` HARD-CODES the sort to `Type 0`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1391-1417 (`try_structure_eta` — eta for registered structures) and :1473-1478 (it fires only inside `def_eq_normalized`, never in `normalize`); kernel/src/recursor.rs:64-71 (`derive_recursor` pins a non-`Prop` inductive's motive to `Sort(Type 0)`); kernel/src/context.rs:253, :419 (`add_inductive` / `add_constructor` are UNCHECKED); kernel/src/prelude.rs:202-340 (every order axiom is about `Int`, so there is no `Nat` `<` for `Fin`'s bound to use)
guards: Catches emitting `Option α` as `Sum Unit α` or as `α` "with a sentinel". The first is a different type with different constructor names, so every `Option.some`/`none` in the source has to be rewritten and no Lean lemma transfers; the second is unsound the moment `α` is inhabited by the sentinel.

Catches `Prod` emitted as an inductive rather than a STRUCTURE. Only structures in the `structures` registry get eta (type_checker.rs:1391-1417), so an inductive `Prod` makes `(p.1, p.2) = p` unprovable — a fact Lean proves by `rfl`. And even as a structure, eta lives only in `def_eq_normalized`, never in `normalize` (:1473-1478), so a proof that routes through `normalize` still fails. See T03-011.

Catches the `Subtype` projection losing the proof component. LOGOS has definitional proof irrelevance (`proof_irrelevant`, type_checker.rs:1547-1567), but it is a LAST-RESORT rule that calls `infer_type` on both sides, so it only fires when both proofs' types actually infer. A `Subtype` emitted with the proof field's type left as `Term::Hole` typechecks — `types_equal` matches `Hole` against anything (:1594-1597) — and then `proof_irrelevant` cannot fire because `infer_type` on a `Hole` is `CannotInferHole` (:313). Two distinct subtype elements become non-equal where Lean says they are equal. See T11-004 and T11-009.

Catches emitting `Fin n` as `Nat`. That drops the bound entirely, so `Fin 0` becomes inhabited and every `Fin`-indexed total function becomes a partial one. And the honest encoding — `{i : Nat // i < n}` — needs a `Nat` `<`, which LOGOS does not have as a primitive: its order axioms are all `Int` order axioms (prelude.rs:202-340), so the relation itself must be emitted as an inductive or a `Bool`-valued recursion, and the bound proofs re-derived.

Catches emitting six types with six different naming conventions. LOGOS keys are flat `String`s with no namespaces (context.rs:442 and the `get_global` chain at :449-464), so `Prod.fst` and a user's `Prod_fst` collide; see T11-003.
oracle: Each of the six types is emitted exactly once; `Prod`, `Sigma` and `Subtype` appear in the `structures` registry (so `try_structure_eta` can fire); `infer_type` accepts every term below; and the loss record contains NO_STRUCTURAL_TYPES and SORT_PINNING_AT_TYPE_0 with a per-type breakdown.
loss: NO_STRUCTURAL_TYPES. Six of the most-used types in Lean core arrive with nothing. Each emitted counterpart is a new LOGOS global with no lemmas, no `@[simp]` set, no `DecidableEq`, and no relationship to any other emitted type. The loss is per-declaration and must be recorded per-declaration, not once for the file.

SORT_PINNING_AT_TYPE_0. `add_structure` fixes the sort at `Type 0` (context.rs:300) and `derive_recursor` fixes the motive at `Type 0` (recursor.rs:64-71). So `Prod`, `Sigma` and `Subtype` land monomorphically at `Type 0`. `Subtype {x : α // p x}` with `p : α → Prop` is the acute case: Lean's `Subtype` is `Sort u`-polymorphic and is routinely used at `Prop`; the emitted one is not, and a `Subtype` over a `Prop` survives only by LOGOS's cumulativity (type_checker.rs:1330-1334), which Lean does not have. See T11-001 and T01-007.

SIGMA_IS_NOT_DEPENDENT_ENOUGH. `add_structure`'s `fields` may reference earlier fields by name (context.rs:275-282), so a two-field dependent record is expressible — but the field type must be a `Term`, and the second component's type in `Sigma β` is `β a`, an APPLICATION of a bound type family. That is representable, yet the derived projection is a `Term::Match` whose motive must be filled by `fill_match_motives`, which handles only Miller patterns. Dependent-pair projections outside that fragment must be rejected, not emitted.

cases.title: `OfNat` overloading — the numeral's meaning is an instance, and LOGOS has no classes
cases.lean: OfNat, OfNat.ofNat, instOfNatNat, Neg / OfScientific, custom OfNat instance, @[default_instance]
cases.target: The literal must be resolved AT ELABORATION TIME to the value the instance produces, and that value emitted directly — `Term::Lit(Literal::Nat)` for `Nat`, `Term::Lit(int_lit)` for `Int`, and a fully applied translated constructor term for a user type. The `OfNat` class itself is NOT emitted.
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:184-189 (`add_instance` stores a flat `Vec<(Term, Term)>` and resolution is FIRST MATCH WINS — there is no priority, no `@[default_instance]`, no coherence check, and no `outParam`); kernel/src/context.rs:201 (`set_binder_kinds` with `ParamKind::{Explicit, Implicit, Instance}` — elaborate.rs:1018-1027 — is the whole of LOGOS's instance-argument machinery, and it is a property of a NAME, not a class); kernel/src/term.rs:13-44 (the `Literal` enum has exactly one numeric-natural variant `Nat` and one integer family `Int`/`BigInt` — a numeral cannot be left polymorphic); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:296-304 (a literal's type is determined by its VARIANT, not by the context: `Literal::Nat` is `Nat`, full stop — there is no "numeral at whatever type is expected"); kernel/src/prelude.rs:18-51 (no `OfNat` in the trusted base)
guards: Catches emitting `OfNat.ofNat` as a global application. `@OfNat.ofNat Nat 5 (instOfNatNat 5)` lowered structurally becomes `App(App(App(Global("OfNat_ofNat"), Global("Nat")), Lit(Nat(5))), Global("instOfNatNat"))` — three unbound globals and a literal buried as an ARGUMENT rather than the term itself. `infer_type` fails with `UnboundVariable("OfNat_ofNat")`, which reads like a missing-prelude-entry bug; the translator then "fixes" it with `add_declaration`, and now the literal `5` is an opaque axiom application that does not reduce, so `isZero 5` is stuck and `normalize` reports the stuck term as normal (reduction.rs:52-69).

Catches resolving the instance at the WRONG TYPE. `(5 : Int)` and `(5 : Nat)` are the same surface numeral and different LOGOS `Literal` variants with different types and different reduction mechanisms (T10-004). A translator that reads the numeral rather than the elaborated `Expr`'s type gets a term that typechecks — `Literal::Nat(5)` is a perfectly good term — but at the wrong type, and the error surfaces only where the two arithmetics diverge.

Catches a USER `OfNat` instance being silently dropped. If the source defines `instance : OfNat Mod7 n := ⟨Mod7.mk (n % 7)⟩`, then `(9 : Mod7)` is `Mod7.mk 2`, NOT `Mod7.mk 9`. A translator that emits the raw numeral into the user type produces a well-typed term with the wrong value. Note that the reduction here uses `%`, which on `Nat` truncates toward zero trivially but on `Int` follows LOGOS's dividend-signed remainder (T10-018) — so a user instance over `Int` can go wrong twice.

Catches assuming LOGOS instance resolution can stand in. `add_instance` takes a flat `(Term, Term)` pair and returns the FIRST match (context.rs:184-189), so two `OfNat` instances for one type silently resolve to whichever was registered first, with no diamond detection (compare T07-013). Instance selection must not be deferred to LOGOS.
oracle: Every numeral in the output is a `Term::Lit` of the correct variant, or a fully applied translated constructor term, with NO occurrence of a global named `OfNat_ofNat` or `instOfNatNat`; and the loss record contains OVERLOADING_IS_RESOLVED_AWAY. A harness asserts that for each numeral the emitted term is `def_eq` to the translation of Lean's own `whnf` of the elaborated literal.
loss: OVERLOADING_IS_RESOLVED_AWAY. Lean's `(5 : α)` is `@OfNat.ofNat α 5 inst`, and its meaning depends on `inst`. LOGOS literals are monomorphic by construction (type_checker.rs:296-304), so the translator must run Lean's instance resolution and emit the RESULT. What is lost is the indirection: a downstream Lean lemma stated about `OfNat.ofNat` generically, or a proof that rewrites through an `OfNat` instance equation, has no target in the output.

NO_DEFAULT_INSTANCE. `@[default_instance]` is what makes a bare `5` with no expected type default to `Nat`. LOGOS's `add_instance` is an insertion-ordered flat list with first-match-wins (context.rs:184-189) and no priority concept, so the defaulting decision cannot be represented at all; it must be made in Lean and baked in.

cases.title: `Literal::Nat` is DEFINITIONALLY `Succ^n Zero` — the accelerated numeral bridge
cases.lean: Nat literal, Nat.zero, Nat.succ, Nat.rec, match on a numeral, OfNat at Nat
cases.target: Term::Lit(Literal::Nat(n)), which the kernel treats as constructor-form: in `extract_constructor` it peels one `Succ` per step, and in `def_eq_normalized` it is interchangeable with the spelled-out Peano term.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:38-44 (`Literal::Nat` is "a compact, accelerated form of the unary Peano numeral `Succ^n Zero`. `Nat(n)` is DEFINITIONALLY EQUAL to `Succ` applied `n` times to `Zero`… in BOTH kernels"); kernel/src/reduction.rs:329-345 (`extract_constructor`'s bridge: `Nat(0)` yields `Zero`'s registration index with no arguments, `Nat(n)` yields `Succ`'s index with the single argument `Lit(Nat(n-1))` — so a `Match` or a derived recursor computes on a literal directly); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1480-1493 (the `def_eq` side: two `Nat` literals are equal iff their `BigInt`s are, and a literal versus a `Zero`/`Succ`-headed term is compared by peeling one `Succ` at a time via `nat_peano_step`, :1434-1440); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:302 (`Literal::Nat(_) => Ok(Global("Nat"))`); kernel/src/prelude.rs:529-552 (`register_nat` — the `Zero`/`Succ` registration order the bridge's indices refer to); kernel/src/recheck.rs (the second, de Bruijn kernel implements the same bridge, which is what "in BOTH kernels" refers to)
guards: Catches the translator that "helpfully" expands literals to Peano form to be safe. It is definitionally correct but destroys the acceleration the bridge exists for: `Succ^n Zero` is `n` heap nodes, `substitute` is O(size) per binder comparison (type_checker.rs:1088), and `normalize`'s fuel is a hard 10000 steps that returns the PARTIALLY reduced term on exhaustion with no error (reduction.rs:52-69). A literal in the low thousands therefore makes a `def_eq` check silently answer "not equal" when the two sides were equal. See T11-005 and T11-007.

Catches the mirror error: assuming the bridge means a `Nat` literal is a `Term` constructor application that can be *pattern-matched on syntactically*. It is not — it is a `Term::Lit`, and any translator-side analysis that walks the term looking for `App(Global("Succ"), _)` will not find it. The bridge lives in the KERNEL's `extract_constructor` and `def_eq`; a translator that re-implements either must implement the bridge too or its own defeq check will disagree with LOGOS's.

Catches the constructor-INDEX assumption. `extract_constructor` looks the indices up by NAME at reduction time — `idx_of("Zero")` and `idx_of("Succ")` (reduction.rs:333-344) — against whatever is registered for `"Nat"`. A translator that emits its own `Nat` (say because it flattened `Nat` from a namespace, or because it declared `Nat` fresh rather than reusing the prelude's) breaks the bridge: the names no longer resolve, `idx_of` returns `None`, and every literal silently stops being constructor-form. Matches on literals then get stuck and `normalize` reports the stuck term as normal.

Catches the boundary at zero. The bridge clamps: `n ≤ 0` maps to `Zero` (reduction.rs:337-341), so a *negative* `Literal::Nat` — which `infer_type` rejects (type_checker.rs:297-301) but which can be produced by a translator bug — computes as `0` rather than erroring. The translator must never emit one. See T10-002.
oracle: For each example below, LOGOS `def_eq` holds between the emitted literal term and the emitted Peano term, AND the emitted term is a `Term::Lit(Literal::Nat)` — not an application spine. A harness additionally asserts that `normalize` of a `Match` on a literal takes O(1) `reduce_step` calls per peeled `Succ`, not O(n) up front.

cases.title: `String` operations — `++`, `length`, `get`, `append`: LOGOS has literally none
cases.lean: String.append (++), String.length, String.get, String.push, String.isPrefixOf, String.toNat?, ToString
cases.target: (none — no sound translation)
evidence: kernel/src/prelude.rs:356 (`ctx.add_inductive("Text", Sort(Type 0))` — the ONLY mention of `Text` as a type in the whole registration path, and it adds ZERO constructors, so `Text` is an opaque carrier with no eliminator); kernel/src/prelude.rs:352-430 (`register_primitives` — the complete list of declared operations: `add`/`sub`/`mul`/`div`/`mod : Int → Int → Int`, `le`/`lt`/`ge`/`gt : Int → Int → Bool`, and the `Duration`/`Date`/`Moment` operations. NOT ONE of them mentions `Text`); kernel/src/reduction.rs:444-506 (`try_primitive_reduce` dispatches on the nine operation names above and nothing else — no string operation can reduce); kernel/src/term.rs:19-20 (`Literal::Text(String)` — a literal injection with no accompanying elimination, unlike `Literal::Nat` which has the Peano bridge at reduction.rs:329-345); kernel/src/prelude.rs:2151-2152 (the only other use of `Text` in the kernel is as the payload of the reflection constructor `SName : Text → Syntax` — a name tag, not a string library)
guards: Catches declaring the operations as axioms. `ctx.add_declaration("Text_append", Text → Text → Text)` compiles and every term using it typechecks. But there is no reduction rule for it — `try_primitive_reduce` matches nine hard-coded names (reduction.rs:455-500) and a new global is not one of them — so `"a" ++ "b"` never becomes `"ab"`, `def_eq("a" ++ "b", "ab")` is FALSE, and every `rfl`-proof in the source fails at a site far from the axiom. Meanwhile the trusted base has grown: `certificate::recheck` rebuilds the context from `StandardLibrary::register` alone (certificate.rs:63-75), so the certificate fails with `UnboundVariable("Text_append")`, which reads like a name-resolution bug. Compare T06-009 and T10-007.

Catches declaring the operations as DEFINITIONS over an invented character list. That at least computes — but only up to `normalize`'s hard 10000-step fuel, after which the partially reduced term is returned SILENTLY (reduction.rs:52-69). Since the element type must itself be invented (`Char` is absent, T10-006, and so is `UInt32`, T10-009), the encoding is three declarations deep before the first character, and every one of them goes through the UNCHECKED `add_inductive` / `add_constructor` path (context.rs:253, :419). See T11-013.

Catches the asymmetry with `Nat`. `Literal::Nat` has an eliminator — the Peano bridge — so LOGOS can compute on numerals. `Literal::Text` has none. A translator that reasons "literals work for `Nat`, so they work for `Text`" will emit terms that typecheck and never reduce.

Catches reaching this case through `ToString`, `repr`, `IO.println`, string interpolation `s!"…"`, or `decide`'s error messages. The rejection must fire on the elaborated `Expr`; string interpolation in particular expands to a chain of `String.append` calls that no longer look like strings in the source.

Catches the claim that string operations are "not mathematical content". They are: a `Decidable` instance driven by `String.decEq`, or a `deriving Repr`, puts a string operation inside a proof term. If it is in the term, it must translate or be rejected.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_OPERATION_ABSENT_FROM_TARGET(String) for every declaration below, emits no LOGOS output for them, and performs zero `add_declaration` calls naming a `Text` operation. A harness asserts that the set of `Text`-typed applications in the whole corpus output is empty apart from `Eq`.
diag: E_OPERATION_ABSENT_FROM_TARGET(String) — must name the specific operation, state that LOGOS's `Text` is a zero-constructor opaque type with no declared operations and no reduction rules, and must NOT offer to declare the operation as an axiom. The diagnostic must distinguish itself from T10-005: the TYPE degrades, the OPERATIONS are rejected.

cases.title: Truncated `Nat` subtraction — Lean saturates at zero; LOGOS has no `Nat` subtraction at all, and its `sub` goes negative
cases.lean: HSub.hSub on Nat, Nat.sub, Nat.pred, `n - m` with `m > n`
cases.target: A translator-emitted structural recursion over the prelude's `Nat`, i.e. `add_definition("Nat_sub", Nat → Nat → Nat, Fix{ … Match … })` implementing `sub n 0 = n`, `sub 0 (Succ _) = Zero`, `sub (Succ n) (Succ m) = sub n m`. The prelude's `sub` is NOT the target.
evidence: kernel/src/prelude.rs:363-381 (`register_primitives`: `sub` is `add_declaration("sub", Int → Int → Int)` — an AXIOM at type `Int`, with no `Nat` counterpart anywhere in the prelude); kernel/src/prelude.rs:529-552 (`register_nat` registers `Nat`, `Zero` and `Succ` and NOTHING else — LOGOS ships no `Nat` arithmetic at all); kernel/src/reduction.rs:455-471 (the `sub` reduction is `a.checked_sub(*b)` on `Literal::Int` operands, falling through to `xb.sub(&yb)` on the exact `BigInt` path at :492 — in BOTH cases an unbounded signed subtraction that can and does produce a negative result); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:297-301 (`infer_type` REFUSES a negative `Literal::Nat`, so a negative result cannot even be re-typed as a `Nat`); kernel/src/reduction.rs:337-341 (`extract_constructor` CLAMPS a negative `Literal::Nat` to `Zero` "so the peel TERMINATES rather than descending toward −∞" — a clamp that is NOT the same as Lean's truncation, see the guard); kernel/src/termination.rs:378-400 (the structural guard that the emitted recursion must satisfy)
guards: THE CENTRAL BUG OF THIS CASE: translating Lean's `Nat` subtraction to the prelude's `sub`. It is enormously tempting — `sub` is right there, it is the only subtraction LOGOS has, and it reduces natively on literals (reduction.rs:455-500) instead of costing one step per unit. It is also wrong, and wrong in a way nothing detects. Lean: `3 - 8 = 0`. LOGOS `sub`: `3 - 8 ⤳ Lit(Int(-5))`. If the translator has also conflated `Nat` with `Int` (T10-004) the term typechecks and silently computes `-5`. If it has NOT conflated them, the term is ill-typed and is caught — which is the argument for keeping the two types apart even though it costs an emitted recursion.

Catches the "clamp it afterwards" repair: emitting `max 0 (sub n m)` or relying on `extract_constructor`'s negative-`Nat` clamp (reduction.rs:337-341). The clamp is a REDUCTION-time safety net for malformed input, not a semantic rule: it fires only inside `extract_constructor`, so a negative value clamps to `Zero` when it is a `Match` scrutinee but stays negative everywhere else — in `def_eq`, in `infer_type` (which rejects it outright, type_checker.rs:297-301), and in any arithmetic built on top. The result is a term that computes one value under `Match` and another under equality. There is no `max` in the prelude to build the repair from either.

Catches losing the truncation at the point where it MATTERS. `n - m + m = n` is FALSE in Lean when `m > n`, and a translator that "fixes" `Nat` subtraction by making it total-and-signed makes that identity TRUE — strengthening the theory. Any Lean proof that relies on the truncation (`Nat.sub_add_cancel` has the hypothesis `m ≤ n` for exactly this reason) becomes a proof of a different statement.

Catches emitting the recursion with the wrong structural argument. The Giménez guard (termination.rs:378-400) accepts a recursive call only when the structural argument is headed by a match-bound smaller variable. `sub (Succ n) (Succ m) = sub n m` decreases on BOTH arguments; the emitted `Fix` must decrease on the one the guard is tracking, or the definition is refused — and a translator that then reaches for `termination_by` finds it does not exist (T04-004).
oracle: The emitted term for `n - m` applies a translator-emitted `Nat`-typed definition, NOT `Global("sub")`; `normalize(emitted(3 - 8))` is `Lit(Nat(0))` (or `Global("Zero")`); and the loss record contains NAT_ARITHMETIC_IS_EMITTED_NOT_PRIMITIVE. A harness asserts over the whole corpus that `Global("sub")` is never applied to a `Nat`-typed argument.
loss: NAT_ARITHMETIC_IS_EMITTED_NOT_PRIMITIVE. Lean's `Nat.sub` is a kernel-accelerated GMP operation with a compiler override; every Lean `Nat` fact about it (`Nat.sub_self`, `Nat.sub_lt`, `Nat.succ_sub_succ`, the whole `omega` normal form) is stated about that primitive. The LOGOS translation is an ordinary `Fix`+`Match` definition, so it computes by ι-reduction at one `Succ` per step: `50000 - 1` takes 50000 reduction steps, which exceeds `normalize`'s hard fuel of 10000 (reduction.rs:52-69). Past that boundary the kernel returns the PARTIALLY reduced term and reports no error, so a true equation becomes unprovable with no diagnostic. The loss record must name the fuel boundary, not just "slower".
NO_NAT_LEMMAS. None of Lean's `Nat` subtraction lemmas transfer; each must be re-proved against the emitted definition or its use rejected.

cases.title: `Int` division and remainder — LOGOS's `div`/`mod` TRUNCATE toward zero; Lean 4's `/` and `%` on `Int` are EUCLIDEAN
cases.lean: HDiv.hDiv / HMod.hMod on Int, Int.ediv, Int.emod, Int.tdiv, Int.tmod, Int.fdiv, Int.fmod, Int.emod_nonneg
cases.target: `Global("div")` / `Global("mod")` — the prelude's opaque `Int → Int → Int` declarations — ONLY for Lean's `Int.tdiv` / `Int.tmod`. For Lean's `/` and `%` (i.e. `Int.ediv` / `Int.emod`) the translator must emit a CORRECTION WRAPPER around them, or reject.
evidence: **Read out of the repo for this case.** kernel/src/prelude.rs:380-381 (`add_declaration("div", Int → Int → Int)` and `("mod", …)` — opaque axioms, no body, no laws: the 16 axioms at prelude.rs:92-340 cover `add`/`mul`/`sub`/order only, and say NOTHING about `div` or `mod`); kernel/src/reduction.rs:455-466 (the `i64` fast path: `"div" => a.checked_div(*b)`, `"mod" => a.checked_rem(*b)` — Rust's `/` and `%` on `i64`, which TRUNCATE toward zero and give the remainder the DIVIDEND's sign); kernel/src/reduction.rs:486-500 (the exact `BigInt` path: `"div" => xb.div_rem(&yb).map(|(q, _)| q)`, `"mod" => xb.div_rem(&yb).map(|(_, r)| r)`); base/src/numeric.rs:350-375 (`BigInt::div_rem`'s own doc comment: "Truncated division toward zero: returns `(quotient, remainder)` with `self = q*other + r` and the remainder carrying the dividend's sign — exactly matching Rust/`i64` `/` and `%`"; the implementation takes `q_neg` as the XOR of the signs and gives `r` the DIVIDEND's sign at :371-372); base/src/numeric.rs:1662-1677 (the test `div_rem_matches_i64_truncation_including_signs` pins this against `i128` `/` and `%` across negative operands); kernel/src/reduction.rs:490 and base/src/numeric.rs:355-357 (division by zero yields `None`, so the term stays STUCK — it does not error and does not produce a value)
guards: THE CENTRAL BUG: mapping Lean's `/` and `%` on `Int` to `div` and `mod` by name. The names match, the types match, the arities match, and the results agree on every non-negative example a translator author is likely to test. `infer_type` accepts the term, `normalize` reduces it, and the answer is wrong by one on the quotient and wrong in SIGN on the remainder for negative dividends. Nothing in LOGOS can detect this, because `div` and `mod` have no axioms to contradict.

Catches mapping Lean's DEPRECATED `Int.div`/`Int.mod` by the same name-directed reasoning. In Lean 4.14 `Int.div`/`Int.mod` are the TRUNCATED operations (renamed to `Int.tdiv`/`Int.tmod`), so `Int.div ↦ div` happens to be correct while `HDiv.hDiv ↦ div` is not — even though `HDiv.hDiv` on `Int` is what the surface `/` elaborates to. A translator must dispatch on the ELABORATED constant, and must know that Lean has FOUR division conventions (`ediv`, `fdiv`, `tdiv`, and the deprecated `div` alias) of which LOGOS implements exactly one.

Catches `Int.fdiv`/`Int.fmod` (FLOOR division, remainder taking the DIVISOR's sign). Floor and Euclidean agree when the divisor is positive and differ when it is negative, so a translator that "fixes" the mismatch by assuming floor semantics gets `7 / (-2)`: Lean's `ediv` gives `-3`, `fdiv` gives `-4`. Three conventions, three answers, one LOGOS primitive.

Catches division by zero. Lean TOTALISES: `n / 0 = 0` and `n % 0 = n`. LOGOS's reduction returns `None` for a zero divisor (reduction.rs:490, base/src/numeric.rs:355-357), so the application stays STUCK — and `normalize` returns a stuck term without any error (reduction.rs:52-69), so `def_eq(n / 0, 0)` is simply FALSE rather than diagnosed. A translation of any Lean proof that uses `Int.ediv_zero` silently fails to go through.

Catches reusing `div`/`mod` for `Nat`. There is no `Nat` division in LOGOS at all (prelude.rs:529-552 registers `Nat`, `Zero`, `Succ` and nothing else), and the primitive hook matches `Literal::Int`/`BigInt` operands only via `lit_bigint` (term.rs:59-63), which returns `None` for `Literal::Nat`. See T10-004.
oracle: For every Lean `/` or `%` on `Int` in the file, the emitted term either (a) is a translator-emitted wrapper whose `normalize` on literal arguments agrees with Lean's value on ALL SIXTEEN sign/divisibility combinations below, or (b) is absent and a rejection was reported. A bare `App(App(Global("div"), a), b)` translating a Lean `/` is a FAILURE. The loss record must contain ROUNDING_CONVENTION_MISMATCH and NO_DIVISION_LAWS.
loss: ROUNDING_CONVENTION_MISMATCH. Lean 4's `Div Int` / `Mod Int` instances are `Int.ediv` / `Int.emod` — EUCLIDEAN division, whose defining property is that the remainder is always NON-NEGATIVE (`Int.emod_nonneg`). LOGOS's `div`/`mod` are TRUNCATED (T-division), whose remainder carries the dividend's sign. The two agree whenever the dividend is non-negative and disagree on every negative dividend not exactly divisible: Lean  `(-7) / 2 = -4`   LOGOS `div (-7) 2 ⤳ -3` Lean  `(-7) % 2 =  1`   LOGOS `mod (-7) 2 ⤳ -1` Lean  `7 / (-2) = -3`   LOGOS `div 7 (-2) ⤳ -3`   (agree) Lean  `7 % (-2) =  1`   LOGOS `mod 7 (-2) ⤳  1`   (agree) So the quotient differs only when the DIVIDEND is negative, and the remainder's SIGN differs in exactly the same cases. A faithful translation of Lean's `/` and `%` must therefore emit a wrapper, not the bare primitive.

NO_DIVISION_LAWS. `div` and `mod` are `add_declaration`s (prelude.rs:380-381) with no axioms at all, so nothing about them is PROVABLE on symbolic arguments — not `a = (a / b) * b + a % b`, not `0 ≤ a % b`, not `a % b < b`. They compute on literals via the reduction hook and are inert otherwise. Every Lean lemma about `Int.ediv`/`Int.emod` must be re-proved from literal computation or rejected.
note: INDEX lists this as `degrade`, which is right for `Int.tdiv`/`Int.tmod` (a faithful map onto `div`/`mod`, losing only the laws). For Lean's `/` and `%` — the operations that actually appear in source — the honest verdict is closer to `reject` unless the translator emits the correction wrapper, because the bare mapping is not lossy, it is WRONG. This file is kept at `degrade` on the reading that emitting the wrapper is a real translation and the loss is NO_DIVISION_LAWS; a translator that emits the bare primitive must be scored as failing the oracle, not as degrading.

cases.title: LOGOS is CUMULATIVE and Lean 4 is not — the target kernel accepts terms the source language rejects
cases.lean: Type 0 / Type 1 ascription, Prop used where Type 0 is expected, Pi variance, universe-level mismatch
cases.target: (none — the Lean source these terms come from is itself ill-typed, so there is nothing faithful to emit)
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1330-1360 (`is_subtype_normalized` — its own doc comment: "Cumulativity lives ONLY here: universes follow `Prop ≤ Type i ≤ Type j`, and a `Π` is contravariant in its domain and covariant in its codomain"); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1299-1323 (`is_subtype`, whose doc comment lists the admitted judgements verbatim: `Type 0 <= Type 1`, `Nat -> Type 0 <= Nat -> Type 1`, `Type 1 -> Nat <= Type 0 -> Nat`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:505-513 (`check_type` ends in `is_subtype(ctx, &inferred, expected)` — so EVERY checking position, including a function ARGUMENT via `infer_type`'s `Term::App` arm at :163, is cumulative); kernel/src/term.rs:405-416 and :282-294 (`level_leq` decides the order over the ℕ-model where `Prop = 0` and `Type n = n+1`, so `Prop ≤ Type 0` holds); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1333 (`(Sort(u1), Sort(u2)) => u1.is_subtype_of(u2)` — the single line that admits all of it); Lean 4 by contrast has NO cumulativity: `Type 0` and `Type 1` are unrelated and `Prop` is not `Type 0` (the error texts are reproduced below)
guards: ### TIER 11 THESIS — THIS CASE IS ITS CLEANEST INSTANCE. **Because LOGOS is cumulative where Lean is not, because `add_inductive` / `add_constructor` are unchecked, and because `types_equal` treats `Term::Hole` as matching anything, LOGOS's kernel accepting a term is NOT evidence that the translation is faithful.** A translator must carry its OWN faithfulness oracle; it cannot outsource that to the target kernel. Every other case in this tier is a different route to the same conclusion. Here the mechanism is one line: `is_subtype_normalized`'s `Sort`/`Sort` arm (type_checker.rs:1333). The tempting workflow — "translate, then run LOGOS `infer_type`, and if it passes we are done" — has a strictly larger acceptance set than Lean's elaborator. So a translator bug that emits a term one universe off, or that confuses `Prop` with `Type 0`, is INVISIBLE to that workflow. It is not merely that the check is weak: the check is being asked to certify a property (this term is the Lean source's meaning) that it was never designed to decide.

Catches the specific silent repair: "the universes did not line up, so I inserted a lift / dropped the level annotation, and it typechecked". In LOGOS a dropped level annotation frequently still typechecks by cumulativity. In Lean it would not. The translator must compare against LEAN's judgement, recorded at translation time, not against LOGOS's acceptance.

Catches over-generalising the leniency. Cumulativity applies at the top level of a checking position, and INVARIANTLY inside a type application: `is_subtype_normalized` delegates every non-`Sort`, non-`Pi` shape to `def_eq_normalized` (type_checker.rs:1358-1360), so `F Prop` is NOT a subtype of `F (Type 0)`. A translator that assumes cumulativity is uniform will emit terms that are rejected for the opposite reason, and will then "fix" them with a `Term::Hole` — which `types_equal` accepts against anything (:1594-1597). Two bugs compose into a passing build. See T11-004.

Catches the `Prop ≤ Type 0` direction in particular, which is also the off-by-one of T11-002 seen from the other side: LOGOS says `Prop : Type 1` (term.rs:196-202) AND `Prop ≤ Type 0` (term.rs:282-294). Lean says `Prop : Type 0` and admits no subtyping at all. There is no consistent reading under which a `Prop`/`Type 0` confusion is harmless.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_TARGET_MORE_PERMISSIVE for each commented form below, emits nothing, and — decisively — a harness re-checks that for every case in the WHOLE corpus, the translator's accept/reject decision was made by its own universe check and not by calling LOGOS `infer_type`. A translator whose only universe oracle is the target kernel fails this tier by construction.
diag: E_TARGET_MORE_PERMISSIVE(cumulativity) — must state that the LOGOS kernel accepting the emitted term proves nothing about the Lean source, name the specific universe judgement that Lean refused, and produce no output. The diagnostic must be raised by the TRANSLATOR's own check, because the target kernel will not raise it.

cases.title: The sort of `Prop` itself — Lean says `Prop : Type 0`, LOGOS's `succ` says `Prop : Type 1`, and LOGOS's OWN level model says `Type 0`
cases.lean: Prop, Sort 0, Type 0, `#check Prop`, a term whose type is the type of Prop
cases.target: (none — there is no level to emit that is right under both of LOGOS's own universe procedures)
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:196-202 (`Universe::succ`: `Universe::SProp | Universe::Prop => Universe::Type(1)`, `Type(n) => Type(n+1)`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:54 (`Term::Sort(u) => Ok(Term::Sort(u.succ()))` — the ONLY place a sort's type is computed, so `infer_type(Sort(Prop))` is `Sort(Type 1)`); kernel/src/recheck.rs:802 (the de Bruijn re-checker computes it the same way, so the second kernel does not catch it); kernel/src/term.rs:282-294 (`to_lnat` — the ℕ-ENCODING the decision core runs over: `Prop => Const(0)`, `Type(n) => Const(n+1)`, and its own doc comment at :276-281 says "`Prop = 0`, `Type n = n+1` … This mirrors Lean's level model"); kernel/src/term.rs:405-416 (`level_leq` = `lnat_leq(simp_lnat(to_lnat(a)), simp_lnat(to_lnat(b)))`), and term.rs:243-249 / :250-254 (`is_subtype_of` and `equiv` are BOTH defined as `level_leq` — so the ℕ-model is the sole arbiter of the level ORDER)
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS.** LOGOS's kernel accepting a term is NOT evidence that the translation is faithful. Here the target kernel is not merely more permissive than Lean (T11-001) — it is INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT, by one, about exactly one universe. Walk it: · `Universe::succ` (term.rs:196-202) sends `Prop ↦ Type(1)`. · `to_lnat` (term.rs:282-294) sends `Prop ↦ 0` and `Type n ↦ n+1`. · In that ℕ-model the successor of `Prop` is `0 + 1 = 1`, and `1` is the encoding of `Type 0`. So under the model that `level_leq` — hence `is_subtype_of`, hence `equiv`, hence EVERY universe comparison the kernel makes — decides over, `succ(Prop)` ought to be `Type(0)`. `succ` says `Type(1)`. The two procedures disagree by one, about `Prop` only. A translator cannot pick a level that is right in both, because the kernel is asking two different questions in two different places, and no emitted term changes either.

Catches "just follow LOGOS: emit `Prop : Type 1`." Lean says `Prop : Type 0`, so every Lean declaration whose type mentions the type of `Prop` — a universe- polymorphic statement instantiated at `u := 0`, a `Sort u`-valued family, anything quantifying over `Sort 0` — comes out one level too high. And because the emitted level is too HIGH, cumulativity (T11-001) will usually accept it anyway: `Type 1` is a supertype of nothing that helps, but a use site expecting `Type 1` will take a `Type 0` happily, so the mismatch surfaces only in the rarer direction.

Catches "just follow Lean: emit `Prop : Type 0`." Then `infer_type` on the emitted `Sort(Prop)` returns `Sort(Type 1)` regardless — `type_checker.rs:54` is not configurable — so the translator's recorded type and the kernel's inferred type differ. Any translator that checks round-tripping ("`infer_type` of the emitted term equals the translation of Lean's type") will report a failure it cannot fix, and the tempting repair is to stop checking round-tripping. That repair disables the faithfulness oracle for the whole corpus.

Catches hoping the second kernel catches it. `recheck.rs` is a deliberate `lean4checker` analogue using de Bruijn indices, and it computes the sort of a sort with the SAME `u.succ()` (recheck.rs:802). Independent re-checking does not help when both checkers share the level algebra.

Catches the `SProp` confusion riding along. `Universe::succ` sends `SProp` to `Type(1)` too (term.rs:198), and `to_lnat` sends `SProp` to `0` as a "never-hit fallback" (term.rs:284-286) while `level_leq` special-cases `SProp` BEFORE the ℕ-encoding (term.rs:409-414). So `SProp` has three different treatments in three places, in a sort that nothing in LOGOS can construct or declare (T01-013). Anything a translator emits at `SProp` is untestable.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_TARGET_UNIVERSE_SEMANTICS_INCONSISTENT(Prop) for every declaration below whose typing depends on the sort of `Prop`, and emits nothing. A harness additionally asserts the discrepancy directly against the target: `Universe::Prop.succ()` must equal `Universe::Type(1)` while `level_leq(Universe::Prop.succ(), Universe::Type(0))` is FALSE and `level_leq(Universe::Type(0), Universe::Prop.succ())` is TRUE — i.e. the kernel itself reports `succ(Prop)` as strictly above `Type 0`, one level higher than its own ℕ-model puts it.
diag: E_TARGET_UNIVERSE_SEMANTICS_INCONSISTENT(Prop) — must state that LOGOS's successor operation and LOGOS's own level-ordering procedure disagree about `Prop`, by one, and that neither choice of emitted level is faithful to Lean in every position. Must produce no output for any declaration whose typing depends on the sort of `Prop`.

cases.title: Flat-name collision — the kernel TYPES a name from one map and REDUCES it from another, silently
cases.lean: hierarchical Name, namespace, `Foo.bar` vs a top-level `Foo_bar`, `_root_`, `export`, `open ... in`
cases.target: (none — two distinct Lean declarations cannot share one LOGOS key)
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:449-464 (`get_global` — the lookup precedence, in order: `self.inductives` → `self.constructors` → `self.definitions` → `self.declarations`. FIRST MATCH WINS across four PARALLEL maps, all keyed by flat `String`); kernel/src/context.rs:442-444 (`add_definition` inserts into `self.definitions` with no check against the other maps — and, note, with no check that `body : ty` either); kernel/src/context.rs:253 (`add_inductive` inserts into `self.inductives`, likewise unchecked); kernel/src/context.rs:474 (`get_definition_body` reads `self.definitions` DIRECTLY — it does not go through `get_global` and therefore does not respect its precedence); kernel/src/reduction.rs:305-314 (delta reduction: `Term::Global(name) => if let Some(body) = ctx.get_definition_body(name) { body.clone() } else { term.clone() }` — the reducer consults `definitions` ONLY); LOGOS_FACTS: LOGOS keys have no namespaces, no `Name` type, no visibility and no attributes
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS.** LOGOS's kernel accepting a term is NOT evidence that the translation is faithful. This case is the sharpest demonstration, because the kernel does not merely accept a wrong term — IT DISAGREES WITH ITSELF ABOUT ONE NAME. Concretely: a Lean inductive `Foo_bar` and a Lean definition `Foo.bar` both flatten to the key `"Foo_bar"`. `add_inductive` puts the first in `context.inductives`; `add_definition` puts the second in `context.definitions`. Nothing complains: the maps are parallel and neither insertion checks the other. Now the kernel splits in two. · TYPING goes through `get_global` (context.rs:449-464), which checks `inductives` FIRST — so `Foo_bar` has the INDUCTIVE's type. · REDUCTION goes through `get_definition_body` (context.rs:474), called directly from the delta rule (reduction.rs:305-314), which reads `definitions` ONLY — so `Foo_bar` unfolds to the DEFINITION's body. The same `Term::Global("Foo_bar")` therefore has one type and a completely unrelated value. `infer_type` succeeds. `normalize` succeeds. They are describing different objects. No error is raised at any point, and no amount of re-checking helps, because the inconsistency is in the environment, not in the term.

Catches the "namespaces are just sugar" assumption. In Lean, `Foo.bar` and `Foo_bar` are DIFFERENT names that can both exist in one file, and `_root_.Foo_bar` can exist alongside a `Foo.bar` in an open namespace. Flattening with `.` ↦ `_` is not injective. Neither is stripping the namespace: `List.map` and `Array.map` both become `map`.

Catches the collision that is invisible in the SOURCE. The two colliding declarations need not be in the same file, or written by the same person; the second may arrive from a dependency, or from the translator's own emitted support code (a `List_map` emitted for T10-012 colliding with a user's `List.map`). A translator must maintain a global injective key map, and must fail when it cannot extend it.

Catches colliding with the PRELUDE. `StandardLibrary::register` occupies bare keys including `Nat`, `Int`, `Bool`, `true`, `false`, `Eq`, `refl`, `And`, `Or`, `Ex`, `add`, `sub`, `mul`, `div`, `mod`, `le`, `lt` (prelude.rs:352-381, :529-552, :593-604, and throughout). A Lean file with a top-level `def add` flattens onto the prelude's `Int` addition axiom — which lands in `declarations`, the LAST map `get_global` checks (context.rs:463), so the user's definition WINS for typing while the primitive reduction hook in `try_primitive_reduce` (reduction.rs:444-506) still fires on the name `"add"` for literal operands. Typing and reduction disagree again, now against the trusted base.

Catches the mangling that merely moves the problem. Appending a hash or a counter is fine for soundness and terrible for certificates: `PRELUDE_VERSION` pins the trusted base (certificate.rs:28) but nothing pins the translator's mangling, so two runs of the translator can produce two different key sets for one Lean input and the certificates will not be comparable. See T11-015.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NAME_COLLISION_AFTER_FLATTENING for the pairs below and emits nothing. A harness additionally asserts, over the whole corpus output, that (a) the map from Lean `Name` to LOGOS key is injective, and (b) no emitted key appears in more than one of `inductives` / `constructors` / `definitions` / `declarations`, and (c) no emitted key collides with a name registered by `StandardLibrary::register`.
diag: E_NAME_COLLISION_AFTER_FLATTENING — must name BOTH colliding Lean declarations, print the single LOGOS key they map to, say which of the four maps each would land in, and emit nothing. A mangling scheme that avoids the collision is acceptable ONLY if the translator proves it injective over the whole input.

cases.title: `Term::Hole` in emitted output — `types_equal` matches it against ANYTHING, so one `Hole` disables type checking wherever it sits
cases.lean: `_` placeholder, metavariable `?m`, implicit argument left unsolved, `sorry`-free elaboration that postpones, `@f _ _ x`
cases.target: (none — a `Hole` must never reach the kernel; the translator must instantiate every placeholder before emitting)
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1592-1597 (`types_equal`: "Hole matches anything (it's a type wildcard)" — `if matches!(a, Term::Hole) || matches!(b, Term::Hole) { return true; }`, BEFORE any structural comparison); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1310-1315 (`is_subtype`'s FAST PATH is `if types_equal(a, b) { return true; }` — so the `Hole` leniency leaks straight into subtyping, ahead of normalisation and ahead of `is_subtype_normalized`); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:505-513 (`check_type` ends in `is_subtype`, so every checking position inherits it); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:454-470 (`check_type`'s own two `Hole` short-circuits: a `Hole` TERM is accepted whenever the expected type is any `Sort`, and a `Hole` EXPECTED TYPE accepts any well-typed term); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:311-313 (`infer_type` on a bare `Hole` is `Err(KernelError::CannotInferHole)` — the ONLY place a `Hole` is refused, and it is reachable only when the `Hole` is in HEAD position, never when it is an argument or a binder type); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1103-1104 (`substitute_avoiding`: "Holes are never substituted", so a `Hole` survives every reduction); kernel/src/elaborate.rs:138 (elaborator metavariables are `Term::Var` names starting with `?`, NOT `Term::Hole` — so the two placeholder mechanisms are different and a translator that conflates them emits the wrong one)
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS, IN ITS PUREST FORM.** LOGOS's kernel accepting a term is NOT evidence that the translation is faithful — and a single `Term::Hole` is the proof, because it turns the kernel's verdict into an unconditional "yes" at that position. `types_equal` returns `true` before looking at either side (:1594-1597), and `is_subtype` calls it FIRST, before normalising (:1314). So `is_subtype(Hole, T)` and `is_subtype(T, Hole)` hold for every `T` whatsoever — including terms that are not types, including `False`, including a type from a different inductive family. A translator that emits a `Hole` for an implicit argument it could not resolve has not produced an under-specified term that the kernel will complete; it has produced a term whose typecheck is a no-op at that position.

Catches "the `Hole` is only in a TYPE argument, which is erased anyway". It is not erased — LOGOS has no erasure — and the type argument is exactly where it does the most damage: `Eq Hole a b` typechecks for ANY `a` and `b`, of any two different types, because `check_type(a, Hole)` succeeds for any well-typed `a` (type_checker.rs:466-470). That is heterogeneous equality by accident, in a kernel that deliberately has no `HEq` (T06-016).

Catches the `Hole` that arrives by "helpful" repair. The realistic path is: a term fails to typecheck because of a universe mismatch (T11-001) or a missing structural type (T10-013); the translator patches the offending position with a `Hole` to get past it; the build goes green. Two bugs compose into a passing build, and the second one hides the first.

Catches the `Hole` that SURVIVES normalisation. `substitute_avoiding` explicitly does not substitute into a `Hole` (type_checker.rs:1103-1104), and `normalize`'s base case returns it unchanged (reduction.rs:302). So a `Hole` emitted once stays in the term forever, and every later `def_eq` against that subterm is vacuously true — including inside a certificate that is then re-checked by `recheck.rs` and passes.

Catches conflating `Term::Hole` with the elaborator's metavariables. LOGOS's elaborator represents an unsolved metavariable as a `Term::Var` whose name begins with `?` (elaborate.rs:138), NOT as `Term::Hole`, and such a name must be fully instantiated before the kernel sees the term. A `?`-named `Var` that reaches the kernel is an UNBOUND VARIABLE and errors loudly; a `Hole` that reaches the kernel is accepted silently. The failure modes are opposite, so the choice of placeholder decides whether the bug is caught or hidden.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_HOLE_IN_OUTPUT for any declaration it cannot fully instantiate, and the decisive harness assertion is structural, not behavioural: the emitted term tree for EVERY case in the whole corpus must contain zero `Term::Hole` nodes. Because the kernel cannot detect a `Hole`, this check must be performed by the translator's own serialiser, on the term it is about to hand over.
diag: E_HOLE_IN_OUTPUT — must name the declaration and the position of the `Hole`, state that `types_equal` matches a `Hole` against anything so the kernel's acceptance of the term is meaningless, and emit nothing.

cases.title: `normalize` has a hard fuel of 10000 and returns the PARTIALLY reduced term without saying so
cases.lean: deep computation by `rfl` / `decide`, Nat.pow, Ackermann-ish recursion, long unfolding chains, `Nat.rec` over a large literal
cases.target: The faithful term, PLUS a loss record naming the reduction-budget boundary. There is no LOGOS knob to raise the fuel — it is a literal in the loop.
evidence: kernel/src/reduction.rs:52-69 (`normalize`: `let mut fuel = 10000; loop { if fuel == 0 { /* If we hit the fuel limit, return what we have */ return current; } fuel -= 1; let reduced = reduce_step(ctx, &current); if reduced == current { return current; } current = reduced; }` — the exhausted branch and the normal-form branch return the SAME shape of value, `Term`, with no flag, no `Result`, and no way for a caller to tell them apart); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1310-1323 (`is_subtype` normalises both sides then compares — so an exhausted normalisation makes a TRUE subtyping judgement come out FALSE); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1465-1520 (`def_eq_normalized` likewise); kernel/src/reduction.rs:329-345 (the Peano bridge peels ONE `Succ` per step, so a `Nat` recursion costs one unit of fuel per unit of the numeral); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:890-902 (`substitute`'s fast path avoids recomputing `free_vars` when the variable does not occur — but each step that DOES substitute is O(size), so fuel is consumed by steps of growing cost, see T11-007)
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS.** LOGOS's kernel accepting a term is not evidence of faithfulness — and here the kernel's REJECTION is not evidence of unfaithfulness either. A `def_eq` that answers `false` because the fuel ran out looks exactly like a `def_eq` that answers `false` because the terms differ. A translator that treats "LOGOS says these are not definitionally equal" as a reason to go back and change the translation will change a CORRECT translation into an incorrect one that happens to normalise faster.

Catches the silent-truncation failure mode in its worst direction. Because the exhausted result is a partially reduced term, `def_eq(a, b)` on two terms that reduce to the same normal form in 12000 steps returns `false` — a false NEGATIVE, which merely loses a proof. But `def_eq(a, b)` on two DIFFERENT terms that happen to agree on their first 10000 steps of reduction returns `true` — a false POSITIVE, which accepts a wrong proof. The second is rare and is the reason the loss record must name the boundary rather than just "some proofs may fail".

Catches the "expand it for clarity" move that pushes a case over the line. Emitting a `Nat` literal as `Succ^n Zero` (T10-015), inlining a definition at each use site instead of emitting one `add_definition` (T03-011), or spelling out a wildcard pattern as one case per constructor (T04-010) each multiply the step count, and any of them can turn a 3000-step reduction into a 30000-step one. A translator must account for the budget when it chooses an encoding, not only when it emits a term.

Catches assuming the fuel is per-call in a helpful way. It is per `normalize` call, and `is_subtype` calls `normalize` twice (reduction.rs:52-69 via type_checker.rs:1318-1322), and `def_eq_normalized` recurses structurally calling `def_eq` on subterms — so the effective budget for a large term is neither 10000 nor a simple multiple of it, and a translator cannot compute it exactly. The honest record is "this declaration's reduction is within an order of magnitude of the budget", not a precise step count.
oracle: The emitted term is the faithful one, AND a loss record with category REDUCTION_BUDGET is produced for each declaration whose estimated `reduce_step` count exceeds a configured fraction of 10000. A harness runs the emitted `def_eq` checks against the target and asserts that every one the translator predicted would succeed did succeed; a `def_eq` failure that the translator did NOT predict is a corpus failure, not a target limitation.
loss: REDUCTION_BUDGET. Lean's kernel has no step limit on whnf; it has a `maxRecDepth`/`maxHeartbeats` that ERROR when exceeded. LOGOS's `normalize` has a step limit that SUCCEEDS when exceeded, returning a partially reduced term. So a Lean proof by `rfl` whose reduction takes more than 10000 `reduce_step` calls does not translate to a proof by reflexivity in LOGOS — it translates to a term whose `def_eq` check answers "not equal". The loss record must state the budget (10000), name the declaration, and give the translator's own estimate of the step count.

NO_DIAGNOSTIC_FROM_TARGET. The boundary is not observable from LOGOS's API: an exhausted `normalize` and a completed `normalize` are indistinguishable to the caller. The translator must therefore carry its own step accounting; it cannot ask the kernel afterwards.

cases.title: Variable capture under the NAMED representation — Lean's de Bruijn binders carry no identity, LOGOS's carry nothing else
cases.lean: nested binders sharing a name, `Expr.bvar` / `Expr.fvar`, shadowing, hygienic macro-generated names, `variable` + `section`
cases.target: (none for a term the translator has not freshened — the obligation is to emit a globally freshened term, and to refuse rather than emit a term it cannot prove capture-free)
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term::Var(String)` — NAMED, not de Bruijn; there is no `bvar`/`fvar` distinction and no binder identity beyond the string); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1088-1140 (`substitute_avoiding` — capture avoidance exists, and its doc comment says exactly when it fires: "When a binder (`Pi`/ `Lambda`/`Fix`) would capture a free variable of `replacement`, the binder is alpha-renamed"); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1113-1121 (the SHADOWING arm: "The parameter shadows `var`: do not substitute in the body" — so an inner binder with the SAME NAME silently stops the substitution, which is correct for a well-scoped term and catastrophic for a mis-scoped one); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:890-899 (`substitute`'s fast path: `if !occurs_free(body, var) { return body.clone(); }` — the capture-avoidance machinery is not even reached when the translator's name choice makes the occurrence check answer wrongly); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1061-1071 (`freshen` avoids `replacement_fvs` ∪ `all_var_names(body)` ∪ `{var}` — it is sound for the substitution it is performing, and knows nothing about names the TRANSLATOR intends to introduce later); kernel/src/recheck.rs (the second kernel deliberately uses de Bruijn, which is the repo's own acknowledgement that the named representation is the fragile one)
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS.** LOGOS's kernel accepting a term is not evidence of faithfulness. A captured variable produces a term that is PERFECTLY WELL TYPED — it just denotes a different function. `fun x => fun x => x` and `fun x => fun y => x` are both well-typed; they are different functions; and in Lean they are `fun _ => fun _ => bvar 0` and `fun _ => fun _ => bvar 1`, which a translator that drops the index and keeps the hint name collapses into one. The kernel cannot possibly object: both results are terms it was designed to accept.

Catches the naive `Expr.bvar i ↦ Term::Var(binderName i)` lowering. Lean's binder names are HINTS with no uniqueness guarantee: `∀ (n : Nat) (n : Fin n), …` is legal Lean, `variable`-inserted binders routinely repeat, and macro hygiene means two binders can share a display name while being distinct. The de Bruijn INDEX is the identity; the name is decoration. Lowering must allocate a fresh name per binder and record the mapping, not reuse the hint.

Catches capture introduced by the TRANSLATOR's own generated names. Emitting support code (a `List` for T10-012, a projection for T03-011, a recursor motive) introduces binders the source never had. `freshen` (type_checker.rs:1061-1071) protects the substitution it is currently performing against names present in the term at that moment; it cannot protect against a name the translator will emit into a different subterm later. The freshening obligation is GLOBAL to the emitted declaration, not local to a substitution.

Catches the SHADOWING arm being mistaken for capture avoidance. When the binder name equals the substituted variable, `substitute_avoiding` deliberately stops descending (type_checker.rs:1113-1121). That is correct — the inner binder shadows — but it means a translator bug that gives an inner binder the same name as an outer one does not produce a capture error; it produces a substitution that silently does nothing, so the outer variable's value never reaches the body that was supposed to use it.

Catches trusting the fast path. `substitute` returns `body.clone()` unchanged when `occurs_free(body, var)` is false (type_checker.rs:897-899). If the translator has already collapsed two distinct binders onto one name, `occurs_free` answers about the wrong binder, the fast path fires, and the capture-avoidance code at :1088 is never reached at all.
oracle: The decisive check is structural and belongs to the translator: in the emitted term for every case in the corpus, no `Pi`/`Lambda`/`Fix`/`Let` binder name may shadow an enclosing binder of the same name, and every `Term::Var` must resolve to the nearest enclosing binder that the Lean de Bruijn index designated. A harness verifies this by round-tripping the emitted named term back to de Bruijn and comparing against Lean's original `Expr` up to alpha — not by asking LOGOS `infer_type`, which accepts both the captured and the uncaptured term.
diag: E_CAPTURE_RISK — must name the declaration, the binder, and the colliding name, and emit nothing. A translator that freshens correctly need never raise this; a translator that cannot prove its output capture-free must raise it rather than emit.
note: This file compiles with `unusedVariables` warnings on the shadowed binders. Those warnings ARE the case's subject: Lean is reporting that an outer binder is unreachable because an inner binder of the same name shadows it. Renaming the binders to silence them would delete the phenomenon under test, so they are left in deliberately and no `set_option` is used to suppress them.

cases.title: Quadratic substitution on a deep telescope — the named representation's cost, and how it interacts with the reduction budget
cases.lean: long dependent telescope, 5000-deep application spine, `variable`-heavy sections, a structure with very many fields, Mathlib-style bundled algebra
cases.target: The faithful term, PLUS a loss record naming the substitution-cost class. There is no sharing in `Term` and no de Bruijn representation available at the kernel API.
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:890-902 (`substitute`: the fast path is `if !occurs_free(body, var) { return body.clone(); }`, and the doc comment explains it exists to turn "quadratic checking (walk the giant argument at every application) into linear" for the NON-dependent case — i.e. the quadratic behaviour is acknowledged and only mitigated where the bound variable does not occur); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1088-1140 (`substitute_avoiding` walks the whole body and rebuilds it, and `free_vars(replacement)` is computed once per substitution at :902); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1061-1071 (`freshen` calls `all_var_names(body, &mut avoid)` — a full traversal of the binder's body — EVERY time a capture-avoiding rename is needed); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:163-166 (`infer_type`'s `App` arm: `check_type(ctx, arg, &param_type)?` then `substitute(&body_type, &param, arg)` — one substitution of the WHOLE argument per application node, so an n-deep spine performs n substitutions into a body that grows with each one); kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term` is a `Box`-ed TREE — there is no DAG, no hash consing, and no sharing, so a substituted argument is CLONED at every occurrence); kernel/src/reduction.rs:52-69 (`normalize`'s 10000-step fuel, which the growing term consumes faster and faster — see T11-005)
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS.** LOGOS's kernel accepting a term is not evidence of faithfulness, and here it is not even evidence that the kernel finished the job. The interaction to guard is with T11-005: substitution cost is paid in `reduce_step` calls, and `normalize`'s fuel is a hard 10000 that returns the PARTIALLY reduced term with no error (reduction.rs:52-69). So a deep telescope does not merely translate slowly — past a threshold it translates to a term whose `def_eq` checks answer "false" because the budget ran out, and the translator sees a type error where there is none.

Catches the mitigation being mistaken for a fix. `substitute`'s fast path (type_checker.rs:897-899) skips the work only when the bound variable does NOT occur in the body — the non-dependent case. A DEPENDENT telescope, which is exactly what a bundled algebraic structure or a `variable`-heavy section produces, defeats the fast path at every level, because each binder's type mentions the previous binders. The optimisation's own doc comment says so.

Catches the capture-avoidance amplification. When a rename IS needed, `freshen` traverses the binder's whole body to collect `all_var_names` (type_checker.rs:1061-1071), and then `rename_var` performs ANOTHER full substitution pass (:1075-1080) before the real substitution descends. A translator that reuses Lean's binder-name hints (T11-006) makes collisions common and therefore makes this path the norm rather than the exception — turning a constant factor into the dominant cost.

Catches "just inline it" as a size remedy. Inlining a definition instead of emitting one `add_definition` removes a delta step but multiplies term size, which makes every enclosing substitution more expensive and brings the fuel boundary closer. The encodings chosen for T10-012 (emitted `List`), T03-011 (projection as a `Match`-bodied definition) and T04-010 (wildcard expanded to every constructor) all trade in this currency, and the translator must budget across them rather than locally.

Catches reporting this as a `translate` with a footnote. The verdict is `degrade` because the emitted term is faithful but the target cannot carry the source's sharing, and because past a threshold the faithful term is not CHECKABLE. A translator that emits it and reports success without the loss record has told the user that a declaration was translated when what was actually produced may not typecheck in a reasonable budget.
oracle: The emitted term is the faithful one, AND a loss record with categories SUBSTITUTION_COST and SHARING_IS_LOST naming the telescope depth and the emitted term's node count. A harness asserts that the translator's predicted node count is within a factor of two of the actual emitted tree size, and that every declaration it predicted would typecheck within budget did so.
loss: SUBSTITUTION_COST. Lean's `Expr` is a hash-consed DAG with de Bruijn indices, so instantiation is cheap and sharing is preserved. LOGOS's `Term` is a named tree, substitution is O(size of body) per binder, and every occurrence of the replacement is a full clone. A telescope of depth n therefore costs O(n · size) to type and the term's size can grow multiplicatively. The loss record must name the depth and the translator's size estimate; "it may be slow" is not a loss record.

SHARING_IS_LOST. This is T00-022's loss showing through at scale: a Lean `Expr` in which one subterm is referenced 100 times becomes a LOGOS `Term` containing 100 copies. The two losses compound — more copies means larger bodies means more expensive substitutions.

cases.title: The `Nat` literal / Peano bridge boundary — where the acceleration stops being an acceleration
cases.lean: Nat literal as a match scrutinee, Nat.rec on a literal, arithmetic on large numerals, `decide` over a `Nat` proposition
cases.target: `Term::Lit(Literal::Nat(n))` throughout, never the expanded `Succ^n Zero`, PLUS a loss record naming the step-cost boundary the bridge does not remove.
evidence: kernel/src/term.rs:38-44 (`Literal::Nat(BigInt)` is "DEFINITIONALLY EQUAL to `Succ` applied `n` times to `Zero`" and "stores the count as one `BigInt` instead of `n` heap nodes"); kernel/src/reduction.rs:329-345 (`extract_constructor`'s bridge — note what it actually does: `Nat(n)` yields `Succ`'s index with the single argument `Lit(Nat(n-1))`. It peels ONE `Succ` PER CALL. The acceleration is in the REPRESENTATION, not in the reduction: a match that recurses down to `Zero` still takes n steps); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1480-1493 (the `def_eq` side: two literals compare by `BigInt` equality in O(1) at :1485, but a literal against a `Zero`/`Succ`-headed TERM is compared by `nat_peano_step` one `Succ` at a time at :1486-1491); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1430-1440 (`nat_peano_step` builds `App(Global("Succ"), Lit(Nat(n-1)))` — one step, one allocation); kernel/src/reduction.rs:52-69 (`normalize`'s hard 10000-step fuel, silently partial); kernel/src/reduction.rs:337-341 (the negative clamp: `n ≤ 0` yields `Zero`, "so the peel TERMINATES rather than descending toward −∞"); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:297-301 (`infer_type` REJECTS a negative `Literal::Nat`)
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS.** The kernel's acceptance is not evidence of faithfulness, and here the specific trap is that the bridge LOOKS like it makes the two representations interchangeable, so a translator stops distinguishing them.
