They are definitionally equal and operationally very different. Emitting `Succ^n Zero` wherever a literal would do is definitionally correct and blows the budget (T11-005); emitting a literal where the source had an explicit `Nat.succ` application is also definitionally correct and changes which `def_eq` path runs. Neither is caught.

Catches the bridge being severed by a re-declared `Nat`. `extract_constructor` looks the constructor indices up BY NAME at reduction time — `idx_of("Zero")` and `idx_of("Succ")` against `ctx.get_constructors("Nat")` (reduction.rs:332-344). A translator that emits its own `Nat` (because it flattened a namespace, or because it declared `Nat` fresh rather than reusing the prelude's) makes `idx_of` return `None`, every literal silently stops being constructor-form, and every `Match` on a literal becomes stuck — which `normalize` reports as a normal form. See T11-003.

Catches the constructor ORDER assumption. The bridge uses the registration positions of `"Zero"` and `"Succ"` (reduction.rs:333-344), and `Match` is positional (type_checker.rs:254-260). The prelude registers `Zero` then `Succ` (prelude.rs:536-551), which agrees with Lean's `Nat.zero` then `Nat.succ` — so this one happens to line up, unlike `Bool` (T10-008). A translator must verify the agreement rather than assume it.

Catches the NEGATIVE boundary, which behaves differently in the two halves of the bridge. A negative `Literal::Nat` is REFUSED by `infer_type` (type_checker.rs:297-301) but CLAMPED TO `Zero` by `extract_constructor` (reduction.rs:337-341). So a negative literal that reaches the kernel errors when typed and computes as zero when matched on. If a translator emits one — e.g. by translating a `Nat` subtraction with the `Int` primitive (T10-017) and re-typing the result — the same term is simultaneously ill-typed and well-behaved, depending on which kernel entry point is called first.

Catches assuming the bridge exists in only one kernel. `Literal::Nat`'s own documentation says the bridge is implemented "in BOTH kernels" (term.rs:41-43), so `recheck.rs` will not catch a bridge-dependent error either — the independent re-check shares the acceleration.
oracle: Every `Nat` numeral in the output is a `Term::Lit(Literal::Nat)`, never an application spine of `Succ`; the emitted `Nat` uses the PRELUDE's `Nat`/`Zero`/`Succ` globals so `extract_constructor`'s name lookup resolves; no emitted `Literal::Nat` carries a negative value; and a loss record with categories BRIDGE_IS_REPRESENTATIONAL_NOT_COMPUTATIONAL and ASYMMETRIC_DEFEQ_COST names the per-declaration step ceiling.
loss: BRIDGE_IS_REPRESENTATIONAL_NOT_COMPUTATIONAL. The bridge makes `Nat(1000000)` cost one node instead of a million, and makes literal-versus-literal equality O(1). It does NOT make `Nat` recursion cheap: `extract_constructor` peels exactly one `Succ` per call (reduction.rs:337-344), so any function defined by recursion on a `Nat` — which, in LOGOS, is EVERY `Nat` function, because the prelude ships no `Nat` arithmetic at all (prelude.rs:529-552 registers only `Nat`/`Zero`/`Succ`) — costs one `reduce_step` per unit of its argument. Against a 10000-step budget that is a hard ceiling around n ≈ 10^4, and Lean's GMP-accelerated `Nat` operations sail past it. The loss record must state this ceiling per declaration.

ASYMMETRIC_DEFEQ_COST. `def_eq(Lit(Nat(n)), Lit(Nat(m)))` is one `BigInt` comparison (type_checker.rs:1485). `def_eq(Lit(Nat(n)), Succ^n Zero)` is n peels (:1486-1491). So the SAME mathematical fact costs O(1) or O(n) depending on which side the translator chose to emit — and the translator's encoding choice, not the source, decides whether a proof fits in the budget.

cases.title: Proof irrelevance is a LAST-RESORT rule that calls `infer_type` on both sides — so it fails exactly where it is most needed
cases.lean: proof irrelevance, two proofs of one Prop, `Subtype` elements differing only in the proof, `Subsingleton.elim`, a proof term inside a data structure
cases.target: The faithful term, PLUS a loss record naming the conditions under which LOGOS's `proof_irrelevant` will not fire.
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1545-1567 (`proof_irrelevant`: it calls `infer_type(ctx, a)`, RETURNS FALSE on any error, then calls `infer_type(ctx, &ta)` and requires the result to normalise to `Sort(Prop)` or `Sort(SProp)`, then calls `infer_type(ctx, b)` and requires `def_eq(ctx, &ta, &tb)` — three `infer_type` calls and one recursive `def_eq`, every one of which can fail); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1465-1545 (`def_eq_normalized`: structural congruence, structure eta and the Peano bridge are ALL tried first; `proof_irrelevant` is the fallback reached only after they fail); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:311-313 (`infer_type` on a bare `Term::Hole` is `Err(KernelError::CannotInferHole)` — so a `Hole` anywhere in a proof term's TYPE makes `proof_irrelevant` return `false` for that pair); kernel/src/reduction.rs:52-69 (the `def_eq(ta, tb)` inside `proof_irrelevant` normalises, so it is subject to the 10000-step fuel and can answer `false` from exhaustion); kernel/src/term.rs:170-176 and type_checker.rs:1556-1562 (`SProp` is accepted here but nothing in LOGOS ever constructs or declares an `SProp` inductive, so this arm is dead — see T01-013)
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS.** The kernel accepting a term is not evidence of faithfulness — and symmetrically, the kernel REFUSING a definitional equality is not evidence that the equality is false. Here that asymmetry is sharp: `proof_irrelevant` answering `false` can mean "these are not both proofs of the same proposition" (a real failure) or "one of my three `infer_type` calls errored" or "the `def_eq` on the types ran out of fuel". A translator that reacts to the `false` by CHANGING THE TRANSLATION — inserting a cast, weakening a type, replacing a proof with a different one — is repairing a symptom whose cause is in the target's conversion checker.

Catches the interaction with `Term::Hole` (T11-004), which is the most common way to disable irrelevance without noticing. A `Hole` makes `types_equal` return `true` (type_checker.rs:1594-1597) so the term TYPECHECKS more easily — and simultaneously makes `infer_type` return `CannotInferHole` (:311-313) so `proof_irrelevant` returns `false` and two proofs of one proposition become UNEQUAL. One `Hole` therefore makes checking more permissive and conversion more restrictive at the same time, which is a combination no single test will reveal.

Catches assuming irrelevance rescues a `Subtype` encoding. `Subtype` is absent from LOGOS and must be emitted (T10-013); `add_structure` builds it with a proof-typed FIELD (context.rs:271-369). Two elements with the same value and different proofs are equal in Lean by irrelevance plus structure eta. In LOGOS that requires `try_structure_eta` (type_checker.rs:1391-1417) AND `proof_irrelevant` (:1547-1567) both to fire, in `def_eq_normalized` and nowhere else (:1473-1478) — so the equality holds under `def_eq` and NOT under `normalize`. A proof routed through `normalize` fails; the same proof routed through `def_eq` succeeds.

Catches the `Prop`-versus-`Type` precondition being read too loosely. `proof_irrelevant` requires `infer_type(ta)` to normalise to `Sort(Prop)` specifically (type_checker.rs:1556-1562). Because LOGOS is cumulative, a proposition can legitimately be CHECKED at `Type 0` (T11-001) — and a term the translator ascribed at `Type 0` for that reason will then have `infer_type(ta) = Sort(Type 0)`, irrelevance will not fire, and two proofs will compare unequal. The cumulativity leniency and the irrelevance rule pull in opposite directions on the same term.

Catches counting on `SProp`. The rule accepts `Sort(SProp)` as well (type_checker.rs:1559), but nothing in LOGOS constructs or declares an `SProp` inductive, so that arm is unreachable and cannot be used to make irrelevance unconditional. See T01-013.
oracle: The emitted term is the faithful one, AND a loss record with categories IRRELEVANCE_IS_CONDITIONAL and IRRELEVANCE_IS_EXPENSIVE is produced for every declaration whose correctness depends on two distinct proof terms being definitionally equal. A harness asserts, for each such declaration, that LOGOS `def_eq` on the two emitted proofs returns `true` — and that the translator PREDICTED that outcome. A `def_eq` failure the translator did not predict is a corpus failure.
loss: IRRELEVANCE_IS_CONDITIONAL. Lean's kernel treats proof irrelevance as a primitive conversion rule: if `a : P` and `b : P` with `P : Prop`, then `a ≡ b`, decided cheaply and unconditionally. LOGOS's is a derived last-resort rule whose preconditions are three successful `infer_type` calls and one successful `def_eq` on the two proofs' TYPES. Whenever any of those fails — an unresolved placeholder, an expensive normalisation, a proof whose type mentions a declaration the translator emitted but whose own typing is delicate — the rule silently does not fire and two proofs of the same proposition compare UNEQUAL. The loss record must name the preconditions, not merely say "irrelevance is present".

IRRELEVANCE_IS_EXPENSIVE. Because it is the fallback, every FAILED definitional equality check in the whole development pays for three `infer_type` calls on the way to answering `false`. On a proof-heavy translation this is the dominant cost, and it compounds with T11-007's quadratic substitution and T11-005's fuel budget.

cases.title: Indexed match — LOGOS has NO index unifier, so it demands a case for a constructor whose indices cannot match, and the case a translator invents is a lie
cases.lean: indexed inductive family (Vect, Fin, Eq), dependent match, impossible-case elimination, `nomatch`, `Nat.noConfusion`
cases.target: (none — a `Match` whose impossible case carries an invented inhabitant is not a translation of a Lean match that had no such case)
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:612-678 (`infer_indexed_match`, in full: it checks coverage with `if cases.len() != constructors.len() { return Err(WrongNumberOfCases) }` at :632-638 — EVERY constructor must be given a case, unconditionally — then checks each case against `compute_indexed_case_type(motive, ctor_name, ctor_type, num_params, disc_params)` at :644-647, which instantiates the motive at the CONSTRUCTOR's OWN indices. The discriminant's indices are used only to build the RESULT type at :650-655. There is no unification step between the two, and no arm that discharges a case because its indices are incompatible); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:254-260 (the non-indexed path has the same positional coverage requirement); kernel/src/context.rs:374 (`add_indexed_inductive(name, sort, num_params)` — the ONLY way to tell LOGOS that part of an arity is indices; `add_inductive` (context.rs:253) treats the WHOLE arity as parameters, which is the default and is silently wrong for a family, see T03-005); kernel/src/prelude.rs:3477 (the prelude itself registers the indexed `BVec` with `add_inductive`, so even the trusted base carries this misdeclaration — T10-010); LOGOS_FACTS: there is no `noConfusion`, no `injection`, no `casesOn`, no `brecOn`
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS.** The kernel's acceptance is not evidence of faithfulness. Here is the mechanism in full. Lean writes `match v with | Vect.cons x xs => …` on a `v : Vect α (n+1)` and needs no `nil` arm, because unification proves `0 ≠ n+1`. LOGOS demands `cases.len() == constructors.len()` (type_checker.rs:632-638), so the translator must supply a `nil` arm. There is no honest term to put there — the arm is unreachable, so its "value" is arbitrary. The three things a translator will reach for are each wrong in a different way: · A `Term::Hole`. Accepted by `types_equal` against anything (type_checker.rs:1594-1597), so the whole match typechecks and the emitted term contains a wildcard that will match any later type. See T11-004. · An arbitrary inhabitant of the result type. Well-typed, silent, and now the function has a DEFINED VALUE on an input Lean said could not occur — so a later proof that case-splits differently, or a `decide` that evaluates the branch, can observe it. · `False.elim` applied to a fabricated proof. That requires proving the case impossible, which is exactly what LOGOS gives no tool for: no `noConfusion`, no `injection`, no index unifier. In every variant LOGOS accepts the term. In none of them does it mean what the Lean source meant.

Catches the params/indices misdeclaration that makes this worse. If the translator uses `add_inductive` rather than `add_indexed_inductive` (context.rs:253 vs :374), LOGOS believes the family has zero indices, the match never reaches `infer_indexed_match` at all, and the index is not related to the scrutinee in ANY way — so cases that Lean rules impossible are not merely undischargeable, they are indistinguishable from possible ones. The prelude's own `BVec` is registered this way (prelude.rs:3477).

Catches the motive. `compute_indexed_case_type` instantiates the motive at the CONSTRUCTOR's indices (type_checker.rs:644-647) while the result type is the motive at the DISCRIMINANT's indices (:650-655). A translator that builds the motive by abstracting the discriminant's indices — the natural thing to do — produces a motive that is correct for the reachable arms and, for the unreachable arm, is being asked to accept a term at a type it was never meant to describe.

Catches the `Eq`-based workarounds. Lean's `Eq.rec`/`Eq.mpr` route around index unification by carrying propositional equalities. LOGOS has `Eq` and a derived `Eq_rec` (prelude.rs:1481-1596), so a translator CAN emit an equality-carrying version — but that is a different term with different computational behaviour, and it must be reported as such, not as a translation of the dependent match.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NO_INDEX_UNIFICATION for every declaration below whose Lean match omits a constructor arm, and emits nothing. The decisive harness assertion is structural: for every `Term::Match` in the whole corpus output, `cases.len()` equals the constructor count AND every case is the translation of a Lean arm that actually existed — no case may be a `Hole`, a fabricated inhabitant, or a `False.elim` of a proof the Lean source did not contain.
diag: E_NO_INDEX_UNIFICATION — must name the inductive, the constructor whose indices cannot match the discriminant's, and the Lean match arm that therefore has no counterpart, and must emit nothing. Must NOT offer to fill the case with `False.elim`, a default value, or a `Term::Hole`.

cases.title: Mutual inductives with unequal parameter counts — the block registers, and only the RECURSOR refuses, long after the damage is done
cases.lean: mutual inductive block, members with different numbers of parameters, mutual recursion over them
cases.target: (none — `derive_recursor` cannot produce an eliminator for such a block, so the inductives are declarable but not usable)
evidence: kernel/src/recursor.rs:193-207 (`derive_mutual_recursors`: it takes `num_params` from `block[0]` at :199, then for every member checks `if ctx.inductive_num_params(name).min(peel_pis(full).0.len()) != num_params { return Err(KernelError::CertificationError("auto-recursor: mutual block members disagree on parameter count ('{name}')")) }` at :200-207 — the check lives in the RECURSOR derivation, not in the declaration); kernel/src/context.rs:570-628 (`add_mutual_inductives` is transactional for POSITIVITY — "if any constructor violates positivity, nothing is added" — but its `MutualInductive` records carry a per-member `num_params` and nothing reconciles them); kernel/src/context.rs:253 (`add_inductive` is UNCHECKED and treats the full arity as parameters, so a translator that declares the members one at a time never reaches the mutual path at all); kernel/src/context.rs:374 (`add_indexed_inductive(name, sort, num_params)`, the only way to set a different split); kernel/src/recursor.rs:36 (`derive_recursor` synthesises `(type, term)` and "the caller must `add_definition` it" — so a translator that never calls it never sees the error); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:254-260 and :612-678 (`Match` is the PRIMITIVE in LOGOS, so a translator can pattern-match on these inductives without ever deriving a recursor)
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS.** The kernel accepting a declaration is not evidence of faithfulness — and here the acceptance and the rejection are SEPARATED IN TIME. The declaration path takes the block happily. The failure surfaces only when `derive_recursor` is called, which is a SEPARATE, OPTIONAL step the caller must initiate (recursor.rs:36). A translator that emits the inductives, emits its functions as `Term::Match` (which is primitive in LOGOS, unlike Lean where `.rec` is primitive — T03-021), and never derives a recursor, produces a context that typechecks completely and in which the mutual block's induction principle DOES NOT EXIST. Every proof by mutual induction in the source then has no target, and the translator discovers this one declaration at a time, far from the block.

Catches the "just declare them separately" workaround. `add_inductive` (context.rs:253) will register each member on its own with no mutual bookkeeping at all, and `add_constructor` (context.rs:419) is UNCHECKED, so a constructor of `Even` mentioning `Odd` is accepted. The block then has no positivity check over the WHOLE block — which `add_mutual_inductives` performs specifically because "a sibling occurrence is a recursive occurrence, a sibling in a negative position is a cross-block paradox" (context.rs:571-578). Bypassing the mutual path to dodge the parameter-count check also bypasses the cross-block positivity check. See T11-013.

Catches EQUALISING the parameter counts by moving a parameter to an index, or an index to a parameter. Either changes the family: a parameter is uniform across all constructors and appears in the recursor's motive telescope before the indices (recursor.rs:208-212), an index does not. Silently re-splitting to satisfy `recursor.rs:200-207` produces an eliminator with the wrong motive shape, and the terms built with it typecheck.

Catches the `.min()` in the check. The comparison is `ctx.inductive_num_params(name).min(peel_pis(full).0.len())` (recursor.rs:200-202), i.e. the recorded parameter count CLAMPED to the member's actual arity. So a member whose recorded `num_params` exceeds its arity is silently clamped rather than diagnosed, and two members can pass the check while disagreeing about what their parameters mean. A translator must set `num_params` from Lean's own params/indices split, never let it default.

Catches assuming Lean's mutual blocks always have equal parameter counts. Lean requires the members of a mutual inductive block to share their PARAMETERS, but not their INDICES — so a block of `Even : Nat → Prop` and `Odd : Nat → Prop` with an extra parameter on one member is expressible in Lean via separate parameterisation in ways that flatten differently, and any block whose members' arities differ will trip `recursor.rs:200-207` if the translator records arity as parameters (which `add_inductive` does by default).
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_MUTUAL_PARAM_COUNT_MISMATCH and emits NO declaration for the block — in particular zero `add_inductive`, `add_indexed_inductive`, `add_constructor` and `add_mutual_inductives` calls. A harness additionally asserts, for every mutual block anywhere in the corpus output, that `derive_mutual_recursors` was actually CALLED and its result registered with `add_definition`; a block whose recursor was never derived counts as an unfinished translation even if every term using it typechecks.
diag: E_MUTUAL_PARAM_COUNT_MISMATCH — must name the block, list each member's parameter count, quote the constraint from `recursor.rs:200-207`, and emit NOTHING. Partial emission — declaring the inductives and omitting the recursors — is the failure this case is designed to catch.

cases.title: Nested inductive outside the unary-container fragment — the compiler refuses, and the workaround silently changes the type
cases.lean: nested inductive through List / Array / Prod / a user container, `Tree` with `List (Tree α)` children
cases.target: (none — `compile_nested_inductive` refuses, and every hand-rolled substitute is a different inductive from the Lean one)
evidence: kernel/src/inductive_compile.rs:220-232 (the specialisability check: `analyze_container_ctor` classifies each constructor argument, and `if kinds.iter().any(|k| matches!(k, ArgKind::Other(_)))` the compile fails with "container '{c}' constructor '{orig_ctor}' has an argument that is neither the element nor a recursive occurrence — specializing it is not supported (only pure containers like `List`/`TList`)" — so a container with ANY extra field, including a length index or a second element type, is outside the fragment); kernel/src/inductive_compile.rs:261-271 (the universe gate: `if decl.sort != Term::Sort(Universe::Type(0))` the compile fails with "'{}' must be a `Type 0` inductive (specialized siblings are `Type 0`); higher-universe nesting is not supported"); kernel/src/inductive_compile.rs:318-327 (the emitted siblings are built with `sort: Term::Sort(Universe::Type(0))` and `num_params: 0` — so the specialisation is MONOMORPHIC and PARAMETERLESS, whatever the source container was); kernel/src/recursor.rs:193-207 (the emitted block goes through the mutual recursor derivation, which requires all members to agree on parameter count — satisfied here only because every sibling is forced to `num_params: 0`); kernel/src/context.rs:630 (`add_nested_inductive(&NestedDecl)` — the entry point); kernel/src/prelude.rs:609-652 (`TList`, the one prelude container inside the fragment)
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS.** The kernel accepting a term is not evidence of faithfulness, and here the trap is the WORKAROUND rather than the refusal. `compile_nested_inductive` refuses loudly, which is good — so the translator's next move is to write the mutual block by hand with `add_inductive`/`add_constructor`, which are UNCHECKED (context.rs:253, :419) and will take anything. The hand-rolled block typechecks. It is a DIFFERENT TYPE from the Lean one: the specialised sibling is a fresh inductive with no relationship to the container it specialises, so `Tree_List` is not `List Tree`, and every Lean lemma about `List` applied to a tree's children has no target. The kernel cannot notice, because there is nothing in the environment recording that the two were meant to be the same.

Catches losing the ISOS. `compile_nested_inductive` emits "the conversion isos, one pair per node … inner-first" (inductive_compile.rs:329-331) precisely so that the specialised sibling can be moved to and from the container. A hand-rolled mutual block that omits them produces a type that cannot be converted at all, so every function the source wrote over `List (Tree α)` must be rewritten over the sibling, and the rewriting is unchecked.

Catches the `num_params: 0` collapse. Every emitted sibling is `num_params: 0` (inductive_compile.rs:322-327), so a nested `List (Tree α)` for a POLYMORPHIC `Tree` specialises to a parameterless sibling — i.e. the element type is monomorphised. If the source instantiates the tree at two different element types, the two instantiations collapse onto one LOGOS global. That is T01-007's silent monomorphisation trap arriving through a different door, and because LOGOS is cumulative (type_checker.rs:1330-1360) the resulting terms very often still typecheck.

Catches the `Type 0` gate being read as a formality. It is not: the siblings are EMITTED at `Type 0` (inductive_compile.rs:322-327), so the gate at :261-271 is enforcing consistency with what the compiler will build. A translator that "works around" it by declaring the nested type at `Type 0` when the source had it at `Type u` has silently monomorphised the universe as well as the element type.

Catches nesting through `Prod`, `Sum`, `Array` or a user container with more than one field. `analyze_container_ctor` rejects any constructor argument that is neither the bare element nor a recursive occurrence (inductive_compile.rs:220-230), so `Prod` — whose constructor takes TWO different element types — is outside the fragment, and so is any indexed container. `Array` is absent entirely (T10-011).
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_NESTED_INDUCTIVE_OUTSIDE_FRAGMENT for each declaration below and emits nothing. A harness asserts that every nested inductive anywhere in the corpus output was produced by `add_nested_inductive` (context.rs:630) — NOT by a sequence of raw `add_inductive`/`add_constructor` calls — and that the conversion isos it emits are present and registered.
diag: E_NESTED_INDUCTIVE_OUTSIDE_FRAGMENT — must name the nesting container, say which of the two gates it fails (non-unary/non-pure container, or non-`Type 0` sort), and emit nothing. Must NOT silently fall back to a hand-written mutual block.

cases.title: `add_inductive` / `add_constructor` are UNCHECKED — the declaration API will build an inconsistent environment on request
cases.lean: strict positivity violation, universe-inconsistent constructor, an inductive whose declaration Lean refuses
cases.target: (none — and, decisively, the translator must use `add_constructor_checked` for every constructor it ever emits, including the ones it emits for types it merely needs as support)
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:246-256 (`add_inductive(name, sort)` — the whole body is `Arc::make_mut(&mut self.inductives).insert(name.to_string(), sort)`. No positivity check, no universe check, no check that the name is fresh, no check that `sort` is a sort); kernel/src/context.rs:413-431 (`add_constructor(name, inductive, ty)` — inserts into `constructors` and appends to `constructor_order`. No check that `ty` targets `inductive`, no positivity check, no universe check, no arity check); kernel/src/context.rs:539-561 (`add_constructor_checked` — the SAFE path: it calls `crate::positivity::check_positivity(inductive, name, &ty)?` and then `crate::type_checker::check_constructor_universes(self, inductive, name, &ty)?` before delegating to `add_constructor`. Both checks exist; both are OPT-IN); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:540-583 (`check_constructor_universes` — its own doc comment names what it prevents: "the universe inconsistency that opens Girard/Hurkens paradoxes"); kernel/src/context.rs:570-628 (`add_mutual_inductives` — checks positivity over the whole block and is transactional, the third safe entry point); kernel/src/context.rs:442-444 (`add_definition(name, ty, body)` is ALSO unchecked: it inserts `(ty, body)` with NO verification that `body : ty`. There is no `add_definition_checked` anywhere in the crate)
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS, STATED AS AN API FACT.** LOGOS's kernel accepting a term is not evidence that the translation is faithful — and the declaration API does not even pretend to check. `add_inductive` and `add_constructor` are `insert` calls. A translator that uses them builds whatever environment it is told to build, including one in which `False` is provable, and every subsequent `infer_type` call is then checking terms against an inconsistent theory. The kernel's "yes" is relative to an environment the translator chose.

Catches the negative-occurrence inductive. `inductive Bad where | mk : (Bad → False) → Bad` is refused by Lean and refused by `check_positivity` (context.rs:545-546) — but ONLY if the translator called `add_constructor_checked`. Via `add_constructor` it registers, and the standard Berardi/Hurkens derivation of `False` goes through with every step typechecking. The kernel is not broken; it was asked to trust a declaration.

Catches the universe-inconsistent constructor. `check_constructor_universes` (type_checker.rs:540-583) enforces that every VALUE argument's sort is `≤` the inductive's result sort, with the impredicative-`Prop` exemption at :556-557 — and it decides `≤` with `is_subtype_of`, i.e. the CUMULATIVE order (term.rs:243-249). So even the checked path is more permissive than Lean's non-cumulative constraint; see T11-019. A translator must therefore run BOTH: `add_constructor_checked` AND its own record of Lean's universe judgement.

Catches the unchecked path being reached by convenience rather than by intent. Tier 10 requires the translator to emit `List`, `Option`, `Prod`, `Sum`, `Sigma`, `Subtype` and `Fin` from scratch (T10-012, T10-013), plus `Nat` arithmetic (T10-017) and possibly a `String`/`Char` layer (T10-005, T10-006). That is a lot of declaration-emitting code, written once, far from the input, and the two-argument `add_constructor` is the shorter call. Every one of those emissions must go through the checked path.

Catches the SAME hole on the definition side, which has no checked path at all. `add_definition` (context.rs:442-444) inserts a `(ty, body)` pair without verifying `body : ty`, and there is no `add_definition_checked` in the crate. So a translator that emits a definition whose body does not have the stated type installs a global whose `get_global` type (context.rs:459-461) and whose `get_definition_body` value (context.rs:474) describe different things — the same typing/reduction split as T11-003, arrived at without any name collision. The translator MUST call `infer_type` on the body and `is_subtype` against the type itself, before `add_definition`.

Catches "the re-checker will catch it". `recheck.rs` re-verifies TERMS against a context; it does not re-derive the environment's well-formedness, and `certificate::recheck` rebuilds only the TRUSTED BASE from `StandardLibrary::register` (certificate.rs:63-75) — every translator-added declaration is taken as given.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_UNCHECKED_DECLARATION_PATH for each declaration below and emits nothing. The decisive harness assertion is about the translator's own call graph, not about any term: over the whole corpus, the number of `add_constructor` calls must be ZERO — every constructor must go through `add_constructor_checked` or `add_mutual_inductives` — and every `add_definition` call must be immediately preceded by a successful `infer_type` of the body and an `is_subtype` check against the declared type.
diag: E_UNCHECKED_DECLARATION_PATH — must name the declaration, state which check (positivity or constructor universes) the Lean source would have failed, and emit nothing. A translator that reaches this diagnostic because it was ABOUT to call `add_constructor` rather than `add_constructor_checked` must treat that as a bug in itself, not in the input.

cases.title: `sorry` smuggled in as an `axiom` declaration — the one translation that is indistinguishable from a proof
cases.lean: sorry, sorryAx, `admit`, a `theorem` whose proof term mentions `sorryAx`, a declaration transitively depending on one
cases.target: (none — and in particular NOT `add_declaration`)
evidence: kernel/src/context.rs:434-438 (`add_declaration(name, ty)` — "Add a declaration (typed assumption/hypothesis)… Used for proof certification where hypotheses are assumed." It stores a TYPE with no body: this is the axiom form, and it is the natural target for `sorryAx : ∀ (α : Sort u), α`); kernel/src/context.rs:449-464 (`get_global` finds `declarations` LAST, so an axiom is looked up exactly like any other global and nothing marks it as an assumption); kernel/src/reduction.rs:305-314 (delta reduction reads `get_definition_body`, which returns `None` for a declaration — so an axiom is simply opaque, exactly like every legitimate prelude primitive); kernel/src/prelude.rs:78 (`dne` — the ONE classical axiom, added with `add_declaration`) and prelude.rs:352-430 (the arithmetic primitives, also `add_declaration`s) — so the trusted base's own axioms are indistinguishable, by API, from a smuggled `sorry`; kernel/src/certificate.rs:28 (`PRELUDE_VERSION = "logos-coc-1"`); kernel/src/certificate.rs:63-75 (`recheck` refuses a mismatched `prelude_version` and then rebuilds the trusted context ITSELF from `StandardLibrary::register`); LOGOS_FACTS: `VerifiedProof.verified == true` iff a kernel term was produced and typechecked (verify.rs:31-43)
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS, AT ITS HIGHEST STAKES.** LOGOS's kernel accepting a term is not evidence that the translation is faithful. `sorry` is where that gap becomes a forged proof. The tempting move is one line: `ctx.add_declaration("sorryAx", Π(α : Sort u). α)`. It compiles. Every theorem whose Lean proof used `sorry` then typechecks in LOGOS, `VerifiedProof.verified` comes back `true`, and a certificate is minted. Lean at least paints the declaration with a yellow warning and lists `sorryAx` under `#print axioms`; LOGOS has no axiom-tracking mechanism at all — `get_global` treats `declarations` as just the fourth map to check (context.rs:463) — so the artefact that was supposed to record incompleteness says the theorem is proved.

Catches the axiom that is not called `sorry`. The realistic path is not a literal `sorry` in the source; it is a declaration whose ELABORATED proof term mentions `sorryAx` because some lemma three files away was left open. The translator must inspect the elaborated term, not the surface syntax, and must propagate: every declaration transitively depending on a `sorryAx`-bearing one is equally unemittable.

Catches "emit it but mark it". There is nowhere to put the mark. LOGOS's `Context` has no attributes, no visibility, no metadata of any kind (LOGOS_FACTS: flat `String` keys, four parallel maps), and `Term::Lit` has no annotation variant. A mark that lives only in the translator's own side-channel is lost the moment the context is serialised into a certificate, and `certificate::recheck` rebuilds only the trusted base (certificate.rs:63-75) — it will not re-derive which of the translator's declarations were placeholders.

Catches the `PRELUDE_VERSION` deception. If the translator instead patches the prelude to include its placeholder axiom, `PRELUDE_VERSION` still reads `"logos-coc-1"` (certificate.rs:28), the version guard at certificate.rs:65 passes, and every certificate ever minted now claims to have been checked against an axiom set that is not the one it was checked against. This is the same failure as T06-009 and T11-015, and `sorry` is the version of it with no upside at all.

Catches the "it's just a hypothesis" rationalisation. `add_declaration`'s own doc comment says "Used for proof certification where hypotheses are assumed" (context.rs:434-437) — which is true, and is why the API is there, and is exactly why it must not be used for `sorry`: a hypothesis is discharged by the theorem's own statement, whereas `sorryAx` is an unrestricted `Π(α : Sort u). α`, i.e. a proof of everything. A translator that cannot distinguish "assume the premises of this theorem" from "assume anything" has no faithfulness oracle at all.

Catches the `Type`-valued `sorry`. `sorryAx` returns any `Sort`, so it can produce DATA as well as proofs — a `sorry`-provided `Nat`, or a `sorry`-provided instance — and such a term reduces to nothing (it is opaque, reduction.rs:305-314), so it silently blocks every computation downstream of it while typechecking perfectly.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_INCOMPLETE_PROOF(sorry) for every declaration below and its transitive dependents, and emits nothing for any of them. The decisive harness assertion is global and is the same one T06-009 uses: the set of names passed to `add_declaration` over the WHOLE corpus must be a subset of the names registered by `StandardLibrary::register`. A translator that never adds an axiom cannot smuggle a `sorry` as one.
diag: E_INCOMPLETE_PROOF(sorry) — must name the declaration, name every declaration that transitively depends on it, and emit NOTHING for any of them. The diagnostic must be a hard failure, never a warning, and must not be suppressible.

cases.title: Trusted-base drift — `PRELUDE_VERSION` is a single hard-coded string, and nothing makes it change when the prelude does
cases.lean: any theorem whose translation adds a declaration, `#print axioms`, an `axiom` declaration, a dependency on a non-prelude primitive
cases.target: The faithful term, PLUS a machine-readable trusted-base record: the `PRELUDE_VERSION` string in force, the complete list of names the translator added with `add_declaration`, and the list of prelude names the translation depends on.
evidence: kernel/src/certificate.rs:28 (`pub const PRELUDE_VERSION: &str = "logos-coc-1";` — a hand-maintained literal, not a hash of the prelude); kernel/src/certificate.rs:50 (`prelude_version: PRELUDE_VERSION.to_string()` — the value is stamped into every certificate at mint time); kernel/src/certificate.rs:63-75 (`recheck` first refuses a certificate whose `prelude_version` differs at :65-69, and then REBUILDS the trusted context itself from `StandardLibrary::register` — the repo's own comment for this is "never trust a context the certificate might carry"); kernel/src/prelude.rs:18-51 (`StandardLibrary::register` — the single function that defines what the string is supposed to describe); kernel/src/context.rs:434-438 (`add_declaration` — the way a translator enlarges the axiom set, with no record kept anywhere); kernel/src/context.rs:449-464 (`get_global` — a translator-added declaration is looked up exactly like a prelude one; nothing distinguishes them)
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS, AT THE ARTEFACT LEVEL.** The kernel accepting a term is not evidence of faithfulness — and here the artefact that was supposed to record what the kernel accepted is itself unreliable. The failure mode is quiet and permanent: a certificate minted against a modified prelude carries `"logos-coc-1"`, passes `recheck`'s version guard (certificate.rs:65-69), and is then re-checked against the CURRENT `StandardLibrary::register` (certificate.rs:73-75) — which may be a different axiom set again. A certificate is only as good as the pinning of the base it names, and this one is pinned by a string literal.

Catches the translator patching the prelude to make something typecheck. This is the exact composition with T06-009 and T11-014: add `Classical_choice` or `sorryAx` to `StandardLibrary::register` so the emitted terms check, and every certificate thereafter lies. The rule is absolute: the translator may not modify `StandardLibrary::register`, and must fail rather than need to.

Catches the OPPOSITE failure — refusing to record a legitimate addition. Some Lean `axiom` declarations are genuinely intended as assumptions and translate correctly to `add_declaration` (see T11-014's contrast case). Those additions are sound and must still be RECORDED, because the resulting LOGOS library's trusted base is then `StandardLibrary::register` ∪ {those names}, which is not what `PRELUDE_VERSION` describes.

Catches assuming `recheck` will surface the difference. It will surface a MISSING name — a certificate mentioning `Classical_choice` fails with `KernelError::UnboundVariable("Classical_choice")` after the rebuild at certificate.rs:73-75 — but that error reads like a name-resolution bug, not like "you added an axiom", and it does not fire at all if the extra declaration was also added to the rebuilt context. The diagnostic quality is the problem, not just the presence of a check.

Catches recording the version once per run instead of once per declaration. A translation is typically incremental: declarations accumulate across invocations, and a prelude change between two runs leaves half the output checked against one base and half against another, with one `PRELUDE_VERSION` string covering both.
oracle: Every emitted declaration carries a trusted-base record naming (a) the `PRELUDE_VERSION` in force, (b) the translator's own `add_declaration` additions, and (c) a CONTENT HASH of `StandardLibrary::register`'s output computed by the translator itself — not the version string, which is what this case exists to distrust. A harness asserts that the recorded hash is identical across the whole corpus, and that (b) is a subset of the axioms the corpus declares legitimate.
loss: TRUSTED_BASE_IS_NOT_PINNED. `PRELUDE_VERSION` is a constant a human must remember to bump. It is not derived from `StandardLibrary::register`, so a change to the prelude that leaves the string alone produces certificates that claim to have been checked against an axiom set that is not the one they were checked against — and the version guard at certificate.rs:65 passes, because the string still matches. The de Bruijn criterion depends on knowing exactly what was trusted; a hand-maintained string is the weakest possible way to record that.

TRANSLATOR_ADDITIONS_ARE_UNRECORDED. Every `add_declaration` the translator makes enlarges the trusted base, and LOGOS keeps no list: `declarations` is just the fourth map `get_global` consults (context.rs:463), with no attribute system and no provenance. So the translator must keep the list itself, and must ship it with the output, or the resulting library's trusted base is simply unknown.

cases.title: `Int` is AXIOMATISED in LOGOS and DERIVED in Lean — the same theorem has a proof in one system and a trusted assumption in the other
cases.lean: Int, Int.add_comm, Int.add_assoc, Int.mul_comm, Int.le_total, Int.ofNat / negSucc, Int.induction_on
cases.target: `Global("Int")` plus the prelude's 16 axioms and 5 primitives; every Lean PROOF about `Int` becomes either an appeal to one of those axioms or a rejection.
evidence: kernel/src/prelude.rs:354 (`ctx.add_inductive("Int", Sort(Type 0))` with NO `add_constructor` call anywhere for it — `Int` is an inductive of arity 0 with zero constructors, i.e. an opaque carrier that cannot be matched on or inducted over); kernel/src/prelude.rs:92-191 (`register_int_ring_axioms` — the EIGHT ring axioms, every one an `add_declaration`: `add_comm`, `add_assoc`, `add_zero`, `mul_comm`, `mul_assoc`, `mul_one`, `mul_zero`, `mul_distrib_add`); kernel/src/prelude.rs:202-340 (`register_int_order_axioms` — the EIGHT order axioms, with `a ≤ b` encoded as `Eq Bool (le a b) true`: `le_refl`, `le_trans`, `le_add_mono`, `le_mul_nonneg`, `le_sub`, `lt_succ_le`, `lt_add1_le`, `le_total`); kernel/src/prelude.rs:363-381 (`add`/`sub`/`mul`/`div`/`mod : Int → Int → Int` and `le`/`lt`/`ge`/`gt : Int → Int → Bool`, all `add_declaration`s — opaque); kernel/src/reduction.rs:444-506 (`try_primitive_reduce` — the ONLY computational content, and it fires only when BOTH operands are `Term::Lit`); in Lean 4, `Int` is `inductive Int | ofNat : Nat → Int | negSucc : Nat → Int` and every one of the sixteen facts above is a THEOREM with a proof term
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS.** The kernel accepting a term is not evidence of faithfulness, and here the acceptance is doing genuinely less work than it appears to. A translated `Int` theorem that typechecks has been checked against SIXTEEN ASSUMPTIONS the Lean source did not make. If any of them is wrong — and they are hand-written `Term` values in a Rust file, not machine-checked (prelude.rs:92-340) — every `Int` theorem in the output inherits the error, and the kernel's verdict is unaffected. The translator must record the dependency; it cannot verify it.

Catches the translator re-declaring `Int` with constructors to recover induction. `add_inductive`/`add_constructor` are UNCHECKED (context.rs:253, :419), so `Int_ofNat`/`Int_negSucc` will register — and the result is a DIFFERENT type from the prelude's `Int`. The sixteen axioms are stated about the prelude's `Int` (prelude.rs:93, :203 both open with `let int = || Term::Global("Int")`), so none of them applies to the shadow type; and `try_primitive_reduce` fires only on `Term::Lit` operands (reduction.rs:455-500), so `add (Int_ofNat 2) (Int_ofNat 3)` never computes. The translation typechecks and proves nothing. See T10-003.

Catches the OPPOSITE move: keeping the prelude's `Int` and silently dropping the Lean proofs of the sixteen facts, on the grounds that "LOGOS already has them". It does have them — as axioms. The translated library's trusted base is then larger than the Lean source's by sixteen statements, and nothing in LOGOS records that (T11-015).

Catches the order encoding. LOGOS states `a ≤ b` as `Eq Bool (le a b) true` (prelude.rs:202-340), a `Bool`-reflected relation, whereas Lean's `Int.le` is a `Prop` defined via `Int.NonNeg`. These are different propositions with different proof terms, and translating Lean's `≤` to LOGOS's encoding silently changes what a proof of `a ≤ b` IS. It also makes the translation depend on the `Bool` constructor names `true`/`false` being the PRELUDE's (T10-008).

Catches `Int` and `Nat` being conflated to dodge all of this. They are different kinds of object in LOGOS — one opaque and axiomatised, one inductive and computational — and conflating them is T10-004's rejection.
oracle: Every emitted `Int` term uses the prelude's `Global("Int")` and the prelude's operation names, with no re-declared constructors; every translated `Int` theorem carries a loss record listing exactly which of the sixteen axioms its proof cites; and every Lean proof by induction or case analysis on an `Int` is REJECTED, not degraded. A harness asserts that no `Term::Match` in the corpus output has an `Int`-typed discriminant.
loss: AXIOMATISED_VERSUS_DERIVED. In Lean, `Int.add_comm` is proved from the constructor structure and `Nat` arithmetic; its proof term is checkable and its truth follows from the definition. In LOGOS it is an `add_declaration` — a trusted assumption with no body (prelude.rs:130-136). So a translated theorem that cites it has a different epistemic status from the Lean original: the Lean version is a proof, the LOGOS version is a derivation FROM SIXTEEN AXIOMS. The loss record must name every axiom the translated proof leans on; "translated to LOGOS `Int`" is not a loss record.

NO_INDUCTION_ON_INT. Lean's `Int` has constructors, so `Int.induction_on`, `Int.rec`, and case analysis on `ofNat`/`negSucc` are available. LOGOS's `Int` has ZERO constructors, so `Match` over it is inexpressible and `derive_recursor` has nothing to derive. Any Lean proof by induction or case analysis on an `Int` has NO translation — that part of the source is a `reject`, not a `degrade`, and must be reported as such.

SIXTEEN_AXIOMS_IS_NOT_A_RING. The axiom set is deliberately small and is not complete for `Int`: there is no additive inverse axiom, no cancellation, no `a * b = 0 → a = 0 ∨ b = 0`, no well-ordering, and nothing relating `div`/`mod` to `mul`/`add` at all (they appear in no axiom — see T10-018). Facts Lean proves easily are simply unprovable about LOGOS's `Int` on symbolic arguments, and provable only on literals via `try_primitive_reduce`.

cases.title: `reduceBool` wires a whole EVALUATOR into kernel reduction — the TCB expansion is real and is not the same one Lean's `native_decide` makes
cases.lean: native_decide, Lean.ofReduceBool, Lean.reduceBool, Lean.trustCompiler, decide
cases.target: `Global("reduceBool")` applied to the translated decision procedure, discharged by `Global("ofReduceBool")` — PLUS a loss record naming the evaluator as a trusted component.
evidence: kernel/src/prelude.rs:1195-1219 (`register_native_decide` — registers exactly `reduceBool : Bool → Bool` and `ofReduceBool`, the LOGOS analogue of Lean's pair); kernel/src/reduction.rs:105-116 (the reduction rule, with the repo's own comment: "Native reduction: `reduceBool t` evaluates `t` with the fast CBV evaluator (the `native_decide` engine). This is the ONLY place the trusted evaluator enters kernel reduction — gated behind the `reduceBool` primitive" — the body is `if name == "reduceBool" { if let Some(b) = crate::eval::eval_bool(ctx, arg) { return Term::Global(if b { "true" } else { "false" }) } }`); kernel/src/eval.rs (`eval_bool` — the entire CBV evaluator, a second implementation of LOGOS's operational semantics, now inside the kernel's conversion checker); kernel/src/reduction.rs:52-69 (`normalize`'s 10000-step fuel does NOT bound `eval_bool`, which runs to completion or fails); kernel/src/prelude.rs:593-604 (the `true`/`false` globals the rule returns are the prelude's, so this rule also depends on `Bool` not being shadowed — T10-008); kernel/src/certificate.rs:28 and :63-75 (`PRELUDE_VERSION` covers the prelude's DECLARATIONS; it says nothing about the evaluator's implementation, which is a different file and can change without the string changing — T11-015)
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS.** The kernel accepting a term is not evidence of faithfulness — and `reduceBool` is the case where the kernel's acceptance is partly delegated to code that is not the kernel. A `reduceBool`-discharged proof typechecks; what it establishes is "the CBV evaluator returned `true`", which is a claim about a program, not a derivation.

Catches emitting `reduceBool` for something that is not a decision procedure. The rule fires on ANY `Term::Global("reduceBool")` application whose argument `eval_bool` can evaluate (reduction.rs:109-115); there is no check that the argument is the `decide` of the proposition being proved. So a translator that reaches for `reduceBool` to make a stuck computation go through — a large `Nat` recursion past the fuel boundary (T11-005), say — has replaced a definitional-equality obligation with an evaluator call that answers a different question, and `ofReduceBool` will happily convert the answer into a proof of the ORIGINAL proposition.

Catches the fuel asymmetry. `normalize`'s 10000-step budget (reduction.rs:52-69) does not apply inside `eval_bool`. So a translator can make a proof succeed by routing it through `reduceBool` — which is exactly the wrong reason to choose an encoding, because it silently converts a budget problem into a trust problem. The choice must be driven by the SOURCE using `native_decide`, never by the target failing to reduce.

Catches the `Bool` shadowing interaction. The rule returns `Term::Global("true")` / `Global("false")` literally (reduction.rs:112-114), which are the prelude's constructors (prelude.rs:599-603). A translator that emitted its own `Bool` (T10-008) gets a `reduceBool` result of a type unrelated to the proposition it was meant to decide — and, because the branches usually have the same type, the term still checks.

Catches leaving `reduceBool` out of the trusted-base record. It is registered by `StandardLibrary::register` (prelude.rs:1195-1219), so it is inside `PRELUDE_VERSION`'s nominal scope — but the EVALUATOR it invokes lives in `eval.rs` and is not described by that string at all (T11-015). A record that names only the axioms understates the TCB.
oracle: A `reduceBool`/`ofReduceBool` pair is emitted ONLY for Lean declarations whose `#print axioms` lists `Lean.ofReduceBool`, never as a fallback for a reduction that did not go through; and each such declaration carries a loss record with categories EVALUATOR_IN_THE_TCB and DIFFERENT_TCB_FROM_LEAN. A harness asserts that the set of corpus declarations emitting `reduceBool` is exactly the set whose Lean proofs depend on `Lean.ofReduceBool`.
loss: EVALUATOR_IN_THE_TCB. Ordinary kernel reduction is a few hundred lines of `reduce_step` (reduction.rs). `reduceBool` admits `eval.rs` — a separate, much larger CBV evaluator — into the conversion relation. Any bug in `eval_bool` is a soundness bug in the kernel, reachable from any proof that uses `native_decide`. The loss record must say so and must name every declaration that uses it, because the set of theorems whose validity depends on the evaluator is exactly that set.

DIFFERENT_TCB_FROM_LEAN. Lean's `native_decide` trusts the Lean COMPILER (`#print axioms` reports `Lean.ofReduceBool`, and via it `Lean.trustCompiler`): the decision procedure is compiled to machine code and run. LOGOS's `reduceBool` trusts `eval.rs`, an interpreter inside the kernel crate. These are different trusted components with different failure modes, so a `native_decide` proof does not translate to "the same amount of trust"; it translates to a DIFFERENT amount, and the record must say which.

cases.title: Recursion Lean accepts structurally that LOGOS's Giménez guard rejects — and the workarounds that make it accept the wrong thing
cases.lean: structural recursion through a helper, recursion on a projection, nested recursion, recursion under a `let`, course-of-values recursion, `Nat.rec` with an accumulator
cases.target: (none for a recursion the guard refuses — LOGOS has no escape hatch)
evidence: kernel/src/termination.rs:378-401 (`verify_structural_arg_smaller`: it peels the recursive call's structural argument to its application HEAD, and accepts ONLY `Term::Var(arg_name)` where `guard_ctx.smaller_than.contains(arg_name)`. Anything else — a literal, a global, a `Match`, an application whose head is not a tracked variable — is `TerminationViolation` with "Recursive call whose structural argument is not headed by a structurally-smaller variable"); kernel/src/termination.rs:402-440 (the `smaller_than` set is populated by MATCH-BOUND binders of the scrutinee, and the extension noted in LOGOS_FACTS accepts `rec (h a…)` for such a variable — i.e. the smaller variable may be APPLIED, but it must still be the head); LOGOS_FACTS: there is NO well-founded recursion, no `termination_by`, no `decreasing_by`, and no equation compiler; kernel/src/prelude.rs:1354-1421 (`register_acc` — `Acc`/`Acc_intro` exist, so `Acc.rec` can be DERIVED, but recursion THROUGH it is not what the guard tracks: see T04-015); kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 (`Term::Fix { name, body }` and `MutualFix { defs, index }` are the only recursion forms)
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS.** The kernel accepting a term is not evidence of faithfulness — and this case is where a REJECTION tempts the translator into an unfaithful acceptance. The guard is a syntactic Giménez check (termination.rs:378-401); Lean's structural-recursion elaborator is strictly more capable, so there are Lean functions that are perfectly structural and that LOGOS refuses. The translator's options are then: reject (correct), or rewrite the recursion until the guard is satisfied (dangerous). The dangerous rewrites all share a shape — they change the function and the kernel cannot tell, because the REWRITTEN function typechecks fine and has the same type.

Catches the accumulator rewrite. Turning `f n = g (f (n-1))` into a tail-recursive accumulator version passes the guard and is a DIFFERENT function unless the fold is proved associative. Lean's own `List.foldl`/`foldr` distinction is exactly this. A translator that silently picks the one that passes has changed the semantics of every proof about it.

Catches the "just add a fuel parameter" rewrite. `f fuel n` with a `Nat` fuel argument always passes the guard (it recurses on `fuel`) and is TOTAL for a different reason than the original: it returns a default when fuel runs out. Every theorem about the original is now a theorem about a function that may return the default, and nothing in LOGOS records the difference.

Catches recursion on a PROJECTION. LOGOS has no `Term::Proj`; a projection is a `Match`-bodied global definition applied to the receiver (context.rs:271-369, T03-011). So `f s.tail` has an application head of `Global("S_tail")`, not a `Term::Var` — and `verify_structural_arg_smaller` (termination.rs:385-394) rejects it outright even though `s.tail` is structurally smaller. A translator that "fixes" this by inlining the projection's `Match` at the call site changes the argument's shape to a `Match`, whose head is also not a `Var`, and the guard rejects that too.

Catches recursion through a HELPER. `f (g x)` where `g` is smaller-preserving is structural in Lean's sense once `g` is unfolded; the guard looks at the SYNTACTIC head (termination.rs:381-384), sees `Global("g")`, and refuses. Delta-unfolding `g` at the call site to satisfy the guard makes the term larger, which pushes against the 10000-step fuel (T11-005) and the quadratic substitution cost (T11-007).

Catches reaching for `Acc`. `Acc`/`Acc_intro` are in the prelude (prelude.rs:1354-1421) and `derive_recursor` will produce an `Acc` eliminator, so it LOOKS as though well-founded recursion is available. It is not: the guard tracks `Fix`, and a recursive call inside an `Acc.rec` motive is still a recursive call the guard must accept. See T04-015.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_TERMINATION_GUARD_STRICTER for every declaration below and emits nothing. The decisive harness assertion is about what was NOT emitted: for every corpus declaration whose Lean recursion is structural but whose translation was rejected, the output must contain no `Term::Fix` at all — in particular no accumulator variant, no fuel parameter, and no inlined-projection variant of the same function.
diag: E_TERMINATION_GUARD_STRICTER — must name the declaration, quote the guard's own reason string, and emit nothing. Must NOT offer to re-express the recursion in a way that passes the guard unless the re-expression is proved equivalent.

cases.title: A universe constraint only Lean's NON-cumulative check catches — LOGOS's constructor universe check decides `≤` with the CUMULATIVE order
cases.lean: inductive storing a field one universe too high, Girard/Hurkens shape, `Type*`-style autobound levels, an inductive whose field is a `Sort u` for unconstrained `u`
cases.target: (none — the Lean source is ill-typed, and LOGOS's own check does not reproduce Lean's judgement)
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:540-583 (`check_constructor_universes` — the CIC universe constraint, and the decisive line is :570: `if !s.is_subtype_of(&target)`, where `s` is the field's inferred sort and `target` the inductive's result sort); kernel/src/term.rs:243-249 (`Universe::is_subtype_of` is `level_leq`, i.e. the CUMULATIVE order, not equality); kernel/src/term.rs:405-416 and :282-294 (`level_leq` decides over the ℕ-model where `Prop = 0` and `Type n = n+1`, so `Prop ≤ Type 0 ≤ Type 1` all hold); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:555-557 (the impredicative-`Prop` exemption: an inductive whose result sort is `Prop` has NO constraint on its arguments' universes at all — `return Ok(())`); kernel/src/context.rs:539-561 (`add_constructor_checked` — the ONLY caller of the check; `add_constructor` at :419 performs none of it, see T11-013); kernel/src/term.rs:196-202 (`Universe::succ` sends `Prop ↦ Type(1)`, which is the off-by-one of T11-002 and which feeds the SORT side of this comparison through `infer_sort` at type_checker.rs:569); kernel/src/recursor.rs:64-71 (`derive_recursor` pins a non-`Prop` inductive's motive to `Sort(Type 0)`, so even a correctly universe-checked inductive at `Type 1` gets an eliminator that cannot reach its own level)
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS, AT THE DECLARATION LEVEL.** The kernel accepting a DECLARATION is not evidence that the declaration is the Lean one. Read `check_constructor_universes` closely: it is a real check, it exists, and it catches the Girard/Hurkens shape its doc comment names. But it decides `s ≤ target` with `is_subtype_of` (type_checker.rs:570), which is `level_leq` (term.rs:243-249) — the CUMULATIVE order. Lean's constraint on an inductive's universe is a constraint in a system with NO cumulativity: `Type 0` is not a subtype of `Type 1`, so Lean's acceptance set and LOGOS's are different sets, and the difference is not uniformly in one direction. Running `add_constructor_checked` is necessary and is NOT sufficient. The translator must additionally record Lean's own judgement and compare.

Catches the `Prop` exemption swallowing a real error. When the inductive's result sort is `Prop`, `check_constructor_universes` returns `Ok(())` immediately with no inspection of any field (type_checker.rs:555-557). Lean has the same impredicative exemption — but Lean ALSO restricts elimination out of such a `Prop`, and LOGOS's elimination gate is a different rule (`is_subsingleton_prop`, T11-020). So the two systems place the restriction in different places, and a translator that checks only the declaration has checked only half of it.

Catches the interaction with T11-002. The field's sort `s` comes from `infer_sort(&ext, param_type)` (type_checker.rs:569), which for a field whose type is `Prop` goes through `infer_type`'s `Sort` arm at :54 — `u.succ()` — and `Prop.succ()` is `Type(1)` (term.rs:198). Meanwhile the comparison `s ≤ target` is decided in the ℕ-model where `Prop` is `0`. So a `Prop`-typed field is measured with one procedure and compared with another that disagrees by one about `Prop`. The check is sound in the direction that matters for paradoxes and is not a faithful model of Lean's judgement.

Catches skipping the check entirely. `add_constructor` (context.rs:413-431) performs no universe check at all, so the universe-inconsistent inductive Lean refused will register silently and the Girard/Hurkens derivation of `False` becomes available. That is T11-013's rejection; this case is the one that remains even AFTER the translator does the right thing and uses `add_constructor_checked`.

Catches assuming a correctly-declared inductive is usable. `derive_recursor` hard-codes the motive target to `Sort(Type 0)` for anything that is not a non-subsingleton `Prop` inductive (recursor.rs:64-71). So an inductive that passes the universe check AT `Type 1` gets an eliminator that can only eliminate into `Type 0` — the declaration is accepted and the type is not usable at its own level.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_UNIVERSE_CONSTRAINT_NOT_REPRODUCED for each commented form below, and emits nothing. The decisive harness assertion is differential: for every inductive in the corpus, the translator must record Lean's computed field sorts and the inductive's declared sort, and must assert Lean's NON-cumulative constraint itself — never delegating to `check_constructor_universes`, whose `≤` is the wrong relation for reproducing Lean's judgement.
diag: E_UNIVERSE_CONSTRAINT_NOT_REPRODUCED — must name the inductive, the field, the sort Lean computed for it, and the sort Lean required, and state that LOGOS's own constructor check uses a cumulative `≤` and therefore does not reproduce the judgement. Must emit nothing.

cases.title: The large-elimination gate measures TWO DIFFERENT TELESCOPES — it admits shapes Lean refuses, and combined with proof irrelevance the admitted direction is inconsistent
cases.lean: Prop-valued inductive, singleton elimination, Acc.rec, Eq.rec (J), False.elim, an indexed Prop whose constructor carries a data field
cases.target: For the shapes both systems admit (`False`, `Eq`, `Acc`, `And`): the derived recursor, via `derive_recursor` + `add_definition`. For every other shape: a rejection. The translator must decide by LEAN's criterion, never by calling `is_subsingleton_prop`.
evidence: kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1688-1716 (`is_subsingleton_prop`, in full). The decisive three lines are :1694-1701: it takes `ctor_type` from `ctx.get_constructors(...)[0]`, takes `ind_type` from `ctx.get_global(inductive_name)`, and computes `let arity = pi_param_count(&ind_type);` — the number of leading `Π` binders of the INDUCTIVE's type, i.e. parameters PLUS INDICES. It then walks the CONSTRUCTOR's telescope at :1703-1710 and applies the propositionality test only when `i >= arity`. A well-formed constructor's telescope begins with the PARAMETERS and then continues with its FIELDS — the indices are not bound there, they are determined by the constructor's target. So the skip of `arity` binders discards `num_indices` genuine FIELDS. Two telescopes, one counter. kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1719-1724 (`pi_param_count` — a plain recursive count, with no reference to `inductive_num_params`); kernel/src/context.rs:374 and :404-411 (`add_indexed_inductive` / `inductive_num_indices` — the params/indices split IS recorded in the context, and `is_subsingleton_prop` does not consult it); kernel/src/recursor.rs:64-71 (`derive_recursor` chooses the motive target using this predicate); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:672-680 (the indexed-match path applies the same predicate); kernel/src/type_checker.rs:1547-1567 (`proof_irrelevant` — any two proofs of one `Prop` are definitionally equal); kernel/src/prelude.rs:1354-1421 (`add_indexed_inductive("Acc", acc_ty, 2)` — `Acc` has arity 3 and 2 parameters, and it is the full-arity skip that makes `Acc` come out a subsingleton and therefore makes well-founded recursion's eliminator exist at all: the behaviour is load-bearing, not merely a latent bug)
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS, AND THE PLACE IT BITES HARDEST.** LOGOS's kernel accepting a term is not evidence that the translation is faithful — and here the admitted direction is not merely unfaithful, it is INCONSISTENT WITH ANOTHER RULE THE SAME KERNEL HAS. Walk it on the example below. · `Tag : Bool → Prop` with the single constructor `mk : ∀ (n : Nat), Tag (n == 0)`. `ind_type` is `Π(_:Bool). Prop`, so `arity = 1` (type_checker.rs:1701). · The constructor's telescope is `Π(n : Nat). Tag (n == 0)` — ONE binder, and it is a FIELD, not a parameter or an index. · The loop at :1703-1710 skips it because `i = 0 < arity = 1`. Nothing is ever tested. `is_subsingleton_prop` returns `true`. · So `derive_recursor` (recursor.rs:64-71) gives `Tag` a `Sort(Type 0)` motive: large elimination is ALLOWED, and a proof of `Tag b` can be eliminated to produce the `Nat` it was built from. Lean forbids exactly this (its `Tag.rec` motive is `Prop`-valued; the error is reproduced below). · Now add `proof_irrelevant` (type_checker.rs:1547-1567). `Tag.mk 1` and `Tag.mk 2` are both proofs of `Tag false`, so they are DEFINITIONALLY EQUAL. Congruence then makes `extract (Tag.mk 1) ≡ extract (Tag.mk 2)`, i.e. `1 ≡ 2`. A proof yields data, and proof irrelevance says that data is equal to other data. The kernel typechecks every step.

Catches the translator delegating the decision. The tempting workflow is: emit the inductive, call `derive_recursor`, and if the kernel gives you a `Type 0` motive then large elimination must be legitimate. It is not — the kernel is answering with the predicate above. The criterion must be computed from LEAN's judgement, recorded at translation time, and compared.

Catches the REFUSED direction, which loses proofs rather than soundness. The same counter runs the other way whenever the inductive's recorded arity is SMALLER than the constructor's parameter prefix — which the translator controls, because `add_inductive` treats the whole arity as parameters while `add_indexed_inductive` takes an explicit split (context.rs:253 vs :374, and T03-005). Register a parameterised `Prop` with a sort that omits its parameters and the gate starts testing parameter binders for propositionality, `infer_sort` returns `Type 0` for a `Type`-valued parameter, and a perfectly legitimate singleton elimination — `Eq`'s J, `False`'s ex falso — is refused.

Catches "fixing" the gate by disabling it. The predicate is load-bearing for the prelude: `Acc` is registered with `add_indexed_inductive("Acc", acc_ty, 2)` at arity 3 (prelude.rs:1379), and it is precisely the full-arity skip that lets `is_subsingleton_prop` return `true` for it, which is what gives `Acc` a `Type 0` motive and makes well-founded recursion's eliminator exist. A translator that works around the gate by re-registering prelude types will break `Acc`, `Eq` and `False` together.

Catches the shapes where the two DO agree, which is most of them, and which is why this is easy to miss. `False` (zero constructors), `And` (one constructor, both fields `Prop`), `Eq` (one constructor, no fields beyond the arity), `Or` (two constructors — refused by both) all come out the same. The divergence needs an INDEXED `Prop` with a data-carrying constructor, which is rare in mathematical Lean and common in program-verification Lean.
oracle: For each declaration below the translator emits a recursor ONLY when Lean's own criterion admits large elimination, and a rejection otherwise; and a loss record with category GATE_IS_NOT_LEAN'S names, per inductive, the parameter count, the index count, and the constructor fields LOGOS's gate would skip. The decisive harness assertion is differential: for every `Prop` inductive in the corpus, `is_subsingleton_prop`'s answer is computed AND Lean's answer is computed, and any disagreement must have been reported — a translator that never computes Lean's answer fails this case even if every emitted term typechecks.
loss: GATE_IS_NOT_LEAN'S. Lean admits large elimination from a `Prop` iff the inductive has zero constructors, or exactly one whose every NON-PARAMETER field is a proof. LOGOS admits it iff the inductive has zero constructors, or exactly one whose constructor telescope, AFTER DISCARDING `params + indices` LEADING BINDERS, contains only propositional entries. On a `Prop` with no indices the two coincide. On an INDEXED `Prop` they do not, and LOGOS's is strictly more permissive by exactly the number of indices. The loss record must state which criterion was used and must list, per declaration, the fields the LOGOS gate skipped.
note: INDEX lists T11-020 as `degrade`, and this file is kept at `degrade` so the conformance IDs stay stable. I disagree with the verdict for half the case and think it should be SPLIT. The two directions are not the same kind of failure: · The REFUSED direction (LOGOS's gate rejects a shape Lean admits) is a genuine `degrade`: a proof is lost, nothing unsound is emitted, and a loss record is the right response. · The ADMITTED direction (LOGOS's gate accepts a shape Lean refuses) is a `reject`. As the first `@guard` shows, it is not merely unfaithful — combined with `proof_irrelevant` it makes two distinct `Nat`s definitionally equal, which is an inconsistency in the emitted theory, not a lost proof. It belongs with T11-013 and T11-014 as a hard rejection with its own diagnostic (E_LARGE_ELIMINATION_NOT_LEAN'S), because "emit the term plus a loss record" is not an acceptable response to it. A harness should therefore score the admitted-direction declarations below (`Tag`, `Sized`) as `reject` cases even while the case ID's nominal verdict stays `degrade`.

cases.title: Emitting a DEAD `InferenceRule` — seven of the 46 variants have no certifier arm, and the failure arrives as a certification error, not a translation error
cases.lean: a temporal/modal-flavoured proof: transitivity of a time order, a safety property by induction over a trace, fixpoint unfolding of an `Always` predicate, an existential witness for an `Eventually`
cases.target: (none — the seven variants below must never appear in an emitted `DerivationTree`; a proof that seems to need one must be re-expressed with a live rule or rejected)
evidence: logicaffeine_proof/src/lib.rs:488-728 (the `InferenceRule` enum, 46 variants); logicaffeine_proof/src/lib.rs:554-582 (the seven modal/temporal variants: `ModalAccess` at :558, `ModalGeneralization` at :562, `TemporalTransitivity` at :568, `TemporalInduction` at :571, `TemporalUnfolding` at :575, `EventualityProgress` at :579, `UntilInduction` at :582); logicaffeine_proof/src/certifier.rs:237 (`certify(tree, ctx)` — the dispatch, a `match &tree.rule` with one arm per implemented rule) and certifier.rs:1558-1562 (the CATCH-ALL: `rule => Err(KernelError::CertificationError(format!( "Certification not implemented for {:?}", rule)))` — a grep of `certifier.rs` for `Modal`, `Temporal`, `Eventuality` or `Until` finds NO rule arm, so all seven land here); logicaffeine_proof/src/verify.rs:25-43 (`VerifiedProof`: "`verified == true` **iff** `proof_term.is_some()` and that term type-checks" — so a tree carrying a dead rule yields `verified == false` with a `verification_error`, never a proof); logicaffeine_proof/src/verify.rs:305-338 (`check_derivation` — the entry point that runs the certifier over an externally supplied tree); logicaffeine_tests/tests/phase_hw_temporal.rs:165,171 (the only other references to two of the variants in the whole repo are `let _rule = …` bindings in a test — nothing CONSTRUCTS them in any engine)
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS, ON THE PROOF-OBJECT SIDE.** The kernel accepting a term is not evidence of faithfulness — and here the analogous trap is that the DERIVATION LAYER accepting a tree is not evidence either. A `DerivationTree` is an ordinary Rust value: it can be constructed with any of the 46 variants, it passes every type check in the proof crate, and it fails only when `certify` reaches its catch-all. So a translator that picks a rule by NAME — `TemporalTransitivity` looks exactly right for a proof that `t1 < t2` and `t2 < t3` give `t1 < t3` — builds a tree that is well-formed, well-typed Rust and is not a proof of anything.

Catches the failure being misread. The error is `KernelError::CertificationError("Certification not implemented for TemporalTransitivity")`, surfaced through `VerifiedProof.verification_error` with `verified == false` (verify.rs:25-43). That reads like a KERNEL limitation — "the certifier does not support this yet" — and invites the translator to retry, to widen the search, or to report the input as unsupported. All three are wrong: the tree the translator built was never certifiable, and the correct response is to rebuild it out of live rules or to reject.

Catches `verified == false` being treated as a soft result. A `VerifiedProof` can carry a `derivation` and still have `verified == false` (verify.rs:29-33), and `compile_theorem` reports exactly that case as "derivation found but NOT kernel-certified (this is not a proof)". A translator that records "a derivation was found" as success has recorded the opposite of what happened.

Catches the rules being plausible. These seven are not obscure: transitivity of a temporal order, k-induction for a safety property, fixpoint unfolding of `Always`, and a witness for `Eventually` are the four most natural shapes in any verification-flavoured Lean file. The variants EXIST, with doc comments stating their logic (lib.rs:556-582), which is precisely what makes selecting one look correct. Existence in the enum is not evidence of implementation; the only evidence is an arm in `certify`.

Catches the generalisation. The lesson is not "avoid seven names" — it is that the translator must verify, per rule, that `certifier.rs` has an arm, and must keep that list pinned the same way it pins `PRELUDE_VERSION` (T11-015). The enum and the certifier are in different crates and can drift.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_DEAD_INFERENCE_RULE for any proof it would have expressed with one of the seven variants, and emits no `DerivationTree`. The decisive harness assertion is structural: the multiset of `InferenceRule` variants appearing in every emitted `DerivationTree` across the corpus must contain none of `ModalAccess`, `ModalGeneralization`, `TemporalTransitivity`, `TemporalInduction`, `TemporalUnfolding`, `EventualityProgress`, `UntilInduction` — checked on the tree before it is handed to `check_derivation`, not inferred from the result.
diag: E_DEAD_INFERENCE_RULE — must name the variant, state that `certifier.rs` has no arm for it and that the catch-all at certifier.rs:1558-1562 will reject the whole tree, and emit nothing. The translator must not hand the tree to `check_derivation` and report the resulting `verification_error` as the user's problem.

cases.title: Only the FIRST `## Theorem` block is proved — a multi-theorem Lean file silently becomes a one-theorem document
cases.lean: a .lean file containing several theorems, a namespace of lemmas, a `section` of results, a theorem that depends on an earlier lemma in the same file
cases.target: One vernacular document PER Lean theorem, each compiled separately — never one document with several `## Theorem` blocks.
evidence: logicaffeine_language/src/compile.rs:1070 (`pub fn compile_theorem(input: &str)`); logicaffeine_language/src/compile.rs:1105-1119 (the decisive lines: after parsing the whole program into `statements`, it does `let theorem = statements.iter().find_map(|stmt| if let Stmt::Theorem(t) = stmt { Some(t) } else { None }).ok_or_else(|| … "No theorem block found in input")?;` — `find_map` returns the FIRST match. Every later `Stmt::Theorem` in the parsed program is silently discarded, with no warning and no count); logicaffeine_language/src/compile.rs:1161 (the only diagnostic the function ever emits about a theorem's status is "derivation found but NOT kernel-certified (this is not a proof)" — there is nothing about discarded blocks); logicaffeine_proof/src/verify.rs:25-43 (`VerifiedProof.verified == true` iff a kernel term was produced and typechecked — it describes ONE theorem, so a `verified: true` result says nothing whatever about the rest of the document); LOGOS_FACTS: the three vernacular surfaces do not interoperate, so "put the lemmas on another surface" is not an escape
guards: **TIER 11 THESIS, AT THE DOCUMENT LEVEL.** A successful LOGOS result is not evidence that the translation is complete. This is the quietest failure in the whole corpus: the translator concatenates a file's theorems into one document, calls `compile_theorem`, gets back a `VerifiedProof` with `verified == true`, and reports success. The result is true — of the FIRST theorem. The other nine were parsed into `Stmt::Theorem` values, passed over by `find_map` (compile.rs:1105-1119), and dropped. Nothing in the return value carries a count, so there is no field to check; the only way to know is to have counted the inputs.

Catches the silence being mistaken for absence of input. `compile_theorem` DOES error when there is no theorem at all — `"No theorem block found in input"` (compile.rs:1116-1119) — which trains the reader to expect a diagnostic when something is wrong with the theorem blocks. There is no corresponding diagnostic for "found ten, proved one".

Catches the intra-file dependency. Lean files are written as lemma-then-theorem chains, and after splitting into one document per theorem the later document has no access to the earlier one's result: each `compile_theorem` call builds its own kernel context from `StandardLibrary::register` plus that document's own premises (verify.rs:338-345). So the lemma must be re-stated as a `Given:` — which changes the theorem's statement — or re-proved inside the second document. A translator that splits the file but does not fix up the dependencies produces documents whose theorems are strictly weaker than the Lean originals, all of which certify.

Catches the "just use a different surface" move. Surface B (`## Axiom` / `## Theory`) accepts a sequence of `Axiom`/`Theorem` lines and so looks like the fix — but its `parse_term` accepts ONLY a bare identifier (formula.rs:427-432), so no arithmetic and no nested function terms survive the move; and Surface C (literate) has no `forall` in its `Statement:` grammar at all. The surfaces do not interoperate, so the choice is per-theorem and is itself a translation decision (T12-011).

Catches counting theorems in the SOURCE rather than in the parse. What `compile_theorem` iterates is `statements`, the parsed program (compile.rs:1103-1105), so the count that matters is how many `Stmt::Theorem` values the LOGOS parser produced from the emitted document — which may differ from the number of Lean theorems if the emitter merged or split any. The check must be on the emitted document.
oracle: The translator emits exactly one vernacular document per Lean theorem, and each document contains exactly ONE `## Theorem` block; and a loss record with category ONE_THEOREM_PER_DOCUMENT names the source file's theorem count and every intra-file dependency that had to be re-supplied as a premise or re-proved. A harness asserts, for every emitted document, that the count of `## Theorem` blocks is 1, and that the number of documents emitted for this file is exactly TEN.
