loss: ONE_THEOREM_PER_DOCUMENT. A Lean file is a sequence of declarations; a LOGOS vernacular document proves exactly one theorem. The translation is therefore one-to-many at the file level, and the loss is the FILE STRUCTURE: the grouping, the ordering, and — critically — the intra-file dependencies, since a later Lean theorem that cites an earlier lemma must have that lemma's statement re-supplied as a `Given:` premise or re-proved, because there is no cross-document lemma environment. The loss record must name the theorem count and the dependency edges that were broken.

cases.title: Surface A (`## Theorem` / `Given:` / `Prove:`) — a pure first-order syllogism
cases.lean: theorem over unary Prop-valued predicates on an opaque domain; ∀-elimination and modus ponens only (no arithmetic, no equality, no data)
cases.target: An English theorem block, parsed by `logicaffeine_language::parser::parse_theorem_block` and proved by `logicaffeine_language::compile_theorem`: ```logos ## Theorem: Socrates_Mortality Given: All men are mortal. Given: Socrates is a man. Prove: Socrates is mortal. Proof: Auto. ``` `Auto` routes to `logicaffeine_proof::verify::prove_certify_check` (compile.rs:1152), whose derivation must carry `UniversalInst` then `ModusPonens` and must come back with `verified == true`.
evidence: language/src/parser/mod.rs:5977-6194 (`parse_theorem_block`: optional `Given` lines, REQUIRED `Prove` line, optional `Proof` line defaulting to `Auto`); language/src/compile.rs:1070-1176 (`compile_theorem`); language/src/compile.rs:1152 (`Auto` ⟶ `prove_certify_check`); tests/phase63_theorem_parser.rs:31-52 (the VERBATIM block above, asserted to compile and to produce `Proved`/`ModusPonens`/`PremiseMatch`); tests/phase63_theorem_parser.rs:136-154 (three-premise chain); tests/phase_studio_grid_proof.rs:51-64 (the same syllogism through `compile_theorem_for_ui`, asserted to keep its `UniversalInst` trace rather than being grounded — see T12-014)
guards: Catches a translator that writes FOL into `Given:`/`Prove:`. Those lines go through the FULL ENGLISH SENTENCE PARSER — `self.parse_sentence()` at parser/mod.rs:6072 and :6136 — not through `logicaffeine_proof::formula::parse_formula`. `Given: forall x, Man(x) -> Mortal(x).` is not a parse error you will notice: the lexer will tokenize `forall`, `x`, `Man` … as ordinary English words and the sentence parser will either error with a syntax complaint that names an English category, or (worse) succeed and build a `LogicExpr` about a *thing called "forall"*. The formal-FOL spelling belongs to Surface B (T12-006), which this surface does not accept.

Catches emitting the Lean predicate names verbatim. The premise/goal predicates must MATCH after the parser's noun canonicalisation — `men` is canonicalised to `Man` (phase63_theorem_parser.rs:29 documents this as the reason the syllogism closes). A translator that renders `Man` as the plural noun in one line and the singular in another is relying on that pass, and a translator that invents a predicate spelling the English lexicon does not canonicalise the same way produces two distinct predicates and an unprovable goal — which surfaces as a *proof failure*, not a parse error.

Catches forgetting that `Prove:` is mandatory. A block with only `Given:` lines returns `ParseErrorKind::ExpectedKeyword { keyword: "Prove" }` (parser/mod.rs:6125-6128); there is no "state the goal last" fallback.

Catches emitting TWO theorem blocks in one document and assuming both are checked. `compile_theorem` takes the FIRST `Stmt::Theorem` it finds (compile.rs:1106-1119, `find_map`) and silently ignores every later one. One Lean theorem per LOGOS document. (T11-022 is the adversarial twin.)
oracle: `compile_theorem(<emitted text>)` returns `Ok(s)` AND `s` contains `"[kernel-verified]"` — the string only `compile.rs:1155-1159` emits. The weaker `s.contains("Proved")` is NOT sufficient, because the unverified branch (compile.rs:1160-1164) also returns `Ok`. See T12-013.
note: This is the ONLY shape of Lean theorem for which Surface A is the right target: an unquantified-over-data, predicate-only entailment. The moment the statement mentions a term operation the answer changes to `reject` (T12-002) or to the raw kernel path (T12-011).

cases.title: Surface A cannot state an arithmetic goal — `∀ n : Nat, n + 0 = n` is not expressible
cases.lean: theorem whose statement contains a term-level operation on a bound variable (HAdd.hAdd / Nat.add) under a ∀ binder
cases.target: (none — no sound rendering on Surface A)
evidence: language/src/parser/mod.rs:6072 and :6136 — a `Given:`/`Prove:` line is parsed by `self.parse_sentence()`, the declarative ENGLISH sentence parser, which produces a `LogicExpr`. There is no term-expression entry point on this path.

language/src/parser/mod.rs:8352-8363 — the English infix operator words `plus`/`minus` exist ONLY in the IMPERATIVE expression grammar: they build `Expr::BinaryOp { op: BinaryOpKind::Add, .. }` through `alloc_imperative_expr`, a different arena and a different AST from the `LogicExpr` a theorem premise is made of. `plus` is unreachable from `Prove:`.

language/src/proof_convert.rs:840-860 (`term_to_proof_term`) — the ONLY route by which Surface A ever emits `ProofTerm::Function("Add", …)` is `canonical_arithmetic_fn` (proof_convert.rs:49-57) applied to a `Term::Function` the parser built in parser/verb.rs:1005-1032 — the comparative-with-differential construction ("… scored 5 points more than …"). That construction produces `Score(x) = Add(Score(y), 5)`: arithmetic over a MEASURE FUNCTION OF AN ENTITY, keyed to the LIA oracle's `Add`/`Sub` vocabulary. It cannot be pointed at a quantified numeric variable.

language/src/compile.rs:1152 — `Auto` reaches `logicaffeine_proof::verify::prove_certify_check`, whose search vocabulary is `ProofExpr` (proof/src/lib.rs:199-244): `Predicate`, `Identity`, `Atom`, connectives, `ForAll`/`Exists` over UNTYPED variables. `ForAll` carries a bare `variable: String` (lib.rs:235-238) — there is no place to put `: Nat`, so the binder cannot even be restricted to the naturals except by adding a guard predicate, which changes the proposition.
guards: THE trap of this tier. `∀ n : Nat, n + 0 = n` reads like English, so the tempting emission is Prove: For all n, n plus 0 equals n. `equals` IS a real logic-mode token (tests/phase22_equals.rs:4-15 asserts `TokenType::Equals` is produced for `"x equals 5"`), and `for all` IS ordinary English, so this line does not look obviously wrong. But `plus` never reaches the logic grammar (parser/mod.rs:8355 is imperative-only), so at best the sentence parser errors on an unexpected word, and at worst it reads `plus` as an unknown noun and builds an `Identity` between a variable and a *thing*. Neither is `n + 0 = n`.

Catches the second tempting wrong move: axiomatising the arithmetic away as a predicate, e.g. Given: Zero is an additive identity. Prove: Every number plus zero is itself. A translator that does this has silently replaced the Lean proposition with an English paraphrase whose LOGOS meaning is a relation between two *entities*. It will "prove" — `Auto` will happily discharge a paraphrase from a paraphrased premise — and the resulting certificate attests a proposition that is not the translation of the Lean type. Every `reject` in this corpus is dangerous; this one is dangerous because it SUCCEEDS.

Catches reaching for the comparative-differential path (parser/verb.rs:1005-1032) as an escape hatch. That path requires an English comparative over a measure of a named entity and always names the measure after a unit or the verb; there is no phrasing of it that makes the measured object a ∀-bound numeral, and its `Add` lands in the oracle's Int vocabulary, not LOGOS `Nat`.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_SURFACE_A_NO_TERM_ARITHMETIC, names the subterm, and writes no `## Theorem` block. If the translator instead routes this theorem to Surface C or the kernel path, that is a PASS provided it records the surface decision — the failure mode being caught is emitting Surface A text.
diag: E_SURFACE_A_NO_TERM_ARITHMETIC — must name the offending Lean subterm (`n + 0`, head `HAdd.hAdd`/`Nat.add`), state that `Given:`/`Prove:` lines are parsed by the English sentence parser and carry no term grammar, and redirect: Surface C (T12-008) has infix `+ - *` and the word `equals`, and the raw kernel path (T12-011) has the real thing. Emitting NOTHING on Surface A is required.
note: INDEX.md records this case as "no term arithmetic exists" on Surface A. That is very nearly right but not literally right, and the difference matters to a translator author: parser/verb.rs:1005-1032 + proof_convert.rs:845-860 do construct `ProofTerm::Function("Add", [Measure(y), k])` for one specific English comparative construction. The accurate statement is: **Surface A has no term grammar a translator can address** — the only arithmetic it can build is a by-product of a fixed English idiom over entity measures, and it is unreachable for a ∀-bound numeric variable. The verdict `reject` is unaffected.

cases.title: Mapping a Lean tactic block onto a Surface A `Proof:` script
cases.lean: `by` tactic block: intro, cases (with `inl`/`inr`/`intro` alternatives), constructor / Or.inl / Or.inr, assumption
cases.target: A `## Theorem` block whose `Proof:` line is anything other than the bare word `Auto`, which parser/mod.rs:6157-6174 collects verbatim and wraps as `ProofStrategy::Script(<joined lexemes>)`; `compile_theorem` then runs it through `ProofState::run_script` and `qed()` (compile.rs:1136-1150). The three verbatim scripts this case targets, quoted from the suite: ```logos ## Theorem: Sad_Implies_Happy Given: Bob is happy. Prove: If Bob is sad then Bob is happy. Proof: Assume h. By assumption. ``` ```logos ## Theorem: Or_Commutative Given: Bob is happy or Bob is sad. Prove: Bob is sad or Bob is happy. Proof: By cases on hp0. Right, by assumption. Left, by assumption. ``` ```logos ## Theorem: And_Commutative Given: Bob is happy and Bob is tall. Prove: Bob is tall and Bob is happy. Proof: By cases on hp0. Split, by assumption, by assumption. ```
evidence: tests/e2e_studio_examples.rs:292-305, :306-320, :321-335 — the three blocks above are quoted verbatim from those tests, each asserted `result.is_ok()` and `output.contains("Proved")`; proof/src/tactic_script.rs:275-292 (the primitive table: `intro`/`exact`/`cases`/`rewrite`/`exists` take one argument; `assumption`/`simp`/`decide`/`omega`/`crush`/`split`/`left`/`right`/`auto`/`induction` take none); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:308-327 (`canonical`: the alias table — `assume`/`suppose`/`let`/`fix` ⟶ `intro`, `destruct`/`consider` ⟶ `cases`, `both`/`constructor` ⟶ `split`, `automatically`/`trivially` ⟶ `auto`); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:298-303 (`is_filler`: `by the on that now with we it a an of to and` are skipped, which is what makes "By cases on hp0" mean `cases hp0`); proof/src/tactic_script.rs:61-64 (`.`, `,` and `;` all lex to the SAME separator token, so sentence punctuation is sequencing); language/src/parser/mod.rs:6079-6094 (unnamed premises are named positionally `hp0`, `hp1`, … — see also T12-004)
guards: Catches a translator that transcribes the Lean tactic block token for token. `intro hp` is fine; `exact (Or.inr hp)` is a `ScriptError` at best — but `exact Or` (if the emitter strips the application) is NOT an error, it is a lookup for a hypothesis named `Or`, which fails at run time with a message about hypotheses, not about terms. The translator must lower Lean's term-valued `exact` into the LOGOS constructor tactics (`left`/`right`/`split`) plus `assumption`, or refuse.

Catches assuming `Proof:` content is validated at parse time. It is not: parser/mod.rs:6157-6174 collects every lexeme up to the next `##` header, a `Dedent`, or EOF and joins them with spaces. Any English at all becomes a `Script(String)`. The failure surfaces only when `run_script` is called inside `compile_theorem` (compile.rs:1145-1149), as a `ParseError::Custom` carrying a `ScriptError` — so a translator that "parses" its own output by calling the LOGOS *parser* will never see the problem.

Catches capitalisation assumptions. `canonical` is case-insensitive (tactic_script.rs:309, `word.to_ascii_lowercase()`), so `Assume` and `assume` both work — but `first`, `try` and `repeat` are matched as EXACT lowercase words in `parse_atom` (tactic_script.rs:221, :232, :236). `Try assumption.` is not `try assumption`; it is an unknown tactic named `Try`.
oracle: `compile_theorem(<emitted text>)` returns `Ok(s)` with `s.contains("[kernel-verified]")`, AND the loss record names TACTIC_GRANULARITY. A translator that emits `Proof: Auto.` for a theorem whose Lean proof was a tactic block has not failed this case — but it must then record STRATEGY_ERASURE, because `Auto` is a different proof object (T12-013, T12-014).
loss: TACTIC_GRANULARITY. Every one of these is a real, silent change of meaning relative to the Lean tactic block, and each must be recorded: · `exact` takes a HYPOTHESIS NAME, never a term (tactic_script.rs:277, `c::exact(&arg()?)` where `arg` returns a `String`). Lean's `exact Or.inr hp` has no rendering; it must be re-expressed as `right; assumption`. · `cases` has no pattern language and no case names. Binder names are assigned by LOGOS: `A ∧ B` ⟶ `h_1`,`h_2`; `A ∨ B` ⟶ `h_l`,`h_r`; `∃` ⟶ `h_w` plus a fresh constant. Lean's `with | inl hp => …` naming is dropped, and the two branches are sequenced by punctuation rather than addressed by name. · `rewrite` rewrites EVERY occurrence; Lean's `rw [h]` rewrites the first match and `conv`/positional targeting does not exist. · `simp` takes no lemma list; `simp only [foo]` cannot be expressed. · `exists` takes a bare constant (`c::exists(ProofTerm::Constant(arg()?))`, tactic_script.rs:280) — no witness terms. · `apply`, `induction_over` and `all_goals` are Rust-API-only and have NO script spelling (tactic_script.rs:275-292 has no arm for them). Because branch structure is carried by *sequencing*, the mapping is only sound when the Lean block's goals are discharged in the order LOGOS spawns them. That ordering is an implementation detail of the tactic engine, not a contract — so the loss record must also carry GOAL_ORDER_DEPENDENCE.

cases.title: Surface A named premise — `Given (h):` binds the hypothesis name a script uses
cases.lean: named hypothesis binder in a theorem signature, referenced by name from the tactic proof
cases.target: A `Given (<name>):` premise line, whose name lands in `TheoremBlock::premise_names` and reaches `ProofState::start_with_names` (compile.rs:1138-1139): ```logos ## Theorem: Or_Comm_Named Given (h): Bob is happy or Bob is sad. Prove: Bob is sad or Bob is happy. Proof: By cases on h. Right, by assumption. Left, by assumption. ``` ```logos ## Theorem: Some_Mortal_Is_A_Man Given (h): Some man is mortal. Prove: Some mortal is a man. Proof: By cases on h. By automation. ```
evidence: tests/e2e_studio_examples.rs:336-350 and :365-379 — both blocks above are quoted verbatim from those tests, each asserted `Ok` and `Proved`; language/src/parser/mod.rs:6079-6100 — the `Given (h):` form: an `LParen` immediately after `Given`, one token taken as the name, `RParen`, then the colon. `premise_names.push(this_name)` runs on EVERY `Given`, pushing `None` for an unnamed one, so the vector is positionally parallel to `premises`; language/src/ast/theorem.rs:29-33 (`premise_names: Vec<Option<String>>`, documented as "so a `Proof:` script can refer to it as `cases h` rather than the positional `hp0`"); language/src/compile.rs:1138-1139 (`ProofState::start_with_names(premises, &theorem.premise_names, goal)`)
guards: Catches a translator that names premises but proves by `Auto`. The names are threaded ONLY through the `Script` branch: compile.rs:1136 tests `if let ProofStrategy::Script(src) = &theorem.strategy`, and the `else` arm (compile.rs:1152) calls `prove_certify_check(&premises, &goal)` — which takes no names at all. Naming a premise costs nothing there, but a translator that believes the name is part of the proposition is wrong: it is proof-script scaffolding only.

Catches the positional/named mismatch. Premise names are POSITIONAL: the unnamed `Given:` lines in a block are still numbered `hp0`, `hp1`, … by position among ALL premises, not among the unnamed ones. A translator that emits `Given (h): …` first and then an unnamed `Given: …` must refer to the second as `hp1`, not `hp0`. Getting this wrong yields a `run_script` failure that reports a missing hypothesis, which reads like a proof-search failure.

Catches emitting a name that is also a tactic word. The name is consumed as a single token by parser/mod.rs:6087-6090 with no keyword check, and it is then spliced into script text where `canonical` (tactic_script.rs:308-327) matches case-insensitively. `Given (left): …` followed by `Proof: By cases on left.` parses as `cases` applied to … the filler-skipped next word, because `left` is itself a zero-argument tactic. Hypothesis names must be emitted from a reserved-word-avoiding namespace (`h0`, `h1`, …), never from the Lean binder name verbatim.

Catches assuming the parenthesised name may be multi-token. Only ONE token is taken (parser/mod.rs:6087-6090 advances exactly once inside the parens), so `Given (h_or_case):` is fine but `Given (my premise):` silently names the premise `my` and leaves `premise` to be consumed as part of the colon scan.
oracle: `compile_theorem(<emitted text>)` returns `Ok(s)` with `s.contains("[kernel-verified]")`, and the emitted script refers to the premise by the name given in parentheses. A differential check strengthens it: replacing `Given (h):` with `Given:` and `cases h` with `cases hp0` must produce the same verdict.

cases.title: `Proof: Induction on n.` — LOGOS's own documented spelling does not parse
cases.lean: `induction n with | zero => … | succ k ih => …`
cases.target: (none — the documented spelling is not accepted, and the accepted spelling cannot carry a Lean `induction` proof; see @note for the correct target)
evidence: language/src/ast/theorem.rs:47-50 — the doc comment on `ProofStrategy::Induction(String)` reads, verbatim: /// Induction on a variable (for inductive types like Nat, List). /// Example: `Proof: Induction on n.` This is the documentation an implementer will read, and it is wrong.

language/src/parser/mod.rs:6151-6174 — the `Proof:` line has exactly TWO outcomes. `if self.check(&TokenType::Auto)` yields `ProofStrategy::Auto`; EVERYTHING else is collected lexeme-by-lexeme to the end of the block and joined into `ProofStrategy::Script(script)`. `ProofStrategy::Induction` is never constructed here or anywhere — the only four construction sites in the workspace are parser/mod.rs:6153, :6171, :6173 and :6178, and they build only `Auto` and `Script`.

proof/src/tactic_script.rs:290 — `"induction" => Ok(c::induction())`. The primitive is ZERO-ARGUMENT: unlike `intro`/`exact`/`cases`/`rewrite`/`exists` (tactic_script.rs:276-280) it never calls the `arg()` closure, so it consumes no following word.

proof/src/tactic_script.rs:298-303 — `is_filler` skips `on`, but ONLY at the start of an atom or before an argument (`skip_filler` is called from `parse_atom`, :212, and from the `arg` closure, :265). After a zero-argument primitive returns, control is back in `parse_chain`/`parse_seq`, where no filler skip happens.
proof/src/tactic_script.rs:162-166 — `at_separator` accepts only `Semi` (lexed from `;`, `.`, `,` — see :61-64) or the literal word `then`. `on` is neither, so `parse_seq` breaks immediately.

proof/src/tactic_script.rs:346-351 — the leftover tokens then trip `return Err(ScriptError(format!("trailing tokens after the script: {:?}", …)))`. For `"Induction on n ."` the reported residue is `[Word("on"), Word("n"), Semi]`.

language/src/compile.rs:1145-1149 — `Err(e) => fail(e.to_string())`, and `Display for ScriptError` (tactic_script.rs:33-37) prefixes `"tactic script error: "`. With `derivation: None`, compile.rs:1165-1175 returns `Err(ParseError::Custom("Theorem '…' failed. … Error: tactic script error: trailing tokens after the script: [Word(\"on\"), Word(\"n\"), Semi]"))`.
guards: This is the single most likely thing to mislead an implementer in the whole tier, because the wrong spelling is in LOGOS's OWN source documentation and the right one is not documented anywhere. An implementer who reads `ast/theorem.rs:43-60`, sees four `ProofStrategy` variants with examples, and writes an emitter that maps Lean's `induction n` to `Proof: Induction on n.` has written code that is consistent with the type and consistent with the docs and cannot work.

Catches the belief that this fails at PARSE time. It does not: parser/mod.rs accepts the line unconditionally (it accepts any English at all) and builds a `Script`. The failure happens later, inside `compile_theorem`, and is reported as a *theorem failure* whose `Error:` field mentions trailing tokens — a message a harness scanning for "proof search failed" will misclassify as "LOGOS could not prove it" rather than "we emitted invalid syntax".

Catches "fix it by dropping the variable": `Proof: Induction.` DOES parse (`Induction` ⟶ `induction`, `.` ⟶ separator, nothing left over) — and that is worse, because the variable the Lean proof inducted on is now gone. LOGOS's `ProofState::induction` (proof/src/tactic.rs:561-570) inducts on whatever variable the FOCUSED GOAL's outermost `∀` binds. If the Lean theorem inducted on a variable that is not the goal's first binder, the two proofs are about different things, and the LOGOS one may still certify.

Catches "fix it with the sibling variant": `Proof: ModusPonens.` (the documented example for `ProofStrategy::ByRule`, theorem.rs:52-54) fails differently and more quietly — `canonical("modusponens")` returns `None` (tactic_script.rs:308-327 has no such arm), so the error is ``unknown tactic `ModusPonens` `` from tactic_script.rs:262. Both dead variants are covered by T12-012.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_DEAD_PROOF_STRATEGY_SPELLING and emits no `Proof: Induction …` line anywhere in its output. Negative oracle for a harness: feeding the documented spelling to `compile_theorem` must return `Err`, and the error string must contain `"trailing tokens after the script"`.
diag: E_DEAD_PROOF_STRATEGY_SPELLING — must state that `Proof: Induction on n.` is parsed as `Script("Induction on n .")`, that `induction` is a zero-argument tactic, and that the variable name is unrepresentable. Must NOT silently rewrite the user's intent to `Proof: Auto.`
note: The accepted spellings, quoted verbatim from the suite, are `"induction; auto; auto"` (proof/tests/tactic_script.rs:150-155, `script_induction_over_nat`, asserted kernel-verified) and its English form `"By induction. Automatically. Automatically."` (proof/tests/tactic_script.rs:195-200, `english_induction_proof`, likewise asserted kernel-verified). Both are run through `ProofState::run_script` directly; no test in the suite drives either of them through a Surface A `Proof:` line, so a translator that emits one into a `## Theorem` block is relying on the lexeme-collection round trip (parser/mod.rs:6157-6174) being transparent, which is untested.

Even with the correct spelling, Surface A cannot carry a Lean `induction n` proof. `ProofState::induction` (proof/src/tactic.rs:561-600) substitutes the bound variable with `ProofTerm::Constant("Zero")` and `ProofTerm::Function("Succ", [K<n>])` — so the premises must be English sentences about `Zero` and `Succ`, which is precisely the term arithmetic Surface A does not have (T12-002). The correct target for a Lean `induction` proof over `Nat` is Surface C (T12-010) or the raw kernel path (T12-011).

cases.title: Surface B (`## Theory`) — an axiomatic development over relations on bare identifiers
cases.lean: axiomatised relation on an opaque sort; theorems proved from the axioms by ∀-elimination and chaining; hypotheses passed explicitly
cases.target: A `## Theory` block whose body is a sequence of `Axiom` / `Theorem` declarations parsed by `logicaffeine_proof::development::parse_development` and discharged in citation order by `prove_library_with_axioms`: ```logos ## Theory Tarski Axiom pseudo_reflexivity: for all a b, Cong(a, b, b, a). Axiom inner_transitivity: for all a b c d e f, if Cong(a, b, c, d) and Cong(a, b, e, f) then Cong(c, d, e, f). Theorem reflexivity: prove for all a b, Cong(a, b, a, b). Theorem symmetry cites reflexivity: prove for all a b c d, if Cong(a, b, c, d) then Cong(c, d, a, b). ``` and, for a theorem with a premise: ```logos Axiom identity: for all a b c, if Cong(a, b, c, c) then a = b. Theorem null_segment: given Cong(P, Q, R, R); prove P = Q. ```
evidence: tests(language)/axiom_theory_blocks.rs:107-133 — the `## Theory Tarski` block above is quoted verbatim from `theory_block_collects_a_multiline_development_body`, which asserts the collected body parses to 2 axioms and 2 theorems and that the second theorem's `cites` is `["reflexivity"]`; tests(proof)/development_parser.rs:49-76 — the same development with a third theorem, run end to end through `prove_development` and asserted `result.verified` for all three; tests(proof)/development_parser.rs:79-93 — the `null_segment` theorem with a `given` premise, verbatim; tests(language)/axiom_theory_blocks.rs:47-66 — a standalone `## Axiom flip: for all a b, Cong(a, b, b, a).` block round-tripping through `parse_formula` to the expected `ProofExpr`; proof/src/development.rs:9-23 (the grammar: `Axiom <name> : <formula>.` and `Theorem <name> [cites n1, n2] : [given <f>;]* prove <f>.`, statements terminated by `.`, clauses by `;`, citations by `,`); tests(proof)/formula_parser.rs:43-93 (the formula grammar: `for all a b`, `if … then …`, `and`, `there exists x`, `a = b`); tests(proof)/formula_parser.rs:99-107 (`symbolic_and_english_spellings_agree`: `∀ a b c d, … ∧ … → …` parses identically to the English spelling); proof/src/formula.rs:439-450 (`ident_to_term`: uppercase- or digit-leading ⟶ `ProofTerm::Constant`, lowercase-leading ⟶ `ProofTerm::Variable`)
guards: Catches the case-convention bug, which is invisible and total. `Cong(a, b, b, a)` under `for all a b` is a universally quantified statement about VARIABLES. `Cong(A, B, B, A)` is a statement about four CONSTANTS — a completely different proposition that the quantifier prefix does not bind. Lean binder names are frequently uppercase (`P`, `Q`, `R`, `α`), so a translator that copies Lean binder names into Surface B formulas will emit constants where it meant variables, and `prove_library_with_axioms` will simply fail to prove the theorem — reported as a proof failure, never as a naming error. Bound variables must be lowercased on emission; free constants must be uppercased.

Catches the citation-order assumption. `citation_order` (proof/src/verify.rs:98-130) topologically sorts by `cites`, treating an UNKNOWN name as an external given rather than an error (verify.rs:110-113: `!known.contains(c) || placed_names.contains(c)`). A translator that misspells a cited lemma name gets no diagnostic at all — the citation is silently dropped and the theorem is attempted without it. Cited names must be emitted from the same mangling function that names the theorems.

Catches conflating the two block spellings. `## Axiom <name>: <formula>.` (one axiom, `Stmt::Axiom`) and `## Theory <name>` (a whole development body, `Stmt::Theory`) are different statements with different parse targets; the `Theory` body is NOT itself parsed by the language parser but collected as text and handed to `parse_development` (axiom_theory_blocks.rs:129). A translator that puts `Axiom`/`Theorem` declarations under a `## Axiom` header loses everything after the first formula.
Catches emitting a `Theorem` with no `prove` clause. `parse_theorem_decl` requires it; `given` clauses are optional and `;`-separated, and the goal is the clause introduced by `prove`.
oracle: `parse_development(<emitted body>)` returns `Ok(dev)` with the expected axiom and theorem counts, and `prove_development(<emitted body>)` returns a result for every theorem with `verified == true`. A weaker oracle that only checks `parse_development` is not sufficient: the case-convention bug parses fine.
note: Surface B is the right target for exactly the Lean theorems this case shows: relational, first-order, over an opaque sort, with no function symbols in the terms. Add one function symbol and the answer becomes `reject` (T12-007).

cases.title: Surface B rejects every non-atomic term — `parse_term` accepts a bare identifier only
cases.lean: a first-order statement containing a FUNCTION SYMBOL in term position: `Add n Zero = n`, `Loves x (father x)`
cases.target: (none — no sound rendering on Surface B)
evidence: proof/src/formula.rs:429-435 — the entire term grammar: fn parse_term(&mut self) -> Result<ProofTerm, FormulaError> { match self.advance() { Some(Tok::Ident(s)) => Ok(ident_to_term(s)), other => Err(FormulaError::new(format!("expected a term, found {other:?}"))), } } One token. No application, no parentheses, no nesting, no literals beyond a digit-leading identifier, no arithmetic.

proof/src/formula.rs:398-416 — a `Name(` opening is consumed as a PREDICATE (`ProofExpr::Predicate { name, args, world: None }`), and its arguments are parsed with `parse_term`. There is no context in which `Name(...)` is read as a term, so `Add(n, Zero)` is a *proposition*, not a number.

proof/src/formula.rs:418-423 — the `=` arm is reached only after `parse_atom` has read a BARE identifier and found no `(`. Once `Add(n, Zero)` has been consumed as a predicate at :398-416, the `=` is never examined here.

proof/src/formula.rs:57-68 — the leftover `=` then reaches the top level, where `if p.pos != p.tokens.len()` produces `FormulaError("unexpected trailing input near token Some(Eq)")`. So `Add(n, Zero) = n` is a *parse error*, and the error names a token, not the construct.

proof/src/lib.rs:140-141 — `ProofTerm::Function(String, Vec<ProofTerm>)` EXISTS in the proof IR, and the engine reasons with it (proof/src/tactic.rs:584-586 builds `Succ(K1)` during induction). It is only the Surface B *parser* that cannot write one. A translator that reads the IR and concludes the surface can express function terms has read the wrong layer.
guards: Catches the near-miss that PARSES. `Add(n, Zero)` alone is accepted — as the 0-argument-free proposition "n and Zero stand in the Add relation". So a translator that renders Lean's `Nat.add n 0 = n` by relationalising the function, e.g. Axiom add_zero: for all n, Add(n, Zero, n). gets a clean parse and a provable development. That is a *different theory*: it has replaced a function by a ternary relation without the totality and single-valuedness axioms that make the two equivalent. Every downstream theorem is then proved in a theory the Lean source did not state. If a translator does this, it is no longer a translator — and the kernel will not catch it, because the relational theory is perfectly consistent.

Catches the same near-miss in its equality form. `Add(n, Zero) = n` errors, but `AddNZero = n` does not — a translator that flattens the application into a single identifier to get past the parser has introduced a fresh CONSTANT (uppercase-leading, formula.rs:439-450) unrelated to `n` and `Zero`. It parses, it is provable from an axiom stating it, and it means nothing.

Catches assuming the symbolic spellings help. `formula.rs` accepts `∀`, `∃`, `∧`, `∨`, `¬`, `→`, `↔` as synonyms (tests/formula_parser.rs:99-107 asserts the two spellings agree) — but they are all CONNECTIVES. There is no symbolic spelling of application, and `+`/`*` are not tokens in this lexer at all.

Catches nesting a predicate inside a term. `Cong(a, father(b), c, d)` fails at `parse_term` on the `(` — error `"expected a term, found Some(LParen)"` — but `Cong(a, b, c, d) and Father(b, e)` parses, and a translator that Skolemises this way must record that it has changed the signature.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_SURFACE_B_TERM_NOT_ATOMIC and writes no `## Theory`/`## Axiom` text. Negative oracle for a harness: `parse_formula("for all n, Add(n, Zero) = n")` must return `Err` whose message contains `"unexpected trailing input"`.
diag: E_SURFACE_B_TERM_NOT_ATOMIC — must name the offending Lean subterm and its head symbol, state that `formula.rs:429-435` accepts a single identifier, and redirect to Surface C (T12-008, which has s-expression application) or the raw kernel path (T12-011). Must emit no `Axiom`/`Theorem` declaration.
note: The prohibition is on the SURFACE, not the engine. Anything a translator needs a function symbol for must go to Surface C or the kernel; there is no partial credit on Surface B, because the only available workaround (relationalisation) changes the theory rather than losing information, which makes it a `reject` and not a `degrade`.

cases.title: Surface C (literate kernel) — `Statement:` with s-expression application and infix arithmetic
cases.lean: arithmetic (in)equalities over free numeric variables: `x ≤ x`, `x < x + 1`, `2 * x ≤ 2 * x + 1`, `add a b = add b a`
cases.target: A literate theorem block executed by `logicaffeine_kernel::interface::Repl`, parsed by `literate_parser::parse_theorem`: ```logos ## Theorem: LeRefl Statement: (le x x). Proof: lia. ``` ```logos ## Theorem: LtSuccInfix Statement: x < x + 1. Proof: lia. ``` ```logos ## Theorem: LinearCoeffInfix Statement: 2 * x <= 2 * x + 1. Proof: lia. ``` ```logos ## Theorem: Commutativity_Add Statement: (add x y) equals (add y x). Proof: ring. ``` which registers `Command::Definition { name, ty: Some(Global("Derivation")), body: try_<tactic> ⌜statement⌝ }` (literate_parser.rs:564-585) and is applied by `Repl::execute` through `infer_type` + `Context::add_definition` (interface/repl.rs:36-72).
evidence: tests/phase_literate_lia.rs:136-145 (`Statement: x <= x.`), :150-159 (`Statement: 2 < 5.`), :165-174 (`Statement: x < x + 1.`), :210-219 (`Statement: 2 * x <= 2 * x + 1.`), :225-234 (`Statement: x - 1 < x.`), :240-249 (`Statement: x ≤ x.`), :255-264 (`Statement: 5 ≥ 3.`) — all quoted verbatim, all asserted to execute; tests/phase_literate_ring.rs:34-43 and :49-58 (the s-expression `equals` forms, verbatim); tests/phase_literate_omega.rs:15,:22,:30,:73,:101 (the `(Lt 2 5)`, `(implies (Gt x 0) (Ge x 1))`, `(implies (Le (mul 3 x) 10) (Le x 3))` forms); tests/phase_literate_simp.rs:38,:46,:64 (`(Eq (add 2 3) 5)`, `(Eq (mul (add 1 1) 3) 6)`, `(Eq (add (mul 2 3) (sub 4 1)) 9)`); kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:519-560 (`parse_literate_theorem`: `## Theorem:` header, name, `Statement` `:` `parse_term` `.`); kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:1217-1252 (`parse_term`: the word `equals` ⟶ `Eq Hole lhs rhs`, the word `implies` ⟶ a non-dependent `Pi`); kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:1261-1290 (`parse_comparison`: `<=`/`≤` ⟶ `le`, `>=`/`≥` ⟶ `ge`, `<` ⟶ `lt`, `>` ⟶ `gt`, NON-ASSOCIATIVE); kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:625-690 (`parse_proof_tactic`: `ring`, `refl`, `lia`, `cc`, `simp`, `omega` each wrap the statement's reflected `Syntax` in `try_<tactic>`)
guards: THE guard for this surface: `Repl::execute(…)` returning `Ok` IS NOT A PROOF. `try_ring`/`try_lia`/`try_cc`/`try_simp`/`try_omega`/`try_refl` are all declared `Syntax -> Derivation` via `Context::add_declaration` (kernel/src/prelude.rs:2984-2990 for `try_ring`, :3020-3026 for `try_lia`, :2685-2691 for `try_refl`). So the emitted definition body `try_lia ⌜goal⌝` is well-typed for ANY `Syntax` argument whatsoever, true or false, and `infer_type` at repl.rs:52 always succeeds. A failed tactic returns a `Derivation` whose `concludes` is `SName "Error"` (tests/phase96_tactics.rs:180-197 asserts exactly this), not a type error. The suite itself concedes the point: `phase_literate_lia.rs:105-108` and :121-124 assert `result.is_err() || result.is_ok()` — a tautology — for the FALSE statements `(lt 5 2)` and `(lt x x)`. A harness that reads `Ok` as "proved" will report `5 < 2` as a theorem.

Catches skipping the `Proof:` line. A literate theorem with no `Proof:` is registered as `Definition <name> : Prop := <statement>` (literate_parser.rs:582-585): the proposition becomes the BODY of a delta-transparent definition typed `Prop`. That is not a theorem at all, it is an abbreviation for the proposition — and `Repl::execute` returns `Ok` for it (tests/phase_literate_ring.rs:19-28 asserts precisely that `## Theorem: SimpleTheorem / Statement: True implies True.` parses with no proof). Emitting a Lean `theorem` this way records the statement and proves nothing.

Catches non-associativity of comparison. `parse_comparison` (literate_parser.rs:1261-1290) parses `additive (op additive)?` — at most ONE comparison. `a < b < c` does not parse as a chain and does not error into a useful message; a translator must decompose a Lean chain into a conjunction of two comparisons, which the `Statement:` grammar has no `and` for, so a chained comparison is out of scope for this surface.

Catches the `Hole`. `X equals Y` builds `Eq Hole X Y` with `Term::Hole` as the implicit type argument (literate_parser.rs:1227-1236). `types_equal` treats `Hole` as matching ANYTHING (type_checker.rs:1594-1597), so an `equals` statement carries a hole into the kernel by construction. That is inside LOGOS's own surface and unavoidable here — but a translator must never EMIT a `Hole` on the raw kernel path (T00-016, T11-004), and must not conclude from this surface's behaviour that holes are acceptable.

Catches `Nat` vs `Int` confusion in the operator vocabulary. `le`, `lt`, `ge`, `gt`, `add`, `sub`, `mul` are the prelude's opaque `Int` primitives (prelude.rs:352-515), axiomatised, not the `Nat` inductive. A Lean theorem about `Nat` subtraction translated to literate `x - 1 < x` is a statement about LOGOS `Int` and is NOT the Lean proposition (Lean's `Nat` subtraction truncates; see T10-017).
oracle: Two steps, both required. (1) `Repl::execute(<emitted block>)` returns `Ok`. (2) The derivation actually concludes the goal: register the statement separately and check that `Eval (concludes <name>)` equals `Eval <goalSyntax>` — the pattern `tests/phase96_tactics.rs:276-301` uses. Step (1) alone is not an oracle for this case; see @guard.

cases.title: Surface C has no `forall` — a `Statement:` cannot bind a quantified variable
cases.lean: `∀`-quantified statement, and the Lean distinction between a universally quantified theorem and one with section/auto-bound variables
cases.target: (none — the quantifier cannot be written; see @note for what a translator may do instead and why it is not this case's target)
evidence: kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:519-560 — `parse_literate_theorem` reads `## Theorem:`, a name, `Statement`, `:`, then calls `self.parse_term()` at :555. That is the ENTIRE statement grammar.

kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:1217-1252 — `parse_term` handles exactly two infix words, `equals` and `implies`, over `parse_comparison`. Nothing in the chain `parse_term → parse_comparison → parse_additive → parse_multiplicative → …` binds a variable.

kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs — the strings `forall`, `for all`, `∀` and `Forall` do not occur anywhere in the file. The sole near-hit is the comment at :2351 ("Should be forall _ : A, B (non-dependent Pi)"), describing the arrow produced by `implies`, which binds nothing.

kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:1239-1250 — `implies` builds `Term::Pi { param: "_", param_type: lhs, body_type: rhs }`. The binder name is hard-coded `"_"`, so even the one Pi-producing construct on this surface cannot be given a name for the body to mention.

tests/phase_literate_induction.rs:1-7 — the test file's own module doc: "Note: These tests focus on the `induction` keyword and bullet syntax. The forall quantifier syntax will be addressed separately." It has not been.
guards: THE trap: free variables in a `Statement:` are NOT unbound — they are effectively universally closed by the tactic that consumes them, and that closure is invisible. `Statement: x <= x.` (phase_literate_lia.rs:136-145) proves for all `x`, and a translator can therefore be tempted to render `∀ x : Nat, x ≤ x` by simply DROPPING the binder. For that one theorem the result is right. It is wrong the instant the quantifier is not outermost and not universal: · `∃ x, P x` — dropping the binder turns an existential into a universal, an unsound strengthening in the direction that still typechecks. · `(∀ x, P x) → Q` — dropping the binder makes the ANTECEDENT's quantifier disappear, and `implies` puts its LHS under a `Pi` binder named `"_"`, so the free `x` in the antecedent and the (absent) `x` in the consequent are now the same free variable. The rendered proposition is `P x → Q`, which is weaker than the source and provable from strictly less. · Alternating quantifiers (`∀ x, ∃ y, R x y`) collapse entirely. A translator must therefore NOT treat "free variable = ∀" as a general rule. It is admissible only for a statement whose Lean form is a prenex `∀` block with no other quantifier anywhere, and even then it must be recorded as a loss, not a translation.

Catches assuming the quantifier can be smuggled in as a lambda. The literate surface does have binder syntax — `given x: Nat yields …` and `|x: Nat| -> …` (literate_parser.rs:29-33) — but those are TERM-level lambdas handled by the DEFINITION parser, not reachable from `Statement:`, whose only entry point is `parse_term` at :555. A `Statement:` beginning `given x: Nat` parses `given` as an identifier and then fails on the `:`.

Catches assuming `implies` gives a usable Pi. It does — `Pi { param: "_", … }` — but with the binder name hard-coded to `"_"`, so the body can never refer to the hypothesis. Every Lean implication whose conclusion depends on the hypothesis (a dependent function type, i.e. most `∀ h : P, Q h`) is out of reach even though the arrow is available.

Catches thinking the OTHER surfaces cover this. They do not interoperate: Surface B has `for all` (T12-006) but no function terms (T12-007), and Surface C has function terms (T12-008) but no quantifier. A Lean theorem that needs BOTH — which is almost every interesting arithmetic theorem, e.g. `∀ n : Nat, n + 0 = n` — is expressible on no vernacular surface at all. That is the observation T12-011 turns into a policy.
oracle: Translator exits non-zero with E_SURFACE_C_NO_QUANTIFIER and emits no `## Theorem: … Statement:` text for any of these. If the translator instead emits the binder-dropped form, it must (a) record QUANTIFIER_ERASURE and (b) refuse for every statement here except `leReflQuantified`, whose Lean form is a bare prenex `∀`.
diag: E_SURFACE_C_NO_QUANTIFIER — must state that the `Statement:` grammar has no binder form, name the Lean binder(s) that cannot be rendered, and distinguish the two failure modes below. Must emit no literate block.

cases.title: Surface C `induction` is hardcoded to `Nat` — the named variable and the type are both ignored
cases.lean: `induction xs with | nil => … | cons h t ih => …` (and the `Nat` case, for contrast)
cases.target: A literate proof using the `induction <v>` tactic with bullet cases: ```logos ## Theorem: Test Statement: True. Proof: induction n. - auto. - auto. ``` which `parse_proof_tactic` routes to `build_induction_derivation` (literate_parser.rs:865-902), producing `try_induction (SName "Nat") <motive> (DCase c1 (DCase c2 DCaseEnd))`.
evidence: kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:865-875 — the whole of the type selection: fn build_induction_derivation( &self, _var_name: &str,        // NOTE: leading underscore — unused statement: &Term, cases: Vec<Term>, ) -> Result<Term, ParseError> { // Build the inductive type (for now assume Nat if not specified) let ind_type = Term::App( Box::new(Term::Global("SName".to_string())), Box::new(Term::Lit(Literal::Text("Nat".to_string()))), ); The inductive type is a LITERAL `"Nat"`. The variable name is bound to `_var_name` and never read, so `induction n.` and `induction xs.` build the identical term.

kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:876-902 — the case list is a flat `DCase`/`DCaseEnd` chain in bullet order, with no constructor names and no per-case binder list. Lean's `| cons h t ih =>` naming has nowhere to go.
tests/phase_literate_induction.rs:14-28 and :31-42 — the bullet syntax quoted above, verbatim; note both tests end in `let _ = result;` ("Document the behavior") rather than an assertion.
tests/phase_literate_induction.rs:48-61 — `Proof: induction.` with no variable is asserted `is_err()`, so the variable token is REQUIRED to parse even though its value is discarded.

tests/phase_literate_induction.rs:67-79 — a bullet count that does not match `Nat`'s two constructors is an error, which is how the `Nat` hard-coding becomes observable: a three-bullet proof fails, whatever the intended type.

proof/src/tactic.rs:561-600 — the SIBLING surface has the same restriction for the same reason: `ProofState::induction` substitutes `ProofTerm::Constant("Zero")` and `ProofTerm::Function("Succ", [K<n>])` (tactic.rs:583-586). `induction_over` (tactic.rs:623-636) is the generic version and is Rust-API only — `tactic_script.rs:308-327` has no word that canonicalises to it.
guards: Catches a translator that emits `induction xs.` for a Lean list induction and takes the resulting `Ok` as success. The parse succeeds (the variable token is consumed, the bullets are counted), the emitted term is `try_induction (SName "Nat") …`, and the definition typechecks because `try_induction` is an opaque declaration over `Syntax`. Nothing anywhere reports that the type is wrong. This is a `degrade` verdict only because the loss record makes it detectable; a translator that omits the loss record has produced a certificate for induction over the wrong type.

Catches relying on the bullet count as a type check. It is a check against `Nat`'s two constructors, not against the source type's. A Lean induction over a two-constructor type that is not `Nat` (`List`, `Bool`, `Option`) passes the count check and is still mis-recorded; a three-constructor type fails with an error about bullet count that says nothing about types.

Catches the variable name. `_var_name` is discarded, so if the Lean proof inducts on a variable that is not the statement's first, the literate rendering inducts on whatever the motive's first binder is. Since Surface C has no binders at all (T12-009), "the motive's first binder" is itself ill-defined — which is why induction on this surface is only usable for statements that are already effectively closed over a single `Nat`.
oracle: `Repl::execute(<emitted block>)` returns `Ok`, AND the loss record contains INDUCTION_TYPE_PINNED, AND — for any Lean source whose induction is not over `Nat` — the translator either refuses or records the loss with the source type named. A harness must additionally check `concludes` against the goal syntax (see T12-008), because `Ok` alone does not mean the induction closed.
loss: INDUCTION_TYPE_PINNED. The proof term records induction over `Nat` regardless of the Lean source's inductive type, and records neither the variable name nor the constructor names. For a Lean `induction n : Nat` proof this loses only the variable name — acceptable, because `build_induction_derivation` takes the motive from the statement and `Nat` really is the type. For any other type it is not a loss but a falsehood; see @guard.

CASE_BINDER_ERASURE. `| succ k ih =>` names the predecessor and the induction hypothesis; the bullet list names neither. On the Surface A sibling the hypothesis is named `ih` and the step variable is a fresh `K<n>` constant (tactic.rs:577, :587), so a script that refers to a Lean-chosen name will not find it.

cases.title: Surface selection policy — which of the four targets a given Lean theorem goes to
cases.lean: the whole of it: this case is the synthesis for tier 12 and the routing rule every other case in the tier is a boundary condition of
cases.target: A per-theorem ROUTING DECISION, recorded in the translator's output alongside the emitted artefact, chosen by the procedure below. There are FOUR targets, not three: K. raw kernel      — `logicaffeine_kernel::Term` + `Context::add_definition` A. English theorem — `## Theorem:` / `Given:` / `Prove:` / `Proof:` B. formal FOL      — `## Theory` / `Axiom` / `Theorem … cites … : … prove …` C. literate kernel — `## Theorem:` / `Statement:` / `Proof:` THE ANSWER, stated plainly: **for almost any real Lean theorem the target is K.** Emit a kernel `Term` for the proposition, emit a kernel `Term` for the proof, `infer_type` the latter, and `add_definition` the pair. The three English surfaces are entry points for HUMAN-AUTHORED content and are not translation targets; each is reachable only by a Lean theorem that has already been narrowed to a fragment far smaller than Lean itself. The decision procedure, applied to the theorem's ELABORATED type: 0. Contains `sorryAx`?                                    ⟶ reject (T06-017) 1. Type mentions a `Sort`/universe, a dependent `Pi` whose body uses the binder at TYPE level, a `Lambda`, a `Match`, a `Fix`, a structure projection, an inductive family, or any typeclass argument?                                ⟶ K 2. Strip the prenex quantifier block. In the remaining propositional skeleton, is every argument of every atom a bare variable or constant (no function application)? · NO  ⟶ A and B are impossible (T12-002, T12-007); go to 3. · YES ⟶ go to 4. 3. Is the ORIGINAL quantifier structure a (possibly empty) prenex ∀-block and nothing else — no ∃, no nested ∀, no quantifier under a connective — AND is every operation in the LOGOS `Int` primitive vocabulary (`add sub mul div le lt ge gt`, or their infix spellings)? · YES ⟶ C   (T12-008; record QUANTIFIER_ERASURE, T12-009) · NO  ⟶ K   ← this is where most arithmetic lands 4. Is the theorem one member of a multi-lemma AXIOMATIC DEVELOPMENT over one opaque sort, with named axioms and lemma-to-lemma citation? · YES ⟶ B   (T12-006) 5. Is it a single small entailment over UNARY predicates whose names are English nouns/adjectives the LOGOS lexicon canonicalises, with ≤ ~10 premises and no equality between distinct constants? · YES ⟶ A   (T12-001) 6. Otherwise                                              ⟶ K
evidence: WHY K IS THE DEFAULT — the vernacular surfaces cannot hold a Lean type. · proof/src/lib.rs:199-244 — Surfaces A and B both terminate in `ProofExpr`: `Predicate`/`Identity`/`Atom`, the connectives, and `ForAll`/`Exists` whose binder is a bare `variable: String` (lib.rs:235-243). There is no type on a binder, no sort, no application in the proposition, no abstraction. · proof/src/lib.rs:133-150 — `ProofTerm` is `Constant`/`Variable`/`Function`/ `Group`/`BoundVarRef`. First-order, untyped. · kernel/src/term.rs:443-545 — `Term` has `Sort`, `Pi`, `Lambda`, `App`, `Match`, `Fix`, `MutualFix`, `Let`, `Const{levels}`. This is the ONLY representation in LOGOS that can hold a Lean `Expr`, and it is reachable only through K (and, in the reflected `Syntax` encoding, C). · kernel/src/context.rs:442 — `add_definition(name, ty, body)`: "a `theorem` is just this with a `Prop` type — there is no separate theorem form." A Lean theorem is NATIVELY a kernel definition. The vernacular adds nothing to a translated theorem that the kernel path does not already have.

WHY THE SURFACES ARE FOR HUMANS, not for translators. · language/src/compile.rs:1070-1105 — `compile_theorem` begins by LEXING ENGLISH: the input goes through `Lexer`, `DiscoveryPass` and the full `Parser` before a `Stmt::Theorem` exists. A Lean `Expr` is already elaborated; re-encoding it as English prose so an English parser can re-derive a weaker structure is lossy by construction. · tests/phase63_theorem_parser.rs:26-29 — predicate identity on Surface A depends on the NOUN LEXICON: "Phase 64: Noun canonicalization ensures 'men' → 'Man' so predicates match." A translator on Surface A does not control its own identifiers. · language/src/compile.rs:1106-1119 — only the FIRST `## Theorem` block in a document is proved (`find_map` over the statements). A Lean file with N theorems needs N separate Surface A documents, and there is no mechanism for the N-th to cite the first. On K, they are N `add_definition` calls into one `Context`, and later ones may use earlier ones by name — which is the ordinary structure of a Lean file. · proof/src/development.rs:20-22 + proof/src/verify.rs:98-130 — Surface B DOES have citation (`cites`), but only within a single `## Theory` body, and an unknown cited name is silently treated as an external given (verify.rs:110-113) rather than reported.

WHY THE THREE SURFACES DO NOT COMPOSE — each lacks what another has, so a theorem needing two features has no vernacular home: · A has ∀/∃ (through English quantifiers) but NO term grammar (language/src/parser/mod.rs:6072, :6136 — `parse_sentence`; T12-002). · B has ∀/∃ and n-ary relations but terms are single identifiers (proof/src/formula.rs:429-435; T12-007). · C has real terms — s-expression application, infix `+ - * < > <= >=`, the word `equals` (kernel/src/interface/literate_parser.rs:1217-1290) — but NO quantifier at all (literate_parser.rs:519-560, :1217-1252; T12-009). The intersection "quantifier AND function term" is empty. `∀ n : Nat, n + 0 = n` — the first theorem anyone writes — is expressible on NO vernacular surface. It is two lines on K.

WHY C IS NOT A KERNEL PATH IN DISGUISE — literate `Proof:` tactics wrap the statement in a REFLECTED `Syntax` term and produce a `Derivation`, not a proof of the statement: literate_parser.rs:625-690 emits `try_<tactic> ⌜stmt⌝`, and prelude.rs:2984-2990 / :3020-3026 / :2685-2691 declare every `try_*` as `Syntax -> Derivation` via `add_declaration`. The resulting definition typechecks for a false statement as readily as a true one; see T12-008.
guards: Catches the most natural and most wrong architecture for a Lean→LOGOS translator: "LOGOS has a theorem vernacular, so translate Lean theorems into it." The vernacular is an English front end whose internal representation is untyped first-order logic. Every dependent type, every universe, every inductive, every recursor, every typeclass — the entire content of tiers 0–7 of this corpus — is inexpressible in it. A translator built on that premise can handle the Socrates syllogism and essentially nothing from a real Lean development.

Catches the opposite over-correction: routing EVERYTHING to K and never emitting vernacular. That is defensible, but it must be a recorded decision, because the four cases this tier marks `translate` (T12-001, T12-004, T12-006, T12-008) are exactly the ones where a vernacular rendering is both faithful and better — a `## Theory` development keeps its axiom names and citation graph, which K flattens into anonymous `String` keys (context.rs).

Catches routing on the Lean TACTIC SCRIPT instead of the Lean TYPE. `by omega` does not mean "arithmetic, send it to C"; `by decide` does not mean "send it to A with `Proof: Auto.`". The routing input is the elaborated type, because that is what determines expressibility. The proof script only influences the `Proof:` line once a surface has already been chosen (T12-003).

Catches per-theorem routing without per-FILE consistency. If `theorem b` uses `theorem a`, both must be on K, because there is no way for a Surface A or C artefact to be cited from a kernel `Term` and no way for a kernel definition to be cited from a Surface A block. Routing must be computed on the dependency closure, not on one declaration at a time.

Catches treating rule 3 as "arithmetic ⟶ C". Rule 3 fires only for a prenex-∀ statement over the `Int` primitive vocabulary. Lean `Nat` subtraction truncates and LOGOS `sub` is the opaque `Int` primitive (prelude.rs:352-515), so `n - 1 < n` is a DIFFERENT proposition on C than in Lean (T10-017); and `Nat` is an inductive in LOGOS while `Int` is axiomatised (T10-004). Most Lean arithmetic therefore falls through rule 3 to K.
oracle: For every theorem the translator emits, its machine-readable output names the target (`K`/`A`/`B`/`C`) and the rule number that selected it. A harness checks: (1) the routing matches the expected target recorded in this corpus for every tier-12 case; (2) the emitted artefact is well-formed for that target and passes that target's own oracle; (3) no theorem is routed to A or B whose type has a function application in an atom's argument; (4) no theorem is routed to C whose type has a non-prenex quantifier; (5) every theorem in a dependency cycle or chain shares one target.
loss: SURFACE_PROVENANCE. Routing to K discards the vernacular entirely: the LOGOS artefact is a `Term` in a `Context`, with no `## Theorem` block, no English rendering, and no `Proof:` line. Nothing about the Lean theorem's tactic script survives, and the LOGOS-side document a human would read does not exist. This is the price of the correct answer and must be recorded.

ROUTING_IS_A_CHOICE. The decision is made by the translator, not forced by LOGOS, and it is observable: the same Lean theorem routed to A and to K yields different LOGOS artefacts with different trust characteristics (T12-013) and, on A, possibly a different engine again (T12-014). The routing decision must therefore appear in the machine-readable output for every theorem, with the rule number that produced it — otherwise a conformance report cannot be compared across translator versions.
note: INDEX.md marks this case `degrade`, and that is right, but the reason is worth stating: the degradation is not in any one translation, it is in the POLICY. There is no routing that carries every Lean theorem faithfully into a LOGOS artefact that is also human-readable at the surface, because the readable surfaces are strictly weaker than the kernel and do not compose with each other. Choosing K everywhere is sound and lossy; choosing a vernacular where it fits is lossy in a different place. What is NOT acceptable is choosing silently.

cases.title: `ProofStrategy::Induction` and `ProofStrategy::ByRule` are dead variants
cases.lean: any `theorem` whose Lean proof a translator would classify as "by induction" or "by a named rule" and encode as a proof-strategy annotation
cases.target: (none — neither variant is constructible from surface text, and neither is consumed by any driver)
evidence: language/src/ast/theorem.rs:41-61 — `ProofStrategy` has four variants: `Auto`, `Induction(String)`, `ByRule(String)`, `Script(String)`.

The complete set of construction sites in the workspace, by grep for `ProofStrategy::`: · language/src/parser/mod.rs:6153  ⟶ `Auto`   (the literal word `Auto`) · language/src/parser/mod.rs:6171  ⟶ `Auto`   (an empty `Proof:` line) · language/src/parser/mod.rs:6173  ⟶ `Script` (everything else) · language/src/parser/mod.rs:6178  ⟶ `Auto`   (no `Proof:` line at all) · language/src/ast/theorem.rs:64   ⟶ `Auto`   (the `Default` impl) `Induction` and `ByRule` are constructed NOWHERE.

The complete set of consumption sites: · language/src/compile.rs:1136 — `if let ProofStrategy::Script(src) = …`, with everything else falling to the `Auto` arm at :1152. · compile/src/ui_bridge.rs:635 — `ProofStrategy::Script(s) => Some(s.clone())` · compile/src/ui_bridge.rs:644 — `is_auto: matches!(…, ProofStrategy::Auto)` No driver has an arm for `Induction` or `ByRule`. Even if one were constructed, `compile.rs:1136` would route it to `prove_certify_check`, i.e. it would behave as `Auto` while carrying a variable name nothing reads.
language/src/ast/theorem.rs:47-54 — both dead variants carry doc comments with worked examples (`Proof: Induction on n.`, `Proof: ModusPonens.`). Those are the two spellings an implementer will copy.
language/src/parser/mod.rs:6157-6174 — the fall-through that turns both spellings into `Script(<joined lexemes>)`.

proof/src/tactic_script.rs:308-327 — `canonical` has no arm mapping `modusponens` (or any inference-rule name) to a tactic, so a `ByRule`-style spelling dies at tactic_script.rs:261-262 with ``unknown tactic `ModusPonens` ``.

proof/src/tactic_script.rs:290 + :346-351 — an `Induction`-style spelling dies with `"trailing tokens after the script"` instead, because `induction` is zero-argument. The two dead variants therefore fail DIFFERENTLY, and neither failure mentions strategies.
guards: Catches an implementer who designs the emitter around the TYPE. Reading `ast/theorem.rs:41-61` gives a four-way classification of Lean proofs — auto, induction, single-rule, script — which is a perfectly reasonable design and maps neatly onto Lean's `by decide` / `by induction` / `by exact` / general tactic blocks. Two of those four branches can never be exercised. A translator built on that classification will emit text for half its cases that is not merely unsupported but *misparsed into the other branch*.

Catches the belief that an unrecognised `Proof:` line is a parse error. It is not (parser/mod.rs:6157-6174 accepts any lexeme sequence), so a translator that validates its output by re-parsing will see no problem. The failure appears only at `compile_theorem`, and both dead spellings surface as theorem failures whose `Error:` field talks about scripts — a harness matching on "proof search failed" will classify them as "LOGOS is not strong enough".

Catches the near-miss `Proof: Induction.` — which is LIVE, because `Induction` canonicalises to the zero-argument `induction` tactic and the trailing `.` is a separator. It parses, it runs, and it inducts on whatever the focused goal's outermost `∀` binds, which is not necessarily the Lean variable. A translator that "fixes" the dead spelling by deleting the variable has converted a loud failure into a silent one. See T12-005.

Catches encoding an inference rule name in a different position — e.g. the theorem NAME or a `cites` list — on the theory that `ByRule` was meant for it. Surface A has no citation mechanism at all; `cites` belongs to Surface B's `Theorem <name> cites <n1>, <n2>: …` (proof/src/development.rs:20-22), and its argument is a THEOREM name, never an inference-rule name. Cited names that do not match a theorem in the development are silently treated as external givens (proof/src/verify.rs:110-113) — no diagnostic.
oracle: The translator's emitted text contains no `Proof:` line whose content is an inference-rule name or `Induction <var>`. Negative oracle for a harness: `compile_theorem` on a block with `Proof: Induction on n.` returns `Err` containing `"trailing tokens after the script"`, and on `Proof: ModusPonens.` returns `Err` containing `"unknown tactic"`. If either returns `Ok`, the LOGOS build under test is not the one this corpus is written against.
diag: E_DEAD_PROOF_STRATEGY — must state that the `ProofStrategy` enum's `Induction`/`ByRule` variants are unreachable from surface text, name the spelling the translator was about to emit, and give the live alternative (`Auto`, or a `Script` built from the tactic vocabulary at tactic_script.rs:275-292). Must emit no `Proof:` line naming an inference rule or an induction variable.
note: INDEX.md classes this `reject`, and that is right for the emitter. Note the asymmetry it creates for a CONSUMER, though: a translator that reads a LOGOS document (rather than writing one) must still handle all four variants in its `match`, because the enum is public and a future LOGOS release could start constructing them. Treating the dead pair as `unreachable!()` is a latent panic.

cases.title: The trust door — a derivation is not a proof; `compile_theorem` returns `Ok` for both
cases.lean: any `theorem`; the case is about how a translator's harness decides that the LOGOS side succeeded
cases.target: Whatever surface the theorem is routed to, the translator's success predicate must be `VerifiedProof::verified == true`, never "a derivation came back" and never "the call returned `Ok`". Concretely, one of: · `compile_theorem(text)` ⟶ `Ok(s)` AND `s.contains("[kernel-verified]")` · `compile_theorem_for_ui(text)` ⟶ `r.verified == true` · `prove_certify_check(&premises, &goal)` ⟶ `.verified == true` · the raw kernel path ⟶ `Context::add_definition` succeeded after `infer_type` returned the goal's type
evidence: proof/src/verify.rs:26-44 — the invariant, in LOGOS's own words: "`verified == true` **iff** `proof_term.is_some()` and that term type-checks in `kernel_ctx`. When verification fails, `derivation` may still be present (the chainer found *a* derivation) but it is never reported as verified".
proof/src/verify.rs:1-15 — the module doc: "A derivation alone never counts as verified — `verified == true` is always backed by a `Term` that re-checks under `infer_type` in the returned `Context`."

proof/src/verify.rs:501-580 — `finish_check` has THREE distinct exits that return `derivation: Some(derivation)` with `verified: false`: · :513-521  certification failed (`certify` returned `Err`) · :540-548  the certified term did not type-check (`infer_type` failed) · :556-563  the goal's own type could not be built and a fourth, further down, when the inferred type is not the goal's type.

language/src/compile.rs:1154-1176 — the door itself. BOTH of the first two arms return `Ok`: Some(derivation) if outcome.verified => Ok(format!( "Theorem '{}' Proved! [kernel-verified]\n{}", …)), Some(derivation) => Ok(format!( "Theorem '{}' — derivation found but NOT kernel-certified (this is not a proof)\n{}", …)), None => Err(…) So `compile_theorem(...).is_ok()` is TRUE for an uncertified derivation, and the only thing distinguishing the two is a substring.

language/src/compile.rs:1129-1135 — the comment at the call site says the same thing: "This door reports a proof when a derivation is found, annotating whether the kernel certified it; the strong (kernel-checked) guarantee is exposed by `verify_theorem` and the `verified` flag on `TheoremCompileResult`."

proof/src/certifier.rs:1546-1557 — a concrete producer of the unverified state: an `InferenceRule::OracleVerification` leaf is deliberately non-certifiable ("oracle (Z3) results are not kernel-certifiable — they attest satisfiability but produce no checkable proof term"), so a goal the engine discharges only through the oracle yields derivation-without-proof.
tests/phase_oracle_trust_boundary.rs:14-35 — that behaviour asserted directly: a hand-built `OracleVerification` leaf must fail `certify`, and the rejection must name the oracle.

proof/src/lib.rs:488-728 — `InferenceRule` has 46 variants; seven (`ModalAccess`, `ModalGeneralization`, `TemporalTransitivity`, `TemporalInduction`, `TemporalUnfolding`, `EventualityProgress`, `UntilInduction`) have no certifier arm and fall to the catch-all at certifier.rs:1558-1560, "Certification not implemented for {:?}" — a second family of derivation-without-proof. (T11-021.)

compile/src/ui_bridge.rs:644 and tests/phase_studio_grid_proof.rs:32-36 — the UI path exposes the flag directly as `r.verified`, which is the predicate the suite's own tests assert on. A translator harness should prefer this path for exactly that reason.
guards: THE guard of this tier, and the one that corrupts a whole library rather than one theorem. A harness written as if compile_theorem(&text).is_ok() { report.pass(case_id) } reports as PROVED every theorem for which LOGOS found a derivation it could not certify. That is not a translator bug at all — the translation may be perfect — it is a *measurement* bug, and it silently inflates the conformance score in exactly the cases where the corpus is most valuable. Worse, the failure is invisible in the emitted text: the same `## Theorem` block returns `Ok` either way.

Catches matching on `"Proved"`. The certified string is `"Theorem '…' Proved! [kernel-verified]"` and the uncertified one is `"Theorem '…' — derivation found but NOT kernel-certified (this is not a proof)"`. Several tests in the suite (e.g. tests/phase63_theorem_parser.rs:47-51) assert `output.contains("Proved")`, which is adequate for those tests because the uncertified string does not contain `"Proved"` — but it is fragile, and `"[kernel-verified]"` is the only substring that means what a conformance harness needs it to mean.

Catches treating a returned `DerivationTree` as evidence. `VerifiedProof` exposes `derivation`, `proof_term` and `verified` separately precisely because they come apart. The checkable artefact is `proof_term`, and even that is insufficient on its own: `finish_check` additionally requires that the term's inferred type BE the goal's type (verify.rs:532-536, "The term must not merely be well-typed — its type must be the goal"). A harness that re-checks a returned `proof_term` with `infer_type` and stops there accepts a well-typed proof of the WRONG proposition.

Catches importing the mistake into the literate surface, where it is worse. On Surface C there is no `verified` flag at all: `Repl::execute` returns `Ok` whenever the definition typechecks, and `try_lia ⌜false thing⌝` always typechecks (T12-008). The literate analogue of this guard is to evaluate `concludes <name>` and compare it to the goal's `Syntax`.
oracle: The harness's pass predicate is `verified == true` (or the `"[kernel-verified]"` substring), and the conformance report records, per case, which of {kernel-verified, derivation-only, no-derivation, parse-error} occurred. A meta-oracle: feeding the harness a theorem whose only route is the oracle must produce a FAIL, not a PASS.
loss: TRUST_LEVEL_UNRECORDED is the loss this case is about: a translator that records "LOGOS accepted it" without recording WHICH door it came through has produced a conformance report in which certified and uncertified results are indistinguishable. The verdict is `degrade` rather than `translate` because every surface can return this state and no surface prevents it; the obligation is to record the trust level per theorem, not to avoid it.

cases.title: The grid-solver fast path silently routes `Auto` to a different engine and a different proof object
cases.lean: a finite-domain entailment: a declared bijection (closure + at-most-one) over two small categories, plus cross-pins, concluding one cell
cases.target: The same Surface A `## Theorem` block as T12-001 — no syntax marks the fast path — proved through `compile_theorem_for_ui`: ```logos ## Theorem: Simon Given: Alpha is a trip. Given: Beta is a trip. Given: Alpha is not Beta. Given: Every trip is in 2003 or in 2004. Given: Every trip is in Florida or in Maine. Given: Exactly one trip is in 2003. Given: Exactly one trip is in Florida. Given: Alpha is in 2003. Given: Alpha is in Florida. Prove: Beta is in Maine. Proof: Auto. ``` whose result carries `verified == true` and a `DerivationTree` built by `logicaffeine_proof::grid_solver::grid_prove` — NOT by the backward chainer.
evidence: tests/phase_studio_grid_proof.rs:17-46 — the block above is quoted verbatim from `grid_cell_proves_via_studio_path`, asserted `r.verified` and asserted that the rendered tree contains `"Contradiction"` or `"DisjunctionElim"`; tests/phase_studio_grid_proof.rs:51-64 — the contrast case: the Socrates syllogism through the SAME entry point must keep `"UniversalInst"` in its tree, i.e. must NOT be grounded; compile/src/ui_bridge.rs:851-905 — the fast path. `if looks_like_grid(&premises)` replaces `prove_certify_check` with: `prepare_premises_opts(&premises, true)`, then `grid_solver::grid_prove`, then `verify::check_derivation`, then `.filter(|vp| vp.verified)`; on failure it consults the RUP tier (`rup::entails_certified`) and only then falls back to `prove_certify_check_bounded(&grounded, &g, 60)`; compile/src/ui_bridge.rs:921-923 — the `else` arm, the ordinary `prove_certify_check(&premises, &goal)`; compile/src/ui_bridge.rs:3939-3953 — `looks_like_grid`: true when `grounding::at_most_one_lemmas(premises)` is non-empty OR any premise is a `ForAll` (possibly nested, possibly under `Temporal`) whose body is an `Implies` with an `Or` consequent. That is the entire trigger — a structural test on the premises, with no flag and no syntax; compile/src/ui_bridge.rs:827-831 — a solved grid table is additionally attached to the result whenever `is_auto && looks_like_grid(&premises)`; compile/src/ui_bridge.rs:3963-3985 — `prepare_premises_opts(.., true)` adds `at_most_one_lemmas`, `definite_property_implications` AND `functionality_lemmas`, the last of which is given ONLY to the grid solver and deliberately withheld from the backward chainer; compile/src/ui_bridge.rs:832-845 — a third route on the same `is_auto` arm: an `Exists`-shaped goal is answered by `answer_wh`, returning witnesses and NO derivation at all (`(None, verified, verr, Some(witnesses))`).
guards: Catches a harness that pins the proof tree. Adding one premise of the form "every X is A or B", or one "exactly one X is A", flips `looks_like_grid` and changes every subsequent derivation in that theorem from `UniversalInst` to `Contradiction`/`DisjunctionElim`. A regression suite that snapshots rendered trees will show a large unexplained diff caused by a premise the translator emitted for unrelated reasons.

Catches choosing an entry point by convenience. `compile_theorem` returns a formatted `String` and is the obvious API; `compile_theorem_for_ui` returns a `TheoremCompileResult` with a `verified` field (T12-013) and is the one the suite's own tests assert on. They are not interchangeable: the former lacks the grid route, the wh-answer route, and the structured trust flag. A translator that develops against one and reports against the other will see theorems that "regress" with no change to the emitted text.

Catches assuming a returned derivation exists. On the `Exists`-goal route (ui_bridge.rs:832-841) the result is `verified == true` with `derivation: None` and an `answer` list of witnesses. A harness that requires `derivation.is_some()` as part of its pass predicate will fail every existential goal that LOGOS actually answered.

Catches reading the fast path as an optimisation that cannot change verdicts. It can: the grid route's fallback is `prove_certify_check_bounded(&grounded, &g, 60)` — depth 60 over GROUNDED premises — whereas the general route is `prove_certify_check`, i.e. depth 100 over the originals (proof/src/verify.rs:70-72). A goal reachable at depth 80 in the general engine is not reachable in the grid route's fallback.
oracle: `compile_theorem_for_ui(<emitted text>)` returns `r.verified == true`, AND the loss record names PROOF_OBJECT_IDENTITY whenever `looks_like_grid` would fire — which a translator can predict from its own emitted premises without calling LOGOS: any premise rendering as `∀x(P x → (A x ∨ B x))`, or any "exactly one" premise. A harness must NOT assert on derivation shape for such cases, and must not compare trees across entry points.
loss: PROOF_OBJECT_IDENTITY. The theorem is the same and the `verified` flag is the same, but the artefact is not: the fast path returns a solver tree (`Contradiction` / `DisjunctionElim` over grounded, quantifier-free premises) where the general path would return `UniversalInst` / `ModusPonens` over the quantified originals. Any translator obligation phrased over the derivation — round-tripping it, diffing it against the Lean proof term, counting rule applications, asserting a proof *shape* — is measuring a different object depending on premise structure it did not choose.

PREMISE_SET_AUGMENTED. The proof is not of `premises ⊢ goal` as emitted. The grid route proves `prepare_premises_opts(premises, true) ⊢ erase_tense(goal)`, where the premise set has been extended with at-most-one lemmas, definite- description implications and functionality lemmas, and tense has been erased from the goal. These are entailed by the originals, so the result is sound — but a conformance report that claims "LOGOS proved exactly the premises we emitted" is overclaiming.

ENGINE_NONDETERMINISM_ACROSS_ENTRY_POINTS. `compile_theorem` (language/src/compile.rs:1152) has NO grid branch: it always calls `prove_certify_check`. `compile_theorem_for_ui` (compile/src/ui_bridge.rs:851) does. So the same emitted text proved through the two public entry points takes two different engines, and may differ in success as well as in shape — the fast path exists precisely because the general chainer is impractical on these premises.
